title: Source: Vikings will trade for a quarterback today
summary: The clock is ticking toward 4:00 p.m. ET.
full_text: The Vikings' quarterback situation has been a rollercoaster with more lows than highs since Kirk Cousins left for the Falcons and Sam Darnold left for the Seahawks. They're expected to make their next attempt at fixing the situation on Tuesday. A source with knowledge of the situation tells PFT that the Vikings will trade for a quarterback before Tuesday's 4:00 p.m. ET deadline. The options, per the source, are "Daniel Jones, Geno Smith, Mac Jones, Kirk Cousins, TBD surprise, TBD huge surprise, but it will be someone." Other possibilities mentioned by the source were Marcus Mariota and Jameis Winston. Whatever the Vikings do, it's going to cost them. If they'd had a deal in place before Monday night's game, it would have been cheaper. After last night's debacle from Carson Wentz, teams will be putting their thumbs — and elbows — on the scale. Regardless, they need to do something. If they don't, 6-2 could become 6-11. And that would possibly result in a new coach in Minnesota come 2027. In the categories of "surprise" and/or "huge surprise" would be (and this is just the throwing of a dart): Justin Herbert, Matthew Stafford, and Sam Darnold.
author: Mike Florio

title: Report: Kendre Miller to visit Cowboys on Tuesday
summary: The Cowboys need a running back with Tyler Goodson injured and they're reportedly set to meet with a veteran option on Tuesday.
full_text: ' The Cowboys need a running back with Tyler Goodson injured and they're reportedly set to meet with a veteran option on Tuesday. Todd Archer of ESPN.com reports that Kendre Miller will be visiting the team. Miller was released by the Saints ahead of their Week 9 win over the Browns. Miller had 57 carries for 159 yards and two touchdowns in six games for New Orleans this season. The 2023 third-round pick had 184 carries for 656 yards and five touchdowns during his entire run with the Saints. He also caught 29 passes for 217 yards. Goodson is expected to miss multiple weeks with a knee injury. Cowboys owner Jerry Jones said on Tuesday morning that the team was likelier to add help behind Javonte Williams via free agency than a trade.
author: Josh Alper

title: Not many players are truly untradeable
summary: In recent days (including today), reports have emerged that certain players will not be traded.
full_text: In recent days (including today), reports have emerged that certain players will not be traded. That definitely does not mean they're untradeable. It means only that the team has yet to get an offer it will accept. The mere process of working the insiders to send that message could give the process one final goosing. Regardless, not many players are truly untradeable. For all but a handful of players, there's an offer that his current team would accept. The only players who currently wouldn't be traded, in our view, are Bills quarterback Josh Allen, Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow, Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes, Bears quarterback Caleb Williams, Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence, Packers quarterback Jordan Love, and probably 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy. Any other can be had, at the right offer (up to and including three first-round picks plus more). By now, teams know whether the right offer will be made. Which makes it easy for them to throw out their chests and say the player won't be traded. And to reverse course if an offer they can't refuse is made before 4:00 p.m. ET today.
author: Mike Florio

title: Bengals call off trade for Arnold Ebiketie
summary: Tuesday morning brought word that the Bengals had agreed to acquire pass rusher Arnold Ebiketie in a trade with the Eagles, but that agreement will not be finalized ahead of the 4 p.m.
full_text: Tuesday morning brought word that the Bengals had agreed to acquire pass rusher Arnold Ebiketie in a trade with the Eagles, but that agreement will not be finalized ahead of the 4 p.m. ET trade deadline. According to multiple reports, the Bengals have called off the trade and will not be sending a 2027 sixth-round pick to Philadelphia. The reports surfaced shortly after a tweet by OverTheCap.com contributor Nick Korte explained the compensatory pick ramifications of the deal . According to Korte, who focuses on the compensatory pick system, acquiring Ebiketie would put the Bengals in position to forfeit the third-round compensatory pick that they are currently set to receive for Trey Hendrickson leaving the team to sign with the Ravens. That would greatly increase the price that the Bengals were going to pay to acquire Ebiketie and it appears they found it too high to move forward with the deal.
author: Josh Alper

title: Falcons signing K Jake Moody, releasing K Nick Folk
summary: The Falcons are swapping out one kicker for another.
full_text: The Falcons are swapping out one kicker for another. Atlanta is signing Jake Moody off of Baltimore's practice squad and releasing Nick Folk, according to Jordan Schultz of The Schultz Report. Folk missed a field goal in two consecutive games and has made just 13-of-18 this season. He’s also missed an extra point, going 17-of-18 in the category in nine games. With Tyler Loop on injured reserve, Moody was elevated from the practice squad and served as Baltimore’s kicker for Thursday’s loss to the Jaguars. He made a 53-yard field goal and an extra point. Moody kicked for three different teams last season, finishing 19-of-23 on field goals and 15-of-16 on extra points. Baltimore will need another kicker with Loop on IR for at least few more weeks.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Jordan Davis is "a little disappointed" to be traded by Eagles
summary: For players with no-trade clauses and most starting-level quarterbacks, there's no reason to worry about a rogue wind blowing them to a new team in a new city.
full_text: For players with no-trade clauses and most starting-level quarterbacks, there's no reason to worry about a rogue wind blowing them to a new team in a new city. For everyone else, it can happen at any time. It happened on Monday to defensive tackle Jordan Davis. After the deal was done that sent him to the Jaguars for a 2027 first-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick, Davis commented on the situation. "A little disappointed but, you know, understanding that they're in the rebuilding process glad and you know, for the picks — first-round and second-round pick — obviously helps the team and, you know, I love those guys," Davis told Jeff Skversky of Fox 29. "So however I can help the team, even in my departure, I’m absolutely glad to be doing that ." He may or may not be glad for the likely uptick in his workload. In Philly, Davis was on the field for 52 percent of the snaps. Given what the Jaguars gave up for him, they'll need more than that to justify the trade. Either way, it's part of life in the NFL. Even though the 32 businesses are independent, they're branches of the same tree. An involuntary transfer is always a possibility for the vast majority of players.
author: Mike Florio

title: Brandon Aiyuk likely will be cut by 4:00 p.m. ET today
summary: A key fact has come into focus regarding the Brandon Aiyuk situation.
full_text: ' A key fact has come into focus regarding the Brandon Aiyuk situation. And it points to a likely conclusion to the 49ers' portion of the situation by 4:00 p.m. ET today. The 49ers likely will release Aiyuk. Although it's not clear how this happened (the Player Personnel Manual indicates that his 2025 salary of $1.17 million should have tolled into 2026 due to placement on the reserve/left squad list), official NFL records now show Aiyuk as having a base salary of $13.75 million for the balance of 2026. This means that, if he's on the roster at the close of business on Tuesday, his salary for Week 10 vests — at $1.52 million. They surely won't be able to trade him at that number. And they surely don't want to give him $1.52 million. Even more surely, coach Kyle Shanahan doesn't want him in the building. The only realistic option is to cut him. There's still a story to be told as to the deal that was done to get the league to reinstate Aiyuk. The NFL and 49ers were putting the squeeze on Aiyuk to refund upwards of $13 million in previously-paid bonus money. Our guess? Aiyuk wired a sizable payment to the 49ers (maybe $6 million or $7 million), the NFL reinstated him, and now Aiyuk will get his freedom. The next question will become where he lands.
author: Mike Florio

title: Report: Dolphins DT Zach Sieler to have season-ending biceps surgery
summary: The Dolphins will reportedly be without one of their top defensive players for the rest of the season.
full_text: ''' The Dolphins will reportedly be without one of their top defensive players for the rest of the season. Adam Schefter of ESPN reports that defensive tackle Zach Sieler tore his biceps early in Sunday's loss to the Lions. He was able to play the rest of the game, but needs to have surgery that will end his season. Sieler started the first eight games of the season for the Dolphins. He had 24 tackles and two sacks in those appearances. He joined the team during the 2019 season and has 377 tackles, 37.5 sacks, two interceptions, five forced fumbles and six fumble recoveries during his time in Miami. Sieler signed a three-year extension with the Dolphins ahead of the 2025 season. The deal ties him to the team through the 2029 season with cap hits of more than $20 million each year.
author: Josh Alper

title: Bengals agree to acquire Arnold Ebiketie from Eagles
summary: The Bengals are bringing in some help for their defensive front.
full_text: The Bengals are bringing in some help for their defensive front. Per Ian Rapoport of NFL Network, Cincinnati is trading for Philadelphia edge rusher Arnold Ebiketie. The Eagles will receive a 2027 sixth-round pick to complete the deal. Ebiketie signed a one-year deal with Philadelphia in March. He’s recorded 25 total tackles this season with two QB hits in nine games. A second-round pick in 2022, Ebiketie has recorded 16.5 sacks in his 76 career games.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Cardinals add QB Joey Aguilar off Jaguars' practice squad
summary: After trading quarterback Jacoby Brissett, and then losing his replacement Gardner Minshew to a potentially season-ending elbow injury, the Cardinals are bringing in quarterback reinforcements.
full_text: After trading quarterback Jacoby Brissett, and then losing his replacement Gardner Minshew to a potentially season-ending elbow injury, the Cardinals are bringing in quarterback reinforcements. Joey Aguilar will join the Cardinals' 53-player roster from the Jaguars' practice squad, according to Jeremy Fowler of ESPN. The 25-year-old Aguilar was the starting quarterback for the Tennessee Volunteers last season and spent a total of seven years in college football, with two at City College of San Francisco, two at Diablo Valley College and two at Appalachian State before transferring to Tennessee. The only healthy quarterback in Arizona right now is rookie Carson Beck. Aguilar will presumably back him up on Sunday against the Rams, and the Cardinals will likely add another quarterback to their practice squad or active roster this week.
author: Michael David Smith

title: The Vikings, as expected, are making calls about adding a quarterback
summary: The clock is ticking, and it won't be cheap to trade for a starter.
full_text: They did it in 2016, after Teddy Bridgewater suffered a season-ending knee injury in late August. They did it in 2023, after Kirk Cousins suffered a season-ending torn Achilles tendon. They're doing it today, in order to avoid having the season end at 6-11. According to ESPNFL, the Vikings have begun making calls regarding a possible trade for a quarterback. Of course they're making calls. Coach Kevin O'Connell made that fairly clear last night. The real question is whether they can get a deal done. They're not operating from a position of strength, especially after a horrendous showing from Carson Wentz, whose passer rating against Buffalo was 8.9. The greater a team's perceived need, the more the other team will want. The Vikings' best hope is to stumble into a situation where multiple teams are looking to unload a starter. By persuading one team that the Vikings will strike a deal with another team, the price could come down. There aren't many current starters who would even possibly be available. Two of them — Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins and Colts quarterback Daniel Jones — have experience in Minnesota. Others include, potentially, Jets quarterback Geno Smith and Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert. Backups could be available. Mac Jones had been linked to Minnesota in the past. The 49ers would have to feel comfortable with the alternative to Mac Jones as the understudy to Brock Purdy. If a team trades its No. 2, it assumes the risk that the starter will get injured in the very next game. That happened to the Steelers in 2019. They traded Josh Dobbs to the Jaguars after Nick Foles was injured in Week 1. In Week 2, the Steelers lost Ben Roethlisberger for the year. Then came the Duck Hodges show. At this point, it's fair to wonder whether a quarterback upgrade will even matter for the Vikings. The flaws in the offense may run deeper than the quarterback position. Still, it's obvious that they need someone who can perform more efficiently than Kyler Murray or Carson Wentz, who in all fairness should be cut today. And if the Vikings can't upgrade at quarterback, they need to listen to offers for receiver Justin Jefferson. His prime is being wasted, and he surely would love to move on (even if he'd never say that out loud). The last-ditch effort could be to sign Jimmy Garoppolo, who would likely be an instant upgrade to the very low bar that Minnesota's current quarterbacks have established.
author: Mike Florio

title: The Vikings need to trade for a quarterback tomorrow
summary: Failure to act leads to one conclusion: The Vikings are dysfunctional.
full_text: The biggest test of the still-new partnership between Vikings G.M. Nolan Teasley and Vikings coach Kevin O'Connell has arrived. What will they do about a team with a Super Bowl-caliber defense and an offense that could barely function in the MAC? The window remains open until 4:00 p.m. ET on Tuesday. The Vikings were in this spot three years ago, when Kirk Cousins tore an Achilles tendon two days before the deadline. That time, the Vikings didn't have many options; they ended up with Josh Dobbs. This time, there are two former Vikings on other teams who know the Minnesota offense: Colts quarterback Daniel Jones and Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins. If the calls haven't already been made, they should be. Immediately. What will it take to salvage a season that is disintegrating before everyone's eyes, despite the 6-2 record? It wouldn't be easy to plug and play a new quarterback, but there's history with Jones and Cousins. It would be easier to get them up to speed than if they brought in someone who would be learning everything from scratch. If, in the end, the Colts want too much for Jones and the Raiders want too much for Cousins (neither is untouchable; the question is the amount of the compensation), the only other starter potentially available would be Geno Smith. Some have suggested a play for Justin Herbert. At this point, however, it's impossible to know whether his implosion is about his surroundings or about Herbert. Then there's Jimmy Garoppolo, who remains a free agent — and who has been largely forgotten. Whatever the Vikings do, staying the course with Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz is a middle finger to the fan base. And Max Brosmer, by all appearances, isn't good enough to make a difference. The fans know it. The boos were frequent, loud, and warranted on Monday night. So what will Teasley and O'Connell do? And, perhaps more importantly, when will the narrative change about O'Connell being a quarterback whisperer? He didn't want 2024 first-rounder J.J. McCarthy, who had fallen to third on the depth chart before he was given away for a fifth-round draft pick. O'Connell preferred Murray, who has been underwhelming. Wentz landed at No. 2 on the depth chart, and when the lights got bright Wentz winced.. It's a pivotal moment for Teasley, O'Connell, and the entire franchise. They can continue to act like everything is fine, that 6-2 is a good record, whatever. Anyone who's paying attention knows the truth. The Vikings, after starting 6-0, are sinking like a smooth stone in a septic tank. Failure to act amounts to dysfunction. And, yes, dysfunctional teams do dysfunctional things. Some around the league have suggested in recent years that the Vikings are low-key dysfunctional. Right or wrong, they're definitely the worst 6-2 team we've ever seen — and the only question at this point is whether they'll figure out how to win another game.
author: Mike Florio

title: NFL reinstates WR Brandon Aiyuk from reserve/left squad list
summary: 49ers' get a two-week roster exemption.
full_text: ' Brandon Aiyuk is back, and the ball is in the 49ers' court. The NFL reinstated the 49ers receiver from the reserve/left squad list on Monday. The league also gave the 49ers a two-week roster exemption, giving the team a window for making a decision about what to do with Aiyuk. The 49ers now have an immediate decision to make about Aiyuk. If he's on the roster on Tuesday at 4:00 p.m. ET, he's owed a game check for the week. Based on the Player Personnel Manual, placement on the reserve/left squad list apparently tolled his 2025 salary. That means he'll return to the $1.17 million base salary from 2025, with the 2026 salary of $26.015 million delayed until 2027. It gives the 49ers a window to trade Aiyuk, with the new team getting him for the rest of the season at only $585,000 in non-guaranteed pay. The 49ers can carry Aiyuk as an extra man on the roster until Monday, November 23. It's unclear, currently, whether Aiyuk agreed to refund past bonus money to the 49ers in order to get the league to reinstate him. If the 49ers trade or release Aiyuk, the 49ers lose the ability to get money back from Aiyuk.
author: Mike Florio

title: Jesse Minter does not address Lamar Jackson's injury, says he'll keep conversations with QB private
summary: Over the weekend, reporting emerged that Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson told teammates that he intends to return to play in 2026.
full_text: Over the weekend, reporting emerged that Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson told teammates that he intends to return to play in 2026. Baltimore head coach Jesse Minter, however, was not inclined to give any update on the star QB in his Monday press conference. Jackson is reportedly out for 6-9 weeks with a fractured and dislocated thumb. He is currently on injured reserve. Minter was asked what the chance is that Jackson will be able to return this season. “You know, I’m going to keep most of the conversations between Lamar and I between Lamar and I ,” Minter said. “Again, just like before, it’s a guy when you’re dealing with something, that no one wants to be on the field more. He’s probably going to do everything he can to put himself in position [to play]. But I’ll leave it at that.” Minter also did not say whether or not Jackson requires or already has had surgery. “I’m going to keep all that stuff between me and him,” Minter said. Does that mean the public won’t know the nature of Jackson’s injury and if he can return? “You may know, but that’ll come from him,” Minter said. There was one more follow-up in the press conference, with Minter being asked if it’s accurate to say Jackson’s thumb was fractured and dislocated. Minter chuckled before saying, “Again, that is specifics. I’ll keep it between me and him.” Jackson has technically started five games this season. But he played just a half against Tennessee and threw only one pass against Buffalo before having to exit due to injury. Jacoby Brissett is now set to take over as Baltimore’s starting quarterback with Jackson and Tyler Huntley on injured reserve.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Report: Jaguars plan to keep Brian Thomas Jr. at trade deadline
summary: The Jaguars have been bringing players in to fortify the roster for a deep postseason run.
full_text: The Jaguars have been bringing players in to fortify the roster for a deep postseason run. They don’t intend to send one out. Jeremy Fowler of ESPN reports the Jaguars plan to keep receiver Brian Thomas Jr. — barring a surprise. Thomas has been rumored to be on the trade block largely due to his lack of production this season. He’s received just 22 targets in eight games, catching 10 passes for 117 yards with two touchdowns. The No. 23 overall pick of the 2024 draft, Thomas caught 87 passes for 1,282 yards with 10 touchdowns as a rookie. But his production dipped even last year — the first season under head coach Liam Coen — with Thomas catching just 48 passes for 707 yards with two TDs. Even with Fowler’s report, plans can change. If a team seriously needs a receiver and is willing to pony up, the Jaguars may change their mind about dealing Thomas before the 4 p.m. ET deadline.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Jaguars trades for Jessie Bates, Jordan Davis could complicate deadline deals
summary: It's Let's Make A Deal day in the NFL, with the window on trades closing at 4:00 p.m.
full_text: It's Let's Make A Deal day in the NFL, with the window on trades closing at 4:00 p.m. ET. And the deals made on Monday could become a complication. The Jaguars gave up a lot for two of the three players they acquired. As to safety Jessie Bates III, it was a second-round pick and a fifth-round pick. For defensive tackle Jordan Davis (a run-stopper with 52-percent playing time), it was a first-round pick and a second-round pick. Those deals will hover over today's talks. Teams that are considering trading players will, at some level, be concerned about the perception that they didn't get enough, relative to what the Jaguars invested on Monday. If the Jaguars intended that, they're next-level super geniuses. Go all in, acquire players who'll help the team get to the Super Bowl and win it, and make it harder for other contenders to do the same thing today. As it relates to Jacksonville receiver Brian Thomas Jr., a first-round pick in 2024 who had 1,282 yards as a rookie and doesn't fit the current offense, that could also result in a better haul, if/when the Rams join the effort (which includes the Chiefs, Steelers, and Commanders) to wrest Thomas away from the Jaguars. Regardless of the motivation(s), Monday's trades by the Jaguars could make it harder for deals to get done on Tuesday. Most notably, it could make the Colts decide not to take the best offer on the table for running back Jonathan Taylor. With the Giants offering a two and a five, would the Colts be willing to accept for Taylor what the Jaguars gave up for Bates? How much more will it take to get the Colts to believe it's a proper return given the investment made in getting Bates? However it plays out, if not much happens at the deadline, the wrench thrown into the gears by the Jaguars could be a factor in that.
author: Mike Florio

title: Justin Jefferson: Vikings' offense didn't get it done, we've got to figure it out
summary: Jefferson finished with three catches for 58 yards in the Vikings' 23-6 loss to the Bills.
full_text: Vikings wide receiver Justin Jefferson has been visibly frustrated on the field the last two weeks as the offense hasn't been able to move the ball in back-to-back losses. After Monday night's loss to the Bills, he said the offense needs to stop squandering the work of a great defense. "The offense didn't get it done," Jefferson said. "Defense did a phenomenal job once again, getting it done against a very good offense. We've got to figure it out on offense." Jefferson said everyone on the offense has to do better, although he admitted he doesn't know all the answers. "We've got to figure it out," Jefferson said. "That's something we don't have the answer to at the moment. We've just got to figure it out." Although quarterback Carson Wentz was terrible on Monday night, and Kyler Murray hasn't been much better for most of the season, Jefferson called it "an all 11 thing" and said it's not just on the quarterback. "It doesn't really matter who's throwing the ball, as long as it gets to us, that's all that matters, and it's up to us to make those plays. It's tough. Definitely tough," Jefferson said. The Vikings' offense has been tough to watch.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Vikings' 17:28 time of possession was their lowest in franchise history
summary: The Minnesota Vikings have played 1,064 games in the history of their franchise, which started in 1961.
full_text: The Minnesota Vikings have played 1,064 games in the history of their franchise, which started in 1961. Before yesterday, they had never played a game in which they possessed the ball for less than 17 and a half minutes. Now they have. The Vikings' time of possession of 17:28 in Monday night's 23-6 loss to the Bills was their lowest in franchise history. The previous franchise low was 17:38, set in the NFC Championship Game after the 2000 season, when the Vikings lost to the Giants 41-0. On Monday night, the Vikings' offense could not stay on the field. The first quarter set the tone: They had three possessions, which were two three-and-outs and one possession on which they lost a fumble on the first play. Their longest possession of the night lasted 3:11, and on that possession they ran five plays, totaled just 10 yards, and punted. The Vikings' defense played well, but not so well that the Bills weren't able to sustain some long drives, including three drives that took more than six minutes off the clock. The Bills gained 22 first downs; the Vikings gained just nine. The Bills' 42:32 time of possession was their second-best in franchise history, trailing only a 1989 game in which they possessed the ball for 42:53 and beat the Jets 34-3.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Sean McVay on Puka Nacua injury: I'd be lying if I said I wasn't questioning that play call
summary: Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua is set to go on injured reserve after suffering MCL, PCL and turf toe injuries in Sunday's win over the Commanders.
full_text: ' Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua is set to go on injured reserve after suffering MCL, PCL and turf toe injuries in Sunday's win over the Commanders. Nacua's injuries occurred on the Rams' final offensive play when he was tackled after rushing for five yards on third-and-11. Nacua took a handoff on the play and head coach Sean McVay was asked at a Monday press conference if he second-guessed himself for putting Nacua in position to take a hit at that point in the game. McVay said he's "kicking myself about those kinds of things" and called it something the Rams have to think about "internally" as they move forward. "I’d be lying to you if I said I haven't questioned the decision-making on that last play over and over in my head of what could have been another option that you felt like could have gotten a conversion, and maybe ended the game that would've led to him not taking a violent hit to his right knee," McVay said. "It's stuff that I feel tremendous responsibility for, and we've got to be able to figure out how to protect these guys while also putting them in positions that help our team and allow them to be able to shine. He's a guy we have to be intentional about because it's a bummer. Because he can do so much, you want to make sure you don't take that for granted." With Nacua and Davante Adams now out for the indefinite future, the Rams may be in the market for receiving help before the trade deadline passes at 4 p.m. ET on Tuesday. They do not have their 2027 first- or third-round picks, their 2028 second-round pick or their 2029 third-round pick thanks to their trades for Myles Garrett and Trent McDuffie.
author: Josh Alper

title: Carson Wentz: This one felt pretty terrible
summary: The Vikings' quarterback had perhaps the worst game any NFL quarterback has had this season in Monday night's loss to the Bills.
full_text: Vikings quarterback Carson Wentz had perhaps the worst game any NFL quarterback has had this season in Monday night's loss to the Bills. He didn't sugarcoat it afterward. “This one felt pretty terrible. I’m not going to lie," Wentz said, via the Associated Press. Wentz completed 8 of 25 passes for 81 yards, with no touchdowns and two interceptions against the Bills. His passer rating of 8.9 was the lowest for any quarterback in any game in which he threw more than three passes this season. Wentz said he knows the Vikings' defense can win with competent quarterback play, and he did not provide that. “To go kind of lay an egg, personally, the way I struggled early, especially with our defense playing as good as they’ve been all year, honestly," Wentz said. "They did it again tonight, and we just didn’t help them out. I didn’t help them out. It’s hard to put my finger on the why.” The Vikings need to put their finger on the how, as in how to fix their offense. Or else a great defense is going to waste.
author: Michael David Smith

title: James Cook's 31 carries vs. Vikings were the most in any NFL game this season
summary: Against a Vikings defense that has been teeing off on opposing quarterbacks this season, Bills coach Joe Brady knew he needed to lean on his running back on Monday night.
full_text: Against a Vikings defense that has been teeing off on opposing quarterbacks this season, Bills coach Joe Brady knew he needed to lean on his running back on Monday night. And so he did, with Bills running back James Cook getting 31 carries for 107 yards and a touchdown in a 23-6 win over the Vikings. Cook's 31 carries were the most any running back has had in any NFL game this season. Cook led the NFL with 1,621 rushing yards last season, but he's actually been even more productive so far this season. He's averaging both more carries per game and more yards per game in 2026 than he did in 2025. Josh Allen makes the Bills' offense go, but the Bills rely on their running back as much as any team in the NFL, and on Monday night, Cook delivered.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Todd Monken not ready to name starter at QB for Week 10
summary: Shedeur Sanders has given Todd Monken something to think about.
full_text: Shedeur Sanders has given Todd Monken something to think about. The Browns' head coach told reporters in his Monday news conference that he's not ready to name a starter at quarterback for the Week 10 matchup against the Texans. That came after Jeremy Fowler of ESPN reported that Deshaun Watson would be back in the saddle after missing Sunday's game. "I really haven’t thought through it other than getting through this morning’s tape," Monken said. "I just got done meeting with the guys. They’ll flush the game and then we’ll have a chance to meet offensively more [extensively] later today. We went through the tape, immediately had to break, go to personnel, then the team comes in, and we haven’t had a chance to circle back as an offensive staff." Watson started the first eight games of the season for Cleveland, generating five game-winning drives for the team’s five wins. Sanders, who started after Watson missed the first two days of the practice week while in concussion protocol, completed 19-of-31 passes for 297 yards with two touchdowns and no picks against the Saints. “Well I’m awfully proud of him ,” Monken said of Sanders. “It’s been 10 weeks since he had reps with the ones. I think it showed up, the reps that we gave him in camp. “I thought he battled. I thought he showed composure in the pocket, getting to his check-downs at times. He made plays with his feet in escaping. He made the scramble play to Jerry [Jeudy]. He made a big third-down conversion early and he made one right there in four-minute, right before the holding call that gave us a first down. So, that’s what you wanted to see.” Monken noted that philosophically, he doesn’t really think of a player losing a job due to injury. “It’s week to week,” Monken said. "A player doesn’t lose or win a job — I don’t know what that means. Each week, we put the best players on the field that give us a chance to win.” Monken added that Sanders’ play didn’t necessarily alter his thinking about whether or not Sanders could play at some point this season. “I was thrilled. I was happy for him,” Monken said. “Every player wants to go and play and play well. And there were moments [where] I didn’t coach well enough, he didn’t play well enough. But there were moments at the end of the game where he made plays, right? He got it in the players’ hands, did a really good job, was in command. So, I was really pleased for him. And I was hopeful he’d play well. I thought he had a great week of practice and there is no guarantee that will carry over. So I’m really happy for him. “Does it give me confidence? From what I saw in the fall, you bet it does. It gives me more and more confidence that what I saw in the fall, there’s something to build on — for sure.” We’ll see how that translates as the season continues. But the fact that Sanders played well enough to make it an open question does say something about his development.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Andy Reid: Patrick Mahomes day-to-day with elbow injury
summary: Reid said he had seen Mahomes on Monday and the QB was in "good spirits."
full_text: While Patrick Mahomes' elbow injury looked bad when it happened on Sunday, he was able to finish the game, helping power the Chiefs to a 35-12 win over the Jets. It sounds like he might not miss any further playing time either. "Patrick, he is really day-to-day right now ," head coach Andy Reid told reporters in his Monday news conference. "It was more positive news than negative news on Patrick. It looks like it’s just a matter of some rehab in there and getting rid of some of the soreness. And we’ll just see where it goes from there. "But he’s in good spirits today — I have seen him today, so he’s in good spirits today." Mahomes suffered the injury late in the first half. In the third quarter, he completed 7-of-10 passes for 81 yards. He was 5-of-6 for 41 yards in the fourth quarter. Additionally, Reid mentioned Xavier Worthy (hamstring) and Jaylon Moore (ankle) are day-to-day with their respective injuries. The Chiefs will be on the road to play the Falcons in Week 10. The first injury report of the week will be issued on Wednesday.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Gardner Minshew having tests on right arm after injury on Sunday
summary: Cardinals quarterback Gardner Minshew remained in Sunday's loss to the Seahawks after hurting his right arm late in the first half, but his status for the team's Week 10 game against the Rams is not certain.
full_text: Cardinals quarterback Gardner Minshew remained in Sunday's loss to the Seahawks after hurting his right arm late in the first half, but his status for the team's Week 10 game against the Rams is not certain. Head coach Mike LaFleur said at a Monday press conference that Minshew is undergoing tests on his arm and he said it is a possibility that he will not be able to play this week. The Cardinals traded Jacoby Brissett to the Ravens last week, which puts third-round pick Carson Beck in position to start if Minshew is unable to play. Beck has not appeared in any games yet this season. Minshew's injury is one of several negative injury updates LaFleur delivered on Monday. He also announced that wide receiver Michael Wilson is out for the year with a neck injury and that center Hjalte Froholdt is in the concussion protocol.
author: Josh Alper

title: Eagles say Jaguars made an offer they couldn't refuse for Jordan Davis
summary: The Eagles announced the trade that sent defensive tackle Jordan Davis to the Jaguars, saying the "Jaguars made an offer that executive vice president/General Manager Howie Roseman simply could not refuse."
full_text: The Eagles announced the trade that sent defensive tackle Jordan Davis to the Jaguars, saying the "Jaguars made an offer that executive vice president/General Manager Howie Roseman simply could not refuse." The Jaguars are sending a 2027 first-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick to the Eagles. "We are extremely grateful to Jordan for his contributions to our team on the field and in the Philadelphia community since we drafted him five years ago," the team said in a statement. "He has been a key contributor to our team culture and on-field success, which included two Super Bowl appearances and a world championship in 2024. His growth and development as both a player and a leader are a testament to his hard work and character. We wish Jordan nothing but continued success." The Eagles now have first-round picks in the 2027 draft, two first-round picks and two second-round picks in the 2028 draft and multiple second-round picks in 2029. The Eagles made Davis a first-round pick in 2022, and he totaled 193 tackles, 9.5 sacks, 15 quarterback hits and 11 passes defensed in 73 games.
author: Charean Williams

title: Receiver-needy teams should call about Justin Jefferson
summary: If the Vikings aren't going to upgrade at QB, they should give Jefferson a chance at a championship.
full_text: Vikings receiver Justin Jefferson is the ultimate team player. And he'd ultimately never say publicly if he wanted to be traded to a new team. Teams looking for a receiver should make the call. Few players are untouchable, when it comes to a trade. And even if the Vikings would hang up the phone and not listen, teams that need a high-end pass-catcher should try. The Rams currently are in a pickle, thanks to the placement of Puka Nacua on injured reserve, where he joins Davante Adams. The Chiefs could use help at the position, too. Ditto for the Steelers, who (like the Chiefs and Commanders) have interest in Jaguars receiver Brian Thomas Jr. Then there are the 49ers, who are always lurking when it comes to possibly making a big move. Regardless, it makes sense to make the call. If the Vikings aren't going to make a move for a functional quarterback, they should stockpile picks and give Jefferson a chance to chase the championship that won't happen in Minnesota — especially if they waste his seventh season by not upgrading at the quarterback position. Yes, a trade would come with a 2027 cap charge. The Vikings also would avoid the $30 million he's due to make in 2027, and the upgrade to meet the increased market that he surely already wants. At the end of the day, it's one or the other. Trade for a better quarterback, or trade Jefferson to another team. Of the available options, doing neither makes the least sense.
author: Mike Florio

title: Kevin O'Connell on potential quarterback trade: "I'll defer to Nolan [Teasley] on that"
summary: Vikings coach doesn't rule out making a deal by Tuesday's deadline.
full_text: After Monday night's 23-6 loss to the Bills, during which Carson Wentz completed eight of 25 passes for 81 yards, two interceptions, and an 8.9 passer rating, Vikings coach Kevin O'Connell was asked whether the team will consider trying to acquire a quarterback by the trade deadline at 4:00 p.m. ET on Tuesday. "I'll defer to [G.M.] Nolan [Teasley] on that," O'Connell said. "We've had dialogue about a lot of different positions. And tight turnaround obviously playing the Monday night game before that, and we'll get right to work on any potential moves that can be there. But really just focused on the game tonight, which was not good enough in any way, shape, or form." No, it wasn't. It was worse than horrible. O'Connell was asked at one point whether he has ever felt as challenging as it does right now, as a play-caller. "No," he said. They have options. Several teams could be looking to make a deal. And even if it won't be cheap, it's necessary to salvage what was, only nine days ago, a very promising season. It still can be. A return of Kirk Cousins would be a B-12 shot to the franchise. Even Daniel Jones would make things better than they are. And if they want to go all in, try to make a deal for Justin Herbert — who may be thrilled at this point to don an eye patch and escape from L.A. Whatever the Vikings do, they need to do something. Otherwise, there may not be a quarterback change when the season ends. There could be a coaching change.
author: Mike Florio

title: Klint Kubiak: We wouldn't be where we are without Kirk Cousins' "amazing" decision-making
summary: The Raiders signed Kirk Cousins in April with the idea that he would start for the entire season while No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza develops.
full_text: ' The Raiders signed Kirk Cousins in April with the idea that he would start for the entire season while No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza develops. That plan has had solid returns, with Cousins completing 64.1 percent of his passes for 2,340 yards with 20 touchdowns and eight interceptions. But three of those picks came in Sunday’s loss to the 49ers, which was Cousins’ worst game of the season. On Monday, head coach Klint Kubiak was asked about the QB’s decision-making on the giveaways. “Kirk has been an extremely solid decision maker all season,” Kubiak said, via transcript from the team. “There’s ones he wants back. He wants back the first play of [the] second half. [He] wants back the one in the red zone where we did not give him protection to make a good decision. In the last play of the game, we’re trying to make a play, so he wants those back. “But we’re not in the position that we are without the amazing decisions he’s made all year. So, we’ve got to coach up those ones and help him learn from them. But again, I’m very pleased with — the quarterback has to be the best decision-maker on the team, any organization. He wasn’t on those two plays, and that last one I’m calling a heave-ho.” With the trade deadline rapidly approaching and the Raiders sitting at 4-5, there have been rumors about teams being interested in Cousins. Kubiak was asked how he thinks players like Cousins and Maxx Crosby — who expressed no interest in being traded — are handling that situation. “Well, that’s the business that we’re in,” Kubiak said. “That’s the business of football, and those guys are veterans. They’ve been around that, so you just keep working. There’s a lot of things that are out of your control.” If the Raiders were to trade Cousins, it would signal that the team feels Mendoza is ready to take over as starting quarterback. But because Las Vegas is still in the thick of things in the AFC as the current No. 9 seed, they may not be inclined to shake things up at the game’s most important position.
author: Myles Simmons

author: Michael David Smith

title: 2026 NFL trade deadline tracker: Latest deals, grades as Jordan Davis heads to Jacksonville
summary: Track every completed deal before the Nov. 10 deadline, including Jacksonville's blockbuster Monday
full_text:
A steady stream of blockbuster moves in advance of the 2026 NFL trade deadline redistributed some of the league's top talent at numerous positions. Even more impactful transactions could be on the way before Nov. 10, but in the meantime, the Chicago Bears are the biggest winners of the deadline thus far with their highly fruitful acquisition of Jeffery Simmons , the Jacksonville Jaguars are the most aggressive buyers with their pursuit of a host of defensive players and the Indianapolis Colts emerged as the most aggressive sellers in dealing Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner .
Trade watch continues for a myriad of stars on struggling teams, including Jonathan Taylor , Khalil Mack , George Pickens and others. At the same time, teams battling for position at the front of the postseason race must decide how much to invest in those standouts who are available on the trade market.
There is only one more game until the trade deadline, so this year's contenders and pretenders are about as clear as they will be before it is too late to buy and sell. It is safe to expect a flurry of moves in the next 24 hours as those franchises gear up for the home stretch or look ahead to the future.
Below is every in-season trade ahead of the NFL's 2026 deadline.
The Cincinnati Bengals were reportedly trading a sixth-round pick to the Eagles for pass rusher Arnold Ebiketie . However, the Bengals front office didn't realize they would also lose a third-round pick in the deal.
Nick Korte of Over The Cap pointed out that Ebiketie was signed by the Eagles as a compensatory free agent. The Bengals lost three compensatory free agents this offseason and signed two. With the addition of Ebiketie, the Bengals would lose a 2027 third-round compensatory pick that was coming after Trey Hendrickson signed with the Ravens.
About an hour later, the trade reportedly collapsed. Korte noted that the Bengals may have thought offensive lineman Cordell Volson counted as one of their CFAs lost. However, he has not played a single snap this year and does not count toward the formula.
Just when it seemed like the Jaguars had filled all of their needs, they went out and made their biggest move of all. Jacksonville's acquisition of Davis is a blockbuster in every sense of the word. The standout defensive tackle will be on the team's books through 2029 after signing a lucrative contract extension with the Eagles earlier this year and will be among the faces of the franchise as it pursues its first Super Bowl. His arrival marks the third trade for a defensive player in one day for Jacksonville and gives them a star in the trenches who should make an already superb group even more impenetrable.
On the other side, Philadelphia is officially in tear-down mode for 2026. Nothing signals a rebuild like moving a foundational player months after locking him into a new contract. The Eagles now have 10 picks in the first two rounds of the next three drafts and can seek an expedited return to playoff contention with a couple of massive draft day hauls.
The Lions should be better off than they were before in the defensive backfield with the addition of Cisco, but by how much? Cisco arrives in a unit that ranks dead last in stopping the pass at 260.9 yards per game. He slipped from his status as an every-week starter and was at the top of the Jets' depth chart for just four of nine games this season. While he remains productive, this is not a home-run transaction for a Detroit team that has to be better on his side of the ball in order to achieve its goals. This could age much better if and when Kerby Joseph returns to the lineup, because Cisco would be a pleasant depth option behind both Joseph and Brian Branch .
New York will have to wait a year to reap the benefits of this trade. It is a success to get something in return for a player who started fewer than half of his games this season, but the Jets need all the draft capital they can stockpile in order to pull themselves out of their rebuild, and 2028 is a long way away.
Jacksonville entered the week with needs at safety and defensive tackle and filled both of them in a matter of hours. Shortly after acquiring Jessie Bates III, the Jaguars made a play for Godchaux, boosting a defense that may already be Super Bowl-caliber. This is a necessary addition for general manager James Gladstone after he watched DaVon Hamilton go down with a torn quad in Week 8 and one that should keep the NFL's No. 5 run defense in the top echelon.
The pick heading to New Orleans will become a 2027 sixth-round pick if the Jaguars acquire one, according to ESPN . They do not currently own one but are projected to receive two compensatory sixth-round picks, according to Spotrac . Even with the caveat on the return, the Saints upgraded in the deal considering they spent a seventh-rounder to acquire Godchaux in a trade last year. He was a questionable fit in a run defense that ranks fifth-worst in the NFL, anyway.
The Jaguars secured a rental for their secondary and an impactful one at that. Bates is a perennial All-Pro safety who not only beefs up the starting lineup with renowned playmaking ability but also adds depth to a group that is dealing with injuries and just lost Eric Murray for the year with an elbow issue. Jacksonville is right in the midst of its contention window and is in play for the AFC's No. 1 seed, so any move that strengthens its Super Bowl chances is justifiable, even if it gives up quite a bit in the way of draft picks to pull it off.
Those picks make this deal a beneficial one for the Falcons, too. Atlanta should have expected to lose Bates in free agency this coming offseason, since he was not among the many players it extended this past summer. The second-round pick is better than any compensatory pick that would have come with his departure, and the 2028 fifth-rounder sweetened the deal even further. Now is the time for the Falcons to turn expiring contracts into future assets, because, at 3-6, they are unlikely to contend for anything beyond a potential first-place finish in the NFL's weakest division.
Baltimore agreed to trade for Cardinals QB Jacoby Brissett and completed the deal over the weekend after its "Thursday Night Football" loss. This was an expected move for the Ravens, because their quarterback situation went from bad to worse in Week 8. The highly anticipated return of starter Lamar Jackson lasted just one play. Jackson suffered a thumb injury and is now on injured reserve. Tyler Huntley , who started in place of Jackson, took over but also went down. He is out for the season with a turf toe injury. The team relied on emergency third quarterback Joe Fagnano to finish the game and started him on Thursday.
Brissett spent the last two seasons with the Cardinals, who benched him in his final game with the team and turned instead to Gardner Minshew . The return of draft capital for a quarterback who lost his job, was unhappy all offseason about his contract situation and projected as a bridge to an eventual first-round pick is a huge success for a rebuilding Arizona team.
In giving up two first-rounders to secure a perennial All-Pro defensive tackle , the Bears went all-in and opened their Super Bowl contention window. The transaction paid immediate dividends when Simmons logged a sack and led the team with six tackles in his Chicago debut: A commanding 34-17 road win over the Seahawks . Mortgaging so much of their future first-round capital showed that the Bears trust their roster, as currently constructed, to compete at the top of the league, and Simmons is the kind of game-changing talent worth the steep price. His production in the pass rush and in run defense could help Chicago maximize its high-octane unit on the other side of the ball led by Caleb Williams .
This move sends the Titans deeper into their rebuild. Questions lie ahead about whether to stick with Cam Ward at quarterback, and with the first-round picks they acquired from…
author: Carter Bahns

title: Jonathan Taylor mock trades: How Giants, Broncos, Seahawks could target Colts star RB
summary: The Colts need to replenish their draft assets, and dealing their three-time Pro Bowl running back could produce a significant return
full_text:
After a loss to the previously winless Titans dropped the Colts to 2-4 on the young season, Indianapolis fired GM Chris Ballard . It was the first firing by Colts owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon, and it might not be the last. Shane Steichen has zero postseason trips in four seasons as the Colts' coach, and while he's still leading the way for now, there's no doubt his seat is and has been warm. How much warmer it became after Ballard's firing is unclear, but it's clear Irsay-Gordon expects better than what the Colts are producing.
It's also clear that the Colts (now 2-7) aren't close to getting to the level Irsay-Gordon expects. Daniel Jones has been a turnover machine, and the defense is below average, with issues rushing the passer and defending the run. The Colts are 28th in yards per play allowed and 26th in net yards per attempt allowed.
Sometimes it has to get worse before it gets better, and that may be the case for the Colts. Indianapolis is already down a 2027 first-round pick, traded to the Jets at the 2025 trade deadline, but the Colts could be sellers -- and maybe major sellers -- this year.
The biggest name would be star running back Jonathan Taylor . He had 20 touchdowns and nearly 2,000 yards from scrimmage last year, and he's on his way to another big season, but the Colts are stuck going nowhere once again. He's 27 and has played in just one playoff game -- as a rookie in 2020. In fact, Taylor headlined Jordan Dajani's list of five players we want to see moved by the Nov. 10 deadline.
Taylor would have plenty of suitors if made available, and the situation isn't too dissimilar from what the Panthers were going through with Christian McCaffrey in 2022. McCaffrey is a more versatile player than Taylor in the passing game and was younger than Taylor is now when that deal happened, but he had also been injured. In the deal with the 49ers in 2022, Carolina received second-, third-, fourth- and fifth-round picks.
With that in mind, here are five teams who could come calling about Taylor and what a mock trade might look like:
Giants receive: RB Jonathan Taylor Colts receive: RB Cam Skattebo , 2027 second-round pick, 2028 fourth-round pick
John Harbaugh said he "would love" to have a " Derrick Henry circumstance or a 'Saquon Barkley circumstance." Whether he meant to or not, it was surely a bummer for Giants fans to hear Harbaugh mention his running back from last year and a former Giants running back in the same sentence. Regardless, Taylor could be that type of workhorse. The Colts getting two high draft picks over the next two years, plus Skattebo, who showed promise as a rookie but didn't have a single touch Sunday, on a cost-effective deal, would be a solid start. The Giants are leading a historically bad NFC East, and even if it doesn't finish that way, having Taylor next to Jaxson Dart next year would be an enticing prospect.
One thing to note, though, is that Harbaugh comes from one of the most patient, draft-and-develop franchises in Baltimore. This would be a significant departure from that.
Bengals receive: RB Jonathan Taylor, 2027 fourth-round pick Colts receive: RB Chase Brown , 2027 second-round pick, 2027 fifth-round pick
This would be similar to the package the Panthers got for McCaffrey, but instead of a third-round pick, the Colts would get Brown. At 26, he's younger and has less wear and tear than Taylor. He's also an accomplished player and productive pass catcher who has handled a bell-cow workload before. A change of scenery could do him good, as he has struggled to get going early this season. For the Bengals , this would be a second major win-now move in just over six months; they sent the No. 10 pick to the Giants in April for Dexter Lawrence . The Bengals have tried to work in more under-center looks, but are among the worst teams using it. Taylor could change that single-handedly. Cincinnati also has an extra third-round pick, which helps make giving up so many picks easier to swallow.
Broncos receive: RB Jonathan Taylor, 2027 fifth-round pick Colts receive: RB J.K. Dobbins , 2027 second-round pick, 2027 fourth-round pick
The Broncos traded a first-round pick for an upgrade at wide receiver in Jaylen Waddle this offseason (though it hasn't really worked out yet). Would they make another big deal for an upgrade at running back in Taylor? The Broncos have struggled to muster much on the ground, exacerbating quarterback Bo Nix's struggles. Dobbins is on a two-year deal, though there's an out after this year should the Colts choose to use it.
Seahawks receive: RB Jonathan Taylor Colts receive: RB Jadarian Price , 2027 second-round pick
It'd be rare to see a team move on from a first-round pick so quickly, but the Seahawks are in a rare position as the first team to lose a Super Bowl MVP in over two decades. Seattle very much misses Kenneth Walker III and is struggling to find much of anything on the ground without him. Emanuel Wilson and George Holani have had devastating fumbles. Offensive coordinator Brian Fleury has been with the 49ers since 2019, so he knows the value of a great top running back. Indianapolis would get a good young running back and ample future picks.
Vikings receive: RB Jonathan Taylor Colts receive: RB Jordan Mason , 2027 second-round pick, 2027 fifth-round pick
Taylor would be a game-changer, and combining him with a mobile quarterback in Kyler Murray or another QB acquired in a trade, would be a treat for Kevin O'Connell. Mason, meanwhile, is a good player on his own accord. Plus, the Vikings have draft capital to spare, with an extra third, two extra fifths and two extra sixths.
author: Zachary Pereles

title: Dolphins lose captain Zach Sieler for season with ruptured biceps
summary: The Dolphins captain ruptured his biceps on the opening play against the Lions but remarkably finished the game
full_text:
The Miami Dolphins (1-7) didn't just lose a game in their 19-9 defeat against the Detroit Lions in Week 9, but they also lost one of their best players. Defensive tackle Zach Sieler , one of the team's best players and team captains, ruptured his biceps and will undergo surgery with a projected 5-6 month recovery, thus ending his 2026 season, per ESPN .
Sieler sustained the injury on the first play but finished the game. Sieler signed a three-year, $64 million extension in 2025 that has him under contract through 2029, but at the age of 31 for a rebuilding team, he may have been a prime trade deadline acquisition candidate had he not gotten injured.
The Dolphins captain totaled 24 tackles and two sacks in eight games played for Miami this season. Sieler joined the Dolphins in 2019, and he has 37.5 sacks and 235 quarterback pressures with Miami. Both of those numbers lead Miami in those two key pass-rush categories in the span of Sieler's Dolphins career.
author: Garrett Podell

title: Bengals call off Arnold Ebiketie trade with Eagles after nearly botching compensatory pick situation
summary: The Bengals were in line to lose a 2027 third-round pick awarded from Trey Hendrickson's departure
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals ' trade to acquire Arnold Ebiketie from the Philadelphia Eagles in exchange for a 2027 sixth-round draft pick has officially fallen through, as reported by NFL Network's Ian Rapoport . While the teams agreed to the deal, it had not yet become official before the Bengals realized major compensatory pick ramifications may be tied to finalizing the move.
On the surface, it looked like a fairly ordinary deal: Cincinnati would acquire a rotational pass rusher for a late-round pick. The Bengals are going for a Super Bowl this year, while Philadelphia has spent most of this deadline gearing up for a draft-heavy reload. As it turns out, though, Cincinnati's front office nearly committed a major gaffe with the trade. By acquiring Ebiketie, whom the Eagles signed as a compensatory free agent this offseason, the Bengals would have forfeited the 2027 third-round compensatory pick they were set to acquire after losing Trey Hendrickson in free agency. Nick Korte, who contributes to the contract source site OverTheCap, was first to point this out .
Oh that's brutal on the 3rd round comp pick! as noted by @nickkorte pic.twitter.com/OwwyNB71PA
Why does Ebiketie count against the Bengals' formula, you ask? According to Appendix V of the NFL Collective Bargaining Agreement ...
If a Club trades for a player who was a CFA during that League Year, whether the player was another Club's CFA or the acquiring Club's own CFA, the player will be considered a CFA gained by the acquiring Club and will be included in the Compensatory netting process described above.
It's important to note -- as Korte did -- that the Bengals may have believed former guard Cordell Volson counted as one of their CFAs lost. However, Volson has not played a single snap this year and, as the chart above shows, does not count toward the CFAs lost formula. Whether it's a miscalculation or a misunderstanding of Volson's standing, it's not a great look for Bengals director of personnel Duke Tobin and the rest of the front office.
Korte's compensatory pick expertise has now helped the Bengals twice. In March 2024, he noticed Cincinnati wasn't getting the appropriate draft compensation for losing Jessie Bates III in free agency. The NFL issued a rare correction, and the Bengals went from getting two sixth-round picks to getting a third-round pick and a sixth-round pick in the upcoming draft.
It remains to be seen if Cincinnati, who sit at 6-2 in the No. 6 seed of the AFC wild card as of the trade deadline, will look elsewhere for edge rushing help. The Bengals used both free agency (EDGE Boye Mafe , DL Jonathan Allen , S Bryan Cook ) and trade acquisitions (acquiring DL Dexter Lawrence from the Giants ) to boost their defense this year, but apparently felt it needed reinforcements at EDGE after rookie Cashius Howell (wrist) landed on injured reserve. Mafe has lived up to the offseason hype with 5.5 sacks in eight games, but no other edge rusher has more than two.
It is also uncertain as to what happens with Ebiketie. The 2-7 Eagles are having a massive sale amid a disastrous 2026. Monday, Philadelphia parted ways with standout defensive tackle Jordan Davis on Monday, sending him to the Jaguars for a 2027 first-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick. Earlier in the year, they sent center Cam Jurgens to the Ravens for a 2027 fifth-round pick and a 2028 second-round pick.
author: Zachary Pereles

title: After Puka Nacua injury, five receivers the Rams should target at the 2026 trade deadline
summary: With Puka Nacua and Davante Adams both out, the Rams suddenly need some help at wide receiver
full_text:
With NFL trade deadline coming up at 4 p.m. ET on Tuesday, one team to watch is going to be the Los Angeles Rams , who are currently in desperate need of some help at receiver.
The Rams first took a hit at the position back in October when Davante Adams went down with an injury and they took an even bigger one this week with the loss of Puka Nacua . The Rams' star, who is dealing with MCL and PCL sprains in addition to turf toe, is expected to be placed on injured reserve this week , which will knock him out until at least Week 15.
With Adams and Nacua both out until at least December, that means a Rams team that went all-in this season with a Myles Garrett and Aaron Donald juggernaut defensive line to maximize reigning MVP Matthew Stafford's remaining window is down to Konata Mumpfield , Tutu Atwell , and Jordan Whittington at receiver. That trio has combined for just 20 receptions, 273 yards, and one receiving touchdown this year. During an interview Monday, Sean McVay admitted that a trade might happen by the deadline.
"You look at all avenues to solve the situations that come up. I would never rule it out," McVay said.
If we know one thing about Rams general manager Les Snead, it's that he loves to wheel and deal. He's proven throughout his career that he's not shy when it comes to pulling the trigger on a big trade, so it's very possible we'll see the Rams make some sort of deal by 4 p.m. ET.
The options for those deals are narrowing quickly, though. According to ESPN, the Jacksonville Jaguars are planning to keep wide receiver Brian Thomas Jr . on their roster despite him having just one reception for 12 yards in their last four games.
With that in mind, let's check out five possible trade options for the Rams at receiver.
There is no team that loves to make a big trade more than the Rams, and this would be huge. Going after Pickens would make sense, and that's because the Cowboys actually might be willing to deal him. Pickens is playing on the franchise tag this year, and there's a good chance that he ends up leaving Dallas after the season. If that happens, the Cowboys would get nothing, but if they traded him now, they'd at least get something in return.
The only problem with this option is that the Cowboys play in a bad division, so it might not make any sense for them to start trading away their best players. The Cowboys are currently 4-5 and sitting just 1.5 games out of first place. Dallas may still think the NFC East is up for grabs and worth trying to win, especially as the Philadelphia Eagles begin to sell pieces and load up for the future.
On top of that, the Cowboys just might not be active at all this deadline, especially after already making a midseason deal for Joey Porter Jr . . Despite Dallas not playing Pickens in their Sunday win over the Colts , team owner and de facto general manager Jerry Jones said on his weekly 105.3 The Fan radio spot that the decision was "100 percent injury related" and not tied to any pending trades.
Cowboys owner Jerry Jones on @1053thefan said Joey Porter Jr. and George Pickens not playing Sunday was “100 percent injury related.” Jones said “don’t count out” the Cowboys potentially making a move today. But adds “I don’t look for us to make a significant trade today.”
Although the Cowboys are very much still in the division race, our reporter in Dallas, Garrett Podell, still thinks it makes sense for them to trade Pickens, and it's certainly possible that the Cowboys will at least be open to listening to offers at the minimum.
Pickens' production in Dallas has been underwhelming this year. He's caught just 39 passes for 533 yards for the Cowboys, but he might be able to put up bigger numbers if he became the top weapon in a Rams' offense that ranks seventh in the NFL in passing yards per game. A move to Los Angeles would also give Pickens a chance to play with the reigning NFL MVP.
Although adding Pickens would make some sense, it wouldn't be easy. The Rams don't have a lot of draft capital to send to Dallas, so they'd have to get that figured out. The Rams also don't have very much salary cap space, so they'd have to figure out a way to fit the rest of Pickens' fully guaranteed franchise tag salary under their cap. Pickens' deal is worth $27.3 million, and the Rams would owe him the pro-rated amount of that, which would be about $13.65 million.
When Jennings signed with the Vikings back in May, he probably figured he was going to have a big year. With opposing defenses worried about Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison , that should have opened things up for Jennings, but that hasn't happened.
Through eight games, Jennings has caught just six passes for n54 yards, which is an extremely low total even when you take into account the Vikings' offense has been historically bad this year. Jennings has understandably been frustrated, and those frustrations are starting to show on the field.
Jauan Jennings was pissed off he didn’t get the ball when he was wide open in the end zone on Sunday A total of 5 targets in 4 games will do this to you pic.twitter.com/25tacVpI0f
Due to the Vikings QB situation, things likely won't be getting better any time soon. Jennings is a the third option in a loaded offense and even if the Vikings add a QB, that's going ot benefit Jefferson and Addison more than it will benefit Jennings.
One interesting to thing to keep in mind with Jennings is that he had a chance to return to San Francisco: The 49ers had a deal in place to acquire him from Minnesota, but he basically killed the trade . There appears to be some bad blood there and going to the Rams would be a way for him to get revenge on the 49ers.
The veteran receiver caught 55 passes for 643 yards and nine touchdowns while playing for the 49ers last season, and he would probably enjoy a return to the NFC West.
This move feels like it would make a lot of sense for both sides. On the Titans ' end, they have several solid receivers, but everyone is essentially going to waste while playing in a Tennessee offense that ranks in the bottom five in the NFL in passing yards per game. Rookie Carnell Tate leads the team in receiving yards (413) while free agent addition Wan'Dale Robinson is leads the team in receptions (35).
Ridley has basically been the odd man out this year: He's caught just six passes for 91 yards through eight games. If the 1-7 Titans decide to hold a fire sale, then it wouldn't be surprising at all to see them dump Ridley.
The 31-year-old actually took a pay cut this year to stay with the Titans. The upside for the Rams is that Ridley doesn't have any guaranteed money left on his contract after this season, so they wouldn't be on the hook for anything in 2027.
Ridley was recently involved in an incident at the Nashville airport and that could make the Titans more likely unload at him at an even lower price than they might have originally been hoping to get.
One thing that could scare the Rams away is that Ridley (Hip) was on the injury report for Tennessee's most recent game back in Week 8. He also missed a total of 10 games last season due to injury. Considering the Rams' luck with injuries right now, those two things might be enough of a red flag to keep them away, but the 2018 first-round pick would certainly be an intriguing option.
With Alec Pierce still out, the Colts might not be interested in trading one of these two receiver, but with the way their season is going, the Colts should really be open to trading anyone and everyone. At 2-7, the Colts aren't going anywhere this season, so there goal should be to stockpile as many draft picks for the future by trading players away.
On Downs' end, he's in the final year of his rookie deal, which is one reason why a trade could be win-win for both sides. The Colts would get something in return for a player they're possibly going to lose anyway, while the cash-strapped Rams would only have to worry about Downs' $3.9 million base salary. title: 2026 NFL trade deadline: Ranking Vikings quarterback options with Kirk Cousins as best fit in Minnesota
summary: After Carson Wentz exposed Minnesota's offensive problems on national television, the 6-2 Vikings must consider an aggressive move
full_text:
The Minnesota Vikings are the rare 6-2 team in crisis. After a brutal 23-6 loss to the Buffalo Bills , Minnesota finds itself looking for a new quarterback on trade deadline day. Starting in place of the injured Kyler Murray (hamstring), Carson Wentz went 8-for-25 for 81 yards and two interceptions, putting Minnesota's broken offense on display for everyone to see on national television.
Murray has been one of the worst full-time starters in the NFL , and "full-time" is a stretch, considering he's missed two games and most of a third due to two different injuries. Minnesota is 28th is offensive points per game (17.4), and its 11 offensive touchdowns are tied with the Chargers for fewest in the league.
Changing starting quarterbacks in the middle of the season is far from ideal, but so is the Vikings' current situation. Continuing to roll out this level of quarterback play would mean wasting a Super Bowl-caliber defense. What Minnesota does at the game's most important position will change the entire tenor of the trade deadline, and there are quite a few options.
Who says you can't go home? (Or, at least, back to one of your homes?) Kirk Cousins spent 2019-23 with the Vikings, the final two years of which were under Kevin O'Connell. Cousins played high-level football, especially in 2023 before tearing his Achilles, under O'Connell, and he has been a pleasant surprise for the Raiders , keeping the seat warm for No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza .
This would not be a perfect solution -- there are none of those at this point -- as Cousins is coming off a three-interception game and isn't the player he was when he was in Minnesota previously. His mobility has taken a huge hit; he's 38 years old, and the arm strength has waned, too. But this would be the best option in a pinch. Cousins knows how to feed his best players the ball, and the Vikings have a great "best player" in Justin Jefferson . His experience in the system would help on a tight turnaround.
One big question would be why the Raiders would make this trade. Even with Mendoza waiting in the wings, Las Vegas has little reason to do this. It would force Mendoza to make his first career start on a short week of preparation against the Seahawks , one of the league's best defenses. Cousins has been an important part of Mendoza's development, too. Splitting that duo midseason doesn't make sense, and Cousins' presence would continue to pay dividends once Mendoza does eventually take over.
Another well-traveled veteran playing solidly in a placeholder role, Geno Smith would be the second-best option for Minnesota. Moreover, the Jets showed a willingness to make big trade-deadline sales before, having traded both Sauce Gardner and Quinnen Williams at the deadline last year for king's ransom. Trading Smith and getting back some solid trade compensation would add to their considerable war chest of 2027 picks, which currently includes three first-round selections.
Smith had a miserable 2025 with the Raiders but has been much better with the Jets, cutting down on the turnovers while still delivering on some of his trademark downfield aggression. His 16 completions for 20+ yards downfield are the fourth-most in the league this season. Downfield passing has been a disaster for Minnesota this season.
One issue here could be the Jets not having a proven backup. The only other quarterback on the 53-man roster is rookie Cade Klubnik , and Will Levis is on the practice squad. Would the Jets want Murray, who is on a cheap one-year deal anyway? If not, it might be hard to make this move; playing nearly half the season with a middle-round rookie is a tough look, even if New York is well out of the playoff picture. It's important to have a viable offensive ecosystem, if only to evaluate your personnel and keep the team engaged.
The Colts reportedly told Daniel Jones they will not trade him, but what if the Vikings came in willing to overpay? The Colts have already sold off Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner and could move other veterans ( Jonathan Taylor , Josh Downs , Grover Stewart ) before Tuesday's 4 p.m. ET deadline. Jones has endured a brutal season, but he's also had brutal surroundings, including one of the league's most underwhelming groups of pass catchers.
Jones spent time on the Vikings' practice squad in 2024, but this would be an underwhelming reunion. Jones has been a turnover machine and one of the worst starters in the NFL this year, even worse than Murray. He has not had a single game with more passing touchdowns than interceptions. Perhaps O'Connell sees something we don't, but it's hard to envision Jones providing any meaningful upgrade.
