title: NFL Week 10 picks and score predictions: Lions run over Patriots in Germany, Bengals survive
summary: John Breech predicts every Week 10 game, including a Lions victory over the Patriots in Munich
full_text:
I just got back from the NFL game in Spain, and I think I should probably start going more often, since Week 10 ended up being my best week of the year for picks.
I went 14-1 straight up, and yes, I should probably just retire at this point, but I don't want to retire while I'm on top; I want to retire when I hit rock bottom, which might actually happen this week. Speaking of rock bottom, I went to McDonald's four times while I was in Spain, and let me just say, I only went there because Madrid had the nicest McDonald's I've ever seen. I mean, just look at this place.
I'm now starting to understand why those Falcons players went to McDonald's. This is like the nicest McDonald's I've ever seen in my life. Wouldn't put it past Madrid to have a Michelin rated McDonald's #Bengals #Falcons #Spain https://t.co/w8WixT6iN2 pic.twitter.com/TMAeeXm9Fk
There were also people tailgating inside of a Taco Bell.
Taco Bell is in fact a mad house. NFL fans everywhere.  Nothing like a pregame cheesy gordita crunch. #Bengals #Falcons #Spain #Madrid https://t.co/0uAafegmaM pic.twitter.com/cpjfyWy33X
If you need just one reason to ever visit Spain, tailgating at Taco Bell has to be it. Unfortunately, there's no game in Spain this week, so there will be no tailgating at Taco Bell, but there is a game in Germany, and it will be the final NFL game of this year that kicks off at 9:30 a.m. ET, which is definitely for the best, because I've reached my maximum limit for 9:30 a.m. ET games.
The Patriots and Lions will be playing in the early game on Sunday. So who's going to win? Let's get to the Week 10 picks and find out.
Actually, before we get to the Week 10 picks, here's a quick reminder that you can check out the weekly picks from every CBSSports.com NFL expert by clicking here . Also, I'm in charge of the NFL newsletter here at CBSSports.com and if you want me invading your inbox twice a week, then you should definitely sign up. If you want to subscribe, all you have to do is click here and enter your email address . If you do that, it will instantly make us best friends and you don't even have to feel bad about that because I've already let all my best friends know that they might be replaced this week.
Alright, now let's get to the picks for real
Based on everything I've seen from the Commanders , I already know exactly how this game is going to play out: Washington is going to keep this thing close until the end only to lose (or tie) because no one in the organization has any idea what to do in any key late-game situation.
For instance, let's go back to Week 5 when the Commanders pulled off one of the all-time worst late-game gaffes in a tie with the Giants . Washington had the game won. All Jayden Daniels had to do was literally anything except what he actually did.
The Commanders can't get the play off in time and this game ends in a tie pic.twitter.com/WmPp6q5hU0
Look at the Giants players in that clip. They're celebrating. When the other team is CELEBRATING a tie, that means you lost.
Surely Daniels and the Commanders learned their lesson, right? Wrong. In their Week 9 game against the Rams , they needed a 32-yard touchdown on the final play, but instead of throwing it in the end zone, Daniels threw the ball five yards past the line of scrimmage because the Commanders apparently thought they were going to be able to lateral the ball to each other all the way into the end zone. There's a reason that never works.
With the game on the line Jayden Daniels can’t get the ball out of his hand. pic.twitter.com/2D8I1YWsiA
Now, you could blame Daniels for this stuff, but ultimately, it falls on the coaching staff. In the Rams' game, Daniels said he was just running the play that was called . In the Giants' game, someone on the coaching staff should have made it clear to everyone on the field that the clock has to come to a stop on that play, whether it's a spike or a player running out of bounds.
So what does this mean for this game? It means that the Commanders are actually playing decent football and if their coaching staff doesn't let them down, I think they have a good chance of winning. The Giants are beat up at quarterback, they're beat up at running back, and they're surviving by the skin of their teeth. Four of their five wins have come by one score. Good teams win close games -- are you taking notes, Commanders -- and I'm starting to feel like the Giants might be a sneaky good team.
To me, this is arguably the most fascinating game of Week 10. If the Commanders lose, their season is all but over, but if they win, they'll be right back in the NFC East race. I feel like this is a pick I'm going to regret as soon as I make it, but I'm taking the desperate Commanders.
PICK: Commanders 24-17 over Giants
With this game being played in Munich, I feel like this would be the perfect time to answer the one question that has been on all of our minds over the past few months: Who would win a beer-chugging contest between Mike Vrabel and Dan Campbell?
With these two guys heading to the beer capital of the world, there's no reason not to find out. And to be honest, based on how the Patriots have been playing recently, Vrabel could probably use a few beers right about now. I'm not in charge of scheduling events for the NFL in Germany this week, which is probably for the best, but if I were, I would rent out the Hofbrauhaus and then give both Campbell and Vrabel one full stein of beer to chug. Instead of a coin toss on Sunday, this is how we would decide who's getting the ball first.
I was at the Hofbrauhaus once and it took me an hour to finish my beer. The Germans were definitely laughing at me.
What's the record for most beers drank in one sitting here? I think I'm going to try to break it. pic.twitter.com/UQ5kOtxyPL
The Germans might be laughing at the Patriots, too, if they can't turn things around this week. Vrabel is known as one of the smartest defensive-minded coaches in the NFL, but he hasn't figured out how to stop any NFC North teams. The Patriots have faced two NFC North teams this year and not only have they gone 0-2, but they're surrendering an average of 37.5 points per game. Yikes.
The NFC North is so good that I might not pick against any of their teams for the rest of the season unless they're playing another NFC North team. If you've looked at the NFL standings at any point over the past 24 hours, you may have noticed that the NFC North is arguably the best all-around division in the NFL this year and possibly ever.
All four teams are at least three games over .500, which is the first time that's ever happened through the first nine weeks. Oh, and did I mention that the NFC North is 20-4 against all other divisions. They are destroying everyone. On the other hand, you have the Patriots, who are 3-1 against AFC East opponents, but 2-3 against everyone else. The Patriots have had one of the worst passing defenses in the NFL over the past several weeks, and now, they have to face off against a QB in Jared Goff who ranks in the top five in passing yards per game this year.
The Lions might put up 50 points. The good news for the Patriots is that even if the Lions do put up a 50-burger, New England might still keep up. Detroit has given up the MOST passing yards per game this year (260.9), so Drake Maye could certainly get some turkey carving practice for Thanksgiving here by carving up the Lions' defense. That being said, I've decided not to trust Maye against good teams.
The Patriots have faced six opponents this year with winning records, and in those games, Maye has thrown 11 interceptions to nine touchdowns. Based on how I think this game is going to go, Vrabel might need a Hofbrauhaus beer after it's over.
PICK: Lions 34-27 over Patriots
Deshaun Watson did not play in Week 9 for the Browns , but there's no chance he's going to miss this game. This is the ultimate revenge, though, I can't say for sure whether this is more about the Texans trying to get revenge…
author: John Breech

title: Prisco's NFL Week 10 Power Rankings: Top 5 remains same, Bengals and Packers surging thanks to MVP candidates
summary: Pete Prisco shares his Week 10 Power Rankings for the 2026 NFL season, including the Vikings dropping five spots
full_text:
Run the ball. Run the ball. Run the ball.
That's all we ever hear about NFL offenses. If you don't run the ball, you are dead.
Let's take a look at the Cincinnati Bengals and Green Bay Packers. They don't run it well at all. Yet both enter Week 10 as legitimate Super Bowl contenders. Why? They can throw the heck out of the football.
They are the top two passing offenses in the NFL, with the Bengals averaging 285.5 yards per game and the Packers right behind at 279.7. Both have averaged over 300 the past three games.
Run games? The Bengals are 30th in rush yards per game, while the Packers are dead last. Neither is close to 100 yards per game, although their numbers are slightly up over the past three games. Neither team averages 4.0 per rush; the Packers are at 3.0, which ranks 31st in the league.
Throw to score. Run to win.
Both will have to run it better when they need to run it late in games, but, for now, having Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow and Packers quarterback Jordan Love sling it around is the way these teams need to play.
I jokingly say that neither should ever call a run play until they are leading late in games. Ok, so I'm half-joking. But you get the idea. If they keep playing with the foot on the pedal, with two big-play quarterbacks, each with a pair of down-the-field receivers, they will be tough to beat.
Both are now in my top 10 of the Power Rankings, with Green Bay moving up to No. 10 this week, with the Bengals a few spots ahead at No. 7.
Staying there for both of them will mean continuing to play the same style of football, which means not allowing the old, tired run-it folks to influence play-calling. Play to the strengths and don't get caught up in the adages about running the football.
Run the ball? Not these two. Nor should they —and both just might ride the right arms of their quarterbacks to a Super Bowl.
author: Pete Prisco

title: Six lessons learned from NFL Week 9: Arvell Reese a superstar in the making, C.J. Stroud having career year
summary: Plus, there's a bell cow running back emerging for one of the NFL's best teams
full_text:
With the trade deadline today, I am reminded that self-awareness is of one of the best attributes an organization can have, from top to bottom.
The team that comes to mind immediately is one we've heard a lot from -- not in a good way -- this year: the Colts . Around this time last year, Indianapolis sent away two first-round picks for Sauce Gardner in a trade-deadline blockbuster. Indianapolis was 7-2 at the time, but was it really a team that needed to go all-in? No. Daniel Jones was playing so over-his-head well, and a smart front office would have recognized the great record was a product of a very soft schedule, a little bit of luck and an unprecedented hot streak. There was no rush here. The 2025 season was supposed to be a transition one, and a medium-sized cornerback addition would have been fine. Again, just a few months earlier, Indianapolis was basically taking a flyer on Jones.
You know how the rest of the story goes. Jones and the offense start to fall off, then Jones ruptures his Achilles. Now, the Colts are 2-7 and in the midst of a franchise-altering sale while not even owning their first-round pick. If the draft started today, Indianapolis would send the No. 4 pick to the Jets . Yikes!
The Jets, meanwhile, continue to profit in a big way off of that trade and the Quinnen Williams trade. They currently own the No. 4 (Colts'), No. 6 (their own) and No. 13 ( Cowboys ') picks. They knew this would be a long process. They knew it could be ugly for a while, and this year's 2-7 mark confirms that. But New York could have a terrific kickstart to their rebuild in a few months' time.
One team fell for fool's gold. The other knew exactly where it was and embraced its unenviable role.
The Jets are still waiting to fully invest in their rebuild. The other New York team? Well, it has already started -- and is way ahead of schedule -- thanks to a different type of self-awareness.
Please just watch these highlights first, then pick your jaw up from off the floor and continue reading below.
ARVELL REESE COMPLETELY TOOK OVER AGAINST THE EAGLES. 12 TKL, 10 SOLO, 3 SACK, 1 FF vs Eagles. Reese is the DROY favorite and making a case for DPOY consideration. https://t.co/zAwPLEFwnv pic.twitter.com/xJGzta0fCF
The biggest question surrounding Reese during the build-up to the NFL Draft was "Where do you play him?"
The answer should have been another question: "Why does it matter?"
And the Giants were exactly right to take that approach. Reese was an EDGE at Ohio State who moonlighted at off-ball linebacker. When the Giants initially drafted him, John Harbaugh basically said he'd play linebacker but also move around. Through eight games, Reese has now played at least 30 snaps at seven different spots: right inside linebacker, left inside linebacker, right linebacker, right EDGE, left linebacker, middle linebacker and left EDGE.
This is the way the NFL is trending. Think about guys such as Seattle's Nick Emmanwori , technically a safety who really plays everywhere, and someone we've talked about in this column before. Reese is of that ilk: a truly, laughably absurd athlete. A weapon who transcends positional labels. His strip sack of Joe Milton happened in 2.29 seconds, the fastest sack of the year per Next Gen Stats.
Arvell Reese Ladies and Gentlemen #BigBlue pic.twitter.com/BeoQwGZG3A
Here's where the self-awareness portion comes in. The Giants knew neither they nor Reese had to have it figured out on Day 1. The Giants are in Year 1 under John Harbaugh and defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson. Reese is 21 years old. The world was (and still is!) their oyster to experiment. Reese looks phenomenal. The Giants are 5-2-1 despite having started three different quarterbacks, and players such as Reese give them a bright future, too.
I do not blame you if you didn't watch -- or even think twice (or once) -- about the Texans-Chargers Week 9 matchup. The Chargers are unwatchable, and the Texans are middling after coming into the season with Super Bowl expectations.
What you missed and may have missed for much of this season, though, is C.J. Stroud playing outstanding football. He threw five touchdown passes Sunday, and his highlights ranged from heart-warming ...
C.J. Stroud to Tank Dell for the TD 🗣️ HOUvsLAC on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/r0q9mBmr5d
(Welcome back, Tank Dell !)
C.J. Stroud and Kayshon Boutte with a 63-yard TD 👏 HOUvsLAC on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/d6CjZxnTHH
Lest you think "Oh, it's just the Chargers," they've actually been decent on defense this year. This was just Stroud putting on a clinic. It's been this way all year.
The Texans' 3-5 record is mostly due to a surprisingly up-and-down defense and major struggles on the ground. DeMeco Ryans hasn't been great situationally, either. Even if Houston doesn't make the playoffs, Stroud's play is huge for Stroud himself -- he entered the year without an extension on his rookie deal -- and for Houston, which can feel much better about handing Stroud said extension.
On a week in which Jordan Love and Joe Burrow stole the spotlight, don't forget about Stroud.
Did you watch Monday night?
I could leave it there, but I won't. Carson Wentz isn't the answer -- clearly. Kyler Murray has never looked comfortable in this offense. Is Geno Smith the answer? A reunion with Kirk Cousins ? It can't be worse than it's been, and Minnesota simply cannot waste this defense again.
Jonah Coleman recorded 17 carries for 57 yards and a touchdown and caught all four of his targets for 31 yards in the Broncos ' 26-21 win over the Panthers . He played 53 of Denver's 65 snaps, second-most of any skill-position player behind Courtland Sutton . He also played nine of Denver's 10 third-down snaps.
J.K. Dobbins , on the other hand, played just nine snaps overall, and zero on third down. After some injuries earlier this year, Coleman owns this backfield -- especially until RJ Harvey returns -- and that's a good thing.
Yards per rush vs. 8-man box
Pct of runs with missed tackle forced
Coleman already has as many rushing touchdowns (three) as Dobbins has despite having less than half of Dobbins' carries.
Jonah Coleman gets the @Broncos back in the end zone! DENvsCAR on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/E9pCf15J6A
Let's remember that Coleman is a fourth-round rookie, too. He should continue to get better. Denver's reportedly been shopping around for running backs, but if it doesn't land one, Coleman will emerge as an early-down bell cow (with Harvey more in the mix on late downs) down the stretch.
Just, please, Sean Payton, no more pitch plays in late-game, wind-the-clock scenarios. I think Bo Nix agrees .
We highlighted Evan Williams a few weeks ago , but that was really more about Jonathan Gannon. After a game that included an incredible interception, four pressures and five tackles, Williams gets his own slot here.
The four pressures were a season high for Williams, who blitzed a season-high eight times. On one blitz, he basically shoulder-checked Rhamondre Stevenson (a good pass-blocking back) to the side and forced a throwaway. On another, he didn't get near Drake Maye but tracked back and limited Maye's scramble to 3 yards. On his final blitz of the day, he ran right by Lan Larison and nearly got a strip sack.
Williams is a combination of a high-speed train and a bumper car attacking the quarterback. If you don't try to stop him, he'll chase you down, and when you do try to stop him, he bounces off and keeps going. He now has a ridiculous 38.2% pressure rate on 34 pass-rush snaps this season.
Oh yeah, and did we mention he can do this on the back end?
EVAN WILLIAMS OH MY GBvsNE on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/0UorFkoL2o
Evan Williams, man. pic.twitter.com/HWzHimna0E
Good player. Really, really good player. All-Pro player.
It was a rough week for the NFC South. The Falcons got shellacked by the Bengals in Madrid, the Panthers lost at home to the Broncos,…

title: Can Carson Beck convince the Cardinals not to draft a QB? He has eight games to make his case
summary: The third-round rookie has eight games to prove he can be this year's Tyler Shough, but history says that won't be easy
full_text:
Carson Beck wasn't supposed to be the Cardinals' starting quarterback in 2026. But after Jacoby Brissett was benched-and-then-traded to Baltimore following Week 8's loss, and then, seven days later, Gardner Minshew suffered an elbow injury that could require season-ending surgery , those best-laid plans have suddenly changed.
Now the third-round rookie is in line to make his NFL debut against the Rams this Sunday. And Beck will have eight games to convince the Cardinals they don't need to use what will almost certainly be a top-10 pick on another quarterback next spring.
(I say "almost certainly" because while the Cards are currently 3-6 and everything appears to be going wrong, a year ago at this time, the Saints were 1-7, turned to Tyler Shough to finish 5-4 and ended up with the eighth pick instead of something higher. Shorter version: We'll see.)
That's a potentially franchise-changing opportunity for the 65th overall pick, but what exactly would success look like?
Back in June, I wrote that Beck might be the safest quarterback in the 2026 draft class . The former Georgia and Miami QB had started 43 games, was a quick processor, took care of the football and kept the offense on schedule. His 38.6% first-down rate ranked in the 95th percentile among draft-eligible quarterbacks from 2015-26.
But there was a catch. Beck faced pressure on just 19.1% of his college dropbacks, the lowest rate among quarterbacks going back more than a decade, and more than 32% of his throws were screens. He was rarely asked to make something happen when everything around him fell apart because it so rarely did.
That was a big question entering the NFL: Was Beck's high floor the product of his talent, his surroundings or some combination of both? Well, we're about to find out.
Since 2007, 24 quarterbacks drafted in the third round or later made their first NFL start after Week 7 of their rookie seasons. (This is through the 2024 draft class so we can look at Year 2 production, as well.)
Of those 24, only eight started at least four games as rookies. And just three of those eight – Nick Foles, Desmond Ridder and Brock Purdy – started at least eight games the following season. Sam Howell was the only quarterback with fewer than four rookie starts to do so.
How late-starting rookie QBs drafted in Round 3 or later fared in Year 2
What's interesting is that six of those eight quarterbacks improved their yards per attempt between their first two and final two rookie starts. But that improvement didn't necessarily translate to long-term success.
Ridder, for example, went from 5.3 yards per attempt in his first two starts to 7.0 in his final two, with two touchdowns and no interceptions. Atlanta handed Ridder the starting job in 2023 but benched him twice that season before trading him to Arizona the following March. The Falcons then drafted Michael Penix Jr. eighth overall in 2024.
Purdy, obviously, was very different. He averaged 8.6 yards per attempt with four touchdowns and no interceptions in his first two starts, then maintained that production over his final two. He didn't need to improve dramatically because he'd already shown he could play. Now he's one of the league's best quarterbacks.
Five of those eight teams didn't draft a quarterback the following spring. But several drafted one within the next year or two, and where they picked tells us plenty about the decisions they made.
Next draft: first pick used
Matt Barkley, 2013 (R4, No. 98)
2023: No. 8, Bijan Robinson
Michael Penix Jr., 2024 (R1, No. 8)
2011: No. 5, Patrick Peterson
Ryan Lindley, 2012 (R6, No. 185)
2012: No. 26, Whitney Mercilus
Tom Savage, 2014 (R4, No. 135)
Sam Bradford, 2010 (R1, No. 1)
2013: No. 7, Jonathan Cooper
Logan Thomas, 2014 (R4, No. 120)
2015: No. 2, Marcus Mariota
Marcus Mariota, 2015 (R1, No. 2)
2023: No. 87, Ji'Ayir Brown
Kurtis Rourke, 2025 (R7, No. 227)
The Cardinals know this story better than most. Injuries forced them to start rookies John Skelton in 2010 and Ryan Lindley in 2012, but neither was viewed as the long-term answer. Arizona took Patrick Peterson fifth overall in 2011, passing on quarterbacks Jake Locker, Blaine Gabbert and Andy Dalton, then selected Jonathan Cooper seventh overall in 2013, ahead of Geno Smith. Instead of drafting a quarterback, the Cardinals traded for veterans Kevin Kolb and Carson Palmer in those respective offseasons.
That's why draft position matters. Tennessee had the No. 2 overall pick in 2015 and used it on Marcus Mariota after Zach Mettenberger's six rookie starts. St. Louis took Sam Bradford first overall in 2010, but Keith Null had only started four games because injuries forced the Rams to turn to their sixth-round rookie.
San Francisco's situation was different. The 49ers traded up to draft Trey Lance third overall in 2021, but he suffered a season-ending ankle injury in Week 2 of '22. Jimmy Garoppolo took over, then broke his foot in Week 13, giving Purdy, the final pick of the 2022 draft, his opportunity. Purdy won all five of his regular-season starts, then two playoff games, and by the following season he'd taken the job Lance was drafted to fill.
If there's a recent example Beck should hope to follow, it's Tyler Shough. The Saints selected him 40th overall in 2025, and he took over the starting job in Week 9, giving New Orleans nine games to evaluate him.
Shough went 5-4, but it was how he played that mattered . He completed nearly 68% of his passes, made smart decisions and showed he could run the offense without the Saints having to protect him. It wasn't always pretty, but it was enough for New Orleans to pass on drafting another QB in 2026 and enter the season believing Shough could be its long-term answer.
That's the goal for Beck. He doesn't need to become a superstar overnight, but he does need to give Mike LaFleur enough confidence to build around him instead of looking for his replacement – which is exactly what the Saints did in April when they used the No. 8 pick on wide receiver Jordyn Tyson.
And there's reason to think this offense should suit him. Arizona has attempted 58.8% of its passes within five yards of the line of scrimmage, while the offensive line has allowed pressure on 31.1% of dropbacks – the fifth-lowest rate in the NFL, according to TruMedia. Beck's accuracy, anticipation and ability to play on time should, in theory, translate. (The game, I need to remind myself, is not a theoretical exercise, so … we'll see.)
But Arizona also ranks 28th in yards per play, and Brissett and Minshew had not consistently turned those manageable throws into meaningful production. Beck's challenge is to turn those short throws into more first downs and points.
In my preseason projections for the 2026 rookie quarterbacks, I had Beck averaging 6.9 yards per attempt with an 85.8 passer rating – solid numbers that would be an improvement over Arizona's quarterback play to date. But just as important will be whether Beck gets better over the next two months.
The Cardinals don't need to reel off eight straight wins, but they do need to see how Beck responds when defenses take away the easy throws. Can he push the ball downfield, keep drives alive under pressure and avoid costly mistakes?
At Miami last season, Beck showed that he can be an efficient game manager – and his preseason debut suggested those skills could translate . Now comes the part that actually matters: proving he can do it against NFL starters, week after week, when opponents know exactly what he wants to do.
And with a possible top-10 pick awaiting Arizona in April, there's a lot at stake – for the rookie quarterback and an organization that last had a winning season in 2021 (and before that, 2015). Beck doesn't have to prove he's a franchise quarterback during his two-month audition, but he does have to give the Cardinals a reason to believe he could become one.
author: Ryan Wilson

title: Cardinals' Gardner Minshew feared to have suffered a torn UCL, could be out for season, per report
summary: Carson Beck would get the start if Minshew is sidelined
full_text:
The Arizona Cardinals offensive injuries continue to pile up. Shortly after head coach Mike LaFleur announced wide receiver Michael Wilson would be ruled out for the year with a neck injury and added there was a chance Gardner Minshew misses Sunday's game against the Los Angeles Rams , reports came out that the quarterback is feared to have suffered a torn UCL in his throwing arm.
According to NFL Network, Minshew could be out for the season and face "months of rehab," pending further testing. Minshew reportedly suffered the injury before halftime but played through it in last week's 17-3 loss against the Seattle Seahawks .
If Minshew is sidelined, Carson Beck would be the next man up. Beck would be the third quarterback to start for the Cardinals this season. Jacoby Brissett began the year as their starter before being benched and traded to the Baltimore Ravens earlier this month.
Since Beck would be the team's only QB on the depth chart if Minshew is out for the year, team reportedly acted fast to get some backup. On Monday, the team signed Josh Johnson off the Cincinnati Bengals practice squad, according to ESPN . This marks Johnson's 15th NFL team in 14 seasons.
Beck was drafted in the third round of the 2026 NFL Draft at No. 65 overall. The two-time College Football Playoff national champion has yet to make an appearance in the NFL. He would be the third rookie quarterback to start a game this season, joining Tampa Bay Buccaneers undrafted free agent Jalon Daniels and Washington Commanders seventh-rounder Athan Kaliakmanis .
The 24-year-old spent five years at Georgia and his last collegiate season with Miami (FL). He finished with 338 completions, a conference high, for 3,813 yards, 30 touchdowns and 12 interceptions last season. His 72.4 completion percentage was also a conference high.
In 55 total college games, he had 966 completions for 11,725 yards, 88 touchdowns and 32 interceptions.
After Brissett's eight games, the team made a change at QB during the third quarter of their Nov. 1 game against the Cowboys , putting in Minshew. Beck was promoted to backup quarterback, with Brissett demoted to the third-string QB shortly before his exit from Arizona.
Minshew played two games, with a 71.7 completion percentage, 354 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions, going 0-1 in starts.
The Cardinals currently sit at 3-6 and are in fourth place in the NFC West.

title: Jordan Davis trade grades: Eagles kickstart rebuild, Jaguars push for 2026 AFC and Super Bowl titles
summary: Grading how both squads made out in the biggest trade on the eve of the NFL's Nov. 10 trade deadline
full_text:
The Jacksonville Jaguars capped their flurry of activity on the eve of the NFL's 2026 trade deadline with a blockbuster : they traded a 2027 first-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick for Philadelphia Eagles defensive tackle Jordan Davis.
Davis was the 13th overall pick in the 2022 NFL Draft out of Georgia and was also a starter on the Eagles' Super Bowl LIX title team in the 2024 season. Jacksonville doesn't have to worry about a long-term contract with Davis since Philadelphia extended Davis on a three-year, $78 million extension this past offseason. On Monday , the Jaguars have relinquished a 2027 first-round pick, a 2027 second-round pick, a 2028 fifth-round pick, a 2028 sixth-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick for the services of Davis, Atlanta Falcons Pro Bowl safety Jessie Bates III and New Orleans Saints defensive tackle Davon Godchaux.
Meanwhile, the Eagles now have 10 draft picks in the first two rounds of the NFL Draft across the next three years. They have their own first-round pick and second-round pick, plus the Jaguars' first-round pick in 2027. They have their own first-round pick and own second-round pick plus the New England Patriots' first-round pick (A.J. Brown trade) and the Baltimore Ravens' second-round pick (Cam Jurgens trade) in 2028. In 2029, they have their own first-round pick, their own second-round pick and the Jaguars' second-round pick (Jordan Davis trade).
So how does each side grade out in Monday evening's blockbuster deal? Let's dive in.
The Jaguars are right to go all in for the 2026 season. The Buffalo Bills (6-1) have one of the leakiest secondaries in the NFL, allowing 254.7 passing yards per game (the third-most in the entire NFL). The Denver Broncos (7-2) have offensive inconsistency issues because of quarterback Bo Nix, whose 5.6 air yards per pass attempt is the second-worst among 31 qualified quarterbacks this season. Nix's 5.6 air yards per pass attempt is mere decimal points ahead of Kansas City Chiefs (6-2) quarterback Patrick Mahomes' 5.6 air yards per pass attempt to avoid being dead last in the league. Mahomes' league-worst air yards per pass attempt figure has more to do with the Chiefs' limited passing game options than an unwillingness to throw the ball downfield like Nix.
The AFC North-leading Pittsburgh Steelers (6-2) have Aaron Rodgers at quarterback, and he will be 43 years old by the time the playoffs begin. Jacksonville beat the Cincinnati Bengals (6-2) in a narrow, one-score game earlier this season, and the New England Patriots (5-4) just got decimated at home (45-27) by quarterback Jordan Love and his Green Bay Packers.
Jacksonville's timing is right, but the price they paid for Davis is not. A first-round pick and a second-round pick for Davis isn't all that different from what the Chicago Bears gave up (2027 and 2028 first-round picks plus a 2027 fourth-round pick) for All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons, the best defensive tackle in football at the moment. Sure, the Jaguars were never going to get Simmons since he was on an AFC South division rival, the Tennessee Titans, but couldn't they have gotten Davis for a slightly cheaper price? The Bears are getting a player whose 17 sacks over the last two seasons are the most in the league among defensive tackles, while Davis has just 9.5 career sacks.
Yes, Davis can be incredibly impactful in the run game just because of his frame (6-feet-6-inches tall while weighing 336 pounds), but one would think that the Jaguars would have been able to acquire a more well-rounded defensive tackle at the price point of a 2027 first-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick. Davis will certainly help Jacksonville, but what they gave up for him was a little rich.
Hats off to Eagles general manager Howie Roseman because he's done it again. He recognized that the 2026 season was dead with quarterback Jalen Hurts (blood clots) sidelined, and the team was on a seven-game losing streak, putting their record at 2-7 through nine games. Roseman also extended two-time Pro Bowl defensive tackle Jalen Carter on a four-year, $152 million extension last offseason, and it was clear that Philadelphia likely wouldn't be able to keep both Carter and Davis for years to come in order to have a well-balanced roster.
Roseman was able to trade away the lesser player of the two, and he recouped first-round and second-round draft capital in the deal. He couldn't have asked for anything more, and he'll be able to rebuild the Eagles in no time with 10 picks in the first two rounds of the draft across the next three years.

title: Cardinals Michael Wilson out for the year with neck fracture, how it impacts fantasy football
summary: Wilson was the top wide receiver for the Cardinals this season, who have lost a lot of depth at the position.
full_text:
The Arizona Cardinals will be without their top wide receiver for the rest of the 2026 season. Wideout Michael Wilson will be out for the year with a fracture in his neck, head coach Mike LaFleur announced on Monday.
Wilson suffered the injury on the fourth play of the game, but he played through the injury.
"He said he kinda had a kink in his neck, but he's such a warrior he didn't think much of it. When the adrenaline wore down and he got his test today, that's when we knew," LaFleur said .
Despite the injury, Wilson still had with the most receiving yards on the team in their Week 9 17-3 loss to the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks , finishing with six receptions for 60 yards. This season, he leads the team among wide receivers with 51 receptions on 88 targets for 546 yards and two touchdowns through nine games, all of which were starts.
The Cardinals have already taken numerous hits to the wide receiver room. Marvin Harrison Jr . was traded earlier this season, Kendrick Bourne is out for the year, and Jalen Brooks is also on IR. With Wilson out, the team will need to rely on undrafted rookie Harrison Wallace III , rookie fifth rounder Reggie Virgil and veteran Simi Fehoko .
Wallace has one game played, no starts and no targets this season. Virgil has nine receptions for 54 yards and Fehoko has one reception for 17 yards. In total, all three combine for 71 yards on the season, about 13 percent of what Wilson has alone this year. Fehoko, a six-year veteran, only has 11 receptions across his entire career.
Wilson is coming off a career-best 2025 with his first 1,000-yard showing. He finished the year with 1,006 yards on 78 receptions with seven touchdown receptions. The 2023 third rounder has 47 total starts over 55 games, all with the Cardinals, for 2,665 yards on 214 receptions and 16 trips to the end zone.
CBS Sports Senior Fantasy writer Heath Cummings noted that the injury could have major fantasy football implications as league close in on playoffs. Trey McBride is still expected to see a third of the Cardinals' targets, which makes him a "must-start," but his efficency might dip now that teams have no other pass catchers to worry about.
LaFleur added Gardner Minshew could miss Sunday's game against the Los Angeles Rams , as the team fears that Minshew suffered a torn UCL, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport. Minshew is getting more tests, but the injury (that Minshew suffered before halftime but played with) could also put him on season-ending IR. Carson Beck taking over would also impact the team's wide receiver production in a negative way.
If Zonovan Knight returns, Cummings could see him as a high-end flex in the right matchup, as could Tyler Allgeier if Knight misses more time. Cummings warns to "avoid all Cardinals not named McBride."

title: Rams All-Pro Puka Nacua likely to go on injured reserve with knee, toe injuries
summary: The Rams will now likely be without both Puka Nacua and Davante Adams
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams (5-4) can't catch a break from the injury. After All-Pro edge rusher Myles Garrett's triumphant return to the lineup in their Week 9 victory over the Washington Commanders , All-Pro wide receiver Puka Nacua is expected to go on injured reserve.
Coach Sean McVay told reporters on Monday that Nacua, who is dealing with MCL and PCL sprains in addition to turf toe, will likely go on injured reserve, thus sidelining him for at least four games. That's a massive blow for the Rams as Nacua led the NFL in catches (129), receiving first downs (80) and receiving yards per game (107.2) last season. He is also the NFL's all-time leader in receiving yards per game with a career average of 96.2. This season, he has 70 catches for 715 receiving yards and 4 touchdowns while also adding 41 yards rushing and a touchdown on 7 carries. Nacua leads the Rams in every receiving metric this season while being tied for the team lead in receiving touchdowns with six-time Pro Bowl wide receiver Davante Adams . In 2026, he represents 27.6% of the Rams' team target share, which is the eighth-highest rate in the entire NFL this season.
Nacua now joins Adams (hamstring) on injured reserve. Adams went down with a hamstring injury in the team's Week 6 loss against the Arizona Cardinals , and McVay said at the time that Adams would be expected to miss 6 to 10 weeks. That means the earliest Adams could return is against his former team, the Green Bay Packers , in Week 12 on Nov. 25. The earliest Nacua could return is Week 15 against the Dallas Cowboys on Dec. 20, if he misses a minimum of four games. Fortunately for Nacua, Los Angeles' Week 11 bye also gives him an extra week to heal up.
After Nacua and Adams, Los Angeles running back Kyren Williams leads the Rams in targets (46), and he is No. 2 on the team in catches with 36. Tight end Tyler Higbee is No. 3 on the team in receiving yards with 287 after both Nacua and Adams, and tight end Davis Allen (two receiving touchdowns) is No. 3 on the team in receiving touchdowns behind Los Angeles' two injured star wideouts.
Quarterback Matthew Stafford will have to make some magic happen with a depleted arsenal of playmakers, in addition to leaning on Williams and Blake Corum in the run game, in order to maximize the Rams' "all in" 2.0 run in 2026.

title: Why NFL trade deadline evolved from afterthought to hectic: In-season transaction boom is league's new normal
summary: After a record-breaking trade deadline in 2025 and with an active transaction wire in 2026, the times are a-changin' in the NFL
full_text:
Less than a decade ago, it was common for the NFL to feature single-digit trades during the course of the regular season. The trade deadline was generally a snoozer in comparison to that of the other major American professional sports leagues, and the number of moves made at the buzzer could often be counted on one hand. That could not be further from the case anymore.
Twenty-four hours out from the 2026 trade deadline , there were 10 in-season trades in the books. That number will balloon in the final hours before the clock strikes 4 p.m. ET on Nov. 10. Star players could be on the move as Super Bowl contenders gear up for the stretch run and teams falling out of contention seek to jumpstart their rebuilds with premium draft capital. Basketball and baseball fans are used to seeing this flurry of transactions, but it is still relatively new to football fans. Just like in the other leagues, though, this boom is becoming the NFL's new normal.
Last year, there were 22 trades from the first day of the regular season through the deadline. That was the most in any year since at least 1995, according to NFL Research. A whopping 12 players and 14 picks were exchanged on deadline day alone. General managers were busier than ever. That was the extreme continuation of a trend that has been in effect since the mid-2010s, in which front offices mortgage their futures for instant-impact players or, conversely, sell off their most valuable assets to hoard draft picks.
Only once from 2010 through 2017 did the NFL log 12 or more in-season trades, according to the Spotrac trade tracker . Something flipped towards the end of the decade, because that number now represents the low-water mark since 2018.
Why the sudden uptick? There are fundamental processes in the NFL that make this league more trade-averse than other sports leagues, but changes to the calendar and new front-office philosophies have created pathways for teams to bypass some of the roadblocks.
Here are the factors at play.
Trading players in the NFL is not as simple as matching salaries. That is largely why player-for-player trades remain so rare. The way contracts are structured, with teams spreading bonuses out across multiple years, taking on dead money and being on the hook for some of the salary owed to the players they trade away, is sometimes prohibitive. Plus, the NFL has a hard salary cap, so unlike in the NBA , where teams use exceptions to go over the cap, or in MLB, where wealthy owners can pony up as much money as they please, all deals have to result in both teams remaining under that firm number.
Football is also not as plug-and-play as other sports. There are massive playbooks to learn, especially at the offensive skill positions. There is incredibly important timing to perfect, particularly for the quarterback-wide receiver tandem. With 11 players on the field at all times and complicated schemes to comprehend, anyone who joins a lineup in the middle of the season has a lot of learning to do on the fly.
The brevity of a 17-game regular season also keeps a larger percentage of the league in playoff contention deeper into the year compared to 82- or 162-game campaigns. The lack of non-contenders means fewer teams are willing to sell, and thus there is a smaller volume of available players.
Draft picks are also immensely valuable since teams have so many roster spots to fill. And at the same time, rosters are so large that fringe players around the 53-man cutoff can simply be released if the potential trade package is undesirable.
Until 2011, the NFL trade deadline was extremely early in the season. It landed on the Tuesday following Week 6, which was well before the midway point of the campaign. Teams were often still attempting to figure out where they stood in the pecking order when it came time to lock in their rosters. How could a general manager shop one of his stars on an expiring contract when they were not sure whether their team was in the mix for a postseason berth or not? They rarely did.
That changed in 2012 when the NFL and NFL Players Association agreed to move the deadline back by two weeks to the Tuesday following Week 8. And not long after the league adopted a 17th regular-season game, it moved the deadline back another week to where it stands now: The Tuesday after Week 9, which is effectively the midseason point.
It is far clearer where teams stand in the playoff picture after Week 9 than after Week 6. Look no further than the Indianapolis Colts , who emerged as one of the NFL's most aggressive sellers this year. Through six games, they were 2-4 and competitive enough in a couple of their losses to believe that they could right the ship. Now, after nine games, they are a measly 2-7 and own a five-game losing streak. Clearly out of the postseason hunt, they moved on from perennial Pro Bowlers in Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner .
Perhaps the single most impactful change in the rise of in-season trades comes from the mentality surrounding draft picks. While the value of Day 1 picks in the NFL is still tremendous, it is more common now than ever to see general managers move that sacred capital for players who can help them win at the highest level right away instead of a couple of years down the line. Nowhere is this clearer than in Los Angeles, where Rams general manager Les Snead birthed the "F them picks" mantra.
Each of those moves opened or extended the Rams' championship contention windows. They are bets on current stars and their ability to keep playing at a high level, compared to the risk of boom-or-bust picks in the late first round. In order to balance the roster, Snead relies on finding diamonds in the rough in the later rounds, which he has been highly successful at pulling off.
This model delivered a Super Bowl and proved to other teams that it is a viable strategy for roster construction. In the copycat league that is the NFL, the Rams are no longer the only team to go all in to fuel championship runs.
Snead even has direct disciples putting his methodology to practice in other places. Jacksonville Jaguars general manager James Gladstone worked under Snead's tutelage in various roles for nine years before he landed a GM job of his own. On Monday, he pulled off two trades in which he swapped draft picks for immediate-impact players. They may not have been Day 1 picks, but they were draft capital nonetheless.
Draft picks are still gold, even in this era where they are moved like never before. General managers who want the best of both worlds -- to hoard picks and secure immediate impacts -- can balance the two, but they have to be creative. Enter the pick swap. Instead of one team netting a draft pick while the other loses one, pick swaps allow teams to generate value in the aggregate while retaining at least some capital. If a player is valued around a late-Day 2 pick, the buying team could send a second-rounder and receive a Day 3 pick in return along with that player.
Compensatory picks also give general managers the flexibility to take swings at available players. If there is a veteran on an expiring contract who can join a team as a half-season rental, the buying franchise may give up a third-round pick or worse to acquire them, knowing that they can recoup the pick if the player leaves in free agency.
Gladstone himself pulled off a masterful move ahead of Tuesday's deadline by factoring compensatory picks into the equation. He reached a deal with the New Orleans Saints that sent Davon Godchaux to Jacksonville in exchange for a conditional 2028 sixth-round pick. That pick would become a 2027 sixth-rounder if the Jaguars acquire one through another trade or through the compensatory formula. In essence, Gladstone traded a pick he does not even own yet.
So many things in football are cyclical, but the surge in trade deadline action has staying power. Changes at the league level with regard to scheduling have made it more viable, and general managers are…
author: Carter Bahns

title: Jordan Davis traded: Jaguars going all in, acquire former first-round pick from Eagles
summary: Davis is the third defender the AFC South-leading Jacksonville Jaguars have traded for on Monday
full_text:
The AFC South-leading Jacksonville Jaguars (6-2) are loading up for a run at the Super Bowl just ahead of the trade deadline. After trading for Atlanta Falcons safety Jessie Bates III and New Orleans Saints defensive tackle Davon Godchaux, they are trading for another defender Monday afternoon: Philadelphia Eagles defensive tackle Jordan Davis.
The Jaguars are sending the Eagles a 2027 first-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick for Davis, the 13th overall pick in the 2022 NFL Draft out of Georgia who was a starter on the Eagles' Super Bowl LIX title team in the 2024 season. Jacksonville doesn't have to worry about a long-term contract with Davis as they do with Bates, since Philadelphia extended Davis on a three-year, $78 million extension this past offseason.
We have agreed to trade DT Jordan Davis to the Jacksonville Jaguars in exchange for a 2027 1st-round pick and a 2029 2nd-round pick. pic.twitter.com/jERfS1fw5Q
On Monday alone, the Jaguars have shipped out a 2027 first-round pick, a 2027 second-round pick, a 2028 fifth-round pick, a 2028 sixth-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick for the services of Davis, Bates and Godchaux. Jacksonville entered Monday with the No. 2 scoring defense in football (15.1 points per game), and now they are continuing to fortify that side of the ball to help quarterback Trevor Lawrence and the league's No. 4 scoring offense (28.6 points per game) make a push to win the AFC and advance to the Super Bowl. Just a year ago, the New England Patriots made the leap from picking in the top five to winning the conference, and the AFC appears wide open once again, with both the Kansas City Chiefs and Buffalo Bills each having clear flaws.
Eagles issue a statement on the departure of Jordan Davis. pic.twitter.com/C17UhhpwCB
author: Garrett Podell

title: Eagles coach Nick Sirianni denies giving his fans the middle finger after division loss: 'Absolutely not'
summary: Sirianni said the accusations were a 'surprise' to him, which come after Philadelphia's first home loss to the Giants in 13 years.
full_text:
The Philadelphia Eagles season isn't exactly going as planned, with a losing record and major injuries. When struggles come in sports, frustrations typically follow and Philly's head coach has been accused of letting out those frustrations with a well-known gesture after their 19-11 divisional loss to the New York Giants on Sunday, the team's first loss in Philadelphia to the Giants since 2013.
Nick Sirianni was called out for what some believe was the head coach giving fans the middle finger as he walked off the field after the Week 9 defeat. In the video, Sirianni looks at his hand, then the middle finger is raised higher than the others as he approaches the tunnel.
Nick Sirianni was asked if he was flipping fans off while walking off the field yesterday.   "Absolutely not."   #Eagles  https://t.co/fqKylEJGxw
— Cory Nidoh (@Cory_Nidoh) November 9, 2026
Sirianni denies any ill will on whatever his hand was doing at the time, saying , "Absolutely not. That was a surprise to me. Absolutely not."
This is not the first time Sirianni and Eagles fans have clashed. In 2024, Sirianni was booed by some fans at Lincoln Financial Field, with some yelling for him to be fired during a game against the then 1-5 Cleveland Browns . Fans weren't happy that the Eagles were struggling, coming off a bye, against an easy opponent. Philadelphia went went on to win the game, though narrowly at 20-16.
As he was walking off the field, Sirianni cupped his ears and yelled at fans. At first, he said he was just "having fun" and was "excited to get the win," but then reversed his messaging, issuing an apology to Eagles fans.
"What I was really doing, I was trying to bring energy yesterday, energy, enthusiasm, and I'm sorry and disappointed on how my energy was directed at the end of the game," he said at the time. "And, you know, my energy should be all in on coaching, motivating and celebrating with our guys. And so I've got to have better wisdom and discernment of when to use that energy and that wasn't the time."
Another notable move from the head coach this Sunday was how long it took to start his press conference, with him taking the podium over an hour after the game ended. He said during that time he was talking to players and didn't reveal exactly what it was about. Typically, press conferences begin much sooner than that for a head coach, so many online pointed out the oddity.
The Eagles currently sit at 2-7 and are on a seven-game losing streak. This marks the worst start during Sirianni's time with the team. This marks the first time since 1999 that the team has started 2-7.
If Sirianni wasn't in the hot seat before (he was), he certainly is now after a bad divisional loss that put them in last in the NFC East.
author: Shanna McCarriston

title: Jaguars-Falcons trade grades: Jacksonville acquires All-Pro safety Jessie Bates III to bolster defense
summary: Bates, who is in the final year of his contract, heads to Jacksonville in exchange for two future draft picks
full_text:
On the eve of Tuesday's trade deadline, dominoes are starting to fall across the league with Week 9 largely in the books. And now, the Jaguars have acquired All-Pro safety Jessie Bates III in a trade with the Atlanta Falcons , according to ESPN . As Bates heads to Duval County, the Falcons receive a 2027 second-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick in return.
Bates is in the final year of his contract and is set to be a free agent at the end of this season. While this is looked at as a rental, the 29-year-old should prove to be a key addition to Jacksonville's secondary as it looks to make a serious postseason push following a 6-2 start to the regular season.
In nine games played for the Falcons this season, Bates has recorded one interception, three forced fumbles, and 60 total tackles. The veteran has also allowed a 78.3% completion percentage to go with a 115.2 passer rating in coverage, per TruMedia.
Bates entered the NFL as a second-round draft choice of the Bengals in 2018 out of Wake Forest. After spending his first five years of his career in Cincinnati, he inked a four-year, $64.02 million contract with the Falcons in the spring of 2023 and has been lurking in their secondary ever since.
Bates is tied for the second-most interceptions (28) in the NFL since coming into the league and has been named a second-team All-Pro three times, including in 2025.
Atlanta spent last offseason inking several veterans to extensions, including Bijan Robinson and Drake London . Bates was not among them, and after dropping to 3-6 on the season with a loss to the Bengals in Madrid on Sunday, they're electing to move off of the talented safety for future draft capital.
Jacksonville gave up quite a bit to land Bates. Two picks -- particularly a second-rounder in 2027 -- is a hefty price to pay, especially considering that Bates is set to be a free agent at the end of this season. I do wonder, however, whether that price indicates that Jacksonville views Bates as more than just a rental. After all, the organization does have a history of extending players that they've acquired in midseason trades. For instance, after trading for wideout Jakobi Meyers around last year's deadline, they later signed him to a three-year, $60 million extension. I'll be curious to see if Bates follows a similar path.
Regardless of whether he's with the Jags for the next few months or years, it's a great move for the 2026 squad. Bates is one of the best safeties in the NFL. In fact, he's the player in the past 40 years with at least 800 tackles and 25 interceptions before age 30. He comes in as a premier piece for the secondary, while also deepening a safety room that has been hit by injuries, most recently losing Eric Murray for the rest of the season to an elbow injury.
Give Atlanta the slight edge here. While they are losing a blue-chip player in their secondary, they were probably going to lose him anyway in free agency later this offseason.
The Falcons spent the bulk of last offseason extending key pieces to their core, and that did not include Bates. While the team is technically still in the division race despite a 3-6 record, it doesn't feel like this season will see them making a sizable push if/when they reach the postseason. With that in mind, it's the more prudent move to move off of Bates, get worse in the secondary in the immediate, but collect legit draft capital to position yourself better down the road.
Getting a second-rounder as part of this deal is nothing to turn your nose up at and is better than any sort of compensatory pick they'd receive if Bates walked in free agency.

title: Vikings vs. Bills prediction: Josh Allen faces NFL's top defense on Monday night
summary: Josh Allen and Buffalo's explosive offense face Brian Flores' dominant defense, while Carson Wentz replaces the injured Kyler Murray
full_text:
In the Week 9 edition of "Monday Night Football," the Minnesota Vikings host the Buffalo Bills . Minnesota is coming off its first loss of the season after starting the year with six straight wins. The Vikings turn to Carson Wentz to start in place of Kyler Murray , who is dealing with a hamstring injury. Minnesota sports arguably the NFL's best defense, and it will be put to the test on Monday night against the Bills.
Buffalo has won three consecutive games to improve to 6-1, and last week beat up on the Baltimore Ravens following an injury to Lamar Jackson on the Ravens' first snap of the game. Buffalo is in first place in the AFC East behind its efficient and explosive offense, which has helped offset a defense that has been highly vulnerable this year.
Will the Vikings bounce back, or will the Bills continue to roll? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game.
This is going to be one of the most fascinating matchups of the season, as arguably the NFL's best quarterback ( Josh Allen ) will do battle with arguably the NFL's best defensive play-caller (Brian Flores). We know the state of play: the Vikings are going to blitz on damn near every snap, and the Bills are going to have to figure out how in the world to deal with all the extra bodies the Vikings send against both the run and the pass.
Last week, the Vikings totally shut down one of the best offenses in the league during the first half, holding the Lions to a mere 154 total yards (on 36 plays, an average of 4.3 per play) and only six points prior to the break. They frustrated Jared Goff and the passing game with their heavy blitzing and they limited Jahmyr Gibbs and company to a 25% rushing success rate.
Buffalo has been one of the best running teams in the NFL, averaging 4.8 yards per carry, which ranks fourth in the league. The Bills can lean on James Cook, who, after leading the NFL in rushing last year, is actually averaging nearly six more rushing yards per game than he did a year ago. Buffalo likes to get downhill runs with schemes like duo that create double teams inside, which is tough to do against the Vikings, but can lead to big gains if you can block them up front. Whether the Bills can do that is obviously another question.
It's important to note that Allen has been blitzed on exactly a third of his dropbacks, per Tru Media, meaning he's faced the 11th-highest blitz rate in the NFL. He's 46 of 70 for 587 yards, three touchdowns and three interceptions on those plays, and he's been sacked six times. That's all led to him checking in fourth in yards per attempt (8.4) and seventh in passing success rate (50.0%) but only 15th in EPA per dropback thanks to the interceptions.
The Bills will need to get the ball out quickly against the blitz, which could mean underneath targets like Khalil Shakir and passing-down back Ty Johnson are heavily involved. It might be a lighter game for the likes of Dalton Kincaid and Dawson Knox , as teams often keep their tight ends back in pass protection against Flores' blitz-happy defense.
It might also be tough for DJ Moore and Keon Coleman to get open down the field, but there could be opportunities for big plays if the offensive line does hold up on any given snap. The Vikings have given up the occasional deep shot this year because they send so many men after the quarterback and it leaves them shorthanded on the back end at times.
The Vikings have struggled to move the ball pretty much all season. Their 4.7 yards-per-play average is tied for third-worst in the NFL. Their 1.71 points-per-drive average is fifth-worst in the NFL. And their -0.14 expected points added per play average is second-worst in the NFL, according to Tru Media.
They've yet to gain more than 364 yards in any game, and they've been at 275 or fewer in five of their seven contests. They've scored more than 23 points just one time, and it was back in Week 1 when they had touchdown drives of 28, 1 and 14 yards late in the game against the Green Bay Packers .
Some of the struggles can be laid at the feet of Kyler Murray, who has completed 64.9% of his passes at an average of just 6.6 yards per attempt, with a mere five touchdown passes and three interceptions. Some of the struggles can be laid at the feet of the run game, where the backs have combined to average south of 4.0 yards per carry. Jordan Mason missed four games, but it's not like he's been effective when he's been on the field, having averaged 3.9 yards a pop.
Murray won't be on the field on Monday night. It'll be Carson Wentz under center in his place. Wentz went 23 of 39 for 276 yards and three touchdowns in one-plus games in relief of Murray earlier this year. He seemed to have more command of the offense and more chemistry with Justin Jefferson than Murray does, at the very least. Jefferson went for eight catches for 92 yards and two scores during Wentz's relief appearance back in Week 1, and he was on the receiving end of seven of Wentz's 19 pass attempts in that game. (Wentz's start the following week came in a driving rainstorm in Chicago and doesn't provide much room for analysis.)
If the Vikings can keep Wentz well-protected, there should be some opportunities for Jefferson, Jordan Addison and T.J. Hockenson to find openings in what has been a very leaky back seven. The Bills have been solid against the run this year, allowing only 3.9 yards per carry. Given the Vikings' struggles on the ground, it seems unlikely that they'll have much in the way of success running the ball here.
You can't ask me to buy into this Minnesota offense right now — not even against Buffalo's leaky defense. We just saw the Vikings put up a relatively limp offensive performance against the Lions. And if there's a team out there that can run the ball on Minnesota the way the Lions did, it might be the Bills with Josh Allen and James Cook. Buffalo can win a low-ish scoring game here by doing just that.
Prediction: Bills 20, Vikings 14
author: Jared Dubin

title: Josh Jacobs breaks finger during Packers' win, will undergo surgery and could miss a maximum of three weeks
summary: Jacobs hopes to play through the issue, but grip struggles could force Green Bay to pursue running back help before Tuesday's trade deadline
full_text:
Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs told reporters he broke the ring finger on his right hand during the 45-27 victory over the New England Patriots . Jacobs rushed four times for five yards in the first quarter before exiting the game with what was described as a hand injury. Kaleb Johnson ended up leading the Packers in rushing with 68 yards and a touchdown on 14 carries. Pierre Strong Jr . chipped in with 22 yards on eight carries.
Jacobs is set to undergo surgery on his injured finger this week and is expected to miss a maximum of three weeks , according to CBS Sports' Matt Zenitz.
Jacobs appeared to get one of the fingers on his right hand stuck in the face mask of Patriots safety Craig Woodson during a rushing attempt. He says they will find a way to play through it, but Jacobs struggled to grip the ball.
In three games this season, Jacobs has rushed 36 times for 80 yards and one touchdown. The Packers actually recorded the fewest rushing yards (485) by a winning team through eight games in NFL history, according to CBS Sports Research.
With Jacobs out, it does throw an interesting wrinkle into Tuesday's trade deadline. Green Bay entered Sunday with the worst rushing offense in the NFL at 60.6 yards per game. Could the Packers be interested in acquiring Jonathan Taylor from the Indianapolis Colts or Tony Pollard of the Tennessee Titans ?
The Packers' rushing offense has been a disaster, but Green Bay's passing attack is on fire. Jordan Love threw for 373 yards and three touchdowns against the Patriots, while Christian Watson caught seven passes for 171 yards and one touchdown, and Matthew Golden 10 passes for 164 yards and a touchdown. They became the fourth duo since 2000 to have 160 yards receiving and a receiving touchdown each in a game, and the first since Tyreek Hill and Jaylen Waddle of the Miami Dolphins in 2022.
author: Jordan Dajani

title: Lions-Jets trade grades: Detroit bolsters secondary with Andre Cisco, Jets acquire a late-round pick
summary: It wasn't the splashiest of moves, but Detroit nonetheless strengthened its secondary ahead of Tuesday's trade deadline
full_text:
The Detroit Lions and New York Jets have pulled off a trade ahead of Tuesday's deadline. Detroit is giving New York a 2028 sixth-round pick in exchange for veteran safety Andre Cisco , according to multiple outlets.
Cisco, 26, was drafted by the Jacksonville Jaguars in the third round of the 2021 NFL Draft . He spent his first four seasons in Jacksonville before he signed with the Jets ahead of the 2025 season. Cisco made 12 starts in 17 games in New York.
The 6-foot, 210-pound Cisco has made four starts across nine games this season. He had 23 tackles, one sack, one forced fumble and one pass breakup this season for the Jets, who are off to a disappointing 2-7 start.
Cisco is going to a Lions team that is 6-2 and vying for their third playoff appearance in the last four years. He will look to help a Detroit secondary that is currently last in the NFL in both passing yards (2,087) and touchdown passes (18) allowed. The unit has been playing better in recent weeks, however. The Lions have held each of their last three opponents (the Packers , Vikings and Dolphins ) to 17 or fewer points. Detroit's secondary allowed an average of just 200 passing yards per game over that span.
Who won the trade? Let's find out.
This is a pretty vanilla trade for the Lions and GM Brad Holmes. This is certainly not a splashy trade that will generate much excitement among Lions fans. This trade looks like it was at least partly done so that Holmes can say that he did something to improve the secondary at the trade deadline.
If Holmes is looking for credit, he should get it, even if the praise should amount to a polite golf clap. As the numbers above illustrate, the Lions' secondary has taken its lumps this season. And while the unit has displayed signs of growth in recent weeks, it's fair to point out that the last two quarterbacks they faced ( Kyler Murray and Malik Willis ) aren't exactly setting the world on fire this season. They did contain Jordan Love back in Week 7, though, so the Lions have had success in recent weeks against a top-tier passer.
If nothing else, Cisco can provide depth for a unit that sorely needs it. The bottom line is that the Lions are better for making this trade.
A bland trade merits bland grades. Jets GM Darren Mougey gets some credit for getting something in exchange for a player who was playing out the final year of his contract. The return, however, is the issue here.
Cisco isn't a star, but it's fair to question whether or not the Jets could have gotten more than a 2028 sixth-round pick, especially when you look at where the Lions' pass defense currently ranks among the rest of the NFL. The Jets could/should have gotten a pick in this year's draft for Cisco. Instead, they won't be able to reap the benefit of this trade until 2028.
author: Bryan DeArdo

title: Jaguars agree to trade for Saints DT Davon Godchaux in second defensive trade of the day, per report
summary: Jacksonville is among the most active buyers ahead of the NFL trade deadline
full_text:
Mere hours after they acquired All-Pro safety Jessie Bates III , the Jacksonville Jaguars agreed to a trade with the New Orleans Saints to acquire defensive tackle Davon Godchaux . According to The Athletic , the Jaguars will send a conditional 2028 sixth-round pick to the Saints in exchange for the veteran lineman. That pick can turn into a 2027 sixth-rounder if those conditions are met.
It should be noted that the Jaguars do not currently have a 2027 sixth-round pick, moving it in a trade with the Giants for offensive lineman Daniel Faalele in August. According to ESPN's Adam Schefter , if the conditions are met to upgrade the pick, any 2027 sixth-round pick the Jaguars eventually acquire would go to New Orleans. Jacksonville is currently projected to receive two sixth-round compensatory draft picks, according to Spotrac .
The Jaguars had been in the market for a defensive tackle in the wake of DaVon Hamilton's injury. The starting tackle suffered a torn quad in Week 8, which produced an opening in the middle of the defensive front. This move fills that gap, just like the Bates deal sealed a hole in the secondary, where Eric Murray was lost for the season due to an elbow issue.
Jacksonville's defense may already be Super Bowl-caliber, so the Godchaux acquisition should prevent any drop-off and keep the Jaguars in the hunt for the AFC's No. 1 seed. The unit ranks No. 5 against the run at just 89.3 yards allowed per game and is second-best in scoring at 15.1 points per game.
Godchaux heads to the fourth different team of his career since his arrival in 2017 as a fifth-round pick and will primarily make his impacts in run defense. He has not recorded a sack since 2022 but remains proficient against the rush and owns 15 tackles on the season with one of them coming in the form of a tackle for loss.
Godchaux started five of the Saints' first eight games and could slot directly into the Jaguars' lineup upon his arrival ahead of the Week 10 road game against the Tennessee Titans . Coach Liam Coen could either insert Godchaux into action or have him come off the bench in favor of Ruke Orhorhoro , who would have likely started if not for the trade. Arik Armstead remains the other starting interior defensive lineman.
The Jaguars are going for it. General manager James Gladstone is busy ahead of the trade deadline and successfully plugged two holes on the defense to keep Jacksonville squarely in the championship hunt. Godchaux is no game-changing addition but one who will do exactly what the Jaguars need, which is to plug gaps in run defense. What's more, they conditionally traded a draft pick they do not even own yet, which is some savvy negotiating on Gladstone's part. Since the Jaguars are projected to secure two compensatory sixth-rounders in 2027, that pick will likely vest and go to the Saints, but they will still have one left over.
The Saints own the fourth-worst run defense in the NFL , so Godchaux was clearly not working for them. The pick they got in return for him is decent compensation for a non-impact player. Plus, when they traded for Godchaux a year ago, they gave the New England Patriots a seventh-rounder, so they got that back and a little more by parting with him. It is only a slight upgrade in draft capital, but anything helps for a team that might not even make the playoffs in the league's worst division.
author: Carter Bahns

title: NFL Week 11 schedule flex: Giants-Jaguars moves to 4:25, Steelers-Eagles shifts to 1 p.m.
summary: New York and Jacksonville will receive a larger Week 11 spotlight as the league swaps their start time with the intrastate matchup between Pittsburgh and Philadelphia
full_text:
The NFL has moved the Week 11 Philadelphia Eagles ' home game against the Pittsburgh Steelers from 4:25 to a 1 p.m. ET start on Nov. 22. In a corresponding move, the New York Giants ' home game against the Jacksonville Jaguars has been moved from 1 p.m. to 4:25 p.m. Both games will be shown on CBS.
The league's decision to switch these starting times is obvious. New York (5-2-1) and Jacksonville (6-2) lead their respective divisions, and while Pittsburgh (6-2) also leads its division, Philadelphia (2-7) has lost seven straight games and is sitting in last place in the NFC East.
The NFL is also probably banking on the Steelers-Eagles game still getting decent viewership. It's an intrastate rivalry with a compelling storyline: Aaron Rodgers will try to lead the Steelers to the franchise's first win in Philadelphia since 1965.
The time swap will give Liam Coen's Jaguars an opportunity to showcase their talents before a larger audience. It also represents an opportunity for the Giants to get another big win in what has been a surprisingly successful first season for John Harbaugh in the Big Apple. On Sunday, Harbaugh led the Giants to their first win in Philadelphia since 2013.
The upcoming Jaguars-Giants game could be coined the "Tom Coughlin Bowl." Coughlin, the first coach in Jaguars history, guided Jacksonville to AFC title game appearances in 1996 (the franchise's second year of existence) and 1999. As the Giants' coach, Coughlin led New York to a pair of upset wins over the Patriots in the Super Bowl .

title: Seahawks plan to start Drew Lock in Week 10 despite oblique injury, Sam Darnold to miss another game
summary: Lock will make his third start of the season as the Seattle quarterback group battles multiple injuries
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks might have avoided a worst-case scenario in their quarterback group. Although Sam Darnold remains sidelined with a quad injury and broken rib, Drew Lock has a good chance to recover enough from his oblique injury to play against the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 10.
Coach Mike Macdonald said on his weekly radio show on Monday that Darnold will miss another week but that the team will enter their matchup with the Raiders with a "similar plan" to last week. That is, Lock will operate as the starter with Jalen Milroe backing him up. Macdonald said that Lock had a "good exam" on his oblique and that it is "something that we can manage" as he gears up to make his third start of the season.
Lock briefly entered the sideline medical tent during the Seahawks' win over the Arizona Cardinals with an oblique issue that initially made his Week 10 status uncertain. He also dealt with elbow tendinitis in the lead-up to his start against the Cardinals. Although he was effective, completing 19 of 28 passes for 175 yards and a touchdown, Lock was visibly short of 100% health. The Seahawks had only a modest day offensively against a Cardinals defense that entered Week 9 allowing the fifth-worst defensive EPA/play in the league, according to NFL Next Gen Stats.
"I was pressing to do everything I possibly could all the time, and [the fans] were able to pull me back a little bit," Lock said after the game . "Jalen did a fantastic job throughout the week in practice filling in for me. It was a collective effort from everybody to get to Sunday, and shoot, here we are 17-3. Go Hawks."
Holding Darnold out for another game essentially gives him a free week to recover, because the Seahawks will hit their bye after the matchup with the Raiders. That sets him up to return for a critical NFC West showdown on the road against the San Francisco 49ers on Nov. 29. So long as Seattle can get there without any setbacks, it will be a massive opportunity for the reigning champions to draw within striking distance of the division lead.
Lock is 2-0 in his two starts this season, both of which came against the Cardinals. He operated the offense tremendously in Week 2 when the Seahawks put up 31 points on their division rivals and has done everything Seattle could ask of him. This is still Darnold's offense, though, and he figures to rejoin the lineup on the other side of the bye week as the locked-in starter.
In the event that Lock's oblique or elbow prevents him from playing, Milroe will be waiting for the opportunity to make his first appearance of the season. The former third-round draft pick has not thrown a pass in his career but handled three carries for four yards in three games as a rookie in 2025. Seattle also has Adrian Martinez on its practice squad.

title: Cam Skattebo injury update: Giants RB 'full go' for Thursday night vs. Commanders
summary: Cam Skattebo is set to return from a hamstring injury as the NFC East-leading Giants prepare for a rematch with the Commanders
full_text:
Giants coach John Harbaugh said Monday that running back Cam Skattebo will be "full go" for New York's "Thursday Night Football" game against the Commanders to open Week 10.
Skattebo missed the Giants' 19-11 win over the Eagles in Week 9 due to a hamstring injury he suffered in Week 7 against the Texans . Harbaugh said the second-year back was "very close" to playing, but with a short week ahead, the team opted to play it safe.
With Skattebo out and Tyrone Tracy Jr . (hamstring) on IR, the Giants struggled to get much going on the ground in Philadelphia. Devin Singletary shouldered a heavy workload with 21 carries but turned that into just 31 yards (1.5 yards per carry). Still, New York managed to grind out a win to get to 5-2-1 without its top back.
Skattebo's return should provide some significant juice to an offense that needs it. Furthermore, it sounds like New York will have its current top quarterback-running back battery available, with Harbaugh saying he expects J.J. McCarthy (hip pointer) to play . McCarthy briefly left Sunday's game against the Eagles after taking a hit to the ribs, and Jameis Winston led the team's lone touchdown drive.
Skattebo leads the Giants in carries (98) and rushing yards (418), both by a wide margin, but it hasn't necessarily been the easiest year for the bowling-ball former Arizona State star. After a solid start to the year, Skattebo had a crucial fumble in Week 5 against the Commanders, a game that ended in a tie. He was a complete non-factor the next week, receiving zero touches on minimal snaps. He responded from that, though, with a 124-yard, one-touchdown day in an impressive win over Houston to right the ship. Now, he'll be in line for another busy day as the Giants look to extend their NFC East lead.

title: Falcons cut Nick Folk, add Jake Moody as new kicker
summary: After Nick Folk missed for the first time since 2017 inside 40 yards, dropping his season field goal percentage to 72.2%, it seemed very likely the Falcons would move on.
