title: Week 10 NFL Power Rankings: Midseason Report Cards
summary: The halfway point of the season has concluded, which means it’s time to take a look at each team’s first half and see if they have lived up to expectations. As always, when grading teams, it’s best to do it on a curve. Expectations provide needed context, which helps shape our mid-season grades. Please note […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - NOVEMBER 09: Josh Allen #17 of the Buffalo Bills walks the field with teammates prior to the game against the Minnesota Vikings at U.S. Bank Stadium on November 09, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Stephen Maturen/Getty Images) | Getty Images The halfway point of the season has concluded, which means it’s time to take a look at each team’s first half and see if they have lived up to expectations. As always, when grading teams, it’s best to do it on a curve. Expectations provide needed context, which helps shape our mid-season grades. Please note that these grades reflect no moves made on Tuesday before the deadline. With that in mind, let’s dive into our WCG Week 10 NFL Power Rankings! 1. San Francisco 49ers (7-1) Mid-season Report Card Grade: A+ Injuries have continued to be an issue, but the 49ers have somehow persevered. So far, San Francisco has consistently been the best team in the league, and with better health, they’ll be very hard to beat down the stretch. Overall, it’s hard to ask for much more than what we’ve seen from them so far this season, but don’t sleep on the other two teams in this division to make things interesting over the final two months of the season. 2. Buffalo Bills (7-1) Mid-season Report Card Grade: A If you were asleep all offseason and didn’t know the Bills made a change at head coach, you’d probably think this was just business as usual for Buffalo. In many ways, it has been, but it’s been pretty impressive to see them pick up as nothing changed with the coaching staff. Quarterback Josh Allen is awesome, but the defense will once again define how their season ends. Right now, it hasn’t been good enough, but they’ve kept winning anyway. Will a deadline move (or two) get that unit heading in the right direction? We shall see. 3. Jacksonville Jaguars (6-2) Mid-season Report Card Grade: A What’s not to like about the Jaguars right now? They have three wins by 23 points or more, Trevor Lawrence is playing like a top-tier quarterback, and the defense continues to dominate, especially in the run game. This is an extremely well-rounded team that shouldn’t be discounted because of the division they are in. This is a Super Bowl contender with a very good roster and coaching staff. 4. Chicago Bears (7-2) Mid-season Report Card Grade: A Coming into Sunday night, the Bears were off to their best start since 2012. All of that while missing quarterback Caleb Williams for three games and figuring out the defense along the way. The addition of Jeffery Simmons is huge, but it’ll come down to whether they can start winning divisional games. They should be a Super Bowl favorite, but if they have one weakness, that is it. We’ll see how things go coming out of the bye, because starting Thanksgiving, the road to finishing the regular season is a gauntlet. 5. Detroit Lions (6-2) Mid-season Report Card Grade: A The Lions are playing their best football in two seasons, and knock on wood, their defense is finally improving. Losing All-Pro linebacker Jack Campbell was scary and a big blow to this team, but getting back both high-level safeties should help. The offense will ultimately dictate how far this group can go, but they are well-coached and have plenty of talent. Don’t sleep on the Lions over the second half of the season. 6. Cincinnati Bengals (6-2) Mid-season Report Card Grade: A The Bengals have been hard to figure out so far this year, mainly because of their slow starts. The talent is there, and the defense is better, but can they improve enough to chase down the Steelers for the AFC North title? A lot will come down to how much the defense improves over the last two months of the season. It’s all in front of them, and with the Ravens fading fast, the road gets a little easier. 7. Green Bay Packers (6-3) Mid-season Report Card Grade: A- This season started as a disaster for Green Bay, but they’ve found a way to push through adversity and come out looking like a much better team on the other side. Quarterback Jordan Love is playing at a high level, and the defense has rounded into form, despite missing star pass rusher Micah Parsons. Existing in the NFC North is tough, and like the other three teams, there’s going to be little margin for error down the stretch. The good news is, the Packers have plenty of experience pushing through to the postseason. 8. Denver Broncos (7-2) Mid-season Report Card Grade: B+ Despite a slow start, mostly due to the offense, this is still a very good team that might have its best football ahead of it. The biggest issue has been Bo Nix’s play. Without a step up, it’s hard to imagine they’ll be able to win the AFC. That said, with a step in the right direction, they are as dangerous as any team in the conference. Finding another playmaker on the offensive side of the ball should be a priority, so we’ll see how it all plays out. 9. Kansas City Chiefs (6-2) Mid-season Report Card Grade: A Their 5-0 start felt like a dream, but reality has hit over the last few weeks. The good news is that this is clearly a good team. The question remains whether or not they can ultimately win the division. This team desperately needs at least another pass catcher, but if they get into the playoffs, which they should, they’ll be dangerous with the high-level experience of winning the big game. 10. Pittsburgh Steelers (6-2) Mid-season Report Card Grade: A Color me surprised that the Steelers have somehow been better under Mike McCarthy than they were in Mike Tomlin’s final seasons. In many ways, their defense has carried the momentum. Still, credit goes to this offense, and especially 43-year-old quarterback Aaron Rodgers, for continuing to play at a high enough level. I’m still not sold that they can maintain this all season, but the last month they have looked like a very good team. We’ll see if it lasts. 11. Minnesota Vikings (6-2) Mid-season Report Card Grade: B+ The defense is playing at a 1985 Chicago Bears level, but the offense is bottom three in most key statistical categories. Maybe a change at quarterback (although head coach Kevin O’Connell hasn’t made it permanent) will make the difference, but the schedule ahead will be the ultimate test to show how good this team is as a whole. Adding a high-level running back will help, but without better quarterback play, their ceiling is limited. 12. Los Angeles Rams (5-4) Mid-season Report Card Grade: D+ In many ways, it’s been a disastrous start to the season for the Rams, yet they come out of Week 9 above .500. Getting back Myles Garrett will be big, but the injuries they’ve suffered on the defensive side of the ball can’t be ignored. If all goes well, the Rams and Seahawks will be fighting for a playoff spot, but this team has a long way to go to find enough consistency to live up to being heavy Super Bowl favorites. If they make the playoffs, it will likely be from a Wild Card spot, which is a tough ask for any team. 13. Seattle Seahawks (5-4) Mid-season Report Card Grade: D Are the Seahawks a good team? I believe they are. They have too much talent and too much already established for them to fall off completely. That said, they are in a tough division and conference, and so far this year, it’s shown. The defense is still elite, but without better quarterback play, they are severely capped. All in all, it’s been a disappointing start, but I expect to see them in the playoffs come January. 14. New York Giants (5-2-1) Mid-season Report Card Grade: A+ Count me as one of the people who didn’t quite believe that John Harbaugh’s presence would automatically make the Giants a good team. I was wrong, and I’m totally OK admitting that. Not only are they leading the NFC East, but they’ve done it starting three quarterbacks. Once Jaxson Dart was lost, it would have been easy to write them off, yet they’ve kept their pace and have played solid football along the way. The Giants aren’t likely to be a big threat in the playoffs, but count this as a…

title: Bears vs. Bucs Game Balls: Some How, Some Way
summary: The Chicago Bears walked away from Sunday Night Football this week with their seventh win of the season (and first on Sunday night since 2018). And yet, many fans went to bed on Sunday evening with some uneasiness about their favorite football team. Caleb Williams, after a masterful start in the first quarter, ended up […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - NOVEMBER 08: Luther Burden III #10 of the Chicago Bears carries the ball past Tykee Smith #23 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and scores a touchdown during the first quarter at Soldier Field on November 08, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Geoff Stellfox/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Chicago Bears walked away from Sunday Night Football this week with their seventh win of the season (and first on Sunday night since 2018). And yet, many fans went to bed on Sunday evening with some uneasiness about their favorite football team. Caleb Williams, after a masterful start in the first quarter, ended up having his worst game as a pro. Rome Odunze once again had a case of the drops. And the Bears suffered more injuries that left some big question marks moving forward. Bears fans are in a very different place as a fan base than they were a couple of years ago when most would have done just about anything for a win on prime time, no matter how it came about. These days, if a win isn’t dominant enough, some sections of the fan base are calling for heads. That is to say, expectations have risen. But even though some (many) things were undoubtedly sloppy in this week’s game against the Bucs, the Bears never trailed and Williams delivered a game winning drive in crunch time when the team demanded it most. Let’s just hope this is an experience that results in growth down the stretch. Let’s get to the game balls. Offense Game Ball: WR Luther Burden III Burden suffered a concussion near the end of regulation when he took a helmet-to-helmet hit from Rueben Bain Jr. along the sideline. The hit caused Burden to drop the ball, resulting in a turnover that led to the Bucs tying the game with a touchdown and successful two-point conversion. While the result of the play was costly, I’m not sure there’s a player in the league that could have taken that hit and not dropped the ball. And there’s certainly an argument to be made that the hit should have resulted in a flag, whether the helmet-to-helmet hit was intentional or not. But I digress. Prior to this play, Burden was once again the Bears’ number one and most reliable receiver throughout the game. He had seven catches for 97 yards and one touchdown. Burden’s 56-yard touchdown was the Bears’ second of the night and a beautiful sight, including a couple of broken tackles. At this point, it appeared the Bears were going to run the Bucs out of the stadium. Caleb Williams to Luther Burden III for a 56-yard touchdown 🙌 TBvsCHI on NBC/Peacock Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/zXsKY9tZ2H — NFL (@NFL) November 9, 2026 Even though the Bucs would end up coming back, and credit to their defense for forcing several turnovers, Burden was the steady hand throughout most of the night on the offensive side of the ball. Defense Game Ball: LB Devin Bush Much has been written about Jeffery Simmons serving as a “multiplier” for a defense, and Bush has been one of the largest benefactors of said multiplication here in Chicago. With Simmons drawing double teams and attention up front, there is less of an opportunity for blockers to get to the second level and get their hands on Bears linebackers. This has led to Bush being able to utilize his top notch speed and become a real weapon on defense. That was certainly the case on Sunday night. Bush ended the night with 9 tackles, one tackle for loss, and two passes defended. Devin Bush hit pic.twitter.com/wXZgsXveya — ✶Ⓜ️𝕒𝕣𝕔𝕦𝕤 ▶️✶ (@_MarcusD3_) November 9, 2026 Devin Bush's speed on this TFL 😮‍💨 TBvsCHI on NBC/Peacock Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/MY7ucqU8U0 — NFL (@NFL) November 9, 2026 The pick is no problem because Devin Bush just blew up this 4th down attempt from Bucs. Bears are back in business already in great field position. pic.twitter.com/iW2OHo9vGl — Ross Pins (@chisportsross) November 9, 2026 Honorable mentions on defense: DT Jeffery Simmons, DE Austin Booker, CB Jaylon Johnson, and CB Cam Lewis. This one really was a close call this week. Booker would have likely been my next choice. Who would have received your game balls? Let us know in the comments section below.

title: Complementary football allows the Chicago Bears to get to 7-2 at the bye
summary: If the Chicago Bears have a defense that can keep them in games when the offense gives the ball away five times, then this team truly deserves to be in the Super Bowl conversation. The addition of Jeffery Simmons has changed the look of the defense, and it’s changed what defensive coordinator Dennis Allen can […]
full_text: Nov 8, 2026; Chicago, Illinois, USA; Chicago Bears defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons (99) sacks Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield (6) in the second half at Soldier Field. Mandatory Credit: Matt Marton-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect If the Chicago Bears have a defense that can keep them in games when the offense gives the ball away five times, then this team truly deserves to be in the Super Bowl conversation. The addition of Jeffery Simmons has changed the look of the defense, and it’s changed what defensive coordinator Dennis Allen can do. The bye is coming at a perfect time for Allen and his coaches to self-scout and rework how they want to attack offenses now that they have a game-wrecker on the defensive line. Ben Johnson and the offense could use a recalibration as well after Caleb Williams’ worst game of the season with four interceptions, and a run-pass ratio of 17 called run plays (not counting the two kneel-downs) to 41 pass plays. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers’ fantastic defense had a lot to do with the latter, but you know the Bears will dive into their run game and make some tweaks for the second half of the season. But even with the offense having a stinker on Sunday night, it’s still a top-10 unit, and with the defense coming along and leading the NFL on third downs, the Bears are closer to becoming a complete team. The third phase came up big with the game-winning field goal, but overall, it’s been inconsistent this season. The bye will allow special teams coordinator Richard Hightower to get in some self-scouting as well. All in all, the 7-2 Bears are in a great position to continue the playoff push through the season. title: The Bears needed an ugly win like this. Now, never do it again.
summary: Sometimes, it’s good to win ugly. After all, what do you learn from steamrolling everyone and making things look easy all the time? That’s the silver lining I’m trying to take from the Chicago Bears’ messy 27-24 walk-off win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday Night Football.  I, like many, scoffed at the idea […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - NOVEMBER 08: Rome Odunze #15 of the Chicago Bears reacts after a first down reception against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers during the second quarter at Soldier Field on November 08, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by John Fisher/Getty Images) | Getty Images Sometimes, it’s good to win ugly. After all, what do you learn from steamrolling everyone and making things look easy all the time? That’s the silver lining I’m trying to take from the Chicago Bears’ messy 27-24 walk-off win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday Night Football. I, like many, scoffed at the idea that the then-3-5 Bucs would “humble” the Bears the way several analysts had suggested Tampa would. And for the first quarter or so of action, it looked like we’d be right. Unfortunately, we weren’t. It was terrible football from there on out. Five turnovers (four interceptions, varying in their degrees of bad, and an unfortunate fumble by Luther Burden III while he was concussed). The Bucs willed their way back into the game and eventually tied it up. The 2025 Bears played and won some rough games, but nothing quite that bad. But a win is a win, especially on a short week, and sometimes complementary football requires you to pick up your guys when they’re struggling. The offense did it in Week 1 as the defense couldn’t stop a nosebleed, scoring 59 points. This time, it was the defense’s turn to work their magic. We even got a Jaylon Johnson pick-six, for crying out loud! And in the end, the offense did just enough—thanks to some busted coverages by the Bucs—to seal the deal with Cairo Santos’ 38-yard field goal. The most important thing: the Bears will go into their bye week at a strong 7-2, with their opportunity to seize the division lead still intact when they return. Get healthy. Learn from the failures of this game. Get back on the horse in Week 11 against the New Orleans Saints. Also…let’s not do this again. In the same way as the Bears didn’t need to continually prove their mettle in the clutch the way they did last year, they certainly don’t need to demonstrate they can give the ball away five times and still win every week. That’s not going to cut it. Get that out of your system, and get back to being locked in and executing at a high level. The 3-5 Saints might not look like much, but they fight. People are already suggesting the Bucs gave the league the blueprint for how to deal with Chicago’s offense, that this won’t be the last time we see Williams and Ben Johnson struggle like this. For their sake, the Bears need to make sure it is. Because there’s a reason the 2006 Bears are the only other team in NFL history to win a game that brutal: it simply isn’t a winning formula. The good news is that, as easy as it would’ve been for them to lose, they made the choice not to mail it in. And that counts for something. Specifically, it’s another positive number in the win column.
author: Khari Thompson

title: 10 Bears Takes: An Unlikely Win and Some Trade Deadline Thoughts
summary: It’s been yet another impressive week for the NFC North as they continue to prove that they are the best division in football. For the first time in NFL history, there’s a 6-3 team in last place heading into Week 10. If the season ended today, all four teams in the division would be in […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - NOVEMBER 8: Jeffery Simmons #99 of the Chicago Bears in action during the second quarter against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Soldier Field on November 8, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s been yet another impressive week for the NFC North as they continue to prove that they are the best division in football. For the first time in NFL history, there’s a 6-3 team in last place heading into Week 10. If the season ended today, all four teams in the division would be in the playoffs, but with a Vikings loss on Monday Night Football, the Bears will be in sole possession of first place heading into their Week 10 bye. Sunday night’s game was quite the rollercoaster that featured a dominant start, followed by three quarters of flirting with disaster. Despite blowing a 14-point lead, the Bears’ offense was able to march down the field in the final three minutes of the game to set up Cairo Santos’ game-winning field goal to give Chicago a 27-24 victory. More importantly, despite five turnovers, the Bears moved to 7-2 and put themselves in a great position over the final eight games of the season once they return from the bye week. We’ll cover that, some trade deadline thoughts, and much more in a loaded Week 9 installment of 10 Bears Takes. 1. After an unbelievably impressive first quarter, quarterback Caleb Williams set a career-high for interceptions in an NFL game with three in the second quarter alone. The first two-and-a-half drives started like a dream for head coach Ben Johnson and the Bears offense. They marched down the field on back-to-back drives with impressive passing touchdowns from Williams. On the third drive, Williams once again made unbelievable throws, and the NFL world was in awe. Then came a 15-yard personal foul on Zavion Thomas that set the offense back to the 21 on a second-and-goal. On the next play, Williams fired one into double coverage for his second interception of the year. It was clear he was feeling himself, but he got caught trying to do too much, forcing a ball into the end zone for Rome Odunze. A few plays earlier, he hit Odunze in the chest for what should have been an easy walk-in touchdown. In a few plays, what should have been a 21-3 lead remained 14-3. Following a failed fourth-down attempt from Baker Mayfield and the Buccaneers, Chicago had the ball back at the 35-yard line with a chance to build an 18-point lead. Instead, Williams threw off his back foot, couldn’t get the ball out of bounds, and threw back-to-back interceptions on consecutive passes. A few drives later, following a big Cam Lewis interception, Williams threw his third interception of the night off his back foot, once again. Simply put, Sunday night’s second-quarter performance was as uncharacteristic as we’ve seen from Williams throughout his two and a half years in the league. Every quarterback in the league has bad games, but the way it happened felt unbelievable. A few observations: On his second interception, he had D’Andre Swift wide open in the flat as a checkdown option, which would have resulted in a first down, if not more. Despite the interceptions, Johnson did not shy away from calling a pass-heavy attack in the first half. Two of Williams’ three interceptions came off back-foot throws. With the bye week ahead, fans can rest assured knowing that Williams will obsess over his disastrous second-quarter decision-making. As we’ve learned with this offense, things only become a concern when they repeat themselves. Considering his history, this feels like a one-off that we might not see again for multiple seasons. Regardless, those mistakes let the Buccaneers stay in the game going into the half, which I’m sure will be a big talking point as they start prepping for New Orleans after the bye week. 2. In many ways, Sunday night’s game was a complete disaster. Not very often do teams win games when they turn the ball over five times and lose the turnover margin by three. Yet, they found a way to do it when everything was failing them. Following the first quarter, it felt like everything was going wrong for the Bears. Williams threw three interceptions in the second quarter, the Buccaneers scored right before the half, and the offense went completely silent for most of the second half. Most teams would have completely fallen apart, and to a certain extent, the Bears did. This was a very uncharacteristic game for this team under Ben Johnson, and there’s just no real other way to put it. The offense failed to score 30-plus for the first time since Williams’ return, and for the first time in the same time frame, they relinquished a lead. The good news is they still haven’t trailed in those four games, but that was a game where most of this team is probably going to want to flush it and move on. Sometimes these games just happen, and even when everything was going wrong, somehow, some way, the Bears held onto the lead for all but about three minutes. A big reason why the game stayed so close was their five turnovers, but while they lost the turnover margin by three, they allowed just 10 points off those five turnovers, which is pretty remarkable. Ultimately, Chicago is a well-coached team, and the Buccaneers, despite a slow start, were on a bit of a roll and had a chance to take over first place in the NFC South. This was a motivated team with plenty to play for, and even if they don’t have that one game-breaker at receiver, there’s still plenty of talent on both sides of the ball. In fact, heading into Sunday night, Tampa Bay’s defense was leading Seattle’s in many statistical categories. While you never want to see an offense go completely dark and turn it over that many times, when it counted most, Williams found 38 yards to get them into field goal range and eventually win the game. There will be plenty to take away and clean up from this game, but the bye week is coming at the right time. More importantly, their 7-2 start could be good enough to get them into first place by the end of Monday night. For now, we’ll turn our attention to the trade deadline on Tuesday, but as long as this one bad game stays just one bad game, the Bears are right on schedule as Super Bowl contenders. 3. Even with the late touchdown they gave up, the defense played a helluva game and was the reason they found a way to get to 7-2. The impact that Jeffery Simmons has had on this defense cannot be overstated. Despite a sackless first half, they came away with four in the second half, plus a pick-six from the much-maligned Jaylon Johnson. For the most part, they did a good job of bottling up the league’s most dangerous rushing attack. Before Tampa Bay’s final drive of the night, when they scored the game-tying touchdown, Irving had 80 yards and averaged 4.44 yards per carry. While that’s not great for the defense, it was much more manageable than most defenses have been against him this season. In the passing game, they had just one big coverage bust: Kyler Gordon was burned down the field by Tez Johnson for 58 yards. Outside of that, quarterback Baker Mayfield was uncomfortable in the pocket and didn’t consistently hit receivers past 10 yards. On the night, Mayfield finished with 243 passing yards, but had no touchdowns and two interceptions. The defense also defended five passes, despite being on the field for almost six more minutes than the offense. Simply put, without the defensive effort they received, the Bears don’t win on Sunday night. The box score might show 24 points and 352 yards, but they allowed just 10 points off those five turnovers and had four sacks and an additional tackle for loss on the night. This group will be a work in progress until they can get healthier. Honestly, they probably need at least another addition on that side of the ball, but all things considered, they are playing at a much higher level than anyone had expected coming into the season. With any luck, they’ll get…
author: Aaron Leming

title: Bears vs. Buccaneers: Inside the Snap Counts, Stats, and a Familiar Win
summary: If you’re a long-time fan of the Chicago Bears, then this 27 to 24 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers must have felt familiar. The offense kept shooting itself in the foot, so the defense had to bail them out, and then the special teams won it in the end. The Bears looked unstoppable early, […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - NOVEMBER 8: Jeffery Simmons #99 reacts after Jaylon Johnson #1 of the Chicago Bears runs the ball into the endzone for a touchdown after an interception during the third quarter against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Soldier Field on November 8, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images If you’re a long-time fan of the Chicago Bears, then this 27 to 24 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers must have felt familiar. The offense kept shooting itself in the foot, so the defense had to bail them out, and then the special teams won it in the end. The Bears looked unstoppable early, but after jumping out to a 14-point lead, everything that could go wrong did go wrong. But this team found a way to win, and if it felt like “the Bears are who we thought they were” type of game, you’d be right. The Bears became just the second team in NFL history to win a primetime game despite throwing at least four interceptions and rushing for fewer than 75 yards. The first team to do it was the 2006 Chicago Bears against the Cardinals in the “the Bears are who we thought they were” game. Last night the Bucs had more total yards (352 to 349), more first downs (18 to 15), ran more plays (64 to 60), and had the time-of-possession edge (32:52 to 27:08). They also had fewer penalties, with 8 for 45 yards to 9 for 74 for Chicago. The Bears did get the better of the Bucs on third downs as Tampa Bay was just 2-12 (16.7%) to Chicago’s 7-13 (53.8%). Tampa Bay’s record may not look it, but that’s a good football team that just happened to run into a better one on Sunday night. This nugget from CBS Sports’ Doug Clawson shows just how good the Bucs have been playing. “The Bucs are the 1st team with 1,000+ rush yards and 17+ takeaways in a 5-game span since the 1985 Bears.” And this nugget from OptaSTATS shows how much the Bears had to overcome to get the victory, as they are the only team in NFL history to have 5+ turnovers, 9+ penalties, have no 10+ yard rushes, blow a 14+ point lead, and yet still win the game. Let’s look at the Bears’ playing-time breakdown and a few individual stats from the game. OFFENSE This was one of the worst games of Caleb Williams’ career, and the first time he ever threw four interceptions in a game. After the game, he immediately recalled that he threw three picks once in high school and threw three in one game in college. Considering he’s one of the least-intercepted quarterbacks in league history, I’ll view this stinker as an anomaly. He’ll learn from it and come out after the bye focused, playing like the same Caleb we’ve gotten used to. Despite the poor performance, he did lead the offense down the field on a game-winning drive, which was his first this year after a league-leading 6 a season ago. DEFENSE Statistically, Jeffery Simmons had a “quieter” game than his debut, but he still filled the stat sheet, and his presence allowed his teammates to make plays. Simmons plays with a high motor (and he only missed 2 snaps), and that’s infectious to the entire unit. If Simmons can chase wide receiver Emeka Egbuka 20 yards downfield to make a tackle, then every other defender can play with that same kind of effort. Devin Bush had a season-high in tackles and passes defended. Grady Jarrett and Shemar Turner picked up their first sacks of the year. Turner’s was his first career sack. Montez Sweat had his most tackles in a game since he had 7 on October 26, 2025. Jeffery Simmons on seeing Caleb in “2-minute mode”: “I didn’t panic because Caleb is a baller.” Adds “once we put a complete game together, good luck.”😈 pic.twitter.com/H4iilULr9g — CHGO Bears (@CHGO_Bears) November 9, 2026 SPECIAL TEAMS* *The above image has players who only played in the third phase. Cairo Santos was 3 for 3 on extra points and made both field goals, including the 38-yard game-winner. Tory Taylor punted 4 times for a 40.3-yard average, and he had 1 blocked for a second straight game. Zavion Thomas had a 29.3-yard average of the 3 kickoffs that counted. Kalif Raymond had 6 punt returns for 48 yards and 1 fumble that he recovered. Roschon Johnson had 2 special teams tackles. To check out the complete Bears vs. Bucs box score, I find ESPN’s site is easy to navigate. All statistics and snap counts, as well as the accompanying pictures, are taken directly from the NFL’s Game Statistic and Information System.

title: Report: Bengals acquire edge rusher Arnold Ebiketie from Eagles for ‘27 6th-round pick
summary: Update: The Bengals have now called off this trade. ———————————————————————————————————————————— The Cincinnati Bengals have heard your pleas to be active before the trade deadline at 4 PM ET on Tuesday afternoon. According to NFL insider Ian Rapoport, the Bengals traded a 2027 sixth-round pick to the Philadelphia Eagles for edge rusher Arnold Ebiketie. Ebiketie was […]
full_text: Update : The Bengals have now called off this trade. ———————————————————————————————————————————— The Cincinnati Bengals have heard your pleas to be active before the trade deadline at 4 PM ET on Tuesday afternoon. According to NFL insider Ian Rapoport, the Bengals traded a 2027 sixth-round pick to the Philadelphia Eagles for edge rusher Arnold Ebiketie. Ebiketie was selected in the second round, No. 38 overall, by the Atlanta Falcons in the 2022 NFL Draft out of Penn State. He recorded his first sack in his very first professional game and worked his way into the Falcons’ starting lineup by halfway through his rookie year. After his rookie contract, he signed a one-year deal with the Eagles this past offseason. Now the Eagles are riddled with injuries, sit at 2-7, and are shedding contracts in exchange for draft picks. This is clearly a move the Bengals made in response to the injury that landed rookie edge rusher Cashius Howell on IR. It is also a clear signal the Bengals lack trust in their 2025 first-round pick, Shemar Stewart, who only played 10 snaps on Sunday in Spain. Ebiketie hasn’t made any sacks so far this season, but he has racked up 10 pressures, per PFF. He’ll be a rotational asset for the Bengals’ defensive line and will join Stewart and Cedric Johnson behind Boye Mafe and Myles Murphy. Stay tuned for new possible trade news as we near the deadline. Sources: The #Eagles aren't done, trading edge Arnold Ebiketie to the #Bengals in exchange for 2027 6th round pick. pic.twitter.com/8EYzDf6px6 — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) November 10, 2026

title: Bengals Tuesday Trenches: Super in Spain, SNF and more
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals won their fourth game in a row on Sunday morning in front of a national audience from Santiago Bernabéu Stadium in Madrid, Spain, by a score of 34-17. Now, at 6-2 along with Pittsburgh, the Bengals are set to host the Steelers for what kind of feels like the AFC North title […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals won their fourth game in a row on Sunday morning in front of a national audience from Santiago Bernabéu Stadium in Madrid, Spain, by a score of 34-17. Now, at 6-2 along with Pittsburgh, the Bengals are set to host the Steelers for what kind of feels like the AFC North title game even though we’re only in Week 10. The Bengals were almost perfect on offense. They scored on six of their eight drives (I’m not counting the last drive in which they could have scored but were able to kill the clock), and four of those scores were touchdowns. Joe Burrow completed 24/29 passes for 271 yards and three touchdowns — two to Tee Higgins and one deep bomb to Ja’Marr Chase to cap off their first drive of the game. The defense had its moments, but the familiar struggles were there too. In the end, the Falcons’ offense just couldn’t hope to keep up, even though they seemed to hang around a little, especially early in the second half. Still, it never felt like the Bengals were potentially going to lose control of the game. Here are some random thoughts on their three-score win before we get into the Steelers game: Tee Higgins is a monster. He didn’t have a ton of yards (32), but he caught two touchdown passes, and multiple passes—including one of those touchdowns—with guys draped all over him. Higgins looks like a man among boys when he catches the ball in traffic. Ja’Marr Chase is a generational talent. His ability to turn into a running back as soon as his hands touch the ball is remarkable. He breaks tackles like a running back and has 220 yards after the catch so far in 2026. What I’d really like to see, though, is a yards-after-contact stat for him. The offensive line held up beautifully against the Falcons, who came into Sunday morning’s game with 18 sacks and weren’t too far behind the Bengals. Burrow was sacked twice, but one of those sacks was much more of a coverage sack than anything to do with the line. If they can continue to protect Burrow like they did Sunday, the offense can break records. The run game finally made an appearance on Sunday. To be clear, I think Burrow can beat about any defense with Chase, Higgins, and the other weapons he has, but it’s hard to win in the playoffs if you can’t run the ball. The Bengals were able to kill the clock with a solid running game in the fourth quarter. Chase Brown had multiple explosive runs, including one for 19 yards—a season-long for the Bengals’ offense. Dexter Lawrence. That’s it. That’s all I have to say. Okay, a bit more: Lawrence didn’t show up on the stat sheet much, but he lived in the backfield and forced Michael Penix into throwing early or on the run. He almost caused an intentional grounding penalty at one point. It’s amazing how much one man can change the face of a defense. The Bengals were unable to sack the quarterback on Sunday. This was their first game without a sack, and hopefully it’s their last game. Cashius Howell is on IR, and the Bengals pretty much relied on Boye Mafe and Myles Murphy. Cedric Johnson only played 13 snaps, and Shemar Stewart played just 10. It would be nice to see a little more rotation to help keep the starters fresh. Regardless of DJ Turner’s PFF score, remember the receiver he’s covering doesn’t get targeted very often. Money Mac strikes again—good from 57 and 43 yards, and that 43-yard kick in the fourth quarter put any hope of a comeback out of reach for the Falcons. Speaking of the Falcons, we can credit the Bengals for breaking Atlanta—The Falcons traded Jessie Bates Monday morning. STEELERS WEEK I honestly don’t think it’s an exaggeration to say that Sunday night’s game against the Steelers at Paycor Stadium is one of the biggest games to be played there in the last several seasons . The Steelers are also 6-2, and with the injuries in Baltimore and the Browns doing Browns things, it’s not crazy to think the winner of this game likely wins the division. The Bengals are not the same team they were that lost to the Steelers in Week 3. The offense is awake and clicking. The defense has its moments, but could use some help. Tuesday (today) is the last day they can make an addition via trade, as the deadline is at 4 PM Eastern. I highly doubt the Bengals make a move, but I also highly doubt they’d trade a first-round pick for Lawrence. Can they pull off another trade just five months after the Lawrence trade? If there was a time to do it, it’s now. The Bengals are in prime position to make a run, and they obviously need a little help, especially on defense, to get things right. They could use depth at cornerback as well as linebacker. They could probably get by without any additions on offense, but adding Jonathan Taylor sure would be cool. The Bengals are favored by 3.5 points, which is a half point over home-field advantage, and a win would put them at 7-2 with a firm grasp on the division, and a handful of winnable games before they host the Chiefs in a little over a month. This is where we hoped the Bengals would be at this point in the season. Relative Song Lyrics: Well, I never been to Spain But I kinda like the music Say the ladies are insane there And they sure know how to use it They don’t abuse it Never gonna lose it I can’t refuse it
author: Jason Garrison

title: The Good, The Bad and The Ugly in Bengals’ 34-17 win over Falcons in Madrid
summary: ¡Olé! The Cincinnati Bengals took their show to Madrid on Sunday, and the stripes looked right at home at the Bernabéu. Cincinnati spotted the Atlanta Falcons a touchdown on the opening drive, then took over behind Joe Burrow and Ja’Marr Chase on the way to a 34-17 win. It’s the first victory in franchise history […]
full_text: ¡Olé! The Cincinnati Bengals took their show to Madrid on Sunday, and the stripes looked right at home at the Bernabéu. Cincinnati spotted the Atlanta Falcons a touchdown on the opening drive, then took over behind Joe Burrow and Ja’Marr Chase on the way to a 34-17 win. It’s the first victory in franchise history in a game played outside the United States. That’s four straight wins; the Bengals are 6-2, and Pittsburgh comes to Paycor for Sunday Night Football next week. Before we turn the page, let’s break this one down. The Good Joe Burrow, MVP candidate. Burrow went 24-of-29 for 271 yards, three touchdowns, no turnovers, and a 140.1 passer rating, then added a 1-yard sneak for a fourth score. He was nearly perfect in the first half, at 16-of-18 for 234 yards and two touchdowns. His 21 touchdown passes lead the NFL, and he has 16 total touchdowns over the last four games. After last week’s three interceptions, this was the clean, surgical Burrow we know. Ja’Marr Chase, “best in the world.” That’s how Zac Taylor described him after the game, and it’s hard to argue. Chase answered Atlanta’s opening score with a 47-yard touchdown on the Bengals’ first possession. He had eight catches for 142 yards in the first half alone, the most first-half receiving yards of his career, and finished with 10 catches for 155 yards. His seven receiving touchdowns lead the AFC. Tee Higgins in the red zone. Higgins only had five catches for 32 yards, but two of them were touchdowns, from 4 and 8 yards out. That’s six touchdown catches on the year, and four in the last two games. A run game that showed up. For the first time this season, the ground game gave defenses something to think about. Chase Brown ran nine times for 57 yards and added three catches for 18 more, and the Bengals ran for 123 yards at 5.1 yards a carry. One week doesn’t fix a season-long problem, but it’s a start. Evan McPherson’s leg. McPherson drilled a 57-yarder right before halftime to make it 24-10 and added a 43-yarder in the fourth. He has now made 23 straight field goals, the longest streak in franchise history and the longest active streak in the NFL. Taking care of the football. Zero turnovers, one week after four of them. Linebacker Barrett Carter also picked off Michael Penix Jr. in the fourth quarter for his first interception of the season. History, twice. It’s the Bengals’ fourth straight game with 30 or more points, tying a franchise record, and their first win ever outside the U.S. Taylor called the turnout of Bengals fans in Spain “unbelievable.” The Bad The run defense, again. Atlanta ran for 157 yards on just 24 carries, a 6.5-yard average, and Bijan Robinson punched in a 1-yard touchdown in the third quarter. For the second straight week, an opponent ran wherever it wanted. Pittsburgh will have watched the tape. No pass rush. The Bengals finished without a sack, and the box score credits them with zero quarterback hits. Penix was never forced into a rushed decision. Against better quarterbacks, a clean pocket all day gets you beat. Getting off the field on third down. Long third downs have been a problem all season, and this game was no exception. On a third-and-13, Robinson took a screen past a missed tackle and moved the chains. That’s a drive that should’ve ended. The slow defensive start. The offense finally started fast, but the defense gave up a touchdown on Atlanta’s opening drive. It’s the third straight week the Bengals trailed early. The Ugly The back end units of the defense. This one’s tough to watch from the back end of the defense’s perspective. It will be interesting to see if this is a position that the Bengals explore for possible trade depth. DJ Turner II was flagged twice for defensive pass interference covering Drake London, and both penalties set up Falcons touchdowns. He also missed the tackle that let Robinson convert that third-and-13 screen. Turner has had many good moments this year, but Sunday was one to forget. The whole back end, including safeties and linebackers in coverage, struggled to rally and tackle in space. Bijan Robinson, including on that third-and-13 screen, finished with six catches for 47 yards on top of his 100 rushing yards. The safeties and linebackers kept letting Atlanta off the hook on third-and-long, a problem that has followed this defense all season. Jordan Battle had an opportunity at an interception after jumping a route, and let a game-sealing interception through his hands (Barrett Carter later atoned for that mistake). To be fair, the raw passing numbers weren’t bad. Michael Penix Jr. threw for just 162 yards, Kyle Pitts was held to three catches for 23 yards, and Drake London had five for 68. The problem is timing. The flags, missed tackles, and third-down breakdowns came at the worst moments and kept Falcons drives alive. Against the Steelers on Sunday night, those mistakes will cost points. Free yards. An offside penalty turned an Atlanta punt into a field goal, and the defense let a late first-half Falcons drive stretch until just 57 seconds remained. Atlanta helped the Bengals out with 12 penalties for 88 yards of its own, plus a missed field goal. A sharper team won’t be so generous. The bottom line: when the offense scores 30-plus every week, the defense can survive days like this. Come January, it won’t be enough. Your turn What was your Good, Bad, and Ugly from Madrid? Is Burrow the MVP front-runner right now, and how worried are you about the run defense with the Steelers coming to town on Sunday night? Let me hear it in the comments.
author: Anthony Cosenza

title: Josh Johnson leaving Bengals practice squad to join Arizona Cardinals
summary: Cincinnati Bengals practice squad quarterback Josh Johnson is being signed to the Arizona Cardinals’ 53-man roster, according to ESPN’s Adam Schefter. This comes as the Cardinals’ quarterback room has been completely flipped upside down. They started with Jacoby Brissett, who was traded to the Baltimore Ravens. They then turned to Gardner Minshew, who unfortunately went […]
full_text: Cincinnati Bengals practice squad quarterback Josh Johnson is being signed to the Arizona Cardinals’ 53-man roster, according to ESPN’s Adam Schefter. This comes as the Cardinals’ quarterback room has been completely flipped upside down. They started with Jacoby Brissett, who was traded to the Baltimore Ravens. They then turned to Gardner Minshew, who unfortunately went down with a likely season-ending torn UCL. Now, they’ll sign Johnson, who started the year off with the Bengals, was eventually cut, and was then re-signed to the practice squad. With veteran QB Gardner Minshew sidelined due to a UCL injury, the Cardinals are signing QB Josh Johnson off the Bengals’ practice squad, per sources. The Cardinals will be Johnson’s 15th NFL team in 14 NFL seasons. pic.twitter.com/5ZIN2IpZRQ — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) November 10, 2026 Despite being 40 years old, Johnson performed actually rather well for the Bengals in the preseason. He actually made it a bit of a debate for some on whether or not to keep him as a third QB, though the Bengals opted to get him onto the practice squad along with Sean Clifford, the latter of whom is now essentially QB3 in Cincinnati. Johnson will now be the NFL’s second-oldest starting quarterback, behind the Steelers’ Aaron Rodgers, whom the Bengals will face this week on Sunday Night Football. Unfortunately for Johnson, he’s already lost his No. 1 target, Michael Wilson, who suffered a neck injury in Week 9 and will miss the rest of the season. With Wilson out, tight end Trey McBride will likely see even more targets, despite already being the team’s leading pass catcher.

title: Bengals Week 9 awards in Spain victory vs. Falcons
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals went to Spain and came home with their first-ever win outside the United States, a 34-17 handling of the Atlanta Falcons at the Bernabéu. It was their fourth straight win, it moved them to 6-2, and it put them in a tie with Pittsburgh atop the AFC North heading into next Sunday […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals went to Spain and came home with their first-ever win outside the United States, a 34-17 handling of the Atlanta Falcons at the Bernabéu. It was their fourth straight win, it moved them to 6-2, and it put them in a tie with Pittsburgh atop the AFC North heading into next Sunday night’s showdown at Paycor. Before we get to the Steelers, let’s hand out some hardware. Here are my nominees for Offensive MVP, Defensive MVP, and Unsung Hero. Then you tell me who takes home the trophy in the comments section. Offensive MVP Nominees Joe Burrow, QB. Burrow went 24-of-29 for 271 yards, three touchdowns, and no turnovers, good for a 140.1 passer rating. He also scored on a 1-yard sneak, giving him four total touchdowns. He was nearly flawless in the first half, going 16-of-18 for 234 yards and two scores, as the Bengals built a 24-10 halftime lead. His 21 touchdown passes lead the NFL, and he has 16 total touchdowns over the last four games. One week after throwing three interceptions against Tennessee, he played a clean, efficient game. If the MVP race were decided today, he’d have a strong case. Ja’Marr Chase, WR. Atlanta scored on its opening drive, and Chase answered on the Bengals’ first possession by hauling in a 47-yard touchdown from Burrow to tie it at 7. He was already at eight catches for 142 yards by halftime, the most receiving yards he has ever had in a first half. He finished with 10 catches for 155 yards on 11 targets, and his seven receiving touchdowns lead the AFC. Zac Taylor said it best after the game: “That’s just Ja’Marr Chase. Best in the world.” Tee Higgins, WR. Five catches for 32 yards won’t jump off the page, but Higgins was the finisher. He caught touchdowns from 4 and 8 yards out, giving him four touchdown catches in the last two games and six on the season. When the Bengals got into the red zone, Burrow looked for No. 5. Defensive MVP Nominees Barrett Carter, LB. Carter tied for the team lead with 10 tackles and broke up a pass. Then, with the Bengals up two scores in the fourth quarter, he picked off Michael Penix Jr. at the Atlanta 43 and effectively ended any thought of a comeback. It was his second career interception and his first of 2026. It’s been an up-and-down year for the linebackers in coverage, so seeing Carter make the game-sealing play was a welcome sight. Bryan Cook, S. Cook also led the team with 10 tackles, five of them solo. On a day when Bijan Robinson and the Falcons’ run game kept getting to the second level, Cook was the guy cleaning things up. Without him, a few of those 10-yard gains would become 30-yard gains. Demetrius Knight Jr., LB. Knight added eight tackles, five solo, and was a steady presence in the middle of a defense that held Atlanta to seven points after the opening quarter. Josh Newton, CB. Newton had five tackles, and the biggest play he made doesn’t show up in the box score as anything more than a pass breakup. Atlanta dialed up a flea-flicker shot into the end zone, and Newton was right there to knock it away. In a game that was 24-17 in the third quarter, that’s a big swing. Unsung Hero Nominees Dohnte Meyers, WR/KR. Meyers was all over the box score. He had two catches for 47 yards, including a 42-yarder, a 16-yard run, and four kickoff returns for 100 yards. That’s 163 all-purpose yards from a guy most fans weren’t talking about before Sunday. When the Bengals needed a spark outside of Chase and Higgins, Meyers gave them one. Evan McPherson, K. McPherson drilled a 57-yarder just before halftime to make it 24-10, then added a 43-yarder in the fourth. He’s now made 23 straight field goals, the longest streak in franchise history and the longest active streak in the NFL. We don’t talk enough about how automatic he’s been. Samaje Perine, RB. Perine handled the dirty work with 11 carries for 43 yards. He also closed the game out the smart way: after picking up a late first down, he slid down instead of chasing extra yards, so the Bengals could run out the clock. That’s veteran football. The offensive line, led by Dalton Risner. Risner made his 100th career regular-season start, and the line paved the way for 123 rushing yards at 5.1 yards a carry. It also allowed just two sacks. After weeks of a stuck run game, the line finally won some battles up front. Your Pick Those are my nominees. Who gets your Offensive MVP: Burrow or Chase? Is Carter’s game-sealing pick enough for Defensive MVP? And who’s your Unsung Hero from Madrid? Make your case in the comments!
author: Anthony Cosenza

title: 3 things we learned from the Bengals’ fun game against the Falcons
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals are cruising right now, thanks in large part to an offense that is just too much for defenses to handle for four quarters. Here are three things we learned from Cincinnati’s 34-17 win over the Atlanta Falcons in Madrid. This is the best offense in the NFL It’s settled. The Bengals are […]
full_text: CINCINNATI, OHIO - OCTOBER 15: Ja'Marr Chase #1 of the Cincinnati Bengals runs with the ball while being chased by Devon Witherspoon #21 of the Seattle Seahawks in the first quarter at Paycor Stadium on October 15, 2023 in Cincinnati, Ohio. (Photo by Dylan Buell/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cincinnati Bengals are cruising right now, thanks in large part to an offense that is just too much for defenses to handle for four quarters. Here are three things we learned from Cincinnati’s 34-17 win over the Atlanta Falcons in Madrid. This is the best offense in the NFL It’s settled. The Bengals are better than the Buffalo Bills, the Dallas Cowboys, the Green Bay Packers or any other high-flying offense, simply because their three elite players outmatch every single defense in the league. Cincinnati is now averaging 30 points per game and has 30 points or more in four straight games. Against the Falcons, they didn’t turn it over, and Joe Burrow didn’t get sacked. Oh, and he threw for another three touchdowns and ran for one. He now leads the league in passing touchdowns and passing yards per game. The best part is that, while the Bengals tend to start slow, we’re now at the point in the season where Burrow, Chase Brown, and the offensive line all get hot, which means (barring injury) this train isn’t slowing down. Ja’Marr Chase is happy again Though a superstar, Chase is truly a team player. So he bit his tongue while the Bengals played around with the under center stuff that saw his numbers take a hit. But the Ravens game seemed to help the offense gain clarity about who they are. Now, after not getting 100 yards receiving his first six games, Chase has gone over 140 in back-to-back games. Cincinnati is back to being the Burrow-Chase-Higgins show, and Uno’s energy and body language show that he’s ready to regularly torch teams again. The defense need a drive or two to get going That’s the third straight game where the opponent surprised the Bengals by taking a lead (though not as big as the leads the Ravens or Titans took). And in all three games, the Bengals’ defense slowed down opposing offenses, especially their running backs, after those early bursts. On Sunday, it was Bijan Robinson who was held to just 58 yards on 16 carries following a huge opening drive, in which he had 42 yards on just three carries. It’s not perfect, but it does show you that the defense is capable of stepping up once Burrow and company put on their fireworks every game.

title: Browns recent losses: Which is more disappointing for fans?
summary: The Cleveland Browns suffered another loss this season, falling 23-22 to the New Orleans Saints in a tough overtime battle. This came after another tough loss, a 27-6 defeat by the Pittsburgh Steelers. While both games were setbacks in a season that was starting to look promising, which of the two losses was more disappointing for the Browns? One of the major differences between the two matchups was that Deshaun Watson started […]
full_text: The Cleveland Browns suffered another loss this season, falling 23-22 to the New Orleans Saints in a tough overtime battle. This came after another tough loss, a 27-6 defeat by the Pittsburgh Steelers . While both games were setbacks in a season that was starting to look promising, which of the two losses was more disappointing for the Browns? One of the major differences between the two matchups was that Deshaun Watson started against the Steelers and Shedeur Sanders stepped in against the Saints. Neither quarterback performed at a high level, but Sanders was able to create more offense in the New Orleans game. In some ways, the loss to Pittsburgh was more disappointing because it was a divisional matchup in which the Browns were completely outplayed. Expectations were lower for the game against the Saints since the team did not have their starting quarterback. At the same time, losing in overtime is especially disappointing when the Browns had several opportunities to secure the win. Sanders showed flashes of strong offensive play, making it disappointing that the Browns couldn’t capitalize on those opportunities against a lesser opponent. title: Browns punter Corey Bojorquez is quietly having a Pro Bowl year
summary: The Cleveland Browns are having a roller coaster of a season. They have beaten only one good team, the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 4, defeated four other clubs considered mediocre, and lost to two bad teams. And now they are faced with some difficult games on their schedule, namely playing their division foe, the Cincinnati […]
full_text: The Cleveland Browns are having a roller coaster of a season. They have beaten only one good team , the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 4, defeated four other clubs considered mediocre, and lost to two bad teams . And now they are faced with some difficult games on their schedule, namely playing their division foe, the Cincinnati Bengals, twice. RELATED: BOJORQUEZ INTERVIEW Consider the fact that there aren’t any really good teams left on their schedule. Could they still make the playoffs? A division title seems out of reach, but it takes 10 or 11 wins to get that #7 seed, and they are already halfway to that goal. There are several players on the Browns roster who are having a good year. Guys like TE Harold Fannin, LBs Carson Schwesinger and Quincy Williams, plus DT Mason Graham are getting their fair share of press regarding possibly getting some major Pro Bowl votes. But one player stands out, and nobody is talking about his season: Browns punter Corey Bojorquez. The Boot is back 🥾 We've re-signed P Corey Bojorquez! 📰 Read more: https://t.co/wQ4NPLBAHA pic.twitter.com/r7RsK8WdCa — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) March 12, 2026 Guys who make their living on special teams are usually only noticed when they miss a field goal, or both a punt, or skip a pass to the holder. Bojo has quietly been killing it as Cleveland’s punter this season. He was re-signed during last March’s free agency period. Currently, he is listed #5 in the league in net average per punt with 44.0 yards. The league leader is just 46.1, so Bojorquez is keeping the rankings tight. He is ranked #4 in average distance per kick at 50.4. Again, the leader’s number is close at 51.8, so one game could alter these numbers. Usually, the punters with the most kicks in a season are on teams whose offensive units can’t finish drives, or are unable to sustain drives. Bojo is ranked #3 in the most punts with 43. The league leader plays for the Philadelphia Eagles, which backs up this stat goes to guys who are on struggling offensive teams. He booted a season-high eight punts in the loss to the New York Jets when the offense could not move the ball. Bojo is considered a field flipper . This means his kicks can alter the opposing team’s field position just off one punt that has traveled 50+ yards. Case in point, in Week 3 against the Carolina Panthers, Bojorquez’s first punt was for 68 yards. Pretty good, eh? His first punt of the second half was 60 yards. Then his final kick was for a whopping 81 yards that went from Cleveland’s 19-yard line into the end zone. The NFL record for the longest punt is Steve O’Neal’s 98-yarder in 1969 while playing for the New York Jets: Take a look at Bojorquez’s 2026 season stats: Week 1 Punts: 3 Yards: 130 Yards per punt average: 43.3 Net yards per punt average: 45.0 Downed inside the 20: 1 Blocked: 0 Long: 48 yards Week 2 Punts: 4 Yards: 198 Yards per punt average: 49.5 Net yards per punt average: 45.0 Downed inside the 20: 2 Blocked: 0 Long: 57 yards Week 3 Punts: 5 Yards: 243 Yards per punt average: 48.6 Net yards per punt average: 45.8 Downed inside the 20: 3 Blocked: 0 Long: 62 yards Week 4 Punts: 4 Yards: 251 Yards per punt average: 62.8 Net yards per punt average: 50.3 Downed inside the 20: 1 Blocked: 0 Long: 81 yards Week 5 Punts: 8 Yards: 421 Yards per punt average: 52.6 Net yards per punt average: 41.8 Downed inside the 20: 1 Blocked: 0 Long: 67 yards Week 6 Punts: 7 Yards: 315 Yards per punt average: 48.0 Net yards per punt average: 36.7 Downed inside the 20: 1 Blocked: 0 Long: 62 yards Week 7 Punts: 3 Yards: 144 Yards per punt average: 48.0 Net yards per punt average: 45.0 Downed inside the 20: 1 Blocked: 0 Long: 59 yards Week 8 Punts: 4 Yards: 199 Yards per punt average: 49.8 Net yards per punt average: 49.8 Downed inside the 20: 3 Blocked: 0 Long: 58 yards Week 9 Punts: 5 Yards: 267 Yards per punt average: 53.4 Net yards per punt average: 39.8 Downed inside the 20: 1 Blocked: 0 Long: 59 yards When a running back breaks a play for 15 yards, those numbers are added to his game rushing stats. But with a punter, he could boot one for 56 yards, and then have it returned for 25 yards, which affects his net average; in this case, that stat would be 31.0 yards. Whereas a fair catch or a touchback gives the punter the exact distance of the kick. So, something the punter has zero control over can affect his overall stats. What is not considered is what kind of 56-yarder this is. Let’s say that this punt has a hangtime of 3.91 seconds and comes down in the center of the field. Even factoring in a long operation time, can one of the gunners get to the spot where the ball finally descends? Even if the gunner had nobody blocking him, there wouldn’t be a chance of this happening because that gunner would need to travel nearly 60 yards in just over 6 seconds. The punt is going to be returned. Another obstacle on a punt is if the returner doesn’t catch the ball and lets it hit the turf. We all know that because of the shape of a football, it can go almost anywhere. Including backwards. This could take off as much as 10 yards on a punt before it is downed. Yet another obstacle to getting larger numbers for punters is the pooch kick. This usually happens when the offense stalls out within 10 yards of the midfield stripe. A long field goal attempt is considered, but the coach decides it is out of the question. And the coach doesn’t want to go for it, whether that is because of field position or an unreasonable down-and-distance. So, the punter trots out. Now, there isn’t much advantage to boom the kick for a touchback, so the kicker wants the ball to land inside the 10-yard line, preferably. And if he accomplishes this, the kick itself may have been downed at the three-yard line, but the punt only traveled less than 40 yards. That is a huge plus for flipping field position for the team, but it hurts the punter’s average. The only positive stat is the “inside the 20” tabulation. But that is pretty vague in itself. There should be another stat that says “inside the 5” to distinguish punters who have the ability to make the ball travel higher so that it descends closer to the goal line. For the past eight games, Bojorquez has had at least one kick of 58 yards or longer. He routinely has contests where he has multiple punts in the 50+ range. That becomes a weapon. His talents were on full display in the loss to the New Orleans Saints . The Browns had to punt after their first possession. Bojo punted from Cleveland’s 26-yard line and was downed at the Saints’ 26. Their next possession was also a punt that went from the Browns’ 40-yard line to New Orleans’ 14-yard line. That’s flipping the field. ball back baby!!!!! #CLEvsNO on CBS pic.twitter.com/JJcPTOYU9p — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) November 8, 2026 Bojo’s only punt in Quarter 2 went to the 20-yard line, where Saints returner Barion Brown fumbled, and Cleveland safety Donovan McMillan recovered. But the kick had traveled 57 yards first. His fourth punt also went 57 yards, while his final punt in the fourth quarter traveled 59 yards from Cleveland’s 16-yard line to the Saints’ 25. This is Bojorquez’s ninth year in the league. In 202, he led the league in yards per punt average with 50.8 while with the Buffalo Bills, kicking about a third of his punts in freezing weather. In 2024, he led the league in number of punts (89) and total yardage (4,387). Last year, Bojo led the league in the same two categories, kicking 91 total punts and gaining 4,165 yards. In three different years, he had the longest recorded punt: 2020 – 72 yards, 2021 – 82 yards, and 2024 – 84 yards. He is also leading this year with that 81-yarder in the Steelers game. Three of these punts are listed in the “Top-30 NFL Punts of All Time.” And yet, with all these accolades and league-leading accomplishments, Bojorquez has never made a single Pro Bowl. This year seems promising.

title: Cleveland Browns news: It’s the most insufferable time of the year
summary: The Cleveland Browns have entered the annual part of the calendar that everyone was hoping to avoid. Welcome to Quarterback Controversy Season! The Browns had barely left the field on Sunday following a loss to the two-win New Orleans Saints before head coach Todd Monken was asked who the starting quarterback will be for this […]
full_text: (Photo by Nick Cammett/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cleveland Browns have entered the annual part of the calendar that everyone was hoping to avoid. Welcome to Quarterback Controversy Season! The Browns had barely left the field on Sunday following a loss to the two-win New Orleans Saints before head coach Todd Monken was asked who the starting quarterback will be for this week’s game against the Houston Texans. Monken rightly pointed out that, you know, the game had just ended, so maybe it wasn’t the right time to discuss such things. On Monday, presumably having had time to sleep on the matter, Monken had the opportunity to put the nonsense to bed before it started, but instead decided to start digging his own grave and state that he has still not made a decision. Let’s assume Monken and the coaching staff are not planning to pull the surprise of the season and start either Dillon Gabriel or Taylen Green against the Texans. So that leaves Monken with two options: The quarterback he handpicked to start the season and, through some form of voodoo, played a role in helping the Browns to a 5-3 record and a spot to play meaningful games in the final two months of the season. The backup quarterback, who was just 5-of-8 for 38 yards at halftime against the two-win Saints, but rallied the troops in the second half thanks to impressive YAC totals from the receivers in a one-point loss. At this point it may not matter much as the defense is worn down after being overrun the past three weeks to the tune of 501 rushing yards. And for all the “explosive plays” on Sunday, the offense needed almost five full quarters of football to score 22 points on a New Orleans defense that was allowing 28 points a game. All Monken needs to do is pick someone- it doesn’t matter who- and stick with them the rest of the season. It’s simply too exhausting to go through all this stupidity again. We’ve had enough – time to get going with today’s edition of the Daily Dawg Chow. title: The big-play potential returns for Browns offense with Shedeur Sanders
summary: The Browns’ offense was dormant for much of the game as Shedeur Sanders started in place of Deshaun Watson. Before you knew it, though, in the fourth quarter and overtime, the two teams were engaged in a shootout as Sanders started letting the ball loose downfield. Unfortunately, Cleveland just fell short in the extra period. […]
full_text: NEW ORLEANS, LA - NOVEMBER 8: Shedeur Sanders #2 of the Cleveland Browns is pressured by Chase Young #99 of the New Orleans Saints during the second half of a game at Caesars Superdome on November 8, 2026, in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Derick Hingle/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Browns’ offense was dormant for much of the game as Shedeur Sanders started in place of Deshaun Watson . Before you knew it, though, in the fourth quarter and overtime, the two teams were engaged in a shootout as Sanders started letting the ball loose downfield. Unfortunately, Cleveland just fell short in the extra period. Below, we analyze the snap counts and stats on offense for the Cleveland Browns ’ Week 9 game against the New Orleans Saints. Quarterback Pos Player Plays % Snaps Stats QB Shedeur Sanders 73 100% 19-of-31 (61.3%) for 297 yards, 2 TD. 10 carries, 28 yards (2.8 YPC). It was a frustrating first three quarters watching Shedeur Sanders . I was excited to see him get an opportunity this week, and my excitement turned to dismay when I saw the number of procedural-looking errors, bailing from the pocket, etc. I saw no growth from what we saw a year ago. I was also frustrated because Sanders at his best is when he’s taking some deep shots. A short, read-and-dissect offense, is not what he excels at. Granted, he needs to be much better at that if he wants to be an NFL quarterback, but for this being a spot start, we needed to let him take some shots. Otherwise, you might as well have started Dillon Gabriel . When the Browns needed to score and he knew it was either “take a shot or take a loss,” Sanders was much better getting the offense moving. He saved his backup job because if the fourth quarter had come-and-gone with no scores, I think he would’ve been moved to third-string next week. Either way, he was not a PFF darling, grading out to a 55.0, third-lowest on offense. In the PFF breakdown, Sanders played better when blitzed or under pressure, and far worse when not under pressure or blitzed. Running Back Pos Player Plays % Snaps Stats RB Dylan Sampson 47 64% 8 carries, 21 yards (2.6 YPC). 3 catches, 27 yards (6 targets). RB Quinshon Judkins 25 34% 15 carries, 43 yards (2.9 YPC). 1 catch, 2 yards (1 target). FB Michael Burton 11 15% No stats registered. Dylan Sampson out-paced Quinshon Judkins in reps by a good margin. Much of that can be attributed to the hurry-up/two-minute offense at the end of the fourth quarter and in overtime. Facing one of the league’s worst run defenses, Cleveland couldn’t get their ground game going. Wide Receiver Pos Player Plays % Snaps Stats WR Denzel Boston 68 93% 6 catches, 98 yards (7 targets). WR KC Concepcion 68 93% 4 catches, 85 yards (6 targets), 1 TD. 1 carry, 3 yards (3.0 YPC). WR Jerry Jeudy 50 68% 2 catches, 37 yards (4 targets). WR Malachi Corley 9 12% 0 catches (1 target). WR Tylan Wallace 6 8% 1 catch, 6 yards (1 target). Hats off to the Browns’ wide receivers this week, especially down the stretch. Denzel Boston made an incredible high-point catch over a defender after putting a nasty move on him to get open. Boston was the Browns’ top-graded player on offense by PFF, with a grade of 73.6. KC Concepcion got his first NFL touchdown, and he used his speed to go a long distance across the field after making the catch to get in. He also ran for 3 yards when there wasn’t much room on that play. Jerry Jeudy stepped up on the final drive of regulation with an incredible sideline 33-yard catch. Those targets aren’t coming often, but Jeudy has done a great job staying motivated with his role and giving this team clutch moments. Tight End Pos Player Plays % Snaps Stats TE Harold Fannin 61 84% 2 catches, 42 yards (2 targets), 1 TD. TE Blake Whiteheart 19 26% 0 catches (1 target). He didn’t have a catch until overtime, but my-oh-my, it was a thing of beauty watching Harold Fannin stiff-arm two defenders for a touchdown. The announcers pointed out that for much of the game, Fannin was helping chip Chase Young . Fannin was credited as having one of his better blocking days, per PFF. Offensive Line Pos Player Plays % Snaps Stats OL Spencer Fano 73 100% OL Elgton Jenkins 73 100% OL Austin Barber 73 100% OL Zion Johnson 73 100% OL Tytus Howard 73 100% OL Zak Zinter 1 1% Spencer Fano was the Browns’ top-graded lineman, per PFF, with a grade of 68.9. The team’s other rookie, Austin Barber , didn’t fare as well. He was the team’s lowest-graded lineman by PFF, with a grade of 51.8 and a terrible pass blocking grade. Penalties continue to kill Cleveland. If you play the butterfly effect, if Zion Johnson doesn’t commit the hold in regulation, maybe Cleveland is able to close out the game on offense.

summary: Cleveland Browns fans are closer to thinking about the upcoming NFL draft than they are to the AFC playoff picture, despite the team being tied for the last seed in the conference after nine weeks. That is what happens with two straight defeats, one being destroyed and the next losing to a bad team. First, […]
full_text: Cleveland Browns fans are closer to thinking about the upcoming NFL draft than they are to the AFC playoff picture, despite the team being tied for the last seed in the conference after nine weeks. That is what happens with two straight defeats, one being destroyed and the next losing to a bad team. First, the Browns may or may not join the NFL trade deadline festivities on Tuesday . Then, HC Todd Monken has to decide whether Deshaun Watson will regain his starting job , following a week off due to a concussion, or Shedeur Sanders did enough in Week 9 to earn that responsibility. While the 2027 NFL draft is a long way away, Cleveland fans have been keeping an eye on the Los Angeles Rams all season following the Myles Garrett trade . The Rams have been overwhelmed by injuries this year, including Garrett missing a month and a half, and: WR Davante Adams ruled out for 6 to 10 weeks DT Poonie Ford ruled out for the year DT Kobie Turner ruled out for a month to a month and a half K Blake Grupe ruled out for the year In Week 9, while trying to salt away another victory , the Rams lost their other star receiver, Puka Nacua, to multiple ligament injuries and turf toe: The #Rams are expected to place WR Puka Nacua on Injured Reserve with MCL and PCL sprains, plus turf toe, coach Sean McVay told reporters. pic.twitter.com/LLWLyGwVMy — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) November 9, 2026 As of now, no word on how long Nacua will be out, with the Rams in ninth place in the NFC and facing a daunting schedule after facing the Arizona Cardinals in Week 10, starting with the Wednesday game for Thanksgiving week: Week 12: Green Bay Packers Week 13: Kansas City Chiefs Week 14: San Francisco 49ers Week 15: Dallas Cowboys Week 16: Seattle Seahawks Week 17: Tampa Bay Buccaneers Week 18: Seattle Seahawks With the NFL trade deadline on Tuesday, Los Angeles could go in a number of directions because of their injuries, including trying to add a receiver to help in place of Adams and Nacua. Currently, the Rams are slotted with the 18th overall pick in the 2027 NFL draft, which will be headed to the Browns. full_text: Among the conversations surrounding the Cleveland Browns after Week 9’s loss to the New Orleans Saints was whether Shedeur Sanders overtook Deshaun Watson as the team’s starting quarterback: There was also a comparison of the two quarterbacks: HC Todd Monken was non-committal after the game, but his answers were mostly based on the timing of the media session right after the game. Sanders’ performance was uneven , but Cleveland’s offense was explosive in the second half. Monken’s befuddling decision to share a conversation with Sanders about plays is just a footnote in a game that was lost by one point after the team went for two points at the end of overtime. Monday, the day before the NFL trade deadline, Monken and the Browns have already decided that Watson would return as the team’s starter, reportedly: The Browns plan to start Deshaun Watson in Week 10 vs the Texans, per source. Shedeur Sanders filled in Sunday in New Orleans, but returning to Watson was the expected move once he cleared concussion protocol. — Jeremy Fowler (@JFowlerESPN) November 9, 2026 The two quarterbacks engaged in a long competition for the starting job throughout training camp, with the veteran winning out. Over the first eight games, Watson has led the Browns to five wins, of the come-from-behind fashion. During his time with the media Monday afternoon, Monken noted that the staff had reviewed the tape but had not gotten back together to discuss the starting quarterback decision. He also pushed back on the idea that he had to have a decision by Tuesday’s game planning session.
