title: Despite win, complementary football continues to evade the Cowboys
summary: The Dallas Cowboys finally got back into the win column Sunday, but nobody should mistake a 27-23 victory over the Indianapolis Colts for a complete performance. Dallas dominated the statistical categories that usually determine the outcome of a football game, outgaining Indianapolis by more than 200 yards, controlling the clock and producing over 500 yards […]
full_text: Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys finally got back into the win column Sunday, but nobody should mistake a 27-23 victory over the Indianapolis Colts for a complete performance. Dallas dominated the statistical categories that usually determine the outcome of a football game, outgaining Indianapolis by more than 200 yards, controlling the clock and producing over 500 yards of offense. Yet somehow, the Cowboys needed a touchdown with just over a minute remaining to escape with a victory. That is the frustrating reality of this team. Dallas has shown it can move the football and generate enough defensive stops to compete. What it still cannot do consistently is put all the phases together. The offense wastes opportunities, the defense gives up momentum-changing plays, and the entire team continues to shoot itself in the foot with undisciplined mistakes. The Cowboys won Sunday, and at 4-5, they will gladly take it. But against a Colts team that had lost four straight games, this should never have been as close as it was. Dominating the stat sheet means nothing if you cannot finish drives Dallas finished the afternoon with 508 total yards of offense. The Cowboys also held a commanding advantage in time of possession, keeping the ball for 35 minutes. Dak Prescott threw for 335 yards and two touchdowns, completing 21 of 34 passes without an interception. CeeDee Lamb was spectacular, catching 10 passes for 195 yards and a touchdown. Javonte Williams added 101 rushing yards and a score, while former Colts running back Tyler Goodson contributed another 77 yards on the ground, a career high. On paper, that is a dominant offensive performance. The Cowboys averaged 6.4 yards per play and moved the football at will for long stretches. Yet, somehow, after all those yards and all that success moving the ball, Dallas found itself losing with 1:38 left. Dallas converted just 5 of 16 third-down opportunities, a 31.3% conversion rate. The offense also committed two turnovers, including a wacky Lamb fourth-quarter fumble that wiped out a huge play and a Colts error that could have sealed the victory earlier in the game. The fumble was weird. It felt like the same kind of voodoo magic that rears its ugly head just as the Cowboys have a chance to win. Part of the malaise of the losing culture that this team is stewing in. The Cowboys also had to settle for field goals on multiple occasions, including another missed 50-yard attempt by Brandon Aubrey in the fourth quarter. Aubrey’s miss came after a bad snap, but it still wasted another possession in a game Dallas should have been controlling. This play and the result of it explain the emotional rise and fall of being a Dallas Cowboys fan pic.twitter.com/YJdOmdb2nG — RJ Ochoa (@rjochoa) November 8, 2026 The defense continues to surrender momentum-changing plays Christian Parker’s defense deserves credit for holding Jonathan Taylor to just 46 rushing yards on 13 carries, forcing two turnovers and ultimately delivering the interception that sealed the victory. Quinnen Williams also made a huge impact, forcing a Taylor fumble in the fourth quarter that gave Prescott and the offense another opportunity. But the defense still struggled when the game entered its most important moments. After Dallas built a 20-10 lead in the third quarter, Indianapolis found a way back in with a 55-yard touchdown reception by Ashton Dulin. Cowboys fans had just seen this a week ago with Tyler Allgeier, then had to watch Dulin do it again. Dulin found space and never looked back after more questionable tackling reared its ugly head again in this game. That kind of breakdown has plagued this defense throughout the season. Dallas can generate pressure, make tackles and occasionally force turnovers, but one missed assignment or poor angle seems to undo this defense any time the game gets close. The fourth quarter brought even more problems. DaRon Bland was flagged for a 40-yard pass interference penalty after a deep throw from Daniel Jones, and Dee Winters followed it with a 15-yard unnecessary roughness penalty. Those two flags gave Indianapolis an enormous field-position advantage and helped keep the Colts’ comeback alive. The Cowboys surrendered 16 points in the second half, including two long field goals from Spencer Shrader that gave Indianapolis its first lead of the afternoon. They finished with a positive note, of course. Rookie safety Caleb Downs made the biggest defensive play of the game, intercepting Jones’ desperation throw with 35 seconds remaining to preserve the victory. One clutch play doesn’t erase the problems that came before it. Dallas still has to become more consistent defensively. Yes, there were some bright spots, even against a bad team, but this defense still hasn’t put together a complete game and regularly falls apart when the going gets tough. The penalties are becoming a weekly embarrassment Brian Schottenheimer has been the Dallas Cowboys head coach for 26 games. The team has had double-digit penalties in 8 of them. They are 5-2-1 in those games, though. (via @Stathead , @pfref ) pic.twitter.com/CPO6TSNe1k — RJ Ochoa (@rjochoa) November 9, 2026 If one statistic perfectly captures the Cowboys’ inability to play complementary football, it is the penalty total. Dallas was flagged 14 times for 153 yards against Indianapolis. One hundred and fifty-three yards! That is an absurd amount of free yardage to give an opponent, even in a game Dallas largely controlled. Penalties repeatedly put the offense behind the chains and gave Indianapolis extra chances. Lamb had an 18-yard reception wiped out by offensive pass interference, while multiple flags on the same drive forced Dallas to overcome unnecessary obstacles just to move the ball. The defense was equally guilty. Bland’s 40-yard pass-interference penalty and Winters’ unnecessary roughness call gave Indianapolis a chance to capitalize on mistakes instead of earning every yard. We’ve seen this before, though, haven’t we? Dallas has struggled with discipline throughout the season, and the coaching staff has repeatedly talked about correcting those mistakes. Yet here we are, watching the Cowboys commit another double-digit penalty performance. Dallas finally finished, but not because it seized the victory There is something to be said for the way the Cowboys responded after Indianapolis took a 23-20 lead with 1:38 remaining. Prescott didn’t panic, and the offense finally produced the kind of clutch drive that has been missing in several of Dallas’ losses this season. Prescott connected with Ryan Flournoy for a 46-yard gain, putting the Cowboys in scoring position. A pass-interference penalty moved Dallas to the 1-yard line, and Williams finished the drive with a touchdown run to put Dallas back in front. . @RyanNumba9 makes a big play 👏 📺: #DALvsIND on FOX 📲: Stream on NFL+ https://t.co/XM2vIx7C1d pic.twitter.com/ITQ6dK3HQ2 — Dallas Cowboys (@dallascowboys) November 8, 2026 Then Downs sealed the game with his first career interception, stopping Indianapolis’ final attempt to respond. That is complementary football in its simplest form: the offense scores when it needs to, and the defense makes the play necessary to preserve the lead. Dallas waited until the final minute to put those pieces together. The Cowboys should be encouraged by how their stars played individually. There were legitimate positives, and the team deserves a sliver of credit for finding a way to win a game that could easily have slipped away. Alas, the larger concerns remain. Dallas still struggles to finish drives, still commits far too many penalties and still allows opposing offenses to hang around when it has opportunities to put games away. Schottenheimer and his staff have to find a way to make these performances more consistent. The Cowboys cannot expect Prescott to throw for 335 yards and Lamb to approach 200 receiving yards every week just to survive against…
author: Jorge Guajardo

title: Dak Prescott’s deep shot to Ryan Flournoy rescues Dallas
summary: Another fourth-quarter lead had disappeared. Another disappointing finish was staring Dallas in the face. Then Dak Prescott and Ryan Flournoy changed the game with one throw. Trailing Indianapolis 23-20 with 1:37 remaining, the Cowboys opened their final touchdown drive by attacking downfield. Prescott connected with Flournoy for a 46-yard gain, immediately putting Dallas in position […]
full_text: Photo by Michael Hickey/Getty Images | Getty Images Another fourth-quarter lead had disappeared. Another disappointing finish was staring Dallas in the face. Then Dak Prescott and Ryan Flournoy changed the game with one throw. Trailing Indianapolis 23-20 with 1:37 remaining, the Cowboys opened their final touchdown drive by attacking downfield. Prescott connected with Flournoy for a 46-yard gain, immediately putting Dallas in position to chase the winning touchdown. It was the decisive swing in a much-needed 27-23 victory. Reaching that point was unnecessarily painful. At halftime, Dallas led 17-7 and later held a commanding 20-10 advantage. However, turnovers and penalties kept Indianapolis alive. Despite moving the ball far more effectively than the Colts, Dallas’s 14 penalties for 153 yards and two fumbles prevented them from converting their advantage into a win. Quinnen Williams made a crucial defensive intervention in Dallas territory, forcing Jonathan Taylor to fumble, which Shemar James recovered. However, the offense couldn’t cash in. Indianapolis eventually tied the game, and Brandon Aubrey missed a potential important field goal. Spencer Shrader then kicked a 50-yard field goal with less than two minutes remaining, putting the Colts ahead. Dallas needed an immediate response, and Prescott trusted Flournoy to deliver it. This was no uncontested catch against a defender who had been left behind. Sauce Gardner stayed alongside Flournoy downfield, but failed to turn his head toward the football. Instead, he tried to disrupt the catch through the receiver’s hands and actually grabbed one arm. Flournoy maintained his concentration and secured the pass with the other hand against his body, producing the biggest reception of the afternoon when Dallas needed it most. The importance of that completion went beyond the yardage. Dallas had started the possession needing to move quickly just to give itself a chance. One snap later, the offense could realistically pursue a touchdown and force Indianapolis to answer. The pressure had shifted straight back onto the Colts. Dallas finished the job with help from Indianapolis penalties, and Javonte Williams scored from one yard out with 1:08 remaining. The Cowboys had turned a three-point deficit into a four-point lead in just 29 seconds. There is still plenty to fix. Winning does not erase the mistakes that made this game so difficult. But when Dallas needed a play to prevent another late disappointment, its quarterback and receiver delivered, and the catch was the late-game turning point that helped seal the victory.

title: Ugly wins cannot save these underperforming Cowboys
summary: The Dallas Cowboys found a way to win a football game on Sunday, but the mood across Cowboys Nation remained surprisingly somber. Losing this matchup would have been absolutely devastating, for all intents and purposes ending their season. Falling four games behind the New York Giants in the loss column is a hole simply too […]
full_text: Photo by Michael Hickey/Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys found a way to win a football game on Sunday, but the mood across Cowboys Nation remained surprisingly somber. Losing this matchup would have been absolutely devastating, for all intents and purposes ending their season. Falling four games behind the New York Giants in the loss column is a hole simply too deep to climb out of, especially with a brutal stretch of schedule coming soon. This made Sunday’s win super important, yet at the same time, it offers very little reassurance. The Cowboys may have secured the victory, but once again, what they showed on the field revealed a team that continues to make life incredibly difficult for themselves, even when facing bad opponents. The game looked eerily similar to the prior week’s letdown against the Arizona Cardinals. In a game where it felt like the Cowboys were in complete control, they chose to play around rather than put their opponent away, eventually leading to another shocking moment where they suddenly found themselves trailing late in the fourth quarter. The most troubling part of this situation is how familiar this has become. Over the last two weeks, the team has reproduced that exact gut-wrenching feeling that gave fans major anxiety during those consecutive nail-biting weeks against Baltimore and Houston earlier in the year. It’s the same story. They begin slowly, eventually start to get their act together to build a lead, and then watch it gradually wither away. Fortunately, against the Texans earlier in the season, they were able to escape with a victory thanks to a game-winning drive on the back of a clutch fourth-down conversion. But down in Rio, they weren’t so lucky. Instead of punching the ball into the end zone with just a handful of seconds left on the clock, the offense sputtered and settled for a field goal, allowing the Ravens to make the game-winning play themselves. The heartbreaking finish left fans playing the what-if game and asking why the Cowboys keep letting this happen. Fast forward a month later, and the exact same scenario is unfolding all over again, except this time it is happening against even worse teams. The Arizona debacle last week was an absolute horror show. The Cardinals did not score a single point until late in the first half and were down by two touchdowns in the fourth quarter before things completely fell apart. The most infuriating part is that the offense had the opportunity to run out the clock if they could have secured one measly first down late in the game. They failed, the Cardinals mounted a comeback, and fans everywhere watched their team collapse. On Sunday, it looked like it was happening again. It was painful to watch the offense struggle so mightily to score touchdowns against a poor Colts defense. Up until the final 70 seconds of the game, the offense had only found the end zone twice, and it required a clutch fourth-down grab by Jake Ferguson and a huge coverage breakdown for CeeDee Lamb’s big touchdown right at the end of the first half. Strangely enough, clutch fourth-down execution from Ferguson and Lamb exploding for over 180 receiving yards were identical saving graces in each of their close victory against their AFC South opponents this year. Imagine if those two things didn’t happen? The Cowboys would be sitting at an abysmal 2-7 with a completely dead season, and the entire fanbase would be stressing over how the New York Jets are about to inherit a top-five draft pick courtesy of the front office. All of this is to say that the Cowboys are an absolute mess right now. Are they still within striking distance of the NFC East crown? Sure, but we must remind ourselves that the schedule gets significantly tougher over the second half of the season, and this group has not beaten a single opponent with a winning record all year. In fact, they are 1-5 against teams with a record of 3-6 or better. That is a scary statistic. Of the final eight opponents left on the schedule, five currently boast winning records. The month of December looks particularly ominous, featuring a four-game stretch against teams who all currently have a winning record. The storm is coming. For a team that struggles to put away struggling teams, anticipating how they will hold up against stronger opponents is frightening. This team shows zero signs of turning the corner or correcting their chronic mental lapses. Instead, they prefer to lollygag and repeatedly engage in unnecessary wild finishes. All of this seems avoidable. They have to be better than this, but sadly, they just refuse to play like it. Hang on to your drama subscription because it won’t be going away anytime soon.
author: Dan Rogers

title: Cowboys news: Dallas will be missing a starter, role players due to injury
summary: The Cowboys are happy to get out of Indianapolis with their fourth win of the season, but still left a lot of things that will need a quick fix on the field before returning home to play the 49ers. They come out of the Colts game with some injuries that won’t make dealing with a […]
full_text: Photo by Michael Hickey/Getty Images | Getty Images The Cowboys are happy to get out of Indianapolis with their fourth win of the season, but still left a lot of things that will need a quick fix on the field before returning home to play the 49ers. They come out of the Colts game with some injuries that won’t make dealing with a 7-1 San Francisco squad any easier. The team will need to be firing in all three phases, which means finding a way to continue getting stops on defense, and scoring off of them more than they have been on offense. Dallas Cowboys rule out 3 players for Week 10, while Jake Ferguson and a rising player are set to miss multiple games – Mauricio Rodriguez, A to Z Sports The Cowboys have some key injuries for the 49ers game, including starting TE Jake Ferguson. When asked to walk through the injuries from the Colts game, Schottenheimer didn’t sugarcoat it. “Busy week in the training room for us,” Schottenheimer said. “PJ Locke will not be available this week. Jake Ferguson and Tyler Goodson should both miss multiple weeks. We’re working through that.” Additionally, the Cowboys have a large group of players whose statuses will be up in the air as the week progresses. Cowboys’ emerging RB ‘probably going to miss some time’ with knee injury – Todd Brock, The Cowboys Wire The Cowboys are going to be very thin at running back, after Tyler Goodson played through injury in week nine. The 25-year-old exited the game in the first half and spent some time in the sideline medical tent but was able to return after the break to notch 33 of his 77 rushing yards. He and starter Javonte Williams combined to put up 178 yards on the ground, with Goodson averaging an impressive 6.4 yards per carry. “I’m going to do everything I can to get out there on the field,” Goodson said after the win . “If it’s just a little pain, I’m going to go. But if it’s something where I just can’t go, then I won’t go.” The Cowboys Defense Got 14 Stops: What Did the Offense Do With Them? – Cody Warren, Inside The Star The Cowboys defense is getting off the field, but the offense can’t stay on it as much as they need to either. Dallas led the Colts 10-7 in the second quarter when Parker’s defense forced three consecutive three-and-outs. The Cowboys punted it right back three times. On the last of those possessions, Williams opened with a 14-yard run, Lamb was flagged for a false start, the penalties piled up, and Dallas eventually punted on fourth-and-18. It took a fourth straight Colts punt before Brian Schottenheimer and Dak Prescott made them pay. Dak got the ball at his 25 with 49 seconds left and found Lamb for a 44-yard touchdown before halftime . Download the SB Nation app today! Fewer ads Seamlessly jump between communities and conversations Faster commenting and posting experience! Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . Caleb Downs makes his mark in crucial victory over Colts – Matthew Holleran, Blogging The Boys Every week, Caleb Downs is doing more and more to show why he was one of the top defensive players in this year’s draft class. Expectations were sky-high for Downs at the beginning of his rookie campaign. While the 21-year-old had shown flashes of greatness in Dallas’ first eight games, we’d yet to see him take over a game as he did at Ohio State. For the first time in his NFL career, Downs did just that on Sunday. Downs and Quinnen Williams were the best defenders on the field on Sunday afternoon. Downs showed his ability to impact the game in multiple ways, finishing with a sack, a PBU, and a game-sealing interception in the fourth quarter. Cowboys should relish in Eagles throwing in the towel with Jordan Davis trade – Levi Dombro, The Landry Hat Someone has to win the NFC East, and the Cowboys win over the Colts allows them to keep hoping it can be them, especially with the Eagles waving the white flag. Currently on a seven-game losing streak and having dropped three straight contests against division foes, Howie Roseman is throwing in the towel on the 2026 season. On Monday afternoon, less than a day before the trade deadline, the Eagles traded star nose tackle Jordan Davis to the Jaguars. Eight months after they signed him to a three-year, $78 million deal. And while Roseman is now sitting on a pile of draft picks in Philadelphia, that doesn’t really move the needle a whole lot anymore. This is a good day for Cowboys fans to victory lap their bitter rivals and feel good that they at least have hope for the rest of the season. Brian Schottenheimer on Cowboys’ penalty struggles vs. Colts: ‘It wasn’t good enough’ – Tommy Yarrish, DallasCowboys.com The Cowboys not separating from bad opponents because of penalties is going to continue hurting them against better teams, and the head coach knows it. Through nine games, the Cowboys are now tied for the second-most penalties accepted against them with 42, and have the most penalty yards accepted against them in the NFL with 667. Evidently, it had an impact on their Week 9 game against the Colts and will continue to impact their season if it isn’t corrected. “It wasn’t good enough, and that’s why that came down to the way it came down,” Schottenheimer said. “That game should’ve been where we win by a couple touchdowns maybe, but we let them hang around, we put ourselves behind the sticks on offense a bunch. Explained to the guys, if we don’t clean that up, it’s going to hurt our ability to do what we want to do.”

title: Caleb Downs makes his mark in crucial victory over Colts
summary: After a demoralizing loss to the lowly Arizona Cardinals a week prior, the Dallas Cowboys needed a bounce-back performance in the worst way on Sunday. Sitting at 3-5, Dallas had to leave Indianapolis with a win if they wanted any hope of staying in the playoff hunt. While it was not always pretty, the Cowboys […]
full_text: Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images | Getty Images After a demoralizing loss to the lowly Arizona Cardinals a week prior, the Dallas Cowboys needed a bounce-back performance in the worst way on Sunday. Sitting at 3-5, Dallas had to leave Indianapolis with a win if they wanted any hope of staying in the playoff hunt. While it was not always pretty, the Cowboys showed up on both sides of the ball when it mattered most. Both the offense and defense came through late in the fourth quarter, leading to a crucial 27-23 win over the Colts. The Cowboys had some standout players on both sides of the ball, but rookie safety Caleb Downs had his first signature game. Downs, playing against his older brother Josh for the first time in their professional careers, was a leading force in the victory, earning him this week’s game ball award. Expectations were sky-high for Downs at the beginning of his rookie campaign. While the 21-year-old had shown flashes of greatness in Dallas’ first eight games, we’d yet to see him take over a game as he did at Ohio State. For the first time in his NFL career, Downs did just that on Sunday. Downs and Quinnen Williams were the best defenders on the field on Sunday afternoon. Downs showed his ability to impact the game in multiple ways, finishing with a sack, a PBU, and a game-sealing interception in the fourth quarter. CALEB DOWNS SEALS THE DEAL 📺: #DALvsIND on FOX 📲: Stream on NFL+ https://t.co/XM2vIx7C1d pic.twitter.com/VFZM4RlYdq — Dallas Cowboys (@dallascowboys) November 8, 2026 Downs finished the game with the highest coverage grade of any defender, recording a remarkable 90.6 mark. We’ve seen the Ohio State product struggle a bit in coverage early on in his career, but Sunday was a different story. Indianapolis completed just one of four passes when targeting Downs for a total of 12 yards. If the Cowboys defense wants to get closer to league-average moving forward, Caleb Downs playing like he did on Sunday will be a huge help.
author: Matthew Holleran

title: Dak Prescott, CeeDee Lamb refuse to lose as Cowboys top Colts
summary: Nothing comes easy for the 2026 Dallas Cowboys, but they managed to get back in the win column on Sunday with a 27-23 win at the Indianapolis Colts. It is their first win scoring less than 30 points since last season’s miraculous comeback in Week 12 vs. the Eagles, which gave Brian Schottenheimer’s team their […]
full_text: Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images | Getty Images Nothing comes easy for the 2026 Dallas Cowboys, but they managed to get back in the win column on Sunday with a 27-23 win at the Indianapolis Colts. It is their first win scoring less than 30 points since last season’s miraculous comeback in Week 12 vs. the Eagles, which gave Brian Schottenheimer’s team their first winning streak of that 2025 season. At the end of another rollercoaster game, this fourth win of the season goes in the same bucket as the other narrow win the Cowboys have against another AFC South opponent – Dak Prescott refusing to lose with the ball in his hands, and making the plays when it mattered most to ensure this. The Texans win was defined by Prescott and CeeDee Lamb making all the plays when it mattered, and without George Pickens this time out, Lamb’s big day was even more crucial. There were plays by the defense in the first half that made this game feel like it wouldn’t come close to needing any late game heroics from the offense, but the offense didn’t capitalize early. Then, there were breakdowns on defense that helped the Colts storm back, but also more rallying by Christian Parker’s side of the ball to ultimately put this in the win column. Let’s get to some notes on the gut-it-out performance in Indy. Too Many 3rd Downs For the second straight week, the Cowboys faced 16 third-down attempts. The Cowboys have faced more third downs on offense than their opponents in every game since the Packers loss. Dak Prescott’s third-down fumble in the first quarter was the second straight week the Cowboys had a disastrous negative play in a formation that calls on Javonte Williams to stay in and block. This time around, the Cowboys also had Jake Ferguson in the game. Ferguson was the only pass option running a hot route against the pressure the Colts brought on this play, yet somehow the defense had an answer to bracket him with two defenders while also getting to Prescott. The strip sack set the Colts offense up on a short field they capitalized on to take a 7-3 lead. The Colts would not get points again until midway through the third quarter. While the Cowboys did get two touchdowns before this, they also punted on all four other possessions in this stretch. The touchdown drive that came in response to being down 10-7 got a rare Javonte Williams receiving play that went for positive yards on a 3rd-and-4, then overcame a 2nd-and-19 after a Brevyn Spann-Ford holding penalty, and was gifted an automatic first down after facing 2nd-and-15 on a Tyler Guyton penalty. Even after all this, it still took a 4th-and-2 attempt in the red zone to get points on the board with Jake Ferguson’s touchdown. The other touchdown the Cowboys got came a little bit easier, rewarding a drive that saw what felt like the first successful scramble drill in a long time. Lamb and Prescott made the play when the Cowboys decided to throw on 3rd-and-1, hooking up on the scramble drill for 22 yards. One play later, Lamb got behind Charvarius Ward for his 44-yard touchdown to go ahead 17-7. Yet again, the Cowboys felt in control of a game, but were left scrambling and fighting for their life to actually finish by the fourth quarter. The Cowboys had a perfect 34/34 run-pass split in this game, and Dak Prescott’s 9.9 yards per attempt was a season high, but it still felt like the offense majored in wanting to be in third downs, makings things hard on themselves yet again, and not putting the game away on their own terms early. Instead, they left it until late for more QB heroics that paint a clear picture of what this team is really all about. Defensive Resolve The number one thing the Cowboys defense needs to fix following these last two wild games is limiting the explosive plays for touchdowns. Two weeks in a row, a game has swung in the snap of a finger because any work the defense has done up to a point is wiped out by a long play for a touchdown. Ashton Dulin’s 55-yard touchdown on a screen pass evaporated the Cowboys hopes of taking a two-score lead to the fourth quarter, and led to another game that felt like it could see overtime by the fourth. Marist Liufau, DaRon Bland, and P.J. Locke were the defenders with the best chance to get Dulin on the ground, and none of them could. The Cowboys continued to do some interesting things with Shemar James in this game, as he was involved in the play where Caleb Downs had a sack, and Locke made a big stop on third down early in the game as well, but more consistent fundamentals is still something holding back the Dallas D as a unit. They need to tackle better. After the Cowboys offense squandered their chance by missing a FG with over three minutes remaining in the game, the Cowboys defense needed to come up with a stand. The Colts got into comfortable field goal range, but Josh Downs’ third-down drop stopped the clock and the defense had held Indy to a 23-20 lead after a field goal. The defense did not give up a touchdown, and they got the ball back to the offense with enough time to go win the game. The other defensive resolve point in this cardiac fourth quarter was of course Quinnen Williams forcing a fumble on Jonathan Taylor, recovered by James. We said coming into this matchup that just an arbitrary splash plays from Williams wouldn’t be good enough. So Williams stepped up and made multiple big plays, none bigger than this one, and helped the Cowboys overcome penalties on Bland and Dee Winters prior to the takeaway that made a difference in which team had just enough in the tank to win on Sunday. Kenny Clark even added his name to the splash play list from the defensive interior on the final drive, pressuring Jones into an intentional grounding throw that really wrecked the drive and led to Downs’ game-sealing interception. The highly-paid Cowboys defensive interior made the plays in crunch time. Play-Calling and What’s Next The goal for the Cowboys now resets back to exactly what it was after the Eagles game, don’t get too high after a win (against an arguably even worse team this time), and stay focused enough to get a win streak started in front of home fans next Sunday. To do so, the Cowboys will have to waste no time digesting not only the good things that happened to beat the Colts, but the bad as well. Fourteen penalties for 153 yards is one thing that should be unacceptable even in a win, but the bigger and more long-term concern is the poor play-calling that stamped this game as well. Even while getting Lamb ten catches on 16 targets for 10 catches and 195 yards, nothing outside of Lamb’s long touchdown felt like it came easy for the offense. The protection plans were not sound to give Prescott time to throw when needed. The early down aggressiveness to not face 16 third-down attempts was not there. Worst of all, the static routes, lack of motion, and number of pass plays where all of Prescott’s options were blanketed from start to finish, with receivers not even running hard on many of these plays, were abundant. As good as CeeDee Lamb’s day was – 10 catches, 195 yards, one TD – it could have been better. He had two catches wiped out because of offensive pass interference penalties (one was iffy, for sure) and missed out on another TD when he was unable to get his second foot down. “He… — Todd Archer (@toddarcher) November 9, 2026 This week will be telling when it comes to how Lamb’s leadership is received at large by this team, as even after his huge day he was more focused on what could have gone better and his costly fumble. This is the type of attitude the entire Cowboys team needs to take into the 49ers matchup, as significant improvements from how they played, mainly on offense, will be needed to pull that upset. Brian Schottenheimer’s responsibility for how the offense looks will come up as well, but his postgame locker room approach was quite different in mood than Lamb’s. keep playing & find a way 🗣️ #DALvsIND | @ATT…
author: Sean Martin

title: Cowboys at Colts Stock Report: Caleb Downs, Quinnen Williams excel
summary: The Dallas Cowboys won a football game on Sunday. For real. The win was hardly the prettiest that the Cowboys have ever had, but it counts just the same as the ones that left us feeling happier than that one did. A win is a win, as they say. While the end result was the […]
full_text: Mandatory Credit: Robert Goddin-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Dallas Cowboys won a football game on Sunday. For real. The win was hardly the prettiest that the Cowboys have ever had, but it counts just the same as the ones that left us feeling happier than that one did. A win is a win, as they say. While the end result was the desired one, the path there was bumpy to say the least. There were players who rose to the occasion and others who left us wanting more in several types of ways. Let’s discuss in this week’s stock report. Stock Up: Caleb Downs It has felt like Caleb Downs was trending upward already, but Sunday was officially his announcement to the world. The game-sealing interception is what everybody will remember, but Downs was all over the place. He had a critical sack on an early third down. He was credited with two passes defensed and three tackles. Simply put, he was everywhere. It was needed in the worst way. Stock Up: Quinnen Williams Similarly, the Cowboys officially have a new war daddy. Like Downs, Williams had really been coming along as of late. The start to his season, his first full one with the Cowboys, was a little bit bumpy, but he singlehandedly disrupted so much of what the Colts wanted to do. We have dreamt of having a force of this nature along the interior. Stock Up: Ryan Flournoy It was nerve-wracking when the Cowboys announced that George Pickens would be inactive for this game. Sure, Ryan Flournoy has been very good this season, but elevating to the WR2 role is a very different thing. Flournoy proved more than capable. He was hardly CeeDee Lamb, but he provided the necessary moments opposite of him. Dak Prescott targeted him when the team absolutely needed a spark at the end of the game. The future of George Pickens remains unknown, but the way that Flournoy is playing is going to make those conversations very interesting to say the least. Stock Up: Rashan Gary Obviously there was only up to go for Rashan Gary. But he is a stock up nonetheless. The Cowboys were able to really stifle the Colts’ offense (hardly something to be proud of, but you can only play who’s in front of you) and Rashan Gary even picked up his second sack of the season as the team kept the heat on Daniel Jones. He also contributed six tackles and two TFLs. There has been far and few in between to choose from regarding Cowboys pass rushers this season so we have to take what we can get. Stock Up: Tyler Goodson Caleb Downs is obviously the best new player on the Cowboys (as in players who weren’t on the team at all last season), but Tyler Goodson has a very strong argument for number two. Goodson runs so hard and everything he does is with every bit of his energy. Goodson averaged 6.4 yards per carry and finished with 77 yards. He has been such a breath of fresh air and is a really proper counterpunch to the attack that is Javonte Williams. Stock Up: Christian Parker This is also a “nowhere to go but up” situation, and the quality of the opponent is certainly worth keeping in mind. But let’s say that Christian Parker’s defense generated eight different stops on Sunday, including the one that sealed the game in Caleb Downs’ interception. Is this representative of a turning tide? That would be a huge leap to make. But it is definitely representative of a group that is getting better and that is awesome to see. Stock Up: Brevyn Spann-Ford Jake Ferguson deserves a lot of kudos for the touchdown that he had in this game, especially given that it came on fourth down. To call it clutch would be to not do it due justice. Noting that, Brevyn Spann-Ford is really making the most of his opportunities as of late. He is becoming someone who Dak Prescott clearly trusts and has assimilated well into his new role with the offense at large. Stock Down: Brian Schottenheimer We just mentioned it, but the Ferguson touchdown really was quite fortunate. In that respect it really bailed Brian Schottenheimer out. That touchdown came on fourth and short in the redzone, but the third down play that Brian Schottenheimer called right before it was so silly. While the Cowboys were gashing the Colts their play-caller decided to call a trick play for CeeDee Lamb that lost yardage. You can argue that the decision to go for it on fourth down, even though it worked out, was pressing a bit. This doesn’t even cover the fact that the Cowboys barely beat a really bad Colts team. Heck, they were losing to the team in question late in the game. They almost did lose. Schottenheimer’s squad pulled this one off with zero room to spare. He has to be better. Stock Down: Brandon Aubrey Brandon Aubrey is still fine in an overall sense, but his trustworthiness from downtown certainly has to change . Rather the Cowboys’ trust in him has to change. Aubrey missed a 50-yard field goal that would have given the Cowboys a 23-20 lead in this game late down the stretch. Given that it was such a deep attempt the miss gave Indianapolis the ball at their own 40-yard line and they took advantage by netting a go-ahead field goal themselves. Stock Down: DeMarvion Overshown Drawing an unsportsmanlike conduct penalty for being out in the middle of the field when you are not even active for the game is peak silliness. Overshown’s penalty put a drive that should have started at the Cowboys’ 30-yard line at their own 15. They wound up punting and surrendering points. Those 15 yards were consequential, even if the Cowboys wound up winning. The Cowboys have a clear lack of a lot of things and therefore cannot afford to make silly mistakes. This was a silly mistake in the silliest of ways.
author: RJ Ochoa

title: Cowboys at Colts: The good, the bad, and ugly from Week 9
summary: In a game that was looking very much like a repeat of last week, the Dallas Cowboys were able to avoid another second half collapse by winning 27-23 in close, nail-biting fashion against the Indianapolis Colts. It’s difficult to get too excited about the outcome of the game, however, winning feels much better than losing […]
full_text: Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images | Getty Images In a game that was looking very much like a repeat of last week, the Dallas Cowboys were able to avoid another second half collapse by winning 27-23 in close, nail-biting fashion against the Indianapolis Colts. It’s difficult to get too excited about the outcome of the game, however, winning feels much better than losing no matter how they got there. It was a mixed bag Sunday afternoon for the Cowboys. Today we’ll take a look at the good, the bad, and the ugly from this Week 9 matchup before we start setting our sites on next week’s opponent, the San Francisco 49ers. THE GOOD – WR CeeDee Lamb With George Pickens sidelined, Dak Prescott repeatedly targeted CeeDee Lamb throughout the game Sunday afternoon. The two connected for 10 catches for 195 receiving yards and a touchdown. It ended up being a historic day for No. 88. He made NFL history by breaking the record for the most receptions before turning 28 years old. It would’ve been a near-perfect outing if not for a questionable fumble, but even that doesn’t lessen the impact he made. THE BAD – Penalties The Cowboys were once again nearly their own worst enemy Sunday afternoon against the Colts. They had a total of 14 penalties in this Week 9 matchup and quite a few of them helped Indianapolis hang around longer than they should have. The officials didn’t seem to help matters all that much either. There were several questionable calls that went against the Cowboys, more than a few of them involving WR CeeDee Lamb. Luckily it didn’t cost them the win. THE UGLY – Colts turnovers The Cowboys defense wasn’t dominant by any means, but they did what they needed to do in order to secure the victory in Indianapolis Sunday afternoon. They had two huge turnovers that ended up altering the game of the Cowboys favor. First, the fumble caused by DT Quinnen Williams that put a stop to a promising drive by the Colts, and second, the interception by Caleb Downs at the end of the game to seal the victory. It wasn’t pretty, but it was enough.
author: Brian Martin

title: 5 plays that helped Dallas escape Indy with a win
summary: The Dallas Cowboys needed playmakers to step up against the Indianapolis Colts. They were without George Pickens and Joey Porter Jr. so others needed to step up to avoid another loss to a team they were favored to beat. They made the win a lot closer than it needed to be. Luckily, they were able […]
full_text: Mandatory Credit: Robert Goddin-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Dallas Cowboys needed playmakers to step up against the Indianapolis Colts. They were without George Pickens and Joey Porter Jr. so others needed to step up to avoid another loss to a team they were favored to beat. They made the win a lot closer than it needed to be. Luckily, they were able to get big plays from some of their best players and some from players that have endured a rough stretch as of late. The Cowboys still trail the New York Giants in the NFC East, who also won today, but it feels much better than if they had lost. It wasn’t always pretty. The Cowboys had to overcome difficult situations, largely ones that they created for themselves due to penalties. Still, as the old saying goes: “A win is a win”. Here are five pivotal moments that helped Dallas secure the victory over Indianapolis. 1. Jake Ferguson answers the call on 4th down 2nd Quarter | 14:13 remaining | 4th-and-2 at Indianapolis 10-yard line When you absolutely have to have it, your players need to deliver. Jake Ferguson made one of the better plays of the day and one of the more impressive catches of the afternoon. Trailing Indianapolis 7-3, Dallas faced fourth-and-2 at the Colts’ 10-yard line. Rather than settle for another Brandon Aubrey field goal, the Cowboys elected to keep their offense on the field. Dak Prescott looked toward Ferguson, who made a tremendous adjustment on the football with Colts safety Cam Bynum in coverage. Ferguson displayed strong hands and the ability to battle a very bright sun, while maintaining possession through the catch. The 10-yard touchdown gave Dallas a 10-7 lead and capped a 15-play drive that began late in the first quarter. Jake Ferguson fourth down touchdown! DALvsIND on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/SQTPeUplgs — NFL (@NFL) November 8, 2026 As for Ferguson, he has come under criticism lately and this was exactly the type of response he and the Cowboys needed. Ferguson didn’t just make a difficult catch. He delivered in a situation where failure would have meant leaving points on the field, that’s pressure and he came through. It also rewarded Dallas for its aggressive decision-making and gave the offense some much-needed confidence. Now we’ll see how severe his injury turns out to be. 2. CeeDee Lamb lets loose in the secondary 2nd Quarter | 0:28 remaining | 1st-and-10 at Indianapolis 44-yard line Sometimes all it takes is one busted coverage to change the tide. With less than a minute remaining in the first half, Dallas was protecting a narrow 10-7 lead. The Colts had an opportunity to drain the remaining clock, but a holding penalty pushed Indianapolis backward. Keenan Allen’s subsequent sideline reception stopped the clock, allowing Dallas to preserve a timeout. That was the opportunity Dallas needed. The Cowboys regained possession at their own 25-yard line with 49 seconds remaining. After a nine-yard Javonte Williams run, Prescott connected with Lamb for 22 yards on third-and-1, advancing the ball to the Indianapolis 44-yard line with 38 seconds remaining. Then came the explosive play of the first half. CeeDee TD! Dak Prescott connects with CeeDee Lamb to add on six for the @dallascowboys 📺: FOX/FOX One pic.twitter.com/S1SuT4BFDz — FOX Sports: NFL (@NFLonFOX) November 8, 2026 On first-and-10, Lamb ran free through the Colts’ secondary after a coverage breakdown, and Prescott found his star receiver for a 44-yard touchdown. Just like that, Dallas turned a three-point advantage into a 17-7 halftime lead. The significance of this sequence cannot be overstated. Dallas had struggled to create separation, but the combination of defensive pressure, clock management, Prescott’s execution, and Lamb’s explosive ability completely changed the momentum entering halftime. Granted, the Cowboy would eventually surrender the two-score lead later, but they mismanaged the end of half against the Arizona Cardinals last week. This was progress albeit incremental. It was also a reminder of why Lamb remains the most dangerous weapon in the Cowboys’ passing attack and why you take the very, very good with the occasional very bad as we saw today. 3. Quinnen Williams Forces a Game-Changing Turnover 4th Quarter | 9:55 remaining | 1st-and-10 at Dallas 18-yard line There are defensive plays that look good on the stat sheet, and then there are plays that completely alter the direction of a game. Quinnen Williams delivered the latter. With Dallas clinging to a 20-17 lead, Indianapolis was threatening deep inside Cowboys territory. The Colts had moved the football effectively, aided by Dallas penalties, and appeared positioned to take the lead. Jonathan Taylor took the handoff, but Williams penetrated the backfield and stopped the running back while forcing the football loose. Shemar James recovered the fumble and returned it 11 yards before an unsportsmanlike conduct penalty pushed Dallas backward. Cowboys come right back with a takeaway of their own! DALvsIND on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/NVQtl0FpYU — NFL (@NFL) November 8, 2026 Williams had prevented Indianapolis from potentially taking control of the game. The play also illustrated why Williams’ presence along the defensive front matters so much. Earlier in the contest, his ability to disrupt the pocket helped create problems for Daniel Jones. Later, his pressure contributed to a holding penalty that stalled another Colts possession. Williams repeatedly made Indianapolis account for his presence. The Cowboys needed a defensive difference-maker, and Williams provided exactly that when the stakes were highest. 4. Oh Boy, Flournoy! Flournoy does his best Pickens impression 4th Quarter | 1:37 remaining | 1st-and-10 at Dallas 35-yard line Just when it appeared the Cowboys might let another winnable game slip away, Ryan Flournoy delivered the biggest reception of his afternoon. Indianapolis had taken a 23-20 lead following Spencer Shrader’s 50-yard field goal with 1:41 remaining. Dallas needed at least three points to force overtime, but with only 97 seconds remaining, the Cowboys couldn’t afford to waste opportunities. Prescott wasted no time. title: NFL trade deadline 2026: Denver Broncos latest news and rumors
summary: The NFL trade deadline is Tuesday, November 10th at 2 p.m. MT, and our Denver Broncos could be an active team prior to the deadline. They have been widely connected to Colts star running back Jonathan Taylor in the days leading up to the deadline, but according to 9NEWS Denver’s Mike Klis, the team could […]
full_text: DENVER, CO - NOVEMBER 1: Head coach Sean Payton of the Denver Broncos looks at the scoreboard during the second quarter against the Kansas City Chiefs at Empower Field at Mile High on November 1, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images The NFL trade deadline is Tuesday, November 10th at 2 p.m. MT, and our Denver Broncos could be an active team prior to the deadline. They have been widely connected to Colts star running back Jonathan Taylor in the days leading up to the deadline , but according to 9NEWS Denver’s Mike Klis, the team could explore adding a weapon or two to their offense. He mentions running back, tight end, and wide receiver as the positions that they could add. With Harvey injury and Badie also on IR and injuries across the offense, would expect Broncos to explore adding a weapon or two before trade deadline (RB, TE, WR). https://t.co/TSad3tJ2d3 — MikeKlis9NEWS (@mikeklis9news) October 31, 2026 Looking at the Broncos’ needs heading into the deadline, the most glaring one is running back. Now, the emergence of rookie running back Jonah Coleman helps, but the Broncos still need more from the position. RJ Harvey and Tyler Badie are on the injured reserve, and veteran JK Dobbins has been struggling all season. So, adding another back to pair with Coleman would make sense. The question is, will they go big and add a Jonathan Taylor or Breece Hall? Or make a smaller move for someone like Tony Pollard or someone else? Klis mentions wide receiver, and while it may not be the most pressing need right now, it could be in a few months. Jaylen Waddle has not performed as expected thus far; Courtland Sutton will be 32 next season and has a large cap hit(Also restructured his deal and could be off the team next season); Pat Bryant has been very good, but has been on the IR; Marvin Mims is a pending free agent, while Troy Franklin is buried on the depth chart. Could the Broncos be looking to add a wide receiver who could contribute to this team this season and moving forward? This doesn’t seem as likely, but I wouldn’t rule it out if the right deal comes their way. As for tight end, I don’t know. The only name that could move the needle and that might be available is Dallas Goedert, but is that even worth it? He would certainly improve that room, but the Broncos really do not utilize their tight ends in the passing game. Evan Engram has had a disappointing year, and blocking specialist Nate Adkins leads the group (and, funny enough, the team) in TD receptions with 3, but he only has 6 total catches thus far. We’ll be tracking all the Broncos news and rumors throughout the weekend and right up to the deadline. It’s supposed to be an active deadline, so we’ll see if our Denver Broncos make any splashes or not in the coming days. title: Broncos at Panthers: The No Bull Review
summary: The phrase I kept hearing heading into this game was the dreaded “trap game.” This plucky Carolina Panthers team was supposed to catch the Denver Broncos napping as they look forward to their bye week after a grueling game with the Kansas City Chiefs. Rest assured, Broncos Country, that this Broncos team does not overlook […]
full_text: CHARLOTTE, NORTH CAROLINA - NOVEMBER 08: Devon Key #26 of the Denver Broncos intercepts a pass during the third quarter against the Carolina Panthers at Bank of America Stadium on November 08, 2026 in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by Grant Halverson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The phrase I kept hearing heading into this game was the dreaded “trap game.” This plucky Carolina Panthers team was supposed to catch the Denver Broncos napping as they look forward to their bye week after a grueling game with the Kansas City Chiefs. Rest assured, Broncos Country, that this Broncos team does not overlook anyone. The Panthers fired their former defensive coordinator, Ejiro Evero, leading up to this game. They added some tweaks to their defense. They have a seriously talented quarterback in Bryce Young. All to no avail. The Broncos adjusted. They adapted. They overcame all obstacles. It is just who they are and what they do. This was a hell of a win for the Broncos. Losing both Jaylen Waddle and Riley Moss was rough. While the offense did a good job of staying on track, the defense was honestly shook with the loss of Moss. It completely changed how the defense played, which led to the defense needing to rely on turning the ball over more than playing consistent, effective defense like we are used to. Offense Week after week, this offense continues to evolve in a positive direction. The passing game looked arguably the best it has all season (granted it was against a very dinged-up secondary). The run game had significant trouble being a focal point against the Panthers’ tenacious front. They made do and made plays in fits and spurts on the ground while mainly leaning on Nix’s arm to do the bulk of the offensive work. The playcalling this week was honestly some of the best I’ve seen all season. I personally would like to see a more balanced approach, but that wasn’t going to work this week against this opponent. It was refreshing to see a matchup like this where there’s an obvious weakness in the defensive secondary that the Broncos fully took advantage of. Sean Payton started the game wanting Nix to attack the secondary, and that never changed until it was time to turtle up and run the clock. Quarterbacks Bo Nix sure did respect the position of quarterback in this game (AMARITE, Ditzpatrick!?). He went downfield early and often in this game with air yard numbers that would make Patrick Mahomes cry (still waiting for the talking heads to start wondering if Mahomes is washed with how short his throws are lately). He did throw another boneheaded pass where he decided the route he was throwing immediately and was completely oblivious to the underneath defender that earned him an interception. Outside of that, I thought he played a superb game. What I liked most about Nix in this game was how often he was looking off defenders to set up his passes. What’s cool about this is that it not only manipulates the defenders, but shows how much he’s getting in sync with the receivers and knows where their routes are. He was impressively quick on the trigger a couple of times during these look-offs. Line The biggest thing causing this offense to look clunky is the line. Ben Powers was practically a turnstile on more than a few plays. Luke Wattenburg had a couple of head-scratchers. Mike McGlinchey just got beat multiple times (he got spun backwards on one play I saw that had me seeing visions of Ty Sambrailo). The front for the Panthers won the day from what I saw throughout the game. It honestly had me wondering if they changed up how they were playing vs. what Evero had them doing previously. I’d be curious to know what Panthers fans who know the game would have to say on this…hit us up in the comments. Is your front just that good, or did they change things up? Running Backs Jonah Coleman rightly took over the starting duties this game and emerged as the #1 RB on the team. With the line having so many troubles, he wasn’t producing what we would like to see. He was able to cook with what he was given, though. He showed impressive burst and speed on his touchdown run around the edge. He was also very effective as a receiver out of the backfield with 4 catches for 31 yards. The fumble late in the game was very tough to see. I feel like he and Nix will both need to work their pitches during the bye week to shore that up. JK Dobbins made an excellent cutback and jump step to gain 11 on his first run. He only got 4 carries on the day total, with his other 3 gaining only 7 yards. Receivers Welcome back, Pat Bryant! Our young rock star of a receiver got a 12-yard gain on his second catch off a crossing route. He caught an 11-yard pass to move the chains in the 3rd quarter. Bryant benefitted from blown coverage for the easiest touchdown he will ever catch late in the 4th quarter for 26 yards. On one hand, Courtland Sutton led the team in targets and was a big focus for the offense. On the other hand, they missed 4 of his targets. He is cash money close to the goal line, though, with a quick slant to put 6 on the board. I like seeing him get the timing throws from Nix that allow him to use his frame to protect the catch. Evan Engram had a pretty active game this week as well. He took a screen for 19 yards right behind a blitz. He ended the day with 4 catches for 33 yards. Troy Franklin got involved late with a couple of really nice routes for 1st-down completions, with one of them inside the red zone. He caught another 13-yard pass on a curl. It was good to see Franklin step up and make plays with Waddle out. Franklin isn’t Waddle, but he produced this week when his number was called. Defense The defense had some pretty significant struggles off and on throughout this game. As the 4th quarter rolled around, it appeared to me that Bryce Young was going to be able to have success passing all the way down to the wire. The only way this team was going to be able to win was with some big-time turnovers. Vance Joseph put his players in position to make it work, and they provided the kind of soul-wrenching turnovers that make a fan base want to cry about refs, complain about takebacks, and call your team a bunch of big meanies. This was a gutsy victory for the Broncos defense. They were already out Kris Abrams-Draine, Talanoa Hufanga, and Brandon Jones to start the game. They lost Riley Moss early and seemed to me to switch mainly to zone calls that kept the defense in front of them which just isn’t what this defense is used to doing. It got the job done even though it wasn’t pretty. Many watching the game were complaining about the soft zone calls, but I don’t know that you’d like it if we just put in our normal match zone with the group of depth players we had on the field. Look, the players and coaches talk really big about “Next man up.” They talk about how they expect the backups to come in and have no drop-off. That’s absolute horse shit, honestly. I’m sorry, but Jahdae Barron is no Riley Moss. Taylor Rapp is no Huff. JL Skinner is no Jones. Devon Key isn’t either. These guys are lower down on the depth chart for a reason. Expecting them to be able to press man or match zone in one-on-ones across the board would have been disastrous. The one ace card the Panthers have is a superb young quarterback who knows how to drop dimes. All it takes is one bad half-step by a backup corner or safety, and it would have been 50+ yard touchdowns multiple times. Don’t get me wrong, I hate soft zone looks where your guys are starting 8 yards off their guys and give up pass after pass, just like all of you. The game of NFL football is not so simple that you can just wave a wand and turn a 4th string player into a solid press-man defender. Feel free to disagree, but my hat is off to Vance Joseph. Great defensive coordinators take a game like this and find a way to get the job done. The players made the plays to get the win. Joseph called the game in a way that put them in a position to make…

title: Horse Tracks: Are the Broncos lucky…or just good?
summary: Good morning, Broncos Country! In my pickleball league, we have a common saying, “Better to be lucky than good.” But if Sean Payton were playing in my league, he’d say that because we were good, we got lucky. At least I assume he’d say that…since that’s how he feels about the Broncos’ 16-game streak of […]
full_text: CHARLOTTE, NORTH CAROLINA - NOVEMBER 08: Devon Key #26 of the Denver Broncos celebrates after defeating the Carolina Panthers 26-21 at Bank of America Stadium on November 08, 2026 in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by Todd Kirkland/Getty Images) | Getty Images Good morning, Broncos Country! In my pickleball league, we have a common saying, “Better to be lucky than good.” But if Sean Payton were playing in my league, he’d say that because we were good, we got lucky. At least I assume he’d say that…since that’s how he feels about the Broncos’ 16-game streak of winning one-score games. “When those things keep falling your way, that’s not by accident,” he said. He makes a good point. You create your own luck. And while the Broncos have had some “lucky breaks,” it was because they played well enough to create those situations. Devon Key’s interception wasn’t lucky. It was a good (really good) heads-up play because he was focused on the ball. Last week’s amazing false start to save the day against the Chiefs wasn’t “lucky,” it was a good (really good) Mile High crowd making a huge difference. And 16 wins in a row by one score or less — an NFL record by the Broncos — is not luck. Devon Key on the Broncos winning 16-straight one-score wins: "I wouldn't say it's luck" — Zac Stevens (@ZacStevens) November 8, 2026 As Bo Nix would argue, it’s character, toughness and competitiveness. It’s also skill and practice. “We’re just comfortable in that moment,” Nix said, noting it’s not like they want it to only be winning by one score, but it’s a lot better than losing by one. “Until I figure something out about how to change it, just glad we’re on this side and winning them and not in a streak of losing them.” Nix is also not too interested in the streak, as much as he is what it means — the Broncos keep winning games. “I don’t care. …in 10, 15 years, nobody’s going to care about [the streak],” he added. “They’re going to talk about wins … but it’s cool right now. It’s great as we go, but it definitely would be nice to win by more than a score.” Yes. Yes it would. This is insane: Bo Nix is 8-1 the last two season when trailing by 8 or fewer points in the 4th quarter, per @doug_clawson . The rest of the NFL has a win percentage of 29.6% in those situations. pic.twitter.com/QjxSME7B54 — Zac Stevens (@ZacStevens) November 9, 2026 But as long as the team and its QB have the mentality that getting that go-ahead score, or saving it, is just something they need to do — while playing a lot of really good teams — then it’s probably going to keep happening. “I’ll be honest, it seems like it’s always the same feeling. There’s always a look in the huddle that, like, hey guys, we don’t have a choice right here. We got to go make something out of it,” Nix said, highlighting the second-half touchdowns on Sunday. “Those were really, really important.” Nix highlighted the touchdown drives — the first to go ahead after getting down, 14-13, and the second to extend that lead, 26-14, which became crucial when the Panthers fought for a comeback of their own and scored a touchdown. “I thought that was the best part of the game because it showed that we stacked two drives together, two critical moments and gave our defense some rest on the sideline with those longer drives,” Nix said. “Also, a good cushion and they did just a good job responding and scoring.” But that rest also allowed the defense to be fresh for the “lucky breaks” that came its way. Like after a near lost fumble on the offense’s three-and-out, giving the Panthers three minutes on the clock to try for the comeback win, only to be stymied by a strip sack from Nik Bonitto. “That was big,” said Payton. “We talked about the ball security, and it finally came and it was a huge play, obviously. It was a huge play.” Not lucky. Just good. "This Denver Broncos offense has a lot more rhythm right now.. Bo Nix looks more confident and he's really cutting it loose.. He's looked a lot more like he did last year the last couple of weeks" ~ @danorlovsky7 #PMSLive pic.twitter.com/gFgMbSRtyh — Pat McAfee (@PatMcAfeeShow) November 9, 2026

title: The Broncos are riding high into their bye after comeback victory over Panthers
summary: The Denver Broncos, the comeback kings of the National Football League, pulled off another nailbiter on Sunday. Another impressive fourth quarter comeback was the big factor in their 26-21 win against the Carolina Panthers on Sunday. The Broncos have set a new NFL record with sixteen-straight wins in one-score games. On top of that, they […]
full_text: Nov 8, 2026; Charlotte, North Carolina, USA; Denver Broncos wide receiver Pat Bryant (13) celebrates after scoring a touchdown against the Carolina Panthers during the second half at Bank of America Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Bob Donnan-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Denver Broncos, the comeback kings of the National Football League, pulled off another nailbiter on Sunday. Another impressive fourth quarter comeback was the big factor in their 26-21 win against the Carolina Panthers on Sunday. The Broncos have set a new NFL record with sixteen-straight wins in one-score games. On top of that, they have moved to 7-2 on the season and still hold the top spot in the AFC West. Another game, another mark in the win column. This year’s Broncos haven’t been at their best. Nevertheless, they’ve reeled off five victories in a row and enter the bye week with a lot of momentum in their favor. Now, Denver gets to enjoy their bye week and will have some much-needed time off to recuperate and recalibrate before their Week 11 matchup against the Las Vegas Raiders. After yesterday’s victory, Head Coach Sean Payton reflected on the team’s odds-defying streak of wins. The probability of the Broncos winning sixteen of those close affairs in a row? Presumably 150 million to one. While the wins are great, Payton isn’t content and knows the team still has a lot of work to do to get better in the second half of the season. “Well, part of it pisses me off because there’s been a few of them that you would say shouldn’t have been one-score games and then obviously there’s some that are. Look, they’ve been great. We knew coming in Thursday, we just knew the type of team we were playing,” stated Paton. “They’ve been doing some really explosive things on offense. They were banged up certainly on defense as we were. We’ll take this break, but we still have to be—and it’s not that you’re never satisfied—but we still have some work to do.” The Broncos struggled to find an answer to the Panthers’ offensive prowess late in the first half and at the beginning of the second half. Fourth-year quarterback Bryce Young was able to carve up Denver’s depleted secondary and march down the field numerous times to keep them in the game. At times, the Broncos were their own worst enemies. The penalties and miscues that happened late could have very well cost them the game. But when the stakes were at their highest, the defense was able to force several turnovers and the offense ignited in the fourth quarter to lead the team to their seventh win of the season. One issue that has plagued Denver all season long was third down conversions. Entering the game, they were one of the league’s worst converting less than 30-percent of those opportunities. Against the Panthers, the team was 6-of-10 and had a hot streak late in the game that was a huge difference maker. Quite impressive, considering they were down one of their top receiving targets for the entire second half. Quarterback Bo Nix took time after the game to highlight the other wide receivers who stepped up and were clutch when it mattered most. “We got plays for Jaylen that somebody else has to step in and take. That’s what, in my opinion, was the fun part of today. That was really cool to see Troy, Pat, and Marvin step up and make plays when their numbers were called,” stated Nix. “Even though they didn’t have reps at it all week, they studied and knew what they were supposed to do. To me, that’s fun football, when you’re in there and your back’s against the wall and you just have to figure out a way to go get a first down,” added Nix. Over the first nine weeks of the season, the Broncos have shown a lot of grit and guts. Their resilience is certainly one of their best qualities. No matter how tough things get, they don’t seem to flinch in the face of adversity. In fact, it almost seems like they relish it. Denver’s second half slate of opponents is much easier than the gauntlet they have faced to start the season. That may give them an inside track to have a shot at the AFC’s top playoff seed for a second consecutive season. However, they will need to play much better overall in order to make that happen. One question that looms large is whether or not the Broncos’ brass feels confident that the current group of players are good enough to accomplish that. Coach Payton noted he likes this year’s squad, but will certainly be leaving no stone unturned when it comes to potentially making additions before tomorrow’s trade deadline. “That’s impossible to predict. We’ll discuss what’s out there, and I think we’ll see what happens. But I like this team. There’s room for us to get better, but I like this team a lot. We just got to take advantage of the position we’re sitting in right now.” At 7-2 and atop the AFC West, Denver is in a great spot. Will they make a big move that can help solidify their status as a true Super Bowl contender? We will know that answer to that in the next thirty hours.

title: Broncos Stock Up, Stock Down: Week 10 vs. Panthers
summary: The Broncos did it again! After yet another 4th-quarter comeback, the Broncos won their 5th straight game with their victory over the Carolina Panthers and improved to 7-2 on the season. Like every Broncos game, this game was a rollercoaster from the start. They took an early 10-0 lead, but the Panthers came charging back […]
full_text: CHARLOTTE, NORTH CAROLINA - NOVEMBER 08: Jonah Coleman #20 of the Denver Broncos scores a touchdown against the Carolina Panthers during the fourth quarter at Bank of America Stadium on November 08, 2026 in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by Todd Kirkland/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Broncos did it again! After yet another 4th-quarter comeback, the Broncos won their 5th straight game with their victory over the Carolina Panthers and improved to 7-2 on the season. Like every Broncos game, this game was a rollercoaster from the start. They took an early 10-0 lead, but the Panthers came charging back and were on the verge of going up 21-13. Then it happened. Devon Key’s incredible interception flipped this game upside down and gave the momentum back to the Broncos, and they never looked back. Things did get tight there at the end, but Nik Bonitto called game with a clutch strip-sack, and the Broncos went on to celebrate another remarkable win. Stock up and stock down is a weekly series where I go through the Denver Broncos’ 53-man roster and tell you which Broncos players’ stock is going up, down, or remains unchanged. After yet another 4th-quarter comeback and one-score victory, we have plenty of stocks trending in the right direction, with a few notable stocks going in the wrong direction. Quarterback Bo Nix – Stock up slightly: I thought Bo Nix played well overall on Sunday. He made some good throws and was leading the Broncos up and down the field against this Panthers secondary full of backups. However, he did have the interception and the off-target pitch late in the game. This was Nix’s first interception since the one he threw vs. the Rams, where his arm was hit mid-throw, so I am not going to knock him too much for it. I am going with stock slightly up. He threw for 237 yards and 2 touchdowns, which is a stat line I will take each and every week from Nix. He is beginning to look more and more like the quarterback we saw last season and I believe that will continue as the team emerges from their bye week. Jarrett Stidham – Unchanged: Remains the Broncos veteran backup. Sam Ehlinger – Unchanged: Remains the Broncos’ third-string emergency quarterback. Running Back Jonah Coleman – Stock up: The takeover has happened. Jonah Coleman played 58 of the 75 snaps on Sunday (77%) and was the unquestioned starter of the Broncos’ backfield. He did not disappoint either. He had 17 carries for 57 yards, which is more of an offensive line problem than a running back problem (more on that later), but did score another touchdown and had an additional 4 receptions for 31 yards. Altogether, he had 21 touches for 88 yards and a touchdown. A pretty solid showing for the Broncos rookie running back, but we’ll have to see if they add to this running back room prior to the trade deadline this week. JK Dobbins – Stock down: 4 carries for 18 yards and a 15% snap share. That right there says it all. Dobbins has clearly fallen out of favor in the Broncos’ backfield, and his time with the team could be coming to an end if they add another back at the deadline. We’ll see what happens, but his role has significantly decreased since Jonah Coleman returned from injury. Cody Schrader – Unchanged: Schrader was elevated from the practice squad but did not have a major role in Sunday’s game. Adam Prentice – Unchanged: Played 15 snaps on offense while also being a main contributor on special teams. He has his role on this team and he does it well. Wide Receiver Jaylen Waddle – Unchanged: This was going to be a big Jaylen Waddle game, but unfortunately, the Broncos’ explosive wide receiver was knocked out of the game early after he suffered a concussion from a dirty hit by a Panthers defender. Before he left the game, he had 1 catch for 22 yards and was destined for more. Courtland Sutton – Stock up: I thought Sutton played solid on Sunday. It wasn’t a huge game for the Broncos veteran wide receiver, but he led the wide receivers with 85% of the snaps and had 5 catches for 45 yards and a touchdown. He caught everything thrown his way and made multiple big catches on third down for the Broncos. A solid overall showing. Pat Bryant – Stock up: Welcome back, Pat Bryant! The Broncos’ second-year wide receiver returned from IR before the game and made an immediate impact on the offense. He led the Broncos in receiving yards with 56 and had what ended up being the game-winning 26-yard touchdown late in the 4th quarter. I think we will continue seeing Bryant make more and more impact plays as the season progresses. Troy Franklin – Stock up: Like Sutton, I thought Troy played a solid overall game that nearly ended up being a big game. He finished with 3 catches for 31 yards, but had multiple clutch catches on third down late in the game. However, he nearly had a touchdown right before halftime, but a Panthers defender was able to knock the ball away. It was an incredible pass by Nix to Franklin who was open down the seam. Close, but not cigar. Marvin Mims – Unchanged: Mims did not do a whole lot on Sunday, but played his role. He saw limited snaps on offense but wasn’t able to do much with them and continued being a kick return specialist for them. Lil’Jordan Humphrey – Unchanged: He was inactive. Tight End Adam Trautman – Stock up: He continues to lead the Broncos tight ends in snaps and has seen his role in the passing game increase a little bit in back-to-back games. He had a 20+ yard reception vs. the Chiefs and vs. the Panthers, he had 2 receptions for 15 yards. Nothing to write home about, but the bar is low. Evan Engram – Stock down: The stock down has little to do with his performance on Sunday, but more to do with the reports that the Broncos are looking to trade for a tight end. If they acquire a tight end, it will be a pass-catcher in all likelihood, which would negatively impact Engram’s role and potentially even his roster spot. Now, nothing has happened, but the fact that they are looking isn’t great for Engram. On Sunday, Engram did have 4 catches for 33 yards, which is one of his better performances this season, so we’ll see if anything changes here in the coming days. Nate Adkins – Unchanged: Played 24% of the snaps on offense, but primarily played special teams and made a nice tackle on a return late in the game. He has his role, and he fills it well. Dallen Bentley – Unchanged: Remained inactive. Offensive Line Garett Bolles – Unchanged: Continues to be one of the better blindside protectors in the NFL. Ben Powers – Stock down: The middle of the Broncos’ line struggled on Sunday, and Powers was 50% of the problem. It’s hard to get a run game going when you’re allowing immediate pressure. Luke Wattenberg – Stock down: Here is the other 50% of the problem. Wattenberg is praised for his intelligence, but he was knocked back a bit on Sunday and allowed immediate interior pressure. Both need to play better or it doesn’t matter who our running back is. Quinn Meinerz – Stock up: Stud. Mike McGlinchey – Unchanged: Can’t say I really noticed him positively or negatively on Sunday, which usually is a good thing. Alex Palczewski – Unchanged: Played 5% of the snaps on Sunday, but maybe should see some time at left guard moving forward. Matt Peart – Unchanged: Played on special teams. Alex Forsyth – Unchanged: Played on special teams. Kage Casey – Unchanged: The rookie remained inactive, but maybe should see time at left guard? Defensive Line Zach Allen – Unchanged: I expected the defensive line to dominate a struggling Panthers offensive line, and that did not happen. DJ Jones – Unchanged: Has been solid for the Broncos this season, but the Panthers had success on the ground vs. them. Malcolm Roach – Unchanged: Has been a very underrated part of the Broncos’ defensive line this season, but the unit struggled throughout most of the game. Sai’vion Jones – Unchanged: Played 35% of the snaps and saw a minor boost in snaps with Uwazurike now on the IR. Jordan Jackson – Unchanged:…
