title: Carson Wentz prompts more baseless Stafford trade rumors
summary: The Minnesota Vikings have such a stark contrast between their elite defense and their tremendous issues at quarterback that Rams fans couldn’t expect L.A. to go through one rough patch without hearing Matthew Stafford trade speculation. The Vikings need a quarterback, Kevin O’Connell used to be Sean McVay’s offensive coordinator, and the Rams are flirting […]
full_text: (Photo by Patrick Smith/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Minnesota Vikings have such a stark contrast between their elite defense and their tremendous issues at quarterback that Rams fans couldn’t expect L.A. to go through one rough patch without hearing Matthew Stafford trade speculation. The Vikings need a quarterback, Kevin O’Connell used to be Sean McVay’s offensive coordinator, and the Rams are flirting with disaster as Puka Nacua joins the walking wounded. Well, sorry if you were waiting for another blockbuster trade. The Los Angeles Rams are not going to trade Matthew Stafford ahead of the NFL trade deadline on Tuesday. It’s an idea that makes little to no sense for the Rams, prompted by an especially bad quarterback performance during a standalone game on Monday night. Stafford isn’t having his best season and Los Angeles isn’t even guaranteed a playoff spot at this point, but nothing this franchise has done would indicate they’re interested in such a hard reset. That hasn’t stopped X from speculating about “why it makes sense” anyway. STAFFORD TRADE POTENTIAL This entire thought came to be during Monday Night Football in Week 9, which saw the Minnesota Vikings fall to the Buffalo Bills 23-6 largely because Carson Wentz played one of the worst games in recent memory: 8-of-25, 81 yards, 2 interceptions, a lost fumble on a backwards pass. He was terrible, the Vikings offense wasted a typically stellar effort by their defense and now a team that was once 6-0 has lost consecutive games and is spiraling offensively. There is no hope coming in the form of Kyler Murray, whose “serviceable” stats overstate how limited he is as a passer and holding back the offense by not being able to throw in the middle of the field and isn’t as fast as he used to be. ESPN’s entire broadcast team, from Joe Buck and Troy Aikman in the booth to Scott Van Pelt during SportsCenter after the game openly hypothesized about Minnesota making a move for a quarterback so as not to waste an incredible season from Brian Flores’s defense. That sentiment permeated social media during the game, too. Hear me out. The Rams trade Stafford to the Vikings. They probably aren’t Super Bowl bound anyways with all the offensive injuries + they used a first on Ty Simpson, so just commit. Get some picks. Stafford goes to a 6-2 team that’s only missing a QB. — Kurt Benkert (@KurtBenkert) November 10, 2026 Former NFL quarterback of two career snaps fame Kurt Benkert broached the idea of the Vikings acquiring Stafford from the Rams on Twitter/X, though he wasn’t the only poster to propose or wish for that to come to fruition. It makes sense from the perspective of trying to wishcast a talented quarterback to a potential contender in order to create excitement at the trade deadline, something every Madden player has done in franchise mode at some point. It falls apart, however, when you consider the other team that would have to consummate the deal. I’ve been getting calls all night, and at this point, the rumors aren’t just circulating. They’re picking up serious steam. I’m being told the Los Angeles Rams and Minnesota Vikings are heavily engaged in discussions surrounding a potential BLOCKBUSTER trade that would send… pic.twitter.com/pXvwUyX8yi — El Pepe (@thestevieborys) November 10, 2026 RAMS TRADE DEADLINE DECISION Obviously, this year hasn’t gone according to plan for the Rams. Superstar acquisition Myles Garrett is finally back and is already playing at an All-Pro level, but injuries continue to debilitate the roster that was thought to be the best in the NFL entering the season. Puka Nacua has shouldered a ton of the passing game load but is now headed to injured reserve . Davante Adams has been out for several weeks now. Terrence Ferguson still isn’t ready to play . The offensive line suffered a blow this week with Steve Avila getting hurt , too. Another year…Another trade deadline of people who don't know anything about #Rams football linking Matthew Stafford to the Vikings. — JAKE OLIVER ELLENBOGEN (@JKBOGEN) November 10, 2026 But Los Angeles entered the 2026 season as the odds-on Super Bowl favorites, and despite that rash of injuries and a few difficult losses it’s still in the hunt for a playoff berth, and from there it’s anyone’s game. With the Arizona Cardinals on deck and set to start rookie Carson Beck for the first time, the week that they placed top receiver Michael Wilson on IR, the Rams stand a good chance to be 6-4. There’s still too much on the table for the Rams to punt on the season and commit to a rebuild right now. You’ve got a couple more months of Aaron Donald before he wraps up his career again. The running game has been excellent again this year. Ty Simpson, their hopeful quarterback of the future, still hasn’t taken an NFL snap, and it’s hard to imagine he’s ready for the spotlight regardless of the expectations thrust upon him. Stafford hasn’t played up to his MVP level, and to complete a run to a championship he needs to play better . But that’s no reason to give up on him and the 2026 campaign now. It’s more like the Rams add star power to the roster than ship it away. The Vikings may still find a trade for a veteran quarterback to buoy their team, whether it’s a safe pick like Kirk Cousins (also proposed by plenty of social media users, podcast hosts and more) or a more reckless pick like Justin Herbert (admittedly, proposed by a friend in a group chat during Monday Night Football). But it’s not going to be the reigning MVP who they acquire. The Rams didn’t go all in with big-name acquisition after big-name acquisition this offseason just to pull the plug midway through the year when they still have a winning record. That trade concept is a fun “what if?” scenario, but its grip on reality ends there.
author: Brendan Dzwierzynski

title: The Rams need Matthew Stafford to play like an MVP
summary: The Los Angeles Rams are 5-4 and still in the NFC playoff picture, but the version of Matthew Stafford they have gotten through nine weeks is not the one that carried them last season. Stafford currently has 16 touchdowns and nine interceptions with a 90.6 passer rating. That is functional. It’s nowhere near “MVP” level. […]
full_text: The Los Angeles Rams are 5-4 and still in the NFC playoff picture, but the version of Matthew Stafford they have gotten through nine weeks is not the one that carried them last season. Stafford currently has 16 touchdowns and nine interceptions with a 90.6 passer rating. That is functional. It’s nowhere near “MVP” level. Last year Stafford was manufacturing big-time throws and taking care of the football. He has always been prone to mistakes. But this year has reached a higher frequency and there is less of the good to offset. The gap is evident in the efficiency metrics that separate good from elite. Stafford’s big-time throw rate has cratered from 7.7% to roughly 3% this year. His Pro Football Focus (PFF) offensive grade sits in the upper 60’s, good for no better than 20th among qualified quarterbacks. That is not the profile of a player who is elevating the offense around him. It’s the mark of someone who is mostly managing a system, if not part of the problem. The distinction matters because the supporting cast has not been built to absorb a decline in quarterback play. The Rams spent all offseason retooling their defense. The tradeoff brought minimal reinforcements on offense. Puka Nacua, who will now miss at least the next four games , has been asked to handle an outsized share of targets and production. Even when Nacua is available, the rest of the skill players have failed to consistently generate explosive plays. The run game has taken a step forward in stretches. The offense overall has no chance without it. The defense is better. The offense is far from it. On a net basis, the Rams are a worse team. The Rams need Stafford to be the engine in life without Nacua. The last two games against poor competition demonstrate this offense’s current struggles. In two wins, Stafford combined for 385 yards, two touchdowns, and two interceptions. The Rams won both games. It did so without Stafford producing at the level that turns close battles into comfortable victories. That’s good enough against the lowly Chargers and Commanders. It won’t get the job done in a few weeks against the Green Bay Packers. It’s worth noting that Stafford is also managing an elbow issue that has required regular icing and maintenance. The Rams have downplayed the issue, but it landed the quarterback on the injury report last week. Stafford’s decline, although evident, does not require a dramatic injury narrative in order to explain. What is more concerning is the combination of workload, age, and a lesser supporting cast. The margin for error is gone because a lot of the high-end outcomes have disappeared. Last year’s version of Stafford was capable of overcoming some of these constraints. The 2026 quarterback has not shown the same capacity at any point. The Rams do not need Stafford to replicate his MVP stat line. They do need him to reclaim enough of his efficiency and decision-making that defined last season in order to raise the offense’s floor. Doing so requires fewer mistakes, more big-time throws, and production in the deep area of the field. We’ve seen Stafford carry the Rams against all odds before. He pushed young and unproven rosters to the playoffs in 2023 and 2024. The 2026 defense is better than those iterations. Even if the offensive talent is lesser, the team can likely get by scoring fewer points. If Matthew Stafford is truly the MVP, he will rise beyond the injury adversity to help the Rams reach the playoffs and keep their Super Bowl hopes alive. His team needs him more than ever.
author: JB Scott

title: Rams cannot replace Puka Nacua, may go with who they have
summary: The Los Angeles Rams will be without Puka Nacua for at least four weeks, and with the Tuesday’s trade deadline approaching, should the Rams make a big-time trade for a wide receiver? Whether they do or not, there is no replacing Nacua, who’s carried the offensive passing game since the Rams lost Davante Adams, who’s […]
full_text: The Los Angeles Rams will be without Puka Nacua for at least four weeks , and with the Tuesday’s trade deadline approaching, should the Rams make a big-time trade for a wide receiver? Whether they do or not, there is no replacing Nacua, who’s carried the offensive passing game since the Rams lost Davante Adams, who’s also on IR. If the Rams could make a blockbuster (or any) trade to save 2026, they would, but that may not be an option as the NFL trade period comes to its close. The Rams may choose to go with the group they have, injuries and all, and if they do, then they’ll need to play better. Change for the sake of change doesn’t guarantee success. Though it could be naive of McVay to not make major changes on offense this season, the group of pass catchers we’ve seen may be the group going forward as the Rams wait for guys to get healthy. Waiting for guys to get healthy has been a theme for the L.A. Rams this year. Who could the Rams add at receiver? L.A. has been rumored or speculated as linked to potentially trading for receivers like Josh Downs , Brian Thomas Jr. Stefon Diggs , George Pickens and more. Would any of these receivers do what Nacua does for L.A.’s offense? The run after catch, the physicality, maybe. The relationship he’s s built with Sean McVay, Matthew Stafford and the offense? Can any of the names above fill in well enough for both Nacua and Adams to make a trade worthwhile? The Rams would have to make the trade to find out. Can the Rams trade for a receiver who boosts the offense? Yes. They could also trade for a receiver who struggles to connect and build chemistry with Stafford as L.A.’s veteran quarterback is struggling currently with receivers like Tutu Atwell, Jordan Whittington, Tyler Higbee and Colby Parkinson. Players Stafford has worked with for years. Trading for a receiver like Thomas Jr. is splashy, but would he and Stafford work well together? Does he fit McVay’s scheme? Would a player like Pickens fit McVay’s culture? Are those receivers worth the Rams sending draft capital for? A trade does not guarantee the Rams a playoff spot Are there any receivers available for the Rams to get going into Week 10 that truly increase their odds at a playoff spot? Going into their 10th game of the year, the Rams sit at 9th in the NFC playoff picture , below the Seattle Seahawks. Below the entire NFC North. Well below the 49ers who sit atop the NFC. Injury is playing a role in the Rams struggles, but so is inconsistent offensive play and coaching. The defense for L.A. has overcome missing Myles Garrett, Trent McDuffie, Jaylen Watson, Aaron Donald, Nate Landman and more, but the defense for the Rams has been objectively better than their offense this year. In Week 9, the Rams failed to convert a third down until the second half. The offense had Nacua on the field. Trade or not, the offense needs to be better. The Rams chose to go into 2026 with this receiving group Though it would be financially tough , the Rams could make a trade or add someone new. Just because they could, doesn’t mean they should. And if they do, there is no guarantee that it would work. They can’t trade for Nacua to save their season, and there is no recreating Nacua in the aggregate . The Rams have options, but none of them may be able to help the Rams enough in 2026 to play past Week 18. The Rams had the entire offseason to seriously revamp or retool their receiver room. They didn’t. Was that a feature or a glitch? Due to injuries to Nacua, Adams and even Terrence Ferguson, L.A.‘s passing game has been glitching, but the Rams went into this year thinking their pass catchers were a feature. At this point in the season, it may be too late for a trade to patch it. The Rams may just have to play better with who they have.
author: Danny Stone

title: Sean McVay addresses Rams’ trade speculation
summary: The Los Angeles Rams have lost both Puka Nacua and Davante Adams to leg injuries recently, but head coach Sean McVay told reporters that he doesn’t expect the team to make a trade prior to Tuesday’s deadline, according to ESPN’s Sarah Barshop. McVay was specifically asked about Nacua’s injury and how it relates to the […]
full_text: The Los Angeles Rams have lost both Puka Nacua and Davante Adams to leg injuries recently, but head coach Sean McVay told reporters that he doesn’t expect the team to make a trade prior to Tuesday’s deadline, according to ESPN’s Sarah Barshop. McVay was specifically asked about Nacua’s injury and how it relates to the Rams’ willingness to make a move, implying that another receiver going on IR won’t change L.A.‘s stance. “I think you’ve got to look at all avenues,” McVay said, when it comes to addressing their injuries. Sean McVay had said he didn't expect LA to be active before the trade deadline. He was asked Monday whether Puka Nacua's injury affected that. “I think you’ve got to look at all avenues to try to be able to solve some of the issues or situations or scenarios that have come up." — Sarah Barshop (@sarahbarshop) November 9, 2026 The more transparent answer that McVay could have given is that the Rams don’t have enough money to make a trade. Not as things currently stand, at least. As I wrote weeks ago, the Rams are 32nd in salary cap space . They’d have to move money around to make something work, which makes you wonder if it’s really worth doing that for someone like Brian Thomas Jr who only has 10 catches in eight games despite playing for an offense coached by Liam Coen and in need of a star receiver. If the Rams add a veteran player before the deadline, they’ll need to double down even more future cap commitments to players who they probably want to be able to part ways with next year. Especially given how many important free agents are about to hit the market and potentially leave L.A. in 2027, including most of the offensive line, and Nacua . McVay doesn’t anticipate a trade. So we better anticipate an offense that doesn’t necessarily run through a wide receiver anymore.
author: Kenneth Arthur

title: Puka Nacua headed to IR with MCL, PCL injury in knee
summary: The Los Angeles Rams will be without their biggest offensive weapon for at least the next four games. Wide receiver Puka Nacua is headed to injured reserve after suffering MCL and PCL injuries to his knee, creating a significant challenge for Sean McVay and an offense that has consistently relied on his production. Nacua suffered […]
full_text: The Los Angeles Rams will be without their biggest offensive weapon for at least the next four games. Wide receiver Puka Nacua is headed to injured reserve after suffering MCL and PCL injuries to his knee , creating a significant challenge for Sean McVay and an offense that has consistently relied on his production. Nacua suffered the injury during Sunday’s 20-13 victory over the Washington Commanders. The injury occurred on the Rams’ final offensive possession when Nacua took a hard hit to his knee on a jet sweep. What initially appeared to be a concerning situation has now resulted in a trip to injured reserve and an extended absence. Rams WR Puka Nacua is likely to be placed injured reserve due to MCL and PCL sprains, per HC Sean McVay. pic.twitter.com/ONNnk78zbt — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) November 9, 2026 The timing is particularly unfortunate for Los Angeles. Nacua was coming off an outstanding performance against Washington, recording 14 receptions for 150 yards and a touchdown. He has been Matthew Stafford’s most dependable target and arguably the engine behind the Rams’ passing attack. Nacua has 70 catches for 715 yards and four touchdowns, averaging 102.1 yards per game. He led the NFL with 129 catches and 107.2 yards per game in 2025. Nacua’s production is rare and offenses rarely rely on one player as much as L.A. has put on their number one receiver over the last 3.5 seasons. With Nacua unavailable for the next four games, the Rams will need their remaining offensive playmakers to shoulder a much larger workload. Davante Adams is also on injured reserve, making the situation even more difficult for Stafford. Los Angeles still has postseason aspirations, but losing Nacua for the next month puts additional pressure on McVay to find offensive production elsewhere.
author: Steven Ridings

title: Should the Rams run more? Warren McClendon’s numbers say “yes”
summary: In their fifth game of the season decided by one touchdown or less, the Los Angeles Rams held off the Washington Commanders 20-13 on a sunny Sunday just outside the nation’s capitol. L.A. improved to 2-3 in those nail-biters, won its third consecutive game, and notched up to 5-4 for the season, tied for second […]
full_text: In their fifth game of the season decided by one touchdown or less, the Los Angeles Rams held off the Washington Commanders 20-13 on a sunny Sunday just outside the nation’s capitol. L.A. improved to 2-3 in those nail-biters, won its third consecutive game, and notched up to 5-4 for the season, tied for second place in the NFC West. While the Rams offense has been inconsistent at times, the offensive line has played well, particularly right tackle Warren McClendon. In his fourth NFL season and first as full-time starter, the 6’4” 315 right tackle played in every snap against the Commanders (75) and has not missed a rep in 2026, 634. ESPN rates McClendon as the #2 rated tackle with an 83 percent run block win rate and compliments it with a #11 ranking and 90 percent pass block win rate. As a unit, the Rams offensive line is rated #1 in run block win rate and #10 in pass block win rate for the season. Their 9.5 percent run stuff rate allowed is the lowest in the league and at 49.6 percent, the rushing success rate is #2. As successful as the Rams have been blocking for the run, the offense is only middle of the pack (16th) in rushing attempts per game (26.9). Should the Rams be running the ball more? Here’s a review of the snap counts from Sunday. Players, their snap counts and percentage of play time in bold. Quarterback Mathew Stafford (75, 100%) Staff just doesn’t look comfortable yet this season. His accuracy seems way off early in games and particularly when leading receivers. Indeed, the secondary receivers aren’t doing a lot to help, but there were just as many bad/off throws as dropped passes. To help him find rhythm, the Rams went no-huddle on 17 percent of plays, second highest of the season (Week 4 win over Philly, 22%), and normally under 10 percent. Running back Kyren Williams (48, 63%) Blake Corum (27, 36%) The Rams two-headed monster was again a force to reckon with, 26 carries for 103 yards. Could the Rams do a better job of using the run earlier in games? Yes, but at it’s core, the L.A. offense is pass-based, so when they run the ball 29 times, that’s a very good compliment. I like the jet sweeps, but also remember a time when the McVay offense could, and would use any number of players running them. Now it appears to be Puka Nacua or bust. Wide receiver Puka Nacua (70, 93%) Tutu Atwell (35, 47%) Konata Mumpfield (33, 44%) Jordan Whittington (4, 5%) CJ Daniels (1, 1%) Way too often, the Rams passing offense was “force it in to Nacua” and hope he can make play. Only seven total targets for the rest of the unit, although the drops don’t inspire confidence. After McVay talking about Daniels getting more opportunities, nada, zilch, nil. Nacua is a stud horse and the Rams should ride him, but every screen and jet sweep? That’s not fooling anybody anymore. Speaking of jet sweeps, giving Nacua the ball to milk clock towards the end of the game was senseless. Why? There was zero upside to that play call. Puka Nacua now has 70 receptions through seven games this season. 14 REC, 150 REC YDS, 1 TD, 15 RUSH YDS vs Commanders. He's putting himself right back in the OPOY conversation. https://t.co/s2lafxwoAV pic.twitter.com/WcoZi8XJ0F — Football Performances (@NFLPerformances) November 8, 2026 Tight end Colby Parkinson (55. 73%) Tyler Higbee (60, 80%) Davis Allen (42, 56%) L.A.’s offensive game plan really leaned into multiple tight ends, a 58 percent clip. Five catches on nine targets were split between Parkinson (4 of 4) and Higbee (2 of 5) for 26 yards. Allen was again a run blocking workhorse. Klare didn’t get an offensive snap after playing nearly half of last week’s game. Offensive line Alaric Jackson, Coleman Shelton, Kevin Dotson, Warren McClendon (75, 100%) Beaux Limmer (57, 76%) Steve Avila (18, 24%) Overall, a solid effort. I’m not sure exactly what the Rams can do about the delayed blitzes without a film deep dive. Limmer stepped in for Avila and played well. Special teams Two weeks in a row with no major gaffes. Nothing special either. Who knew that mediocrity would feel so good? Maybe it’s just me, but I thought there was a bit of a spark on Sunday. Defensive line Aaron Donald (47, 76%) Braden Fiske (48, 77%) Tyler Davis (22, 35%) Larrell Murchison (10, 16%) Ty Hamilton (12, 19%) While the Commanders are not a rushing juggernaut, limiting a team to 60 yards on 19 carries is good work. Donald and Fiske make an interesting pairing with their ability to shoot gaps. ESPN has Fiske at #11 in pass rush win rate for defensive tackles. Davis’ snaps are down for the season and way down from last year, it’s not that surprising with the Rams move away from traditional 5-2 fronts and into multiple looks and personnel at the line of scrimmage. Murchison was subbing in on the Commanders opening drive instead of Hamilton, but both of their snaps were down from last week. Edge Byron Young (51, 82%) Myles Garrett (37, 63%) Josiah Stewart (30, 48%) Wesley Bailey (17, 27%) The return of Garrett reverberated throughout the whole defensive front usage. For such a big human, his get-off and ability to dip and square off turning the corner on outside rushes is must-see football. Love that the Rams are going to line him up all over the defensive front. Young gets to go back to what he does best, be a rock solid E#2 that brings hustle and an all -around game. Stewart’s snaps are already trending down from early in the season and will likely settle into last years numbers, 33 to 40 percent. Bailey had a tough day setting the edge and took a terrible angle allowing a short pass to go for a long gain down the sideline. Myles Garrett has his 2nd sack! LARvsWAS on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/n2ihjRZbYN — NFL (@NFL) November 8, 2026 Off-ball linebacker Nate Landman (39, 63%) Omar Speights (21, 34%) Shaun Dolac (10, 16%) Landman played to form and Speights looked have had a third straight good game. Both their snaps were down for the second week in a row. Landman is down nearly 30 percent from his season highs, while Speights down by about half. Out of the blue, Dolac appeared for a handful of snaps. He got juked once, but had three tackles, a QB hit, and shared a sack in just a handful of reps. Safety Quentin Lake (62, 100%) Kamren Curl (62, 100%) Kamren Kinchens (44, 71%) Jaylen McCollough (42, 68%) As has become opponents modus operandi, Washington attacked with a short passing game. While there were some suspect tackling, generally they came up and kept the yards after catch to a minimum. Four explosive plays made up nearly 50 percent of the Commanders passing yards and only one of those could attributed to the safeties expense account. Lake got matched up on a wide receiver in the slot, not his best suit, and couldn’t stay attached causing Rams fans anxiety at the end of the game. Cornerback Josh Wallace (62, 100%) Emmanuel Forbes (62, 100%) Cam Lampkin (4, 6%) Wallace got beat for a big gain on a long-developing crossing pattern, with his limited speed those routes are going to be his weak spot. Forbes played quite well, the most surprising aspect of his game was the aggressiveness when put into a tackling situation. The touchdown he gave up early was clear as day, there are very few corners that can play eight yards off the ball and cover a four yard slant. Going forward The Rams finish out the soft area of the schedule next week against the Arizona Cardinals and then a much needed bye week to heal up a bit before entering the stretch drive. The Redbirds may be 3-6 for the season, but will be looking for a season sweep over L.A. In the first meeting, they utilized a balanced offensive attack en route to a 35-25 minute time of possession advantage and 18-16 win. The remaining schedule will be an uphill slog. There will be no more tomato cans, all seven remaining opponents are still in the playoff hunt. Coming right out of the bye break, the Thanksgiving Eve tilt with the Green Bay Packers sets up as a must win. The 6-3 Pack currently holds…

title: Is Sean McVay blind to the Rams need for another wide receiver?
summary: Sean McVay continues to talk about getting his offensive weapons more involved, but his actions tell a different story. Week after week, Sean McVay’s offense runs through Puka Nacua, leaving Matthew Stafford with limited dependable options when Puka Nacua isn’t the target or if he is not on the field. Nacua is undoubtedly one of […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 18: Head Coach Sean McVay of the Los Angeles Rams looks on during the game against the Arizona Cardinals at SoFi Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Inglewood, California. The Arizona Cardinals won 18-16. (Photo by Alika Jenner/Getty Images) | Getty Images Sean McVay continues to talk about getting his offensive weapons more involved, but his actions tell a different story. Week after week, Sean McVay’s offense runs through Puka Nacua, leaving Matthew Stafford with limited dependable options when Puka Nacua isn’t the target or if he is not on the field. Nacua is undoubtedly one of the NFL’s best receivers, but the Rams cannot continue relying on him to carry such a significant portion of the passing game. Despite McVay’s intentions to distribute opportunities, the offense repeatedly gravitates toward Nacua when it needs a play. That raises a legitimate question: Is Sean McVay naive to the playmakers around Matthew Stafford? Puka had 150 receiving yards yesterday. The Rams' next-closest player had 20 (!!!) yards. The gap between Puka and their WR2 right now is absurd. And unsustainable. https://t.co/QPCJ50FRbR — Cameron DaSilva (@camdasilva) November 9, 2026 NFL commentators have repeatedly pointed out the limitations of the Rams’ supporting cast. Other wide receivers and tight ends have struggled to consistently create separation, particularly when working through their routes and getting out of their breaks. When receivers cannot generate meaningful separation, Stafford is forced to make tighter-window throws or move on to another option. #Rams WR route win rate is 30th in the league. But sure you don’t need anyone 🤷‍♂️ https://t.co/cnBx7Pu6Wk — JAKE OLIVER ELLENBOGEN (@JKBOGEN) November 7, 2026 Drops have only compounded the problem. Stafford has consistently put the ball in positions where his receivers can make plays, but too many opportunities have ended with incomplete passes. For a quarterback playing at a high level, that has to be frustrating. If the problem with the Rams offense is not skill, then it's scheme. What is the disconnect between what Scheelhaase/McVay are running that isn't translating in front of Stafford? Nobody outside a select few analysts even mentioned the potential setbacks losing LaFleur… — Big Tuna 🏈 (@1standtuna) November 8, 2026 The Rams have an elite quarterback and a superstar receiver, but that combination needs more support. McVay cannot keep expecting Nacua to be the answer to every offensive problem. Whether through a trade or another personnel move , Los Angeles needs another legitimate playmaker who can separate, create after the catch and consistently secure the football. The Rams were not hesitant in 2021 to add Odell Beckham Jr to the WR room when they already had Cooper Kupp and Robert Woods. Robert Woods went down with a torn ACL and showed just how important it was to have WR depth for the stretch run. Had Odell Beckham Jr stayed healthy in the Super Bowl, the Rams might have blown out the Cincinnati Bengals because they could not account for Odell Beckham Jr and Cooper Kupp. The longer the Rams wait, the more predictable their offense becomes.

summary: The Los Angeles Rams might have to part ways with an important piece of their defensive line to acquire the wide receiver help they desperately need before the NFL trade deadline. (Photo by Sean M. Haffey/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams might have to part ways with an important piece of their defensive line to acquire the wide receiver help they desperately need before the NFL trade deadline. Braden Fiske could become the trade asset that makes a potential deal possible, particularly if the Jacksonville Jaguars are willing to discuss Brian Thomas Jr. A Fiske-for-Thomas swap could make sense for both organizations. Jacksonville recently lost defensive tackle Davon Hamilton for the season after he tore his quadriceps, creating an immediate need for additional help along the interior defensive line. Fiske could provide the Jaguars with a young, disruptive defensive lineman who still has plenty of upside and multiple years of team control. James Gladstone, the Jaguars GM, was a big proponent of the Braden Fiske pick in 2024. Could he want to reunite with the 2nd rounder with shipping away Brian Thomas Jr to the Rams? Gladstone here gushing about Braden Fiske before the #Rams traded up to get him 👀 #Jaguars https://t.co/bgrflySjRY — @UCjags (@UCJags) November 9, 2026 Meanwhile, the Rams have a different problem to solve. Their offense continues to funnel opportunities through Puka Nacua, while the supporting cast has struggled to consistently separate and make plays. Adding Thomas would give Matthew Stafford another legitimate outside receiving threat and provide Sean McVay with a much-needed offensive weapon. There is also a potential roster squeeze in Los Angeles. Kobie Turner is working his way back from a groin injury, and his return figures to eat into Fiske’s playing time along the defensive front. That doesn’t necessarily make Fiske expendable, but it could make him a more attractive trade chip. Sacrificing a promising defensive lineman is never an easy decision. However, if the Rams can turn Fiske into a young receiver like Thomas, it might be a worthwhile investment in their championship aspirations.

Week 10: @ Arizona Cardinals Since Los Angeles’s embarrassing loss to Arizona at home in Week 6, the Rams have rattled off three consecutive wins, albeit against the Raiders, Chargers, and Commanders. Prediction: Rams 23-17 (Record: 10-5) Week 17: @ Tampa Bay Buccaneers Needing a road win to guarantee a spot in the playoffs, Sean McVay clinches a playoff berth before Week 18; allowing them to rest starters in Week 18. Prediction: Rams 27-20 (Record: 11-5) Week 18: vs. Seattle Seahawks Maybe this matchup is playoffs or bust. Call me an optimist for thinking the Rams will have locked up either the 6 seed or 7 seed by this point. Prediction: Seahawks 20-10 (Record: 11-6) There you have it. PLAYOFFS. 11-6. title: Rob Leonard’s clock ticking after Week 9 San Francisco 49ers loss with historically bad Las Vegas Raiders’ defense
summary: We’ve officially reached the halfway point of the 2026 NFL season, and the 4-5 Las Vegas Raiders are technically in the AFC Wild Card hunt. However, the Week 9 38-17 loss to the San Francisco 49ers means the Raiders still haven’t beaten a playoff-caliber opponent, and a defense that hasn’t given up fewer than 27 […]
full_text: We’ve officially reached the halfway point of the 2026 NFL season, and the 4-5 Las Vegas Raiders are technically in the AFC Wild Card hunt . However, the Week 9 38-17 loss to the San Francisco 49ers means the Raiders still haven’t beaten a playoff-caliber opponent, and a defense that hasn’t given up fewer than 27 points since Week 2 is a big reason for that. Hence, defensive coordinator Rob Leonard leads off this week’s winners and losers column. LOSER: Rob Leonard To be fair, the offense had a pick-six in San Francisco, so the Raiders’ defense “only” gave up 31 points. However, they also became the first team since 2020 (fifth in the modern era) to give up at least 30 points in six consecutive games (h/t The Athletic’s Sam Warren ). The Detroit Lions and the Jacksonville Jaguars were the clubs to do it six years ago, and that was Matt Patricia’s last season as the Lions’ head coach and Doug Marrone’s final run in Jacksonville. While Klint Kubiak isn’t going anywhere in Las Vegas, Kubiak can’t continue to watch the defense struggle and not make a significant change. Leonard may not get fired this week, but he should at least be on the hot seat moving forward. After the game, the head coach was asked about making changes defensively and replied: “We’ll look at the film and make our decisions when we have cooler heads,” per Warren . So, Leonard might be safe for now, but that quote isn’t exactly a vote of confidence. If Kubiak wants to salvage the rest of the season, something has to change defensively, and it might start at the top. LOSER: John Spytek It’s fair to say that Spytek wasn’t going to fix all of the Raiders’ problems this past offseason, but he shoulders at least some of the blame for the defense’s struggles. Between Kwity Paye ($48 million), Quay Walker ($40.5 million), Nakobe Dean ($36.03 million), Eric Stokes ($30 million) and Malcolm Koonce ($11 million), the general manager spent over $165 million in total contract value on defensive players in the offseason. Other than Dean, none of those signings have been consistent and legitimate difference makers so far this season. On top of that, everyone knew that defensive tackle was one of the defense’s biggest needs heading into the offseason. However, Spytek essentially ignored the position. Now, the unit can’t stop the run and has little to no interior pass-rush. His job may not be in danger just yet, but Spytek should be feeling a lot of pressure right now. WINNER: Treydan Stukes Granted, what the GM might point to is the fact that Stukes is showing signs of becoming an impactful defensive back. It feels like he’s been getting better just about every week, and he had a strong performance in San Francisco, nabing his second interception of the season. The second-round pick was also targeted five times and allowed four catches for 19 yards while recording a pair of stops in coverage, per Pro Football Focus . That helped Stukes earn a career/season-high 84.4 grade that ranks fourth among safeties for the week (pre-Monday Night Football) . LOSER: Kirk Cousins A week after temporarily silencing Fernando Mendoza talks , Cousins played his worst game of the season to reignite the conversation. He completed 22 of 32 passes (68.8%) for just 216 yards and one touchdown to a season-high three interceptions. While the veteran quarterback is far from the Raiders’ biggest problem, the only thing keeping him in the starting lineup is that the Raiders are still in the playoff mix. However, as the losses mount and the team continues to show it isn’t a legitimate postseason contender, the more the organization’s focus shifts to the future. LOSER: Spencer Burford The coaching staff is clearly higher on Burford than outsiders are, but it’s getting hard to ignore that his PFF grade has bounced back and forth between good and well below-average every game since Week 4. This past Sunday’s game came in with a 43.6 mark , and Sumer Sports credited him with just one “impact block”. Additionally, Burford had a 48.7 run-blocking grade against the 49ers and is at 58.5 for the entire season while the offense can’t run the ball. At some point, the change up front can’t just be at right guard. Someone else needs to get a shot to replace Burford, especially since he’s only on a one-year contract. WINNER: Jermod McCoy It’s been a tough rookie season for McCoy, who looked rough in his limited playing time before this past weekend. While his production came in garbage time, it was good to see him record a couple of pass breakups on two targets in San Francisco. In a way, it felt like an NBA jump shooter going through a cold streak hitting a pair of free throws just to see the ball go through the hoop. Hopefully, that helps the fourth-round pick build some confidence moving forward, because the defense needs someone to step up at cornerback. LOSER: Adam Butler To be clear, Vegas’ defensive tackle issue extends far beyond just one player. However, Butler isn’t helping matters, and Sunday was a pretty rough afternoon for him. The veteran defensive lineman registered a start and 46 snaps (26 against the run, 18 as a pass-rusher and two in coverage) but posted a season-low 48.3 PFF run defense grade and failed to record a pressure. LOSER: Tim Keenan III On a similar note, Keenan made his first NFL start but failed to seize the opportunity. The practice squad call-up was the Raiders’ lowest-graded defender ( 39.4 ) and didn’t do what he was elevated for: stop the run. San Francisco’s wide zone rushing attack — which it leaned on more than any concept or for 32.6% of the offense’s carries, per Sumer — gave Keenan trouble as he was constantly washed out of his gap. That’s the rookie’s third call-up of the year, meaning he has to be added to the 53-man roster to be active for another game. If the coaching staff was using Sunday as a deciding factor in that decision, then it seems like Keenan will spend the rest of the year on the practice squad unless an injury or full-on youth movement happens down the stretch.
author: Matt Holder

title: Raiders make plays but cough up ball too much in 38-17 thumping to 49ers
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders just couldn’t get out of their own way Sunday afternoon. Five awful second-half turnovers in a disconcerting 38-17 defeat were a testament to that. Facing a well-oiled machine that the San Francisco 49ers are, the Silver & Black fell quickly behind 21-10 after generating just 48 yards through the air and […]
full_text: (Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders just couldn’t get out of their own way Sunday afternoon. Five awful second-half turnovers in a disconcerting 38-17 defeat were a testament to that. Facing a well-oiled machine that the San Francisco 49ers are, the Silver & Black fell quickly behind 21-10 after generating just 48 yards through the air and 27 yards on the ground while yielding 123 passing and 125 rushing yards on defense. And on its first offensive play of the second half, Las Vegas gifted San Francisco seven more points off quarterback Kirk Cousin’s pick six and just like that, 28-10 Niners, and turnover No. 1. The Raiders didn’t go away, however, and put together a solid nine-play, 69-yard scoring drive that culminated in tight end Brock Bowers climbing the ladder for a 21-yard touchdown dart from Cousins to trim the deficit to 28-17. The Silver & Black gained even more momentum with rookie safety Treydan Stukes’ leaping interception of Brock Purdy. But just two plays later, linebacker Fred Warner punched the ball out of Bowers’ hands and the Red & Gold recovered, for Raiders turnover No. 2. A 10-minute sequence that we'll never be able to unsee. pic.twitter.com/DzxMlxsVK6 — Kyle Posey (@KP_Show) November 8, 2026 Again, Las Vegas refused to lay down and Rob Leonard’s much-maligned Raiders defense rose to the occasion stuffing Purdy on a QB sneak to get the ball back to Klint Kubiak’s offense. And it appeared the visitors from the desert were poised to get within four points of their former Bay Area rival when tight end Michael Mayer hauled in a sharp 24-yard pass from Cousins. But as the big pass catcher dove towards the goal line, he lost control of the ball fumbling it into the end zone with Warner recovering for the touchback. No points, and pivotal turnover No. 3. Kyle Shanahan’s 49ers offense responded with a seven-play, 80-yard touchdown drive capped by Purdy’s 37-yard laser of a throw to Jordan Watkins for a pretty 37-yard touchdown catch in which the 49ers wide receiver boxed out rookie cornerback Hezekiah Masses. Trailing 35-17, Kubiak’s offense once again got within striking distance on Raheem Morris’ stingy 49ers defense after Bowers’ 33-yard catch and run to the one-yard line. But the Nines read the QB sneak to perfection to stonewall that, an iffy offensive pass interference by Mayer cost the Raiders six points, and Cousins’ throw to Tre Tucker in the end zone was intercepted on 2nd-and-goal from the 13-yard line to thwart Kubiak’s offense once more — turnover No. 4. After allowing a 49ers field goal, the Raiders ended the day offensively with another Cousins interception — a deep throw intended for Tucker that was picked off, turnover No. 5. Michael Mayer almost had two touchdowns, one was called back due to a penalty and the other, Mayer fumbled the ball at the one yard line and it was recovered by San Francisco. Mayer spoke with the media after the Raiders loss to SF pic.twitter.com/GJ7N8ky2Rf — Raider Nation Radio (@RNR920AM) November 9, 2026 Las Vegas made it fair share of plays, but San Francisco simply made more and the defeat showcases just how far the Raiders are from competing with and beating good teams in the NFL. At 4-5 overall, Kubiak has done well to win four games in his rookie year as a head coach but those victories came against struggling teams. When faced with upper-echelon opposition, the Raiders have come close and no cigar or been boat raced. Sunday afternoon in Santa Clara was a mix of both. Kubiak’s Raiders were in a dogfight and allowing just 10 second-half points against the 49ers is a plus. It’s just too bad Leonard’s defense couldn’t have that kind of performance in the opening half. As I noted when I previewed the Raiders-49ers Week 9 matchup, the team that Kubiak wants in Las Vegas what Shanahan currently has in Santa Clara . The foundational model of a complementary football team that’s disciplined, efficient, and explosive in all three phases (offense, defense, and special teams) is what Kubiak eventually wants in the desert. And today’s loss highlights fleeting moments of that but also the hideous warts of the complete opposite. Let’s hit the quick slants as fast as both teams turned the ball to one another in a topsy turvy third quarter: —The Niners’ 31 points on offense marks the sixth-straight time the Raiders defense has allowed 30 or more points this season — tying a modern era NFL record. Heading into Week 9 play, Las Vegas allowed 230 points total and only the Arizona Cardinals (238) and Baltimore Ravens (236) allowed more. —A week after jumping too early in pass coverage (and not snagging two potential interceptions) , Stukes displayed perfect timing and baiting Purdy on his interception of a pass intended for 49ers tight end George Kittle. The second-round pick is progressing well in his rookie year. Treydan Stukes in the right place at the right time 👏 LVvsSF on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/ybBp5MdnTi — NFL (@NFL) November 8, 2026 —Cousins finished 22 of 32 passing for 216 yards with one touchdown and three interceptions . Sunday’s performance was the worst the veteran quarterback put forth this season and it was a game where the 38-year-old’s arm strength waned as the game progressed. —Even facing top-flight defenses, Bowers continues to be a productive Raider and un-guardable at times. The tight end hauled in seven passes for 111 yards and a touchdown (long of 33) to pace Las Vegas’ offense. Tucker finished behind Bowers with four receptions for 54 yards and Mayer had three catches for 37 yards. —Las Vegas’ run game continues its abysmal performances finishing with 27 yards on 15 carries — three yards less than the first half sum of 27. Ashton Jeanty paced the group with six carries for 25 yards (long of nine) while Bowers added one carry for two yards, Cousins had two carries or no yards (but a touchdown) and Mike Washington Jr. finished with six totes for negative three yards. —Raiders kick return man Dylan Laube continues to be a electric special teamer with seven returns for 197 yards (28.1 average per return) with a long of 57 yards. The Raiders first kick return was hauled in by Laube but he pitched it to wide receiver Dareke Young on a reverse for an additional 25 yards. Quote of Note “We’ll look at the film, and we’ll make our decisions when we have cool heads.” —Las Vegas Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak on whether changes are needed to be made on defense after allowing 30 points for the sixth-straight week “At this time of year, we’re focused on winning games. I really like our team. I don’t like losing games like this. You’ve got to have a lot more resilience to you when you’re playing a really good team that we played today. And when you start that slow, you don’t put yourself in good position. But I’m proud to coach the guys that we’re coaching.” —Las Vegas Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak on the current state of his Raiders roster Up Next The 4-5 Raiders return to the confines of Allegiant Stadium in Week 10 to take on the visiting Seattle Seahawks. The home cooking hasn’t been too good for the Silver & Black as the team is just 1-3 inside Allegiant. Coming off a 17-3 win over the Arizona Cardinals in Week 9, the 5-4 Seahawks bring a team that Kubiak is all too familiar with. How that familiarity benefits his Raiders remains to be seen, however. A better showing and a win would lift Las Vegas back to .500 with a Week 11 AFC West showdown with the Denver Broncos on the horizon.

title: It’s time for the Raiders to trade Kirk Cousins
summary: Kirk Cousins and the Las Vegas Raiders had a bad game against the San Francisco 49ers, but to be clear, that isn’t the reason why he should be traded. Cousins, is 38 years old and playing some of if not the best ball of his career. After getting beaten the way they did on top […]
full_text: (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images Kirk Cousins and the Las Vegas Raiders had a bad game against the San Francisco 49ers, but to be clear, that isn’t the reason why he should be traded. Cousins, is 38 years old and playing some of if not the best ball of his career. After getting beaten the way they did on top of suffering the implosion they did, it should be clear to everyone that head coach Klint Kubiak has the team trending in the right direction. What should also be clear is that as is, the 2026 Raiders have an extremely diminutive chance of making the playoffs. As of this weekend, the Raiders had not received any trade inquiries regarding their starting quarterback Kirk Cousins, nor are they interested in dealing him, per league sources. They plan to keep sticking with him until they believe their No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza is… pic.twitter.com/g9aU9OGyHl — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) November 8, 2026 Raiders ahead of schedule but not that far With a 4-5 record and the defending Super Bowl champions coming into Allegiant Stadium next week, the Raiders’ playoff chances are dwindling down to a mathematical permutation. The solution to that equation is a variable resting between slim and none. Cousins has had a good run, exceeded expectations and been a good bridge for both Kubiak and quarterback of the future, Fernando Mendoza, to come in and get situated. The Raiders are not in a position for Cousins to lead them into the playoffs. Despite lining up in power formations a majority of the time, the Raiders rushing attack is non-existent. In fact, they have as many games above 100 yards (2) as they do under 50 yards as a team. Taking that a step further, after his second successful quarterback sneak for a touchdown against the 49ers, Cousins is leading the team in rushing touchdowns. Defensively, despite a strong start, the Raiders defense stands on the precipice of being historically bad. For six straight weeks, the defense has allowed 30+ points to playoff and non-playoff teams alike. They have been the game on the schedule struggling offenses see on the calendar and circle, because they know a get-right game when they see it. Seven straight games of 30+ points against a defense has never been done in the modern era. A statistic no one should ever want to be associated with and one would be remiss if one declined to state that the Raiders likelihood of setting that record was high. Yes, the 49ers may have had two weeks to prepare for the Raiders on both sides of the ball. But the Raiders had their opportunities to make it a game and blew chunks all over their cleats. All that to say, Cousins needs help and it’s obvious that he’s not going to get it here in 2026. Trading Cousins Cousins has been the dutiful soldier and if possible, should be granted the opportunity to go back where he last had meaningful success in Minnesota with head coach Kevin O’Connell. Currently, the Vikings have an extra third-round draft pick and two additional fifth-round draft picks as well. Trading carries no dead cap hit for the Raiders and the $1.6M salary fits within the remaining $6.17M of remaining cap space the Vikings have. The way Schefter is talking here intimates something massive for the Vikings at QB lol pic.twitter.com/hPHVBkY8s9 — Sayre Bedinger (@SayreBedinger) November 6, 2026 The Vikings have a defense, better wide receivers and a better running game. Everything Cousins needs to take the pressure off himself and contend. Although word on the street is that the Raiders may have missed their window to move him. According to Adam Schefter, there haven’t been any offers made for Cousins, and the Raiders have had no intention of moving him. Ever the optimist, Kubiak is looking at the schedule and still sees the team as being in it, despite not having any answers for better defensive play or balance on offense. The trade deadline is Tuesday 4pm EST/1 pm PST and the Raiders only have six draft picks in the 2027 draft, with lots of holes to fill. It would behoove the Raiders’ front office to take a long, hard look at what they could get for Cousins and weigh it against the near future. Unpopular as it may be.

title: Tuesday Miami Dolphins Thoughts With The Earl
summary: You know, I understand that this season is about growth, development, and resetting the outlook.  But is it too much to ask to get one game of complimentary football from this team?  Yet another frustrating loss when one side of the ball shows up, but the other does not.  Here’s what I saw. THE DEFENSE […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FL - NOVEMBER 08: Miami Dolphins running back Kaytron Allen (30) holds on to the ball despite as effort by Detroit Lions linebacker Joe Bachie (35) to punch it free during the game between the Detroit Lions and the Miami Dolphins on Sunday, November 8, 2026 at Hard Rock Stadium in Mami, FL (Photo by Icon Sportswire) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images You know, I understand that this season is about growth, development, and resetting the outlook. But is it too much to ask to get one game of complimentary football from this team? Yet another frustrating loss when one side of the ball shows up, but the other does not. Here’s what I saw. THE DEFENSE SHOWED UP I can really call them, can’t I? The Detroit Lions and Miami Dolphins had two of the league’s worst defenses coming into this game. I figured there would be a shootout, or at least a higher-scoring affair. Yet the game featured fewer than 500 total yards of offense and only 28 total points. The Lions averaged 29 PPG coming into this contest, scoring less than 20 points only once, and that was against the league’s best defense, the Vikings. They averaged 6 yards per play before this game. Yet, the Miami Dolphins defense limited the Lions to 19 points and 4.6 yards per play. The Lions gained over 100 fewer yards than their per-game average for the season. For the 1st time all season, the pass defense allowed less than a 70% completion percentage. Goff was limited to 6.8 YPA, and he did not throw a TD. He was sacked 3 times. Rookie Chris Johnson got an INT. Not only that, but the run defense showed up again. The Lions gained 102 yards, but 25% of it came on 2 misdirection plays. Jahmyr Gibbs has been the league’s most dominant weapon thus far this season, and he eventually found the end zone. But he was limited to 74 yards on 20 carries and no catches on 1 target. That’s a 3.7 YPC average, and that’s WITH 2 runs of 10+ yards. This was a terrible matchup for the Dolphins, but they stepped up in a big way. MALIK WILLIS IS HURT The offense picked a bad time to be absent. The Lions had allowed 300+ yards in every game but one so far, and that was to the offensively challenged Vikings. They were fairly decent in run defense, although I suspected that was due to lack of volume. They score so much that teams abandon the run. The Dolphins had 21 rushing attempts, which is a little below their standard. Gordon ran fairly well when he got an opening. However, the story is that Willis had 2 scrambles for 7 yards. The stat itself isn’t as striking as watching them happen. Willis is a dynamic runner, and we have seen him make big plays with his legs this season. But in the past 2 games, he has been reluctant to run. He has been on the injury report the past few weeks with a groin injury, but was listed as a full participant. It was obvious that the injury, or maybe something else, is hampering him. He ran slowly and lumbering, not at all like what we have seen from him. That doesn’t excuse the INT, which was a bad decision. But it can explain why he can’t escape pressure like he normally does, and why he ran the way I would have out there. I know fans hate excuses, but anyone who has ever dealt with a groin injury understands. You may feel fine walking around. But the moment you have to run and put forth effort, it’s very painful, and you can’t do it. It can affect everything, including throwing mechanics. Even with that, Willis had good moments. I don’t want to make this about whether he is good enough, but as long as he is limited, the offense will be limited. I honestly wouldn’t mind if they sat him for a while until he is healthy. In the past 2 games, he played at a higher level, and I believe that if he were 100% on Sunday, the Dolphins could have won. Well… there were other issues too. THIS AND THAT Dirty laundry as far as the eye could see. Officiating in the league has been bad this season and too often, the guy sin stripes have been too visible. This game was no exception as there were a combined 20 accepted penalties. This isn’t a “blame the refs” post though. The Dolphins were just bad in this regard. There was a huge pass play to Kevin Coleman Jr. that came back due to a holding penalty. Several drives had crushing penalties that put the offense way behind the sticks. This team doesn’t have the talent to overcome problems like excessive penalties. To invoke the old Flores trope, those issues are the “takes no talent” stuff that should be improving. If I was Hafley, I would have those guys puking their guts out running gassers back and forth to the TNT wall for those penalties. It needs to stop. THERE YOU ARE! You were hiding all along, and we thought you had disappeared. But you came back. I’m, of course, talking about the offensive line we have come to know and hate over the years. Willis was sacked 3 times – I saw 2 of them – and those, I would argue, are due to his inability to escape like he wants to. But he was under assault all game long. He had several where he was flushed from the pocket and couldn’t find an open pass catcher. Austin Jackson was particularly atrocious, and Slowik’s decision to have him go one-on-one with a premier pass rusher defies logic. That hurt the game plan and may have killed any trade value he had. Paul seemed to have a decent day, but everyone else struggled, and it was pretty rough to watch. Will Kacmarek had a rough game. He nullified the huge pass play to Coleman. Then he had a terrible sequence in the 2nd half where he had a false start on 2nd down, then dropped a 3rd-down pass that would have converted. The Dolphins converted the fake punt play right after that, so they stayed on the field. But that was a bad stretch. He was known as a limited but reliable receiver in college. Can’t have those big drops with limited opportunities. Both Douglas and Coleman look like keepers. Douglas is the big-time playmaker, but Coleman has stepped it up. He only had one target, but it was a huge play. Well, it should have been a huge play. Bell remains quiet, and concerns about his ability to create separation are growing. I remain firm in the belief that he is a big slot player. But right now, he isn’t stepping up like his rookie counterparts. Bradley Pinion had the best pass of the game for the Dolphins on the fake punt play. But the shanked punt gave the Lions great field position that led to points. The defense forced a FG, but it was a 40-yard FG. Imagine if the punt had been 45 yards instead of 25. If the same play sequence occurs, the Lions may be forced to kick a 60-yarder instead. Or perhaps they go for it on 4th-and-10. Or maybe they punt. Not that it mattered, because the Dolphins took the ball, marched down the field, and attempted a FGto tie the game at halftime. Gonzalez doinked the kick off the upright. Now, that 6-point swing didn’t necessarily affect the outcome. But look at that sequence of events. A shanked punt led to field position and 3 points from Detroit, giving them a 6-3 lead. What if they don’t get those points because the Dolphins’ defense steps up after a better punt? What if Gonzalez hits that FG and the Dolphins get a 3-point lead going into the half? Again, it’s little mistakes like the poor punt, missed FG, and penalties that can affect the margins, and the Dolphins have to win the margins to have a chance. I can be lenient with rookies like Kacmarek. But Gonzalez and Pinion are literally the oldest players on the Dolphins’ field. That is simply unacceptable performance for those players. Gonzalez has had his 3rd call-up from the practice squad, and the team will have to decide whether to add him to the 53-man roster or let him walk. At this point, I would try out some young kickers and let them have a chance. Who cares if they miss or if they suck? It’s about seeing what kind of gems the team can unearth. Maybe they find a stud kicker. Maybe not. But Gonzalez ain’t it, and neither is Pinion. The Dolphins are 1-7. There is no use…

full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FL - NOVEMBER 01: Miami Dolphins linebacker Josh Uche (9) looks on at the end of a NFL game between the New England Patriots and the Miami Dolphins, on Sunday November 01, 2026, at Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, FL.(Photo by Chris Arjoon/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images). | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Miami Dolphins welcomed the Detroit Lions to Hard Rock Stadium in sunny South Florida on Sunday, and despite Miami’s defense holding the Lions to just 19 points, the team still fell to their opponents. The Dolphins scored just 9 points against a defense that has struggled mightily at times this season — with neither the passing game or running game able to get things going against Detroit. While the loss is disappointing, Dolphins fans have to be encouraged by the showing from their hodgepodge defense that features many young players and stop-gap pieces signed to one-year deals. One such piece is our Most Valuable ‘Phin of the week — EDGE Josh Uche. Miami Dolphins Week Nine MVP – EDGE Josh Uche For the second consecutive week, a pass rusher wins my MVP award — as Chop Robinson took home the award last week. Uche finished Sunday’s game against Jared Goff, Amon-Ra St. Brown, Jahmyr Gibbs and company with one sack and two quarterback hits, one of which affected the trajectory of a Goff pass and allowed rookie cornerback Chris Johnson to nab his first interception as a professional. Uche has already set a single season high in tackles with 34 combined instances — surpassing his previous single season high of 27 set in 2022 while he was with the New England Patriots. That season, he had 9 tackles for loss through 15 games played. He already has 5 of those this season in just 8 games played. His 7 quarterback hits this year is halfway to his single season high — he had 14 of those in his 2022 season. MVP TRACKER Week One – WR Caleb Douglas Week Two – LB Jacob Rodriguez Week Three – OC Aaron Brewer Week Four – EDGE Chop Robinson Week Five – RB Ollie Gordon II Week Six – BYE Week Seven – QB Malik Willis Week Eight – EDGE Chop Robinson Week Nine – EDGE Josh Uche

full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - NOVEMBER 08: Malik Washington #6 of the Miami Dolphins runs onto the field for player intros prior to an NFL football game against the Detroit Lions at Hard Rock Stadium on November 8, 2026 in (Photo by Logan Bowles/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins face off against the Indianapolis Colts in Week 10, a game featuring two teams vying for the first-overall pick in the 2027 NFL Draft. The point total is set at 40.5, while Miami is +116 on the money line for the straight-up win. The Colts are -136 for the win. This week could see massive changes in odds as Tuesday’s trade deadline approaches. Indianapolis is expected to be sellers today, with running back Jonathan Taylor considered one of the top available players on the market, and rumors swirling around defensive tackle Grover Stewart and quarterback Daniel Jones. If the Colts do start making trades ahead of the 4 p.m. Eastern deadline, how will the line move? Miami could also be sellers, with teams reportedly interested in players like linebacker Jordyn Brooks and defensive tackle Zach Sieler. The Dolphins may not be eager to move on from core pieces of their rebuild, but they may be offered a package of draft picks they cannot refuse. Tuesday could significantly affect the odds for this weekend’s game, but for now, the Colts are slightly favored.

title: Fins Up, Fins Down | Winners and losers from Miami Dolphins week nine defeat
summary: The Miami Dolphins played one of the best football teams in the National Football League on Sunday — the Detroit Lions — and while the defense was able to ground their opponents’ typically high-flying offense, it was their own ineptitude while possessing the football that dug the Dolphins’ grave this past weekend. Miami lost 19-9, […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - NOVEMBER 08: Zane Gonzalez #31 of the Miami Dolphins kicks a field goal against the Detroit Lions during the first quarter at Hard Rock Stadium on November 08, 2026 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins played one of the best football teams in the National Football League on Sunday — the Detroit Lions — and while the defense was able to ground their opponents’ typically high-flying offense, it was their own ineptitude while possessing the football that dug the Dolphins’ grave this past weekend. Miami lost 19-9, mostly due to ugly offensive line play and a litany of penalties. The latter is understandable when you consider the youth movement the Dolphins are currently swearing by. They are seeing the most playing time by rookies out of all teams in the NFL. Still, at the midway point of the 2026 campaign, you’d hope to employ a more disciplined roster at this stage. FINS UP Our Fins Up player of the week is pass rusher Josh Uche. Uche ended the day with one sack of quarterback Jared Goff, two quarterback hits, one of which affected the trajectory of Goff’s pass and allowed rookie cornerback Chris Johnson to intercept his first pass as a professional. Uche — 28 years old — signed a one-year deal with Miami that totals just a hair over $1.4 million. His quality season will allow the soon-to-be free agent to ink a more lucrative contract in the offseason — either with Miami or another team looking for pass rush help. Uche has already surpassed his season high best mark in tackles — he currently has 34 combined takedowns this year. He’s also contributed three sacks, five tackles for loss and a fumble recovery, giving Miami a veteran presence on defense that has been sorely needed on this difficult year. FINS DOWN Our Fins Down player is kicker Zane Gonzalez. Against the Lions, Gonzalez missed a 38-yard field goal try by doinking it off of the upright. It is his second consecutive game with a missed field goal — as he also shanked a kick against the Patriots in last week’s narrow defeat. Gonzalez hasn’t shown enough in his three games with Miami to give general manager Jon-Eric Sullivan a reason to promote him full-time to an active roster spot — and with all three of his practice squad call-ups in the rearview mirror, don’t be surprised if the Dolphins are going shopping for a new place-kicker ahead of their clash with the Indianapolis Colts this weekend.

title: Vikings vs. Packers odds: Opening lines for Week 10 matchup
summary: After falling out of first place in the NFC North for the first time this season, the Minnesota Vikings will look to avoid moving into the division’s basement when they head to Lambeau Field in Week 10 to conclude their home-and-home series with the Green Bay Packers for this season. The people who set the […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - NOVEMBER 09: Christian Benford #47 of the Buffalo Bills breaks up a pass intended for Justin Jefferson #18 of the Minnesota Vikings during the first quarter of the game at U.S. Bank Stadium on November 09, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by David Berding/Getty Images) | Getty Images After falling out of first place in the NFC North for the first time this season, the Minnesota Vikings will look to avoid moving into the division’s basement when they head to Lambeau Field in Week 10 to conclude their home-and-home series with the Green Bay Packers for this season. The people who set the betting lines, apparently, don’t like their chances. Our friends at the FanDuel Sportsbook have opened the lines for Sunday’s game, and the Vikings currently sit as a 4.5-point underdog to the Packers. The over/under for the game currently rests at 42.5 points. The Vikings, as we all saw on Monday Night Football, appear to have completely abandoned the concept of offense, as they generated none of it in a 23-6 loss to the Buffalo Bills for their second loss in a row. Carson Wentz stepped in at quarterback for the injured Kyler Murray and turned in what may have been the worst start a Vikings quarterback has put together in recent memory, completing just 8-of-25 passes and turning the ball over three times, including two interceptions. . .a number that could have been significantly higher. The Packers, on the other hand, have won five of their last six after getting off to a 1-2 start. This past week, they absolutely thumped the New England Patriots to the tune of 45-27 behind three more touchdown passes from Jordan Love and a defense that forced Drake Maye into three interceptions. The Packers currently sit in last place in the North, but with a 6-3 record would lead either the NFC South or the NFC East. . .that’s just how good the NFC North has been this season. These two teams met in the regular season opener at U.S. Bank Stadium. Wentz came into the game midway through the first quarter after Murray suffered a concussion, and the Packers had a 22-10 lead with just over five minutes remaining in the third quarter. From there, however, the Minnesota defense took over, leading an onslaught against Love and the Green Bay offense that saw the Vikings score 29 unanswered points to finish the game, including forcing a turnover on downs and generating an interception and a fumble to set up scoring opportunities. Minnesota took home the 39-22 win to get their season off to a 1-0 start. With the NFL trade deadline looming at 3:00 PM Central today. . .or approximately seven hours from when this story goes up. . .we will see if anything the Vikings do (or don’t do) will shift this number at all. As it stands now, however, the Vikings are currently an underdog to their division rivals as the second half of the season officially gets underway.

full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - NOVEMBER 09: Carson Wentz #11 of the Minnesota Vikings reacts against the Buffalo Bills during the third quarter of the game at U.S. Bank Stadium on November 09, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by David Berding/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Minnesota Vikings lost a game 23-6 they should have won easily with even mediocre quarterback play. But instead their starting quarterback, Carson Wentz, could hardly throw a catchable pass all night. He was off early and often and pretty much single-handedly lost the game for the Vikings. Bankruptcies Carson Wentz. Honestly, the average fan could have played quarterback better than Wentz did on Monday night. In the second half, he completed more passes to Bills than Vikings. His adjusted completion percentage was 37%. That means only about one of every three passes was accurate. That’s off-the-charts bad- even for a backup. Should the Vikings trade for a quarterback (which they desperately need to do) Wentz should be cut. It’s inexcusable for a veteran quarterback like Wentz to be that bad and still be employed. He squandered an excellent performance by the Vikings defense and cost the Vikings a valuable win in a tight division by being totally unprepared and awful in his 101st and hopefully last game as a professional- at least with the Vikings. Stock Up The Front Seven of the Vikings Defense. It was really an excellent performance by the Vikings defense. Run defense was stout for most of the game despite the offense being unable to stay on the field more than a couple minutes at a time. The Vikings possessed the ball for just 17 minutes and 28 seconds- the shortest time of possession in franchise history. They pressured Josh Allen on 50% of his dropbacks and really couldn’t be blamed for the limited success Allen had in the passing game. Andrew Van Ginkel, Jalen Redmond, Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins, Dallas Turner, Blake Cashman, and Eric Wilson all played well against both run and pass even after being on the field longer than any defense in a game in Vikings history. Byron Murphy Jr. He made an excellent play dropping back after his man was out of the play to make the interception in the end zone and then return it to nearly midfield. Brian Flores. The dominance of the Vikings defense was on full display for most of the game and really the only thing that has defeated them this season is the Vikings offense. The last two games the offense hasn’t been able to stay on the field or score points, which allows opposing offenses to eventually wear down the defense running ball late in the game. But if the Vikings offense is able to at least possess the ball and score enough points to play with a lead, as it was able to during the Vikings winning streak, that strategy won’t work. On Monday night, an average offense would have been up 20 points by the end of the first half. Small – Cap Standouts Ivan Pace Jr. He doesn’t get many reps on defense, but Pace has quietly done well with the 10-12 he gets each game. He had more on Monday night with Cashman out for part of the game, and managed a sack while also being excellent in run defense. Jake Golday. He got a dozen reps defensively on Monday night and had a stop and generally did well. Elijah Williams. He was activated for Monday night’s game instead of Caleb Banks and did well as a run defender. He had four stops on five tackles in 32 snaps played. Ben Yurosek. He had just ten snaps but over the last couple games has proven to be a solid replacement for Josh Oliver as a blocking tight end who can also catch a pass or two in a pinch. Stock Down Josh Metellus. Metellus had another lapse in coverage that proved costly for the Vikings. On the first Bills touchdown, Metellus was covering Latu but stopped covering him as he looked back to Josh Allen who threw it to Latu for the touchdown. The refs missed an illegal lineman down field on that play, but still no excuse to stop covering a player before the whistle. Kevin O’Connell. You can’t blame KOC for Wentz’s inaccuracies, but he hasn’t been able to make the offense work with any quarterback since Sam Darnold two years ago now. O’Connell said after the game that they haven’t been able to transfer what he sees in practice to the stadium- something he said last year with J.J. McCarthy as well. Wentz wasn’t nearly this bad in earlier performances this year and last season, but at some point the preparation process needs to be scrutinized and improved. Quarterback coach Josh McCown and offensive coordinator Wes Phillips share some blame here, but ultimately it falls on O’Connell to figure it out and get it right. It may also be time for new blood in the offensive coaching staff. There hasn’t been much for either Wes Phillips or Josh McCown to hang their hat on for a couple years now. Sell The Vikings chances of making any sort of playoff run- or possibly even making the playoffs- without acquiring a new quarterback by the trade deadline on Tuesday. Buy The Vikings chances with Kirk Cousins or possibly Mac Jones. Follow me on X/Bluesky @wludford
