title: Vikings’ Pathetic Offense Wastes Another Strong Defensive Effort Against Bills
summary: For the second week in a row, the Minnesota Vikings’ defense held up for as long as they could against one of the better offensive units in the National Football League. And, for the second week in a row, the Minnesota offense did just about nothing to give them any sort of support at all. […]
full_text: Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images | Getty Images For the second week in a row, the Minnesota Vikings’ defense held up for as long as they could against one of the better offensive units in the National Football League. And, for the second week in a row, the Minnesota offense did just about nothing to give them any sort of support at all. The Bills’ offense held the ball for over forty minutes on Monday night at U.S. Bank Stadium, and the Minnesota defense eventually just wore down as the Vikings fell to the Bills on Monday Night Football by a final score of 23-6 in Week 9. Things got off to a less-than-ideal start for the Vikings, as the Bills elected to receive the opening kickoff after winning the opening coin toss and got a big return from Greg Dortch, who took the ball all the way into Minnesota territory at the 36-yard line. But the Vikings’ defense got their first big stand of the night, as Josh Allen and the Bills’ offense went backward, culminating in a Dallas Turner sack of Allen on third down for a three-and-out and a punt that resulted in a touchback. The Vikings’ first offensive possession also resulted in a three-and-out, as Wentz’s first two passes went towards T.J. Hockenson, one a bad miss and a second short of the line to gain. Brett Thorson’s punt put the Bills at their own 33 to start their second possession of the night. The Bills put together a decent drive, with Allen converting on a couple of third-down throws to D.J. Moore and Khalil Shakir. Allen then converted another third down with his legs to put the Bills on the edge of the red zone, but Allen was called for intentional grounding on the next play thanks to Andrew Van Ginkel nearly dragging him down. After a screen got blown up to make it third and long, Allen tried to find D.J. Moore in the end zone, and instead found Byron Murphy for an interception, with Murphy getting a huge return to midfield for a big momentum shifter for the Minnesota defense. . @byronmurphy snatched it! 📺: @ESPNNFL pic.twitter.com/bsJ55mWnhA — Minnesota Vikings (@Vikings) November 10, 2026 But on the very next play, Wentz threw what was supposed to be a screen pass that was too high for Jefferson; it was first ruled incomplete and then, after review, changed to a lateral that was recovered by the Bills for another turnover that gave the ball right back to Buffalo in Minnesota territory. The Bills got themselves into position for a 39-yard field goal attempt for Tyler Bass, who connected to give the Bills a 3-0 lead with just under two minutes left in the first quarter. The Vikings barely avoided another disaster on the ensuing kickoff, as Myles Price got a nice return but had the ball popped out of his hands. Fortunately, the ball went directly to Ben Yurosek, who held on to set the Vikings’ offense up at their own 45-yard line. Unfortunately, the Vikings’ offense once again went three-and-out as Wentz continued to show a complete lack of accuracy on his passes, including one that Jefferson had to leap for that resulted in him going off the field slowly. After the Vikings punted it away, the Minnesota defense forced yet another three-and-out, with the ensuing Buffalo punt once again giving the Vikings good field position at their own 45-yard line as the first quarter came to an end. But the first possession of the second quarter resulted in yet another three-and-out for the Minnesota offense, and the Bills took over at their own 13 following yet another punt from Thorson. Minnesota’s defense, once again, forced a three-and-out as they continued to swarm Allen and gave him no time to get comfortable. After the punt, the Vikings actually got a first down. . .because of a defensive holding penalty on the Bills. But then, they got an actual first down on a pass from Wentz to T.J. Hockenson to move the ball into Buffalo territory. But that was followed by a sack of Wentz and more incompletions, and the Vikings punted again, with Tai Felton making a brilliant play to down the ball at the Buffalo 1-yard line. The Bills did pick up a first down on the ensuing possession, but a few plays later, Andrew Van Ginkel came flying around the edge to sack Allen and appeared to have forced a fumble that the Vikings recovered at the Buffalo 1-yard line to set up a first-and-goal. However, after review, the call was reversed. . .correctly. . .and it was ruled that Allen’s knee was down before the football came loose, resulting in a sack that put the ball at the 2 and forced another Buffalo punt. Myles Price took the punt to the Buffalo 34-yard line to set up the Vikings’ next drive. The Vikings didn’t gain many yards on the ensuing drive, but they did enough. . .by which we mean “didn’t go backwards”. . .but they did enough to give Will Reichard an opportunity from 43 yards out, and he put the ball between the uprights to tie things at 3-3 with four minutes left in the first half. The Bills took over and put together their best offensive drive of the night, marching into Minnesota territory, getting down to the Minnesota 25-yard line with less than a minute left. Then, Allen bought himself some time by rolling out to the right and found a wide-open Keleki Latu in the end zone for a 25-yard touchdown. It was the first touchdown of Latu’s career and gave the Bills a 10-3 lead with 44 seconds left in the first half. Minnesota got the ball back and Wentz, to his credit, managed to string a few completions together and got the Vikings into position for another Reichard try, this one from 53 yards out. Reichard split the uprights again, and the Vikings went into halftime trailing by a score of 10-6. The Vikings got the ball first to start the second half, and things got off to a decent start on a nice kick return by Price. A few plays later, Aaron Jones drew a 19-yard pass interference call to move the ball into Buffalo territory at the 37-yard line. However, on the next play, Wentz was looking for T.J. Hockenson and was intercepted by Bills linebacker Dorian Williams to put an end to what had been a promising drive. The Bills took over and put together another long, sustained drive into Minnesota territory. Allen’s pass on third-and-goal fell incomplete in the end zone, and they settled for another field goal from Bass, a 25-yarder that extended the Buffalo lead to 13-6 with six minutes remaining in the third quarter. The ensuing drive for the Vikings saw them get things going on the ground with three straight carries from Jordan Mason that picked up 24 yards and put the Vikings into Buffalo territory. Then, the Vikings asked Wentz to throw a pass, and he was promptly intercepted by Terrell Bernard to end the drive and give the ball back to the Bills at the Buffalo 34-yard line. Minnesota’s defense got another stop after the interception, with a touchback on the punt giving the Vikings the ball at their own 20. But, once again, Wentz and the Vikings couldn’t manage even one first down as they punted it away again after a three-and-out. The Bills got the ball back and pushed into Minnesota territory at the 38, where they had a 3rd-and-1. Allen pushed forward on a quarterback sneak and appeared to have the line to gain, but Kevin O’Connell challenged the spot and won to make it 4th-and-inches. Allen tried another sneak, and after initially being ruled short, Allen got the first down. Shortly after that, James Cook went into the end zone from five yards out for a score that, essentially, sealed the deal for the Bills, putting them ahead 20-6 with six minutes left in regulation. The Vikings got the ball back after the Cook touchdown and went four-and-out, going for it on a fourth down and failing when a Wentz pass for Jefferson fell incomplete. The Bills took over and added a 52-yard field goal from Bass to extend their lead to 23-6 with just under five minutes left in regulation. After that, the Vikings pulled Wentz from the game in favor of Max Brosmer. Brosmer pushed the ball into Buffalo territory on what would turn…

title: 3-Point Stance: Patriots’ trade deadline isn’t time for a youth movement
summary: Are the New England Patriots sellers at the NFL trade deadline? On Nov. 1, Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer highlighted defensive tackle Christian Barmore and cornerback Carlton Davis as potential Patriots trade candidates ahead of Tuesday’s deadline at 4 p.m. According to Breer, if a deal is struck, New England’s motivation would be centered around adding […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - NOVEMBER 8: Christian Watson #9 of the Green Bay Packers makes a catch against Carlton Davis III #7 of the New England Patriots during an NFL football game at Gillette Stadium on November 8, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Are the New England Patriots sellers at the NFL trade deadline? On Nov. 1, Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer highlighted defensive tackle Christian Barmore and cornerback Carlton Davis as potential Patriots trade candidates ahead of Tuesday’s deadline at 4 p.m. According to Breer, if a deal is struck, New England’s motivation would be centered around adding draft capital and transitioning into a younger roster. As of Nov. 4, head coach Mike Vrabel appeared to disagree with that approach. “I think sometimes national reports have the tendency to do that. I have not shared that information with anybody,” Vrabel said. “This time of year, I think that all these things kind of get drummed up. So, we’re focused on trying to prepare for [the Green Bay Packers] and make the corrections from [the week before]. “This is business as normal here, so I don’t know where a lot of these things come from. Certainly not from any conversations with me.” However, does Vrabel and Co.’s stance about handling the trade deadline change after New England’s brutal 45-27 loss at the hands of the Packers on Sunday? Vrabel offered a simple response when making an appearance on WEEI’s The Greg Hill Show : “No.” “We want a bunch of guys that want to be here,” he added. “That want to make it hard on each other. In preparation, push each other, challenge each other, improve, take accountability, and if that’s not them, then let us know by tomorrow. That’s what we have to do. That’s the mindset.” And from a selling standpoint, his ruling could make sense as a final decision. Regardless of whether or not the Patriots strike a deal involving either Barmore or Davis, trading almost any impact contributor on the roster while sitting at a 5-4 record at the regular season’s midway point, especially in the AFC, is certainly questionable. Both players were also members of the tight-knit group that made a Super Bowl appearance just nine months ago. At the least, a deal of that stature calls for a corresponding “buying” move. Sure, New England’s depth in multiple areas will be a largely discussed topic throughout the offseason regarding the team’s roster-building process. And rightfully so. Vrabel said it himself after a preseason victory over the Philadelphia Eagles, stating at the time that he doesn’t think his team is “very deep.” But six 2027 day-three draft picks make finding immediate, injury-relieving depth manageable. Sending away either Barmore or Davis simply doesn’t make sense at this time. Especially for a franchise still technically in contention for the AFC East title. Trading Barmore creates another need In 2023, Barmore posted his best season as a pro, recording 8.5 sacks, 16 quarterback hits and pressuring those passers 49 times. He also consistently disrupted opposing run offenses, forcing 13 tackles for a loss and totaling 64 combined takedowns. That season-long performance earned the Patriots’ 2021 second-round draft selection a four-year, $84 million contract extension the following offseason. Currently in year two of that new deal, Barmore’s production hasn’t entirely matched the monetary value of his contract, especially in run defense. From just last season, the 27-year-old has seen his involvement in that facet of the defense drop from 62.8% to just 36%. Still, New England evidently continues to view Barmore as a producer when rushing the quarterback, heavily using the defensive tackle during pass-rush downs and critical third-down plays. Barmore’s overall reduced role also doesn’t mean he’s expendable. Trading him shuffles the defensive line, forcing Cory Durden into a new, pass-rush-heavy role and 34-year-old DaQuan Jones, who has contributed as a relief piece for the primary starters, into a heavier workload. Davis’ departure would leave a hole in the secondary As for Davis, the cornerback hasn’t shown signs of regression. But the soon-to-be 30-year-old, entering the final year of his contract with a mighty injury history and owed $22 million in 2027, plays directly into the youth-movement argument. Nonetheless, shipping him off to another franchise creates a glaring hole in the cornerback room. That decision then forces Vrabel and the defensive coaching staff to decide between starting substitute Charles Woods opposite Christian Gonzalez or pulling Marcus Jones away from his natural nickel-cornerback position. With several offenses in the Patriots’ remaining schedule currently ranking top 10 in passing yards per game, that potential decision seems counterproductive. Davis, who recently returned to the starting lineup last week after missing four games, played a significant role in New England’s divisional round victory against the Houston Texans in the playoffs last season, intercepting C.J. Stroud twice. The offseason offers a better time to make a move In Barmore’s case, an eventual deal appears likely. As the Boston Herald’s Andrew Callahan put it , the Patriots seemingly want “out of the Barmore business.” On Friday, Breer wrote that the price for both Barmore and Davis “would likely” be around just a fourth-round selection. An offseason deal, rather than a midseason trade, allows New England greater flexibility to reallocate resources and explore replacements to replicate or improve upon either player’s production while spending less. The Patriots’ loss to Green Bay is concerning. Still, it’s not a season-ending sign. It’s true that New England’s defense has struggled to deliver on the expectations surrounding their offseason additions of Dre’Mont Jones, All-Pro safety Kevin Byard and second-round pick Gabe Jacas. But much like the rest of the roster, that group has dealt with injuries. The team’s matchup against the Miami Dolphins in Week Eight marked the first game the starting cornerback trio of Gonzalez, Davis and Jones all played together since Week Three. Even though eventually moving Barmore or another established contributor makes sense for the team’s long-term roster construction, the Patriots’ timing of a potential trade should account for the franchise’s current position in the AFC playoff picture.
author: Andrew Guindon

title: Patriots News: Slicing up the blame pie
summary: Today is the 51st anniversary of the sinking of the freighter Edmund Fitzgerald into Lake Superior, as it was steaming towards Detroit with a load of iron ore pellets in its hull. Today is also a Tuesday, when the film reviews, analyses and breakdowns of the game are posted, and there are some informative ones […]
full_text: Foxborough, MA - November 8: Green Bay Packers wide receiver Christian Watson makes a catch over New England Patriots cornerback Christian Gonzalez in the third quarter. The New England Patriots played the Green Bay Packers at Gillette Stadium on November 8, 2026. (Photo by Danielle Parhizkaran/The Boston Globe via Getty Images) | Boston Globe via Getty Images Today is the 51st anniversary of the sinking of the freighter Edmund Fitzgerald into Lake Superior, as it was steaming towards Detroit with a load of iron ore pellets in its hull. Today is also a Tuesday, when the film reviews, analyses and breakdowns of the game are posted, and there are some informative ones in the links below. No lives were lost in this past Sunday’s disaster for the Patriots, but more players added to an already-too-long list of injured players. I’m not ready to declare the roster a sinking ship yet though. This also happens to be the NFL trade deadline, today at 4:00 pm ET. I’ve heard many fans bemoaning the fact that the front office isn’t doing anything to try and add pieces to patch up the roster. My opinion is that there are simply too many holes in this boat to fix with a trade – that won’t also break the bank of cap space or future draft assets. If the issue is shoring up one position, then the price may be worth it to sail on to the playoffs. But where would the Patriots even start? OL? RB? WR? The list is too long. My hope is that some injured players start to return to help the team stack up some wins – but I don’t want to see the team jettison draft picks for a quick fix that may or may not even work out. We’ll see what happens today. full_text: Even though they have already matched their total losses from last year, the New England Patriots once again look like a legitimate contender for a playoff spot in the AFC. However, in order to get there, they will have to find a way to overcome the injuries that have ravaged their roster over the first two months of the regular season. While the expectation is that they will get several players back from injured reserve at some point, they also could go for a more radical approach in hopes of improving their team and gearing up for a stretch run in 2026. Like they have done multiple times in 2026 already, they could look at the trade market. Will there be additions to a list that already includes the likes of A.J. Brown, Jaylen Reed, Corey Kiner and Walter Rouse? Or could they move on from some of their players, like they did in 2025 ? We will know soon: the NFL trade deadline is coming up on Tuesday, November 10, at 4 p.m. ET. Until then, please make sure to bookmark and regularly revisit our Patriots trade deadline tracker for all the latest developments. Patriots trades TBD Patriots trade rumors 2026 Latest rumors at the top. For the Patriots, the trade deadline will “likely [be] on the quieter side” | Report Regardless of Christian Barmore’s outlook, the Patriots “want another pass rusher” to complement their current edge group. At the moment, the team has Dre’Mont Jones, Elijah Ponder and Gabe Jacas as its three-player rotation at the position. | Report The Patriots are “lurking” in the wide receiver trade market ahead of the Nov. 10 deadline. They currently have four wide receivers on their active roster, but with A.J. Brown nursing a knee injury could benefit from more depth. Some of it will come in the form of Mack Hollins, with Romeo Doubs expected to return from IR after the Week 11 bye. | Report The Patriots are not actively shopping Christian Barmore or Carlton Davis. That does not mean they won’t listen to offers, but they have not put up the “for sale” signs just yet. | Report The Patriots are conducting “business as normal” with less than a week to go until the NFL trade deadline. | Report The Patriots are looking to buy at the trade deadline, with edge help a particular focus. | Report The Patriots are reportedly looking for a fourth-round draft pick in a potential Christian Barmore trade. | Report Cornerback Carlton Davis is speculated as another trade candidate. | Report Patriots defensive tackle Christian Barmore reportedly “could be had” via trade. | Report Wide receiver Josh Down has requested a trade from the Colts. | Report “Wide receiver-needy teams” have reportedly called the Colts about fourth-year man Josh Downs. title: 6 potential Patriots targets ahead of the NFL trade deadline
summary: The Nov. 10 4 p.m. ET NFL trade deadline is just hours away. Despite being just days removed from an ugly loss, the 5-4 New England Patriots still view themselves as contenders which could impact how they manage the roster. “I want to see us do anything that we can with the roster that we […]
full_text: The Nov. 10 4 p.m. ET NFL trade deadline is just hours away. Despite being just days removed from an ugly loss, the 5-4 New England Patriots still view themselves as contenders which could impact how they manage the roster. “I want to see us do anything that we can with the roster that we have or potentially guys that aren’t here, to continue to improve,” head coach Mike Vrabel said Monday. “That’s the focus here after nine weeks. We played some really good games, have been competitive, and then other days where it just wasn’t good enough as a whole.” After trading a 2028 first-round pick this past offseason, the Patriots are not expected to make any significant investments. But the team does have additional Day 3 draft capital this year to add depth across the roster. As for potential targets, here are six targets who could be on the radar. DT Roy Lopez The Patriots’ run defense has trended in a positive direction in recent weeks, but adding Lopez could help the unit take another step forward. The 29-year-old has shown flashes of being a dominant run defender along the interior and would give New England another reliable option in the defensive line rotation. He is also under contract through the 2027 season for a reasonable salary. DT Dalvin Tomlinson Another option along the interior defensive line, Tomlinson has lost some of the pass-rushing juice he showed earlier in his career but remains a disruptive rotational piece. The 32-year-old is in the final year of his contract with the winless Chargers, with roughly $1.5 million remaining in cash owed to him. That makes him a potentially affordable option compared to Colts nose tackle Grover Stewart, who is owed approximately $6 million in cash. Tomlinson also spent the 2024 season with Mike Vrabel in Cleveland. ED Zaven Collins The Patriots have gotten strong overall production from Elijah Ponder, Dre’Mont Jones and Gabe Jacas along the edge. However, adding another pass rusher could help preserve that production down the stretch and bring some more juice to the unit as a whole. The former first-round pick, who has the size and athleticism New England has gravitated to on the edge, has served in a rotational role for the Cardinals this season and is in the final year of his contract, potentially making him an attainable deadline target. ED Nolan Smith The 2-7 Eagles continued to move pieces ahead of the trade deadline Monday, sending defensive tackle Jordan Davis to Jacksonville in exchange for a first- and second-round pick. Could former first-round pick Nolan Smith be next? Despite the Eagles’ struggles, the 25-year-old has been productive, leading the team with 21 pressures this season while remaining a physical run defender. Philadelphia also exercised Smith’s fifth-year option this past offseason, keeping him under contract through 2027 with under $14 million in cash owed his way. His age, production and contractual control could make him an appealing addition, although it may take a more significant investment than other names on this list. CB Jonathan Jones New England’s secondary was already without cornerback Charles Woods (hamstring) Sunday before fellow cornerback Carlton Davis (knee) left the game early. That left Christian Gonzalez and Marcus Jones with limited depth behind them, as rookies Karon Prunty and Channing Canada were the next options at cornerback. Former Patriot Jonathan Jones has settled into a rotational role with the Eagles, but still offers experience and man-coverage ability that could be valuable for a New England secondary dealing with injuries. Draft capital As noted above, the Patriots are without their 2028 first-round pick after sending it to Philadelphia in the offseason trade for A.J. Brown. While New England is focused on competing this season, there is still a bigger-picture argument for adding draft capital and getting younger across the roster. That probably is more of an offseason focus, but the team could explore the trade market to potentially move a veteran on the current roster if the right offer comes along.

title: Patriots injury analysis after Packers loss in Week 9
summary: The New England Patriots suffered one of their worst losses in recent memory against the Green Bay Packers on Sunday. Not only were they beaten with a final score of 45-27, they also saw multiple players go down with injuries. While not all of those were equally serious, some are a definitive cause for concern. […]
full_text: The New England Patriots suffered one of their worst losses in recent memory against the Green Bay Packers on Sunday. Not only were they beaten with a final score of 45-27 , they also saw multiple players go down with injuries. While not all of those were equally serious, some are a definitive cause for concern. After rewatching the game, let’s go through what is an extensive list for a team that has struggled with injuries all year long. Patriots injury analysis: NFL Week 9 S Brenden Schooler: Already nursing a hamstring issue entering the game, Schooler was limited to just four snaps against the Packers — all within the game’s first five minutes. The final one came on a Mitch Wishnowsky punt in the first quarter, and did not see the team captain suffer any obvious injury while working his typical role as a gunner. His hamstring still prevented him form finishing the game. CB Carlton Davis III: While teammate Christian Gonzalez broke up a fourth-down pass late in the second quarter, Carlton Davis came up limping after making a cut in coverage against Packers receiver Christian Watson. He remained down on one knee on the sideline, and eventually slowly made his way to the blue medical tent. Davis was later announced as questionable to return with a knee injury, and ultimately ruled out instead of reentering the contest. LG Ben Brown: Getting spun around while sustaining a pass block in the late second quarter, Brown went down after the play and received medical attention on the field. He slowly walked off under his own power and was later announced as questionable to reenter the contest with a knee issue. He too never came back. TE Cameron Latu: Latu remained on the ground after a kickoff return in the late third quarter; he was taken down from behind while holding his block for returner Corey Kiner. He eventually jogged off the field and returned for the next special teams opportunity three minutes of game time later. No injury was announced by the team. RB Rhamondre Stevenson: Catching a short pass near the sideline with under four minutes to go in the third quarter, Stevenson attempted to get up as normal but ultimately hobbled and went back down. He received some assistance by the Patriots medical staff, but walked off under his own power and into the medical tent. He departed for the locker room shortly thereafter and was quickly ruled out for the remainder of the game because of a knee injury. S Jaylen Reed: The Patriots’ No. 3 safety took a brief trip to the blue medical tent in the late third quarter, but remained on the sidelines and reentered the contest shortly thereafter. As with Cameron Latu, no injury was announced for Reed either. LT Will Campbell: Early in the fourth quarter, New England’s starting left tackle went down after blitzing safety Evan Williams collided with him from behind. Dealing with a knee injury, he walked off with members of the Patriots training staff and into the blue medical tent. The Patriots announced him as questionable to return, and he finished the game on the sidelines. QB Drake Maye: The Patriots’ starting quarterback took a hard fall on a 10-yard sack with 10 minutes to go in the game. He was a bit slow to get up and eventually pulled from the game, although the decision to remove him had to do with the score at that point — 45-21 — as well as an overall attempt to preserve him rather than any effects from that particular play. WR Kyle Williams: Williams came up limping after an incomplete target in the late fourth quarter (that ultimately did not count anyway due to a roughing-the-passer penalty). He was not on the field for the next two plays, but returned for the two-point conversion after a Corey Kiner touchdown run. The ball again came his way, was not completed, and he was shaken up: the second-year receiver took a hard fall while trying to reach for the overthrown pass. He returned for the game’s final two snaps. What this means for the Patriots As if losing by 18 points wasn’t bad enough, the already injury-plagued Patriots also took some more hits on Sunday. Not all of them appear to be of the major variety, but some certainly are. Rhamondre Stevenson, for example, is reportedly set to miss some time due to a knee tendon injury. Ben Brown, meanwhile, won’t be available for the team against the Detroit Lions in Germany on Sunday. The statuses of Carlton Davis and Brenden Schooler, who also were unable to finish the contest, remain to be determined — as will any other effects from the game. It wasn’t all bad news, though. Will Campbell, for example, said after the game that he could have returned had the score not been out of hand at that point. Still, the Patriots will once again be forced to adapt. At running back, this means potentially being down the top two options this week versus the Lions. Besides Stevenson, TreVeyon Henderson has now missed back-to-back games because of an illness of undetermined origin . This means that Corey Kiner, Lan Larison and practice squad option Terrell Jennings would remain as the only available backs in Week 10. Along the offensive line, meanwhile, the Patriots’ turnover at guard is set to continue. With Brown out, the team will either reinsert Walter Rouse or veteran Greg Van Roten, whose window to return from injured reserve was opened last week. The Patriots will hold their first practice of the week on Wednesday before taking an overnight flight to Munich. They will then hold a light session on Thursday followed by another regular practice on Friday. Kickoff against the Lions is scheduled for 9:30 a.m. ET on Sunday.
author: Bernd Buchmasser

title: Patriots playoff picture after loss to Packers in Week 9
summary: Coming off a Super Bowl berth, the New England Patriots entered the 2026 season with some high expectations. Those have not changed, but Sunday’s 45-27 loss to the Green Bay Packers showed that meeting them might become even more of a challenge than initially anticipated. What will happen over the coming weeks and months remains […]
full_text: Coming off a Super Bowl berth, the New England Patriots entered the 2026 season with some high expectations. Those have not changed, but Sunday’s 45-27 loss to the Green Bay Packers showed that meeting them might become even more of a challenge than initially anticipated. What will happen over the coming weeks and months remains to be seen, of course, but for now let’s focus on the concrete impact that defeat had on the standings. AFC East standings Buffalo Bills (7-1) New England Patriots (5-4) New York Jets (2-7) Miami Dolphins (1-7) The Patriots defending their AFC East title will be a challenge, even though they own the head-to-head advantage over the Bills courtesy of their Week 4 victory in Buffalo. However, what good is that advantage if you cannot get even in the standings? And with New England falling to 5-4 and the Bills winning their seventh game on Monday night against the Vikings, doing so will be tough. Not only will the Patriots need the Bills to start dropping some games to overcome their current 2.5-point deficit, they themself also cannot allow many more slip-ups. Considering that five of their final eight opponents currently reside in either the AFC or NFC playoff pictures, that is far from a given. Elsewhere in the AFC East Week 9 was business as usual. The Jets lost 35-12 to the Chiefs and are inching closer toward rebuild category once more, while the Dolphins — whose lone win this season came against New York — were once again unable to make enough plays to prevent a 19-9 loss to the Lions. AFC playoff standings Buffalo Bills (7-1) Denver Broncos (7-2) Jacksonville Jaguars (6-2) Pittsburgh Steelers (6-2) Kansas City Chiefs (6-2) Cincinnati Bengals (6-2) New England Patriots (5-4) On the bubble: 8. Cleveland Browns (5-4) , 9. Las Vegas Raiders (4-5), 10. Baltimore Ravens (4-5), 11. Houston Texans (3- 5) Not yet eliminated, but let’s be real here: 12. New York Jets (2-7), 13. Indianapolis Colts (2-7), 14. Miami Dolphins (1-7), 15. Tennessee Titans (1-7), 16. Los Angeles Chargers (0-8) Even though they were dominated on Sunday, the Patriots still remain in the driver’s seat for a playoff spot in the AFC. They do have multiple advantages over the only other 5-4 team in the conference, the Browns. New England’s conference record is superior, while it also owns the strength of victory and strength of schedule tiebreakers at the moment. With no head-to-head matchup on the schedule, those tiebreakers might decide who makes it to the postseason when all is said and done. Of course, there is still a long way to go before any conversations about the playoffs become serious. For the time being, though, the Patriots are still in control of their own destiny even if they ended up ceding more ground to the other wild card competitors. NFC playoff standings San Francisco 49ers (7-1) Chicago Bears (7-2) New York Giants (5-2-1) Carolina Panthers (3-5) Detroit Lions (6-2) Minnesota Vikings (6-2) Green Bay Packers (6-3) On the bubble: 8. Seattle Seahawks (5-4), 9. Los Angeles Rams (5-4), 10. Dallas Cowboys (4-5), 11. New Orleans Saints (3-5), 12. Tampa Bay Buccaneers (3-6), 13. Atlanta Falcons (3-6) Not yet eliminated, but let’s be real here: 14. Arizona Cardinals (3-6), 15. Washington Commanders (2-5-1), 16. Philadelphia Eagles (2-7) Losers of back-to-back games following their 6-0 start, the Vikings dropped all the way to the sixth seed in the NFC on Monday night. They are still well-positioned for a playoff push, however, as is the rest of their division: all three wild card spots are occupied by NFC North teams, as is the No. 2 seed. The Seahawks and Rams, meanwhile, are both outside the playoff picture despite their winning records. The fourth seen, meanwhile, is occupied by a 3-5 Panthers team leading the worst division in football.

title: Rhamondre Stevenson injury update: Patriots RB set to miss multiple weeks
summary: The injuries continue to pile up for the New England Patriots, who now are set to be without another key offensive contributor for multiple weeks. Running back Rhamondre Stevenson is dealing with a knee tendon issue that is not expected to require surgery but could sideline him for a short period, according to ESPN’s Adam […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - NOVEMBER 8: Rhamondre Stevenson #38 of the New England Patriots runs with the ball against the Green Bay Packers during an NFL football game at Gillette Stadium on November 8, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The injuries continue to pile up for the New England Patriots, who now are set to be without another key offensive contributor for multiple weeks. Running back Rhamondre Stevenson is dealing with a knee tendon issue that is not expected to require surgery but could sideline him for a short period, according to ESPN’s Adam Schefter. NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport added the injury is to the back of Stevenson’s knee and is expected to keep him out the next few weeks. Stevenson suffered the injury late in Sunday’s 45-27 loss to the Green Bay Packers after being brought down following a six-yard reception. He was quickly ruled out for the remainder of the game. The back has been one of New England’s most dependable players this season, playing 65% of the team’s offensive snaps. Stevenson has totaled 399 yards and two touchdowns on 102 carries while adding 26 receptions for 258 yards and two touchdowns through the air. His contributions in pass protection have also earned consistent praise from head coach Mike Vrabel and his teammates. With Stevenson and No. 2 running back TreVeyon Henderson (illness) sidelined, the Patriots are down to Corey Kiner and Lan Larison as their only running backs on the active roster ahead of their Week 10 matchup against the Detroit Lions in Germany. Kiner has seen the biggest workload in Henderson’s recent absence, carrying the ball 50 total times this season for 244 yards and a touchdown. “I think Corey is working extremely hard. I think Corey has done a really nice job,” Vrabel said Monday. “But there are also some things that Corey has to be able to improve on, just like a lot of guys, as far as recognition of the pressure and then the ability to block the pressure that we saw yesterday, for example.” The Patriots also have running back Terrell Jennings on the practice squad.

title: What waiving Tanner Arkin means for the Patriots
summary: The New England Patriots made a change to their 53-man roster on Monday. Tight end Tanner Arkin, who had been with the team since his arrival as a rookie free agent earlier this year and had made the roster out of training camp, was waived. Let’s assess what the move means for the Patriots. Blocking […]
full_text: The New England Patriots made a change to their 53-man roster on Monday. Tight end Tanner Arkin, who had been with the team since his arrival as a rookie free agent earlier this year and had made the roster out of training camp, was waived . Let’s assess what the move means for the Patriots. Blocking tight end needed The Patriots had four tight ends on their active roster coming out of Week 9, and all of them had seen the field during the 45-27 loss to the Green Bay Packers on Sunday. However, only three of the group — Hunter Henry, Eli Raridon and Arkin — actually were employed on offense; the fourth tight end, Cameron Latu, played exclusively on special teams. With Arkin now waived, the natural follow-up move would be to bump Latu up the depth chart and into a more expansive role as a third tight end and blocking option — one played by Arkin lately as well: in his five games so far, he played 50 snaps either run or pass blocking, and just 10 running routes. That said, the Patriots might not turn to Latu to work as their TE3; the fact Arkin played over him can already be interpreted as the team not fully trusting him in such a role. Instead, New England might just keep its current arrangement in place and use first-round rookie offensive tackle Caleb Lomu as a sixth lineman and de facto blocking tight end (albeit without the occasional receiver rep). Return an option Looking solely at the traditional tight ends on the Patriots’ pay roll right now, we can see that the team is down to three on the active roster plus one each on the practice squad and on injured reserve. The hierarchy is pretty established among them, with Hunter Henry and Eli Raridon the clear 1-2 punch at the position. 53-man roster (3): Hunter Henry (85), Eli Raridon (82), Cameron Latu (36) Practice squad (1): Tanner Conner (80) Injured reserve (1): Julian Hill (80) Should he pass through the waiver wire unclaimed, Arkin re-signing with New England’s practice squad appears to be a foregone conclusion. In that case, the team would be allowed to standard-elevate him to the game day roster on three separate occasions during the regular season. Sign of things to come? NFL teams can return up to eight players from injured reserve during the regular season, and the Patriots have taken advantage of that system four times so far. One would imagine that Arkin’s freed-up roster spot — that puts New England at 52 players — goes to a player set to come back from IR. The prime candidate at the moment appears to be interior offensive lineman Greg Van Roten, who returned to practice last week to open his 21-day activation window. With left guard Ben Brown not expected to be ready for New England’s upcoming game in Germany against the Detroit Lions, more quality depth up front will be important and Van Roten would be able to provide just that. Of course, the Patriots could also opt to go in a different direction. Arkin, after all, split his time between tight end, fullback and special teams this year. Maybe his spot goes to Reggie Gilliam, who is eligible to return from injured reserve as well and would be more of a 1-for-1 replacement. UDFA class takes a hit When the Patriots trimmed their roster to 53 players in late August, three undrafted rookie free agents made the cut. Arkin was one of them, joining linebacker Khalil Jacobs and cornerback Channing Canada. Two months later, only Canada remains on the active team: Arkin was just let go, while Jacobs has been on injured reserve since before the start of the regular season. At the moment, though, another rookie free agent is on the 53-man roster as well. Linebacker Erick Hunter was picked up by New England after his release from the Detroit Lions in early September, and has seen regular snaps on special teams since then.

title: Patriots waive rookie tight end Tanner Arkin from 53-man roster, open spot on practice squad
summary: After making back-to-back starts, Tanner Arkin will be subject to the NFL’s claiming period. The New England Patriots waived the rookie tight end from the 53-man roster on Monday and opened a spot on the practice squad by releasing outside linebacker Jose Ramirez. Arkin, 23, entered the league as part of the organization’s undrafted class […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - AUGUST 13: Tanner Arkin #84 of the New England Patriots runs with the ball prior to an NFL preseason football game against the Indianapolis Colts at Gillette Stadium on August 13, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images After making back-to-back starts, Tanner Arkin will be subject to the NFL’s claiming period. The New England Patriots waived the rookie tight end from the 53-man roster on Monday and opened a spot on the practice squad by releasing outside linebacker Jose Ramirez. Arkin, 23, entered the league as part of the organization’s undrafted class of 2026. The 6-foot-4, 262-pound former transfer from Colorado State to Illinois outlasted the league’s cutdown deadline after his preseason audition. He proceeded to appear in seven games while on the active roster. The stay included 60 snaps on offense and 41 snaps on special teams for Arkin, who also saw time at fullback in the absence of injured incumbent Reggie Gilliam. The blocking tight end’s exit leaves New England’s depth chart in the hands of captain Hunter Henry, No. 95 overall pick Eli Raridon and August waiver claim Cameron Latu. A fourth option in Tanner Conner currently resides on scout team. Ramirez, 27, had re-signed to the practice squad after clearing waivers off the 53-man roster in October and is now a free agent. The 6-foot-2, 252-pound edge rusher first agreed to terms at Gillette Stadium in September after being let go by the Philadelphia Eagles. He appeared in two games upon being promoted , notching one solo tackle across 30 snaps between defense and special teams. Selected by the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in the sixth round of 2023 draft class at No. 196 overall, Ramirez checked into four games during his time in the NFC South. The former MAC Defensive Player of the Year by way of Arizona, Riverside City College and Eastern Michigan finished last campaign with the CFL’s Hamilton Tiger-Cats before returning to the NFL on a futures contract in January. Along with wide receiver Mack Hollins, Patriots opened offensive lineman Greg Van Roten’s 21-day window to return from injured reserve last week and move forward with vacancies on both the 53-man roster and 17-man practice squad. After falling to the Green Bay Packers in 45-27 fashion, head coach Mike Vrabel’s 5-4 team will soon travel to Germany to face the Detroit Lions. Next Sunday’s kickoff at FC Bayern Munich Stadium is set for 9:30 a.m. ET.

full_text: The New England Patriots’ regular season is underway, which also means that their roster and practice squad will undergo near-constant change. For reference, between the opener and regular season finale alone last season, the eventual conference champions made 102 different transactions. It remains to be seen how many there will be in 2026, but things can get confusing quick. title: Saints RB Audric Estime makes Browns pay for letting him go
summary: Sometimes the NFL writes the perfect script, and Audric Estime could not have asked for a better opportunity to make a statement. After being waived by the Cleveland Browns earlier in the week, Estime found himself back home after the New Orleans Saints claimed him on waivers, playing a significant role in the recent victory […]
full_text: NEW ORLEANS, LA - NOVEMBER 08: Audric Estimé #30 of the New Orleans Saints carries the ball against the Cleveland Browns during the first half of the NFL football game at Cesars Superdome on November 8, 2026 in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images Sometimes the NFL writes the perfect script, and Audric Estime could not have asked for a better opportunity to make a statement. After being waived by the Cleveland Browns earlier in the week, Estime found himself back home after the New Orleans Saints claimed him on waivers, playing a significant role in the recent victory against his former club. Estime finished with 15 carries for 72 yards and a big-time touchdown, giving the Saints a much-needed boost in the backfield amid their run game struggles. The Browns had an opportunity to keep Estime after he impressed in his lone appearance with them but ultimately decided to move on. Just days later, he was helping the Saints secure a win against them. It’s difficult to imagine a more fitting way for a player to respond after not being rewarded for his production. For the Saints, Estime’s performance also raised an important question about whether they moved on from him too quickly. With the recent release of Kendre Miller, Estime being around earlier in the season could have been beneficial to New Orleans’ rushing attack. Estime didn’t need a heavy workload to make his presence felt, but his contributions made a difference, especially when the offense has been looking for someone to step up in the backfield. There is still plenty of football left to play, and one strong performance doesn’t guarantee Estime maintain this trajectory moving forward. However, he’s proven to make the most of his opportunities each time he steps on the field, no matter the uniform he’s sporting. He certainly made the most of his opportunity against Cleveland.

title: Saints vs. Browns: The good, the bad, and the ugly in Week 9
summary: The Good: Pass Rush The New Orleans Saints pass rush did a great job getting to Shedeur Sanders on Sunday, sacking the second-year quarterback five times while also getting three additional tackles for loss. Carl Granderson sacked Sanders twice and Chase Young sacked him once. Both players now rank in the top 3 in the […]
full_text: NEW ORLEANS, LOUISIANA - NOVEMBER 08: Shedeur Sanders #2 of the Cleveland Browns is sacked by Carl Granderson #96 of the New Orleans Saints during the third quarter at Caesars Superdome on November 08, 2026 in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Good: Pass Rush The New Orleans Saints pass rush did a great job getting to Shedeur Sanders on Sunday, sacking the second-year quarterback five times while also getting three additional tackles for loss. Carl Granderson sacked Sanders twice and Chase Young sacked him once. Both players now rank in the top 3 in the NFL in sacks with 7.5 for Granderson and 8 for Young, making them arguably the best pass rushing duo in the league so far this season. Khristian Boyd also picked up his second sack of the season, and Kaden Elliss had his best game of the year with one sack and a tackle for loss. The sacks were also very timely, with two of them coming on third down and two coming in goal to go situations which helped hold the Browns to a field goal and a turnover on downs in the red zone. The Saints run game also deserves a shoutout this week, as newly returning Audric Estime ran for 72 yards and a touchdown against the team who just waived him a week prior. Estime’s 72 yards were the most by a Saint this year, a good turnaround from their last game when Tyler Shough led the team with 7 rushing yards. The Bad: Pass Blocking Despite getting to Shedeur Sanders five times, the Saints also let the Browns sack Tyler Shough five times on Sunday. Four of these sacks came on third down as well, one of which probably cost the Saints three points by turning what would’ve been a 43-yard field goal into a 52-yard field goal which was missed. Only one sack came from a defensive lineman however, as the Saints struggled to keep up with the blitzes ran by Cleveland. The Browns have been good at getting to the quarterback this year, as they came into the game averaging just under 3 sacks per game, so hopefully the Saints offensive line will improve with the return of Kelvin Banks Jr. to the lineup. The Ugly: Defensive Backs The Saints defensive backs struggled to keep up with the Browns young receivers on Sunday. They allowed receptions of 60 yards to Denzel Boston and of 64 yards to KC Concepcion which also went for a touchdown. Concepcion beat Martin Emerson Jr. deep and was able to evade both Emerson and Julian Blackmon on his way to the end zone, and Kool-Aid McKinstry got beat deep and then was unable to find an underthrown ball leading to a 60-yard catch and run by Boston. Later in overtime Justin Reid was unable to tackle Harold Fannin Jr. in the open field which led to what could’ve been the winning touchdown if the Saints didn’t stop the ensuing two-point conversion. The Saints pass defense allowed Shedeur Sanders to have arguably the best game of his career and now ranks 28th in the NFL giving up 236 yards per game.

title: Saints vs. Browns: Week 9 Game MVP
summary: To begin the year, the fanbase was worried that the New Orleans Saints did not have a true complement on the opposite side of Chase Young to help generate pressure on opposing quarterbacks. Well, that question has been answered, as Carl Granderson has emerged as the missing edge rusher the Saints have needed this season. […]
full_text: NEW ORLEANS, LA - NOVEMBER 8: Carl Granderson #96 of the New Orleans Saints walks off the field following a 23-22 win against the Cleveland Browns at Caesars Superdome on November 8, 2026, in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Derick Hingle/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images To begin the year, the fanbase was worried that the New Orleans Saints did not have a true complement on the opposite side of Chase Young to help generate pressure on opposing quarterbacks. Well, that question has been answered, as Carl Granderson has emerged as the missing edge rusher the Saints have needed this season. Granderson has now recorded at least 1.5 sacks in four consecutive games. He was in the backfield almost the entire game, finishing with 7 tackles, 2 sacks, 2 QB hits, and 2 tackles for loss. He now has 7.5 sacks on the season and is tied for third in the league, trailing only Chase Young, who has 8, and Will Anderson Jr., who leads the NFL with 9.5. Without the pressure and impact Granderson had on this game, the Saints may have lost. New Orleans pulled out a one-point overtime victory against a scrappy Browns team, and the defense had to make plays to keep the Saints in the game during stretches when the offense was struggling to find its rhythm. Carl Granderson is my choice for Game MVP for Week 9. Do you think the Saints have found their edge-rushing duo? And who do you think should have been the Game MVP?

title: Game Recap: Saints host Browns in Week 9 clash
summary: The New Orleans Saints were back in action after the bye week when the Cleveland Browns visited the Big Easy on Sunday afternoon. Here’s a full recap of the matchup. First Quarter Cleveland began the game by going three-and-out, before Audric Estime got the Saints offense going straight away with three runs totalling 32 yards. […]
full_text: NEW ORLEANS, LOUISIANA - NOVEMBER 08: Jordyn Tyson #0 of the New Orleans Saints runs the ball against Ronnie Hickman #33 of the Cleveland Browns during the third quarter at Caesars Superdome on November 08, 2026 in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New Orleans Saints were back in action after the bye week when the Cleveland Browns visited the Big Easy on Sunday afternoon. Here’s a full recap of the matchup. First Quarter Cleveland began the game by going three-and-out, before Audric Estime got the Saints offense going straight away with three runs totalling 32 yards. Tyler Shough then found Juwan Johnson for 19 more with his first throw, but a few unsuccessful runs and a sack later, the Saints were held to a field goal attempt. Charlie Smyth converted from 30 yards to give the black and gold an early lead. The Browns were then forced into another quick punt as the Saints defense got off to a strong start. Shough found Chris Olave for 11 yards before breaking off for a 14-yard run, but it was soon another field goal attempt after he was sacked on 3rd down. This time, Smyth was no good from 52 yards, and the score remained 3-0. Second Quarter Shadeur Sanders found the first big play of the game for Cleveland with a 16-yard pass to Dylan Sampson, who also had a few short gains on the ground as the Browns drove past midfield. After being stuffed short of the chains on 3rd down, a 41-yard field goal from Andre Szmyt tied the game. Shough then copied a play from Paris with a 52-yard bomb downfield to Barion Brown as the Saints sought to regain the lead. But a play later, Jordyn Tyson fumbled after making a catch, which the defense fell on to return possession to the Browns. New Orleans was able to force another quick punt out of the Browns, but Brown fumbled on the return. Cleveland fell on it in the red zone. A penalty against Carl Granderson helped the visitors set up 1st-and-goal, but he made up for it by sacking Sanders to push them back. A few plays later, Sanders was just short of the goal line on 3rd-and-goal. The Browns offense stayed out there, and the Saints were able to come out big with a stop on 4th down to keep the game at 3-3. Shough connected with Olave for 36 yards to move the Saints out from deep in their own territory, but after another pass for just one yard and two incompletions, they were forced to punt just before the half. Third Quarter New Orleans went three-and-out and punted to begin the second half, before Sanders scrambled for 11 yards on 3rd down to avoid the same fate. He then completed a 60-yard pass to Denzel Boston to set up 1st-and-goal. But the Saints’ defense came up huge once again, with a tackle-for-loss, sack, and incompletion from Sanders limiting Cleveland to a chip-shot field goal that gave them a 6-3 lead. Shough responded with a scoring drive of his own, on a 54-yard drive highlighted by a 12-yard pass to Noah Fant and his own scrambles moving the ball down the field. Smyth’s 27-yard kick tied the game at 6-6. Cleveland then went three-and-out as Granderson got to the quarterback once again, but New Orleans would do the same, which gave the visitors the ball to begin the fourth. Fourth Quarter Sanders got the ball to midfield with a 10-yard pass to KC Concepcion, but failed to find another first down. He threw an incomplete pass to Sampson on 4th-and-2, and the Saints took over on downs again. Taking advantage of the shorter field, Shough moved the black and gold into field goal range with a 9-yard throw to Tyson. After being sacked by Myles Harden, the Saints were forced into yet another field goal, which Smyth converted from 48 yards. But the lead didn’t last long, as Sanders threw a 64-yard touchdown to Concepcion on the opening play of the ensuing drive to give Cleveland a 13-9 advantage. New Orleans then went three-and-out, before Cleveland had another punt of their own around the two-minute warning. Needing a touchdown, Shough found Olave for 33 yards to move the drive into the red zone. He then found Alvin Kamara for 8 more, before Estime ran in the 2-yard score to re-establish the lead for the black and gold. But Sanders threw twice for a total of 37 yards to Jerry Jeudy, which set up a field goal that Szmyt converted from 51 yards to force overtime. Overtime The Saints received first, and Kamara broke off three big runs as the ball moved past midfield. Shough then found Devaughn Vele for 9 yards before Estime ran for 9 more. Shough ran for 8 yards before finding Vele again, setting up a 15-yard touchdown throw to Johnson to give the black and gold a 23-16 lead. Needing a touchdown of their own, two passes from Sanders to Boston helped Cleveland into Saints territory. Sanders then found Harold Fannin Jr for a 39-yard touchdown. Cleveland opted to go for two and the win, which is where the Saints came up with the biggest stop of the day as Sanders’ pass intended for Boston fell incomplete. New Orleans held on 23-22 to set up a huge divisional matchup next weekend with the Carolina Panthers.

title: Saints vs. Browns: Winners and Losers from New Orleans’ thrilling win
summary: The New Orleans Saints found their third win of the season on Sunday, beating the Cleveland Browns en route to taking the lead in the NFC South. The win wasn’t pretty, and there’s plenty to work on, but there is light at the end of the tunnel after New Orleans’ victory out of the bye. […]
full_text: NEW ORLEANS, LA - NOVEMBER 08: Audric Estimé #30 of the New Orleans Saints rushes for a touchdown against the Cleveland Browns during the second half of an NFL football game at Cesars Superdome on November 8, 2026 in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New Orleans Saints found their third win of the season on Sunday, beating the Cleveland Browns en route to taking the lead in the NFC South. The win wasn’t pretty, and there’s plenty to work on, but there is light at the end of the tunnel after New Orleans’ victory out of the bye. Winner: RB Audric Estime Just two weeks ago, the Saints running backs ran for 11 rushing yards on 14 attempts. Going into the bye, that was the only conversation surrounding the Saints. They couldn’t run the ball all season, and it was on full display in another country. Coming out of the bye, the Saints lucked out and found a way to bring running back Audric Estime back on waivers. In his first game back with New Orleans, Estime ran for 72 yards on 15 carries, averaging 4.8 yards per carry and scoring a touchdown. While Travis Etienne’s return is on the horizon, Estime has likely found a role with the Saints where he’ll handle the bulk of the carries until he comes back. Winner: DE Carl Granderson Phew. The Saints have a dangerous pass rush combo. We all knew about Chase Young, who has 8 sacks in 8 games this season. But Carl Granderson has feasted off the attention Young brings and has brought his season sack total to 7.5 sacks. In the win against the Browns, Granderson logged 2 sacks and 2 tackles for loss. He was a game changer for the Saints on Sunday, and entered the week with a chip on his shoulder after a viral video of Shedeur Sanders seemingly laughing when asked a question about the Saints’ defense. While Sanders says he wasn’t laughing at the Saints’ defense, it opened the opportunity to add more motivation for the defense, and Granderson himself took it personally. If the former undrafted free agent can continue to play like this, New Orleans will end the season with two of the top three sack leaders. Loser: Saints’ Secondary Sunday’s matchup against the Browns was favored for the Saints secondary, who were facing a second-year quarterback in Sanders. The 2025 fifth-round pick got his first start of the 2026 season and faced the fierce Saints pass rush. The Saints pass rush did their job, but the secondary was outplayed in the biggest moments. From Denzel Boston missing Kool-Aid McKinstry to Julian Blackmon and Martin Emerson Jr. failing to tackle KC Concepcion after allowing a big catch that turned into a touchdown, we didn’t see the plays we needed from the secondary against Tetairoa McMillan. Loser: The Turnover Battle What stands out the most for me, however, is the Saints’ inability to force takeaways. This was a prime opportunity to force takeaways and come away with a dominant win. New Orleans, however, lost the turnover battle, losing two fumbles and not forcing any turnovers themselves. From Jordyn Tyson’s first reception turning into a fumble three yards from the end zone, to Barion Brown running backwards before losing the ball himself, the Saints are beating themselves. The Saints are -6 on the season in the turnover battle, and it continues to get further away from them.

title: How the NY Giants Dennard Wilson, Arvell Reese destroyed the Eagles’ passing attack
summary: The New York Giants have one of the NFL’s most promising young coaches in Dennard Wilson, who is finding ways to maximize the immense young talent on the roster. Rookie linebacker Arvell Reese credited the coaching staff’s strategic use of him as a key factor in his success. Reese had 1.5 sacks and six pressures […]
full_text: Arvell Reese | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The New York Giants have one of the NFL’s most promising young coaches in Dennard Wilson, who is finding ways to maximize the immense young talent on the roster. Rookie linebacker Arvell Reese credited the coaching staff’s strategic use of him as a key factor in his success. Reese had 1.5 sacks and six pressures heading into the Giants’ Week 9 matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles. The Giants traded Dexter Lawrence during the offseason, leaving a significant void in their ability to generate interior pressure. Lawrence had been a consistent force disrupting quarterbacks from the inside, but Wilson has found another way to manufacture pressure through creative blitz packages that attack the interior. He recognizes Reese’s ability as a pass rusher and the mismatch he creates when matched up against running backs in pass protection. Dennard Wilson has done an elite job scheming to the strengths of rookie LB Arvell Reese. Stack LBs w/ 5 man pressure…send Harris (1T) wide & Pinnock through the B to expand the OGs and isolate Reese vs. RB in protection. Reese is a weapon Wilson knows how to use best. pic.twitter.com/VG1fJjOryB — Nick Falato (@nickfalato) November 9, 2026 New York deployed a variety of pressure looks aimed at the center and guards, with defensive linemen widening their rush paths to manipulate the protection. Players like Kayvon Thibodeaux (5) would feign an outside rush, forcing offensive linemen to account for them as potential threats. This approach occupies blockers and creates advantageous one-on-one matchups elsewhere along the line — opportunities that a versatile talent like Arvell Reese can exploit. The hit heard around the world Charlie Jones fumbled a punt giving the Eagles the ball in Giants’ territory with all the momentum in the world; a situation that would have crippled past Giants’ teams. However, New York forced a third-and-5 pass attempt where Joe Milton was hit hard Reese: Arvell Reese knocked Joe Milton into next week pic.twitter.com/bfnKLaS0dV — Nick Falato (@nickfalato) November 9, 2026 New York schemed three over two to the offensive left side ( where Reese was) ; Dawuane Smoot (96) aligned as a 4i-shade, with Thibodeaux wide of the tackle and Reese wide of Thibodeaux. Micah McFadden (41) sugared the A-Gap, forcing center attention, with Darius Alexander as a three-technique (91), Abdul Carter (3) as a five-technique, and Dru Phillips (22) wide of Carter. The loaded line of scrimmage led to Saquon Barkley (26) accounting for McFadden and the three other rushers to the offensive right – and NO ONE accounted for Reese the left, including Milton. Both Smoot and Alexander dropped off into coverage, with Thibodeaux acting effectively as a spy once his initial rush was stopped and the four-man rush got home for an unblocked sack-forced fumble. Here’s another video of the hit: This sack by Arvell Reese was the fastest (2.29 seconds) in the NFL since week 7 of last season, according to @NextGenStats Reese is the only NFL player with 65+ tackles, 8+ TFL, 1+ INT so far in 2026. pic.twitter.com/uaNi5EmRzC — Dane Brugler (@dpbrugler) November 9, 2026 Reese’s second sack via GIPHY Reese had another third-down sack, this time on third-and-10. Wilson overloaded the offensive right side with four players on the line of scrimmage: Thibodeaux, Smoot, Alexander, and Tae Banks (2); Wilson aggressively aligns the corners in press coverage versus condensed fronts to gain a numbers advantage in the pass rush — Wilson isn’t shy about sending the cornerback to creatively cover the receiver. Reese is stacked behind Alexander, and he slants opposite to the protection slide toward McFadden and Carter, who both have one-on-one matchups due to the pressure-look. Elijah Mitchell (39) did an excellent job picking up McFadden, and Reese was stopped by the guard, so he slid off the rush and eyed Milton, who attempted to run into green grass, but instead found the waiting arms of an elite Ohio State rookie linebacker. Reese’s third sack via GIPHY Reese’s third sack came on third-and-10 with 7:22 left in the fourth quarter. Reese was aligned off the line of scrimmage in a 4i-shade with Thibodeaux to his right, wide of the tackle. Alexander was over the center, which isolated Reese against the guard, Landon Dickerson (69). New York ran a game with Reese penetrating the B-Gap for Thibodeaux to undercut and loop into the A-Gap, while another twist happened with Alexander and Carter. Final thoughts Wilson is on a tear. He’s generating pressure in a variety of different ways with a lot of exotic coverage looks on the back-end. Wilson uses disguise on a loaded line of scrimmage, while dropping his short-zone coverages off the line of scrimmage after declaring a rush, which effectively wastes blockers and isolates players like Reese and Abdul Carter into valuable one-on-one matchups. Not only do the Giants have immensely talented young defensive players, but the coach understands how to best maximize the talent. Arvell Reese is now the favorite to win defensive rookie of the year, but conversations about defensive player of the year are starting to happen. With performances like Week 9, it’s not crazy to mention his name in that conversation.

title: NFL power rankings: Nick’s picks for how teams stack up before Week 10
summary: No. 1 — Buffalo Bills (6-1) | SAME A defensive effort in which the Bills stopped the Vikings’ Carson Wentz-led offense, while Josh Allen and the offense did enough to secure a pivotal road victory against Minnesota. No. 2 — Chicago Bears (7-2) | SAME Caleb Williams started in his typical efficient self, and it […]
full_text: No. 1 — Buffalo Bills (6-1) | SAME A defensive effort in which the Bills stopped the Vikings’ Carson Wentz-led offense, while Josh Allen and the offense did enough to secure a pivotal road victory against Minnesota. No. 2 — Chicago Bears (7-2) | SAME Caleb Williams started in his typical efficient self, and it looked like he could do no wrong, but then he proceeded to throw four interceptions, and the Bears’ offense stagnated for much of the game after taking a 17-3 lead. The Buccaneers made the game interesting, forcing five turnovers, but Chicago held strong and defeated Tampa Bay, 27-24. No. 3 — San Fransico 49ers (7-1) | SAME Brock Purdy went 17 of 25 for 232 yards with a pair of touchdowns to help the 49ers defeat the Las Vegas Raiders, 38-17. The Raiders kept the game interesting up until about half-time, but the 49ers scored two touchdowns in the third quarter to pull away from the Raiders. The defense forced an insane five turnovers. San Francisco remains a top team in the NFL. No. 4 —Jacksonville Jaguars (6-2) | SAME Jacksonville is one of the hottest teams in the NFL, but they faced a Joe Fagnano’s Ravens team that only scored 10 points. Jacksonville won the game 33-10 and Trevor Lawrence only completed 16 passes. The Jaguars are an excellent young football team playing complementary football. No. 5 — Denver Broncos (7-2) | (6th) 📈 1 spot Denver found a way to earn a tough road win, again! Pat Bryant returned from IR and caught a touchdown from Bo Nix. Jonah Coleman continues to dominate touches as the team’s No. 1 back. Coleman had 17 carries for 57 yards and a touchdown in the game. No. 6 — Cincinnati Bengals (6-2) | (6th) 📈 3 spots The Bengals offense is playing very well. Joe Burrow tossed three touchdowns and 271 yards against the Falcons. Ja’Marr Chase caught ten passes for 155 yards with a touchdown. The rushing attack is still a work in progress for Cincinnati, but the Bengals have now won four games in a row, scoring over 30 points in each matchup. No. 7 —Minnesota Vikings (6-2) | (5th) 📉 2 spots The Minnesota Vikings battled the Bills but lost at home to Josh Allen. The Carson Wentz experience was not enjoyable, as he threw several interceptions and could not move the offense. Minnesota still has the best defense — and possibly the best unit overall — but this offense is bad. No. 8 —Kansas City Chiefs (6-2) | 📉 1 spot Kansas City got right against the Jets in a 35-12 victory. Patrick Mahomes completed 23 of 31 passes for 242 yards with a pair of touchdowns, and Kenneth Walker III rushed for over 100 yards with both receiving touchdowns. The Chiefs dominated an inferior opponent. No. 9 — Detroit Lions (6-2) | (8th) 📉 1 spot Detroit went into Miami and won a gritty game that relied on defensive football. Each team turned the football over once, and neither team earned 300 yards on offense. Kudos to Miami’s defense, but the Dolphins were a fish out of water for the Lions in Miami. No. 10 — Green Bay Packers (6-3) | 📈 3 spots The Green Bay Packers demolished the New England Patriots in their home. They forced four turnovers and gained 478 yards of offense. Jordan Love played out of his MIND, completing 23 of 29 for 372 yards and three touchdowns. Few teams are hotter than the Packers right now, and their defense matched their offense in New England. Green Bay did, however, lose running back Josh Jacobs to a broken finger. The Packers still have concerns, but Love is playing at an MVP rate. No. 11 — Seattle Seahawks (5-4) | (SAME Drew Lock is 2-0 this season for Seattle; he completed 19 of 28 passes for 175 yards and a touchdown in this low-scoring 17-3 win over Arizona. Seattle travels to Las Vegas to play the Raiders before going into a bye week. No. 12— Pittsburgh Steelers (6-2) | SAME The Pittsburgh Steelers were on their bye in Week 9. No. 13 —New York Giants (5-2-1) | (15th) 📈 2 spots The Giants continue to win football games because they’re well coached in every phase. The defense pressured and harassed Joe Milton all game, sacking the young quarterback seven times, while Matt Nagy called a fine game for multiple quarterback. Jameis Winston led the only touchdown drive against Vic Fangio’s defense. The Giants earned their first win in Philadelphia since 2013. No. 14 — Los Angeles Rams (5-4) | SAME The Rams defeated Washington 20-13 on the road, but lost their star receiver Puka Nacua in the last play of the game. Los Angeles is a good team that is well coached, but injuries are stacking up, and a lack of offensive playmakers is problematic. They may receive Terrance Ferguson back soon, but Matt Stafford is losing targets weekly. No. 15 — New England Patriots (5-4) | (10th) 📉 5 spots The Patriots were embarrassed by the Packers, 45-27. They’re an injured squad at receiver and Drake Maye tossed three interceptions and was harassed throughout the game. It was a tough look for New England on defense – they surrendered a surprising 478 yards to Jordan Love and the Packers. No. 16 — Houston Texans (3-5) | (20th) 📈 4 spots The Texans came off the bye week and blew the Chargers out, 44-22. C.J. Stroud went nuclear, finishing 21 of 35 for 384 yards with five touchdowns and a pick. Kayshon Boutte went four for 125 and two; Tank Dell four of 105 for one, and Nico Collins four for 55 with one as well. Houston played to their talent against the worst team in the league. No. 17 — Cleveland Browns (5-3) | (16th) 📉 1 spot Cleveland lost 23-22 in overtime. Shedeur Sanders went 19 of 31 for 297 yards with two touchdowns with exceptional individual efforts from Harold Fannin Jr. and KC Concepcion on the two 64 and 39 yard touchdown passes. Tyler Shough turned it on down the stretch of the game and the Saints found a way to secure victory at the end of the game. Cleveland has a decision to make next week – Sanders or DeShaun Watson? They’re a power-run team with an opportunistic, well-coached defense, but the Bears withstood a valiant come-from-behind effort. Tampa Bay lost 27-24. No. 19 — Baltimore Ravens (5-5) | (20th) 📈 1 spot Baltimore lost to Jacksonville, 33-10, but they were forced to start Joe Fagnano, who went 10 of 18 for 60 yards. The Panthers are now 3-5 with three straight losses. Brock Bowers caught seven passes for 111 yards with a touchdown on eight targets. The Raiders can’t beat a team like San Francisco on the road while throwing three picks and putting the ball on the ground three more times ( two of which were recovered by the other team ). Audric Estime, who was on the Browns’ practice squad last week, rushed for 72 yards and a touchdown for the Saints.
