title: NY Giants news: Trade deadline day, Cam Skattebo should be ‘full-go’, more
summary: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the stories you need to know as the Giants get set to face off with the Washington Commanders this Thursday. John Harbaugh is Giants’ biggest asset in years. Can he lead them on a dream playoff run? | The Athletic “I thought we had good players,” Harbaugh […]
full_text: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the stories you need to know as the Giants get set to face off with the Washington Commanders this Thursday. John Harbaugh is Giants’ biggest asset in years. Can he lead them on a dream playoff run? | The Athletic “I thought we had good players,” Harbaugh said as he was leaving Lincoln Financial Field as the first Giants head coach to win in this building since Tom Coughlin in 2013. “I didn’t really know the personality of the team, but I think what I learned is these guys have what it takes. They’re tough-minded, they’ve got big hearts and they’re willing to do what it takes. Having what it takes means you’re willing to do what it takes, and they’ve been willing to do it. They work, they believe and they don’t flinch.” Giants radio booth on Nabers as a teammate "It's not a ME thing. It's a WE thing." @CarlBanksGIII shares what John Harbaugh told him about Malik Nabers' leadership behind the scenes during their film breakdown. pic.twitter.com/TDXYL28bLR — Bleav (@BleavNetwork) November 9, 2026 Week 9 NFL Takeaways: Giants working the trade market aggressively | SI.com All of that’s enough to give any playoff-starved fan of Big Blue a sugar high. And yet, they’ll tell you this isn’t about going all in on anything, happy as they are with where the team is. No, under Harbaugh, and with holdover GM Joe Schoen, this is now their default setting. Which, they’ll tell you, has little to do with adjusting any sort of preseason expectation. “No, that’s not how we look at winning,” Harbaugh texted me from the team bus, heading back to New Jersey on Sunday night. “You’re never ONE thing away. This is not addition and subtraction. The math is running on multiple levels of formulas and algorithms and humanity. You have to assess your options and opportunities. Seek value. What makes your team better shorter- and long-term and avoid what hinders your team, even in possibility. It’s a case-by-case decision regarding options. The work is on finding and creating the options. That’s where the stones have to get turned over. We are building day-by-day for what’s coming tomorrow and in the future BOTH.” The five things we learned from Giants’ Week 9 win: The trade deadline priority is clear | New York Post The Giants ended their 13-game losing streak at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia with an inelegant but effective 19-11 victory over the Eagles, providing further separation from first place (the Giants are 5-2-1) and last place (the Eagles are 2-7) in the NFC East. Is finding help stopping the run more important than adding a running back at the trade deadline? Buying or Selling Latest Rumors Ahead of 2026 NFL Trade Deadline | Bleacher Report Giants Are Serious Suitors for RB Jonathan Taylor. The Giants could be an aggressive suitor for multiple reasons. They’re in the driver’s seat in the NFC East, and their lead ball-carrier, Cam Skattebo, missed the previous game with a hamstring injury. Furthermore, this season, when healthy, Skattebo has had ball-security issues, and the Giants benched him in Week 6. He has four fumbles in seven outings (six starts). Also, keep in mind that head coach John Harbaugh had workhorse running back Derrick Henry in his last two years with the Baltimore Ravens. Taylor isn’t the physically imposing ball-carrier that Henry is, but the three-time Pro Bowler is a trustworthy running back who can handle a big workload on the ground and help Big Blue establish a physical offensive identity. Verdict: Buy Chris Simms on Arvell Reese Arvell Reese is one of the best defensive players in the NFL 9 games into his rookie year. pic.twitter.com/DWZOJ0rfpm — Chris Simms (@CSimmsQB) November 9, 2026 Like a true defensive weapon, Arvell Reese is everywhere for Giants | The Record In the aftermath of Sunday’s 19-11 victory over the Eagles, the Giants’ first at Lincoln Financial Field since 2013, D.J. Reader added to the list of what makes Reese special: the intense purpose with which he approaches each snap. “Arvell proved yet again what I already knew, and I see it before every game, man,” Reader said. “He’s got this look in his eyes, he’s just ready to play. He’s gonna be special. He is special. I don’t know any young player that can do the things he does. I’m gonna be honest with you: you’ll have to find him. Maybe the kid in Seattle [safety Nick Emmanwori]. Because, you don’t find a kid that can cover the way he can cover. Come down and fill gaps in the run game. Rush the passer. Doesn’t miss tackles. He’s serious, man, and it’s special to watch. It’s very special.” NFL Week 9: Big takeaways, questions and fantasy spin from Sunday’s games | ESPN.com Linebacker Arvell Reese needed only 2.29 seconds to sack Philadelphia’s Joe Milton in the second quarter. It was the fastest time to a sack for a Giants player in the past 10 seasons when Reese got a free run at Milton and forced a fumble. It was part of a monster game for the impressive rookie, who had 12 tackles, three sacks, three quarterback hits, three tackles for loss and the forced fumble. Eagles’ Joe Milton tips cap to New York Giants DC Dennard Wilson | USAToday.com During his postgame press conference, Milton said the Giants “played great today” and specifically credited their approach. “They had great defensive calls and great players over there,” Milton told reporters. “What they did today was just pressure and play over the top.” He added that it was “great calls by the defensive coordinator” and offered a shout-out to the unit for stopping Philadelphia and making plays. title: Jordan Davis trade shows why Giants need to capitalize on 2026 opportunity
summary: The Philadelphia Eagles’ trade on Monday of defensive tackle Jordan Davis to the Jacksonville Jaguars is a perfect illustration of why the 5-2-1 New York Giants need to take advantage of the opportunity they have in the NFC East this season. The Eagles have won the division in three of the past four years, with […]
full_text: Jordan Davis | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles’ trade on Monday of defensive tackle Jordan Davis to the Jacksonville Jaguars is a perfect illustration of why the 5-2-1 New York Giants need to take advantage of the opportunity they have in the NFC East this season. The Eagles have won the division in three of the past four years, with two Super Bowl appearances and one title along the way. They won’t win it this time around. They are now 2-7 and riding a seven-game losing streak after Sunday’s 19-11 loss to the Giants. They are as far down as an Eagles team has been since 2020, when Philadelphia went 4-11-1. You have to know, though, that general manager Howie Roseman is not going to let the Eagles stay down. The Davis trade netted Roseman and the Eagles the massive return of a 2027 first-round and 2029 second-round pick. Per Adam Schefter , the Eagles now have 10 (yes, 10!!!) draft picks in Rounds 1 and 2 over the next three drafts. It looks like this: 2027: 1st, 2nd, Jaguars’ 1st (Jordan Davis) 2028: 1st, 2nd, Patriots’ 1st (A.J. Brown), Ravens’ 2nd (Cam Jurgens) 2029: 1st, 2nd, Jaguars’ 2nd (Jordan Davis) So, yes, the Eagles will be reloading quickly. Per Team Rankings , the Giants now have a 71.4% chance to make the playoffs, and a 69.6% chance to win the NFC East. The door is wide open for the Giants. They need to be mindful of what the Eagles are doing, which might add another reason for the Giants to be aggressive before Tuesday’s 4 p.m. ET trade deadline. By the way, the Jaguars must really be fearful of the Giants’ offense. Jacksonville visits MetLife Stadium in Week 11. On Monday, the Jaguars traded first- and second-round picks for Davis, acquired defensive tackle Davon Godchaux from the New Orleans Saints for a conditional sixth-round pick, and got safety Jessie Bates III for a 2027 second-round and 2028 fifth-round pick.

title: Fantasy Football 2026: Waiver Wire, week 10 edition
summary: Welcome to the Fantasy Football Waiver Wire for Week 10. We’re at the halfway point of the NFL season, and for most fantasy leagues, only five weeks remain before the playoffs start. A critical stretch of the season is here, and with the bye weeks still in play and lots of players battling injuries, the […]
full_text: Pop is popping off | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Welcome to the Fantasy Football Waiver Wire for Week 10. We’re at the halfway point of the NFL season, and for most fantasy leagues, only five weeks remain before the playoffs start. A critical stretch of the season is here, and with the bye weeks still in play and lots of players battling injuries, the Waiver Wire continues to be an important resource, even if it’s mostly been picked clean in the last month or so. The NFL trade deadline is Tuesday at 4 p.m., and whether certain players (Jonathan Taylor, Tony Pollard, George Pickens, Josh Downs, Brian Thomas, Jr., Dallas Goedert, and a few others) get shipped will have an impact on waiver moves. Pay close attention to trade news. The Process : Each week, I try to identify the top Waiver Wire targets and evaluate the short- and long-term prospects of those players. I also do my best to reveal which players who are coming off a big week are fool’s gold. Finally, I look at streamers who might help you in a pinch (this is usually more important during Bye weeks). Some players discussed won’t be available in your league. I try to list players who are available in more than 50% of leagues. But what does that even mean? A 10-team league with six bench spots will have a much larger Free Agent pool than a 14-team league with eight. Most leagues fall somewhere in between. This isn’t “one size fits all.” By way of example, I won’t list Bryce Young , Kirk Cousins , Tyler Allgeier , Devin Singletary , Jordyn Tyson , or Ryan Flournoy , among others who probably aren’t available in any of your leagues. Note that I’m writing this column BEFORE the Week 9 Monday night game (MIN@BUF). WEEK 10 BYES: Bears, Broncos, Buccaneers, and Eagles Week 10 Waiver Wire Quarterback: Geno Smith makes my list once again. I think that makes five straight weeks. He struggled against the Chiefs, as expected, in a game played without Garrett Wilson (concussion). The Bills are up next, and Geno will be forced to play catch-up in that contest. The Chargers and Dolphins follow. Geno continues to be a viable play as a QB2. Aaron Rodgers has been decent for fantasy this season and a mainstay in my QB waivers list. Coming off the bye this week, the Steelers get the red-hot, high-scoring Bengals. Rodgers threw for almost 300 yards and three TDs against Cincinnati in Week 6. He should be getting some more receiving help soon, and is a nice streaming option this week and beyond. The QB2 options have thinned out due to injuries and poor play. Here’s a telling statistic: 47 QBs have started games through Week 9 and that’s the second highest total this century. There are quite a few available “starters” that I wouldn’t look to add, either because they don’t offer much upside ( Joe Milton III , J.J. McCarthy , Gardner Minshew II , any QB on the Chargers ) and/or it’s not clear how long they’ll be the starter ( Shedeur Sanders , Drew Lock ). I’m curious to see how Carson Wentz plays on Monday night, and he could be one to consider if you’re desperate. I have him ranked ahead of the guys I just listed. Note that McCarthy and Lock are not locks to be healthy enough to play this week. Need a Week 10 streamer? Jacoby Brissett might be available in your league. I’m not a big believer, but he should be ready to start for the Ravens in Week 10 and if you’re stuck, you could do worse than a date with the Chargers, who gave zero effort on defense against the Texans. I don’t think the Raiders are trading Kirk Cousins or benching him any time soon. Stashing Fernando Mendoza isn’t worth the roster spot at this point. Running Back: The trade deadline figures to have the biggest impact here. Seth McGowan is apparently still available in more than half of leagues on some big platforms. If Jonathan Taylor gets moved, his value shoots up. Even if he stays put, McGowan is getting more work and is one of the better handcuffs to roster. The same is true for Tyjae Spears and Nick Singleton on the Titans, if Tony Pollard gets traded. Corey Kiner stands to be the Week 10 starter for the Patriots if Rhamondre Stevenson misses time. Stevenson left Sunday’s blowout loss to the Packers with a knee injury (plus, he lost a fumble), and TreVeyon Henderson missed the game with an illness. The Patriots only have one game before their Week 11 bye, so I wouldn’t go too crazy with a bid for Kiner, but he’s going to be a very popular add this week. Audric Estime is another back who could get more run as the de facto “starter”, but it could be short-lived, depending on when Travis Etienne, Jr., is back. Estime ran well as the “early downs” back on Sunday (15-72-1), while Alvin Kamara got most of the third down and passing game work. He’ll be a competitive add this week, as this is a good offense and Etienne’s imminent return isn’t assured. This week’s matchup (CAR) is a juicy one. Kaleb Johnson and Marshawn Lloyd are worth adding, with Josh Jacobs possibly headed to IR. Green Bay can’t run the ball, but volume is volume. Lloyd missed Week 9 with a knee injury so I’d prioritize Johnson. Backs who should be rostered: Kenneth Gainwell, Dylan Sampson, Emmett Johnson , and Kaelon Black. Jonathon Brooks (IR stash) is another to consider if you have an IR spot. Wide Receiver DeMario Douglas is filling the void created by A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs being out of the lineup, and he’s my top choice at WR. The volume is inconsistent, but he’s quietly put up three Top-10 weekly finishes at his position over the past five weeks. I’ll recommend another guy with the same last name. Miami’s passing offense is bad, but Caleb Douglas is emerging as their top target, and a decent downfield threat. He’s put up between 70-95 receiving yards in three of four complete games he’s played. Kayshon Boutte and Tank Dell both went off in the Texans’ rout this week, but I’d be careful chasing those performances too hard. Both receivers are boom/bust deep threats, and the Chargers didn’t show up at all this week. The 49ers and Rams continue to lose receivers like I lose my eyeglasses. I always eventually find them, though. These two teams have struggled to find replacements who can step up. It’s hard to recommend much here, but I think you can consider Jordan Watkins , De’Zhaun Stribling (IR stash), and with Puka Nacua now joining Davante Adams on IR, one of Konata Mumpfield or Tutu Atwell is likely to step up (and keep an eye on the Rams trying to add a receiver via trade). Need depth? I’ll repeat a bunch of names I’ve listed in recent weeks, together with some new ones: Antonio Williams , Pat Bryant , Keenan Allen , Jahan Dotson, Jakobi Meyers, Savion Williams , and Chimere Dike . Tight End: Mike Gesicki finally didn’t score last week. He’s very TD-or-bust, and so is Pat Freiermuth . If you need a replacement this week, I like both as streaming options (their teams face each other). Darren Waller went off in Week 9, after vanishing for more than a month, so he’ll be a popular target this week. It’s buyer beware, but an 8-90-1 line on 10 targets will always turn heads. Just know that you might get one catch for four yards next week. Chig Okonkwo has been in this column for a solid month now. He hasn’t popped but has been serviceable. Terrance Ferguson was expected back last week but wasn’t activated. Hopefully his ankle will be OK this week, as the Rams will be without Nacua and Adams for at least the next month. Ferguson will compete with the other tight ends in L.A., but when all is said and done, he should be the best of the bunch, in an offense that’s going to have to feature them. That’s all I’ve got. Good luck with your waiver claims! ***This column appears each Monday right here at Big Blue View. Each Thursday, my weekly fantasy preview with my rides, fades and sleepers (start/sit) appears here, and on Fridays you can find my weekly Giants Props of the week, also right here. ***
author: David Hartman

title: PFF grades and advanced stats for the Giants’ 19-11 victory over the Eagles
summary: The curse of The Linc has finally ended, and while it wasn’t pretty and it wasn’t dominating, it was a win, and a division win, nonetheless. The New York Giants now have about a two in three chance of winning the NFC East Division. That is probably their only avenue to the playoffs since most […]
full_text: The curse of The Linc has finally ended, and while it wasn’t pretty and it wasn’t dominating, it was a win, and a division win, nonetheless. The New York Giants now have about a two in three chance of winning the NFC East Division. That is probably their only avenue to the playoffs since most teams in the NFC North and NFC West are likely to finish with better records, but the Giants will take whatever they can get. Let’s take a look at Pro Football Focus grades and advanced stats to better understand who played well and who didn’t against the Eagles. PFF grades: Offense Jameis Winston showed why he is the ideal NFL backup quarterback. Pressed into action after J.J. McCarthy’s hip pointer in a game that was hanging in the balance with the Giants behind 8-6, Winston coolly led the Giants to the go-ahead touchdown that turned the game around. He finished 6 of 8 for 71 yards and the TD to Isaiah Likely and was credited with one big-time throw. J.J. McCarthy didn’t play great early on when the Eagles’ defense seemed to be taking away his first reads and they were getting pressure on him, but he came back onto the field and gutted it out after his injury and overall played pretty well, with two big-time throws credited by PFF. The flip side to the good quarterback play was the subpar offensive line play. The pass blocking was not bad. Bryan Hudson continues to play at least adequately at center, though he did surrender one sack. Jon Runyan gave up a hit and two hurries and Sisi Mauigoa a sack and a hurry, which are not terrible results against that tough Eagles interior defensive line. Andrew Thomas got an average pass block grade but only gave up one hurry, while Jermaine Eluemunor had a completely clean stat line and an excellent pass block grade. It’s in the run game that we see the offensive line’s shortcomings. Every starting lineman besides Hudson had a below average run block grade, and Mauigoa, Runyan, and Thomas all had terrible run block grades. If the Giants do manage to trade for Jonathan Taylor, don’t expect him to look like the JT that ran behind Quenton Nelson all those years in Indianapolis. Why was the line so bad Sunday when it looked good in Houston? Most likely because the Texans’ DL strength is on the edge, while the Eagles’ strength now is in the interior. The other reason the Giants’ running game is in tatters is because their two best running backs are injured. Devin Singletary didn’t do much in a starting role. The biggest excitement was from Greg Desrosiers, who actually bounced one outside for 9 yards, a rare sight this season, and showed some giddyup the Giants might consider making more use of if Cam Skattebo isn’t back by Thursday. As for the receivers, Malik Nabers was quiet yesterday (on the field, anyway) with only 43 yards and 5 receptions in 8 targets. That would have looked a lot better if he’d hauled in that beautiful end zone throw from McCarthy that was just a tad long but not impossible to catch for one of the NFL’s best receivers. The best news is that Darnell Mooney had his best game as Giant with three receptions in three targets for 54 yards; he got the best PFF grade of any Giants receiver. Isaiah Likely had a more quiet day than in some previous games but still caught the key TD pass that turned the game in the Giants’ favor, winding up with 53 yards. Malachi Fields didn’t have any spectacular plays like the one in Houston, but he had his usual day with three catches in five targets for 40 yards. Fields has had at least two receptions in every game this season. PFF grades: Defense You’ll probably be shocked to see that Arvell Reese was not the Giants’ most highly rated defensive player yesterday. That’s for one primary reason – pass coverage. It’s the one part of Reese’s game that is still under construction. Yesterday he gave up seven completions in eight targets for 55 yards including 26 YAC. Three of those completions were to wide receivers (Makai Lemon and Darius Cooper), and you can’t blame Reese for not making those plays; wide receiver on linebacker is always advantage, offense. When he was doing his day job, though, Reese excelled, getting an elite grade in pass rush because of his three sacks and his usual very good grade in run defense due to two run stops. Here’s a great angle on Reese’s obliteration of Eagles QB Joe Milton III with an interesting stat line from The Athletic’s Dane Brugler: This sack by Arvell Reese was the fastest (2.29 seconds) in the NFL since week 7 of last season, according to @NextGenStats Reese is the only NFL player with 65+ tackles, 8+ TFL, 1+ INT so far in 2026. pic.twitter.com/uaNi5EmRzC — Dane Brugler (@dpbrugler) November 9, 2026 Defensive Rookie of the Year? How about Defensive Player of the Year? (The latter won’t happen but you can make the case.) Elsewhere on the defense, Greg Newsome was the highest graded Giant with an elite 88.4 defense grade. Newsome’s game-by-grades as a Giant: 38.2, 51.9, 66.4, 63.7, 60.3, 71.5, 88.4. This is a reminder to us all not to judge players too quickly. Newsome seems to have progressively adjusted to Dennard Wilson’s defensive philosophy and is starting to play at a high level reminiscent of his early NFL career. No wonder the Giants extended him. Newsome made 6 tackles yesterday and gave up 2 receptions in 4 targets for only 13 yards. The rest of the cornerback room was less successful. Dru Phillips played his usual great game in run defense but was only adequate in pass coverage. Deonte Banks had a subpar score, mostly the result of his 30-yard pass interference penalty on a pass to Darius Cooper that set the Eagles up on the 3-yard line and led to their only TD. At safety, Ar’Darius Washington has taken on an increased role in recent games. He made three tackles and was targeted once, unsuccessfully. Jason Pinnock played adequately but uneventfully, with nothing on his stat line (including targets). Jevon Holland had an average stat line, with 2 tackles (both stops) and 3 assists and one 10-yard reception in 2 targets. The missing name? Tyler Nubin, now apparently a special teams player only – zero defensive snaps yesterday after only one in Houston. Some interesting things are happening on the interior defensive line. Darius Alexander had his best game of the season, with a sack, a hit, and a hurry and adequate run defense. Likewise sixth-round rookie Bobby Jamison-Travis is now getting a consistent 20-ish snaps per game (63 in the past three games after not playing on defense at all before that). As advertised, he provides nothing in the pass rush but he’s had six tackles, three of them stops, in the run game and hasn’t missed a tackle yet. D.J. Reader, now the stalwart of the IDL, had a sack, a hit and two hurries in addition to a tackle and an assist. If BJT further develops Shelby Harris may be the odd man out. Yesterday he played 35 snaps, typical of previous games, but had his second consecutive poor game because of his run defense (or lack thereof). He had one pressure yesterday, but that’s only his third of the year from a player who at one time was considered one the league’s better pass rushing IDLs. On the outside, Kayvon Thibodeaux was given only an average grade by PFF, but he had a good stat line, with two QB hits, two hurries and three tackles, two of them stops. Abdul Carter had one of his most quiet games, with no QB pressures and just one tackle (a stop). Shoutout to Dawuane Smoot in his first action as a Giant – he had a sack and a hurry in addition to one tackle (a stop), even though his overall grade was not great. Finally, with all the attention on Arvell Reese, let’s mention Micah McFadden, who had a sack and a QB hit yesterday in addition to five tackles (two of them stops) and four assists. He only gave up two receptions for 13 yards in five targets, but his coverage grade was low, suggesting that the players he was covering were getting open more often than the number of balls coming his way would…

title: NY Giants planning ‘White Out’ game vs. Commanders
summary: The New York Giants are preparing to host Thursday Night Football against the Washington Commanders, and they want to make it a unique experience at MetLife Stadium. With the Giants in first place at 5-2-1, the team wants to have a playoff-like atmosphere to give the players a homefield advantage. The Giants are wearing all […]
full_text: The New York Giants are preparing to host Thursday Night Football against the Washington Commanders, and they want to make it a unique experience at MetLife Stadium. With the Giants in first place at 5-2-1, the team wants to have a playoff-like atmosphere to give the players a homefield advantage. The Giants are wearing all white against the Commanders, and they are encouraging the fanbase to do the same. From a press release issued by the team: “The Giants are set to wear their “Vintage White” uniforms and fans are strongly encouraged to wear white to the game to “White Out” MetLife Stadium. All attendees will receive a rally towel along with wearable light bands, which will be used for coordinated stadium-wide displays throughout the game. Fans are encouraged to arrive early and be in their seats by 7:45 p.m. for special player introductions, fireworks and a laser show,“ a press release read. “The Giants are also providing fans with an opportunity to gear up for gameday by visiting the “White Out” Shop, featuring a limited edition “White Out” collection from Starter along with other apparel including the “Vintage White” jerseys. The shop will be open for early access on Wednesday, Nov. 11 from 11 a.m. to 7 p.m. outside MetLife Stadium between the MetLife and Verizon Gates. Parking for the Wednesday shop is free in Lot F, and no parking pass is required.“ The Giants wore their vintage white jerseys for their Week 9 win against the Philadelphia Eagles, and they hope they can go undefeated in those jerseys for the season. It’s the only time the vintage jerseys will be worn at home this season, and it’s meant to be a celebration of the 1980’s when the franchise won its first Super Bowl. “The Vintage White jerseys and pants resurfaced in 2016 as part of the NFL’s Color Rush concept, which commemorated 50 years of games being broadcast in color. The white jersey features blue numbers with a red outline, just like the Giants wore on the road for two decades.”

Here’s some popcorn, Jets fans; this should be a fascinating couple of hours as we sit on the edge of our seats. title: Jets trade defensive back for 2028 draft pick
summary: The Andre Cisco era is over for the New York Jets. Actually, that’s a misnomer. These days we seem to always designate something an era that in no way merits the term. Andre Cisco falls firmly in that category. The New York Jets have traded backup safety Andre Cisco to the Detroit Lions for a […]
full_text: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - SEPTEMBER 13: Cam Ward #1 of the Tennessee Titans evades pressure by Andre Cisco #8 of the New York Jets during the first half of the game at Nissan Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Chris Carter/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Andre Cisco era is over for the New York Jets. Actually, that’s a misnomer. These days we seem to always designate something an era that in no way merits the term. Andre Cisco falls firmly in that category. The New York Jets have traded backup safety Andre Cisco to the Detroit Lions for a 2028 sixth round draft pick. That’s better. The Jets originally acquired Andre Cisco by signing him as an unrestricted free agent in 2025. Cisco was brought in expecting to be a playmaker in the back end of the defense, but it did not work out that way. After eight weeks of uninspired play in 2025 in which Cisco racked up zero interceptions, one pass defended, one tackle for loss and one fumble recovery, with little in the way of defensive playmaking, Cisco’s 2025 campaign ended with a season ending injury. The Jets let his contract expire in 2026 and Cisco explored free agency before the Jets brought him back on a one year, $2.2 million deal. He was expected to compete with Dane Belton for the safety spot opposite Minkah Fitzpatrick, but Belton is clearly the better player. Fitzpatrick missed time early in the season, opening up playing time for Cisco, but Cisco did little with the opportunity. Once Fitzpatrick returned to action Cisco was relegated primarily to special teams play. Over parts of two seasons Andre Cisco played 17 games for the Jets, starting 12. He racked up a total of 64 tackles, one sack, two passes defended, one forced fumble, three tackles for loss and one fumble recovery with the Jets. Cisco allowed an abysmal 115 passer rating in coverage during his time with the Jets. The trade of Cisco opens up playing time for 2025 fourth round draft pick Malachi Moore in the short run. 2026 seventh round pick V.J. Payne also stands to benefit from the trade as he works his way back from a preseason injury that has kept him out of action so far this season.

title: Eagles-Bengals trade canceled
summary: Just an hour after news broke that the Eagles were trading edge Arnold Ebiketie to the Bengals, Cincinnati has cancelled the move after re-considering how it would impact their compensatory draft picks next year. The initial trade terms were: Eagles: EDGE Arnold Ebiketie Bengals: 6th round pick in 2027 The problem, however, is that Ebiketie […]
full_text: Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images | Getty Images Just an hour after news broke that the Eagles were trading edge Arnold Ebiketie to the Bengals , Cincinnati has cancelled the move after re-considering how it would impact their compensatory draft picks next year. The initial trade terms were: Eagles : EDGE Arnold Ebiketie Bengals : 6th round pick in 2027 The problem, however, is that Ebiketie was signed by the Eagles as a compensatory free agent, which means the Bengals would ultimately be giving up their comp pick from trading Trey Hendrickson during the offseason. So while on paper they were only trading a sixth-rounder, they really were giving up a third-round pick as well — notably, it’s interesting the Bengals hadn’t considered this factor before agreeing to terms… Arnold Ebiketie was signed as a compensatory free agent by the Eagles. The Bengals lost 3 CFAs and signed 2 (Cordell Volson not qualifying), thus while they gain a 2027 6th rounder, they lose a 2027 3rd round comp pick that was via Trey Hendrickson going to Baltimore. https://t.co/DxWAA8L0KN — Nick Korte (@nickkorte) November 10, 2026 There’s still several hours until the NFL trade deadline, but for now, Ebiketie will stay in Philadelphia — and will stay knowing he was someone the team was willing to move. The trade indicated that the Eagles are likely committing to Nolan Smith long term, and with Jonathan Greenard healthy, Ebiketie’s playing time was already reduced. Vibes in the #Eagles ’ building right now after this one fell through: 🤬 — Mike Garafolo (@MikeGarafolo) November 10, 2026

title: Eagles-Bengals trade: Arnold Ebiketie to Cincinnati
summary: The Philadelphia Eagles are hardly done making deals prior to Tuesday’s NFL trade deadline. The latest move by Howie Roseman is as follows, according to NFL insider Ian Rapoport: PHILADELPHIA EAGLES RECEIVE — 2027 sixth-round pick CINCINNATI BENGALS RECEIVE — EDGE Arnold Ebiketie The Eagles originally signed Ebiketie to a one-year contract with $4.3 million […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PA - OCTOBER 26: Philadelphia Eagles linebacker Arnold Ebiketie #17 looks on during the game between the Dallas Cowboys and the Philadelphia Eagles on October 26, 2026 at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia, PA.(Photo by Andy Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles are hardly done making deals prior to Tuesday’s NFL trade deadline. The latest move by Howie Roseman is as follows, according to NFL insider Ian Rapoport: PHILADELPHIA EAGLES RECEIVE — 2027 sixth-round pick CINCINNATI BENGALS RECEIVE — EDGE Arnold Ebiketie The Eagles originally signed Ebiketie to a one-year contract with $4.3 million guaranteed during free agency back in March. He’s played 48% of the Eagles’ defensive snaps this season, logging zero sacks, zero tackles for loss, and two quarterback hits. As a rotational edge rusher, Ebiketie would’ve played even less if the Eagles weren’t dealing with injuries to Jonathan Greenard, Jalyx Hunt, and Nolan Smith. With that trio seemingly getting healthier, Ebiketie became expendable as a player unlikely to return to Philly after the 2026 season. And so getting anything of value for Ebiketie is a win. A Day 3 pick in the 2027 NFL Draft is hardly thrilling but it’s better than nothing. The Eagles are now projected to have these selections in the 2027 NFL Draft: 1st (own) 1st (from Jacksonville Jaguars) 2nd (own) 3rd (projected compensatory pick) 4th (own) 5th 5th (from Baltimore Ravens) 5th (from New England Patriots) 6th (from Cincinnati Bengals) 7th (from Minnesota Vikings) And the Eagles are probably not done adding to this stockpile. Ebiketie’s departure also opens up a spot for the Eagles to potentially sign rookie Keyshawn James-Newby or Mason Reiger from the practice squad to the roster.

title: Eagles News: ESPN says Jordan Davis trade is a disaster for the Jaguars
summary: Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! I really like Jordan Davis. I wanted the Eagles to draft him and I enjoyed rooting for him. But taking what the Jacksonville Jaguars offered for him was a no-brainer. There were people talking about the Eagles potentially getting trade offers […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - JANUARY 4: Jordan Davis #90 of the Philadelphia Eagles looks on against the Washington Commanders at Lincoln Financial Field on January 4, 2026 in Philadelphia, United States. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! I really like Jordan Davis. I wanted the Eagles to draft him and I enjoyed rooting for him. But taking what the Jacksonville Jaguars offered for him was a no-brainer. There were people talking about the Eagles potentially getting trade offers for Jalen Carter for a similar price of a first-round pick and a second-round pick. To get that for Davis, who is a lesser player who isn’t trusted to play as much as Carter … it’s insane. Howie Roseman clearly overpaid Davis but he’s very good at not doubling down on mistakes and instead making his wrongs right. Well done by the Eagles. Very interested to see how they utilize their draft picks to help spark the next era of success. Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … NFL trade deadline grades: Deals for Jordan Davis, Jessie Bates III, Andre Cisco – ESPN There’s no other way to start this: This trade is a disaster for Jacksonville. The Jaguars are absolutely right to go for it. Entering Monday, they had a 12.8% chance to win the Super Bowl, per ESPN’s Football Power Index, second highest of any team and best in the AFC. And that’s why I was OK with them rolling the dice on Jessie Bates III earlier in the day. A late-round pick for Davon Godchaux, too? Fine. But first- and second-round picks for Davis? Reckless would be putting it mildly. The numbers do not paint a picture of Davis being someone who is worth anywhere near that type of trade compensation. He has played 52% of snaps for the Eagles. That number is not particularly unusual for a run-stuffing nose tackle, but that’s exactly the point: The Jaguars just dealt first- and second-round picks for a part-time player who helps only against the run! There is no world where that is worth it. Davis has a run stop win rate in the 71st percentile among interior defenders this season. He was in the 93rd percentile in 2025 and the 52nd percentile in 2024. This season, he has a 13.5% run stop rate — the rate at which a player records a tackle on a run that resulted in a successful play for the defense by EPA — per NFL Next Gen Stats, 14th best among defensive tackles with at least 100 run defense snaps and just behind former Eagles teammate Moro Ojomo. In other words, he has been a good run defender, not elite. Eagles are stockpiling draft picks through 2029 – BGN The Eagles surprised just about everyone when it was announced that they were trading Jordan Davis to the Jaguars ahead of the NFL trade deadline, but they got a huge return for their defensive tackle, including a first-round draft pick in 2027 and a second-round pick in 2029. Those two acquistions give Howie Roseman 10 total picks in the first two rounds over the next three drafts, 26 total projected through all rounds. That’s insane! Jordan Davis trade grades: Jaguars-Eagles blockbuster as Jags load up for Super Bowl run – SB Nation Philadelphia Eagles grade: A. I am always going to give a big-time writer’s tilt when it comes to teams accepting the position they’re in. When news first emerged that the Jaguars traded a 1st and 2nd for an Eagles DT we all assumed at SB Nation that Jacksonville was getting Jalen Carter, not Jordan Davis. Philly gave up a player they can replace and got a significant return. This was a very smart move for a team that doesn’t have a shot in 2026 and is playing for next year. Their picks in 2027 can help address their much larger need concerns along the offensive line, and simply improve the team from the bottom up — which needs to happen. This is an example of an incredibly well-oiled franchise taking advantage of a team desperate to make an impact. It wasn’t neccesarily a seller’s market on run stopping DTs, but they made it one anyway. Another trade! Jaguars land their defensive game-changer in Jordan Davis – Big Cat Country There’s always a danger in handing out top grades for blockbuster trades. Draft capital matters, and surrendering a first and second-round pick is a considerable commitment. But the Jaguars have a genuine opportunity to do something special this season. They’ve lost important defensive starters to injury, identified the positions that need strengthening and gone out to acquire established NFL talent. Godchaux brings experience. Bates brings leadership and playmaking ability. Davis brings size, power, youth and the potential to anchor the defensive interior for the foreseeable future. Most importantly, these additions complement a roster that was already performing at an exceptionally high level. James Gladstone and Liam Coen clearly believe this team is ready to compete for the biggest prize in football. Rather than sitting back and hoping their existing roster is good enough, they’ve invested heavily in making sure it is. This is what going ALL IN looks like. The Jaguars have made their intentions abundantly clear, and the rest of the league have just been put on notice. NFL trade grades: Jaguars overpay for Jordan Davis while going all in on Super Bowl chase – The Athletic Eagles grade: A+. This is an impressive return for Roseman, and the Eagles are now loaded with future draft capital. They now have two first-round picks in 2027, and two first-round picks in 2028, their own and the Patriots’ pick from the A.J. Brown trade. They also own two second-round picks in 2029. That is a ton of ammunition to use in whatever fashion Roseman sees fit. They could stick and pick. They could trade any of those picks for veteran players. They could package them to move around in the draft. As our Jonathan Jones wrote in our trade deadline live blog, “What the Eagles have now is total optionality.” This clears the way for the Eagles to extend Ojomo, who is on the final year of his rookie deal. It is always difficult to hand out three large contracts to one position group. The Eagles are also paying Jalen Carter a top-of-market contract. They will incur a palatable dead-money charge of $15.4 million for Davis in 2027, according to figures from Over The Cap. Roseman is doing the right thing, turning a losing season into future opportunity. NFL trade grades: Evaluating every deal made ahead of the 2026 deadline – NFL.com Davis has been a good run defender for his career, but his 13.5% run-stop rate this season ranks 14th among DTs with a minimum of 100 run plays defended — behind teammate Moro Ojomo, I should add — with a 1.8 run stuff percentage (T-58th). Last year, before he got paid, was his best season with a 16.5% run-stop rate (fourth among DTs) with a run stuff rate of 4.3%, behind that of DaVon Hamilton, whom he’s essentially been brought in to replace. There is the risk for the Jags. It feels like a knee-jerk reaction to Hamilton’s injury led to a massive overpay. Davis can be a good player, stuff the middle and can provide a little more pop for a nose tackle in the passing game. However, a first-round pick and a future second? We know DTs have been scarce in this market, but paying that much for a run defender is a lot. But what do I know. Maybe DC Anthony Campanile sees something in Davis that he can unlock. Maybe the Jags really just believe that stuffing the run and eating up blockers so they can get to third-and-long is worth that investment. Maybe next to Josh Hines-Allen and Travon Walker we’ll get a better version. Maybe Davis, having heard all the negative chatter about how the Jags overpaid for him, will be motivated and bring a wrecking-ball attitude to Duval and storm his way through the postseason on a mission. For me, that’s a lot of maybes to hang a first- and second-rounder on. Jaguars may plan for Jordan Davis to play more than 52 percent of the time – PFT In nine starts this…

title: Jordan Davis trade: Eagles acquire Jaguars’ first-round pick
summary: The Philadelphia Eagles were expected to be dealers ahead of Tuesday’s NFL trade deadline, but they still surprised everyone with news they are sending team captain Jordan Davis to the Jacksonville Jaguars. The move gives the Eagles another first-round pick in the 2027 NFL Draft and a second-rounder in 2029 — totaling 10 picks in […]
full_text: Photo by Kathryn Riley/Getty Images | Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles were expected to be dealers ahead of Tuesday’s NFL trade deadline, but they still surprised everyone with news they are sending team captain Jordan Davis to the Jacksonville Jaguars. The move gives the Eagles another first-round pick in the 2027 NFL Draft and a second-rounder in 2029 — totaling 10 picks in the first two rounds of the next 3 drafts. Blockbuster: the Jaguars are trading a 2027 first-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick to the Eagles for defensive tackle Jordan Davis, sources tell ESPN. This is the Jaguars’ third trade for a defensive player today while the Eagles now are poised to have 10 picks in the… pic.twitter.com/NTGnLf2MoT — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) November 9, 2026 There had been speculation that the Jaguars were interested in trading for Eagles defensive tackle Jalen Carter — with Jacksonville being reportedly aggressive to add an interior defensive lineman after Jeffrey Simmons was traded by the Titans —, but the team didn’t want to move on from JC. Instead, it seems they were okay getting rid of Davis, who had risen to being a leader in the locker room. The Eagles had just signed Davis to a new, big-money contract back in March, 3-years for $78 million. The team made the move to re-sign Davis after he had shown extreme commitment to being in the best shape possible, and for the energy he brought to the defense, and even to special teams. Now, Davis will be saying goodbye to the team and city that drafted him, and will look to make a big impact for the Jaguars who are going all-in on their 2026 run. Through Week 9, they are 6-2, and made two other big trades ahead of the NFL’s deadline on Tuesday, November 10. Davis will always been appreciated for his time in Philly, and contributing to a top defense that won a Super Bowl, in addition for everything he did on and off the field. The Eagles told teams heading into the deadline that they were trying to keep Moro Ojomo and re-sign him after the season, so this move will give them more incentive to do so to keep the team strong up front. title: Where will this Eagles season rank among the all-time worst?
summary: There was a time when virtually every Eagles season was like this. Prior to 1988, the autumn was generally a depressing time in Philadelphia. There were very few seasons to celebrate. But since Buddy Ryan broke through with the first of his three straight playoff appearances in ‘88, the Eagles have been one of the […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - NOVEMBER 08: Joe Milton #14 of the Philadelphia Eagles scores a two-point conversion during the first quarter against the New York Giants at Lincoln Financial Field on November 08, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Caleb Bowlin/Getty Images) | Getty Images There was a time when virtually every Eagles season was like this. Prior to 1988, the autumn was generally a depressing time in Philadelphia. There were very few seasons to celebrate. But since Buddy Ryan broke through with the first of his three straight playoff appearances in ‘88, the Eagles have been one of the marquee teams in the NFL. Their .575 winning percentage over the last 39 seasons is 5th-best , with only the Chiefs (.578), Patriots (.596), Packers (.602) and Steelers (.611) better. Seasons like what we’re experiencing now have been few and far between over that stretch. After another brutal offensive showing with their fourth quarterback in a 19-11 loss to the Giants at Lincoln Financial Field on Sunday, Nick Sirianni’s Birds have lost seven in a row and dropped to 2-7 on the season. This would be just the 10th losing season in the last 39 for the Eagles. They are in last place in a laughingly bad NFC East, having lost to each of their three divisional opponents in three consecutive weeks by a combined score of 84-42. And while it’s highly unlikely the team will lose their final eight games and finish 2-15 this year, it’s difficult right now to envision how they’re ever going to win again. When all is said and done, will this be the worst Eagles team of the last 40 years? There are four other squads they’ll have to contend with for that dubious honor. Let’s take a look at how this year’s Eagles, through nine games, compare with the very worst of the last four decades. View Link There are a few key terms that are helpful to know more about. Yards +/- quantifies the difference in yards gained and yards allowed and where that team ranks in the NFL. The higher the number, the worse the ranking. Strength of Schedule helps paint a picture of how difficult a schedule the Eagles had to deal with that year. Negative numbers mean an easier schedule. Margin of Victory is the average difference in score per game. SRS is a metric by Pro Football Reference called Simple Rating System that takes into account margin of victory and strength of schedule and provides a number relative to average (0.0), that can be considered a point spread. So, a -6.7 SRS means that team, on average, would have been a 6.7 point underdog. OSRS and DSRS measure offensive and defensive Simple Rating System. Based on the numbers, the 1998 season is quite clearly the worst team the franchise has fielded in the last 40 years, and it actually isn’t all that close. Ray Rhodes’ final campaign was an utter disaster. Their -183 point differential and -11.4 point margin of victory drove their -12.8 SRS that was far and away the lowest of any of the five teams we’re discussing. As painful as the 2026 offense has been to watch, Rhodes’ ‘98 team averaged 10.1 points per game against one of the easiest schedules in the NFL that season. Koy Detmer, Bobby Hoying and Rodney Peete “led” an offense that scored 20+ points just ONCE , in a Week 4 24-21 loss to the Chiefs. They didn’t score more than 17 points in any of their final 12 games, and they were shut out three times that season. Somehow Duce Staley ran for 1,065 yards, and Jeff Graham was their top receiver in yards (600). They threw 7 touchdowns as a team and tossed 18 INTs. Defensively, they had nine interceptions as a defense, with Brian Dawkins, Troy Vincent and Mike Zordich with two each. Hugh Douglas piled up 12.5 sacks, and the legendary Al Wallace was 2nd, with 6. It was a tough watch. Incredibly, the team made a highlights video for this unit, entitled “A New Beginning.” You’ll notice most titles of highlight videos of terrible teams that resulted in the firing of a head coach have similar themes. “A New Beginning.” “A New Era Begins.” “Into The Great Wide Open.” “Free Fallin’.” Sorry, those last two were just Tom Petty songs. And they got 23 whole minutes out of it, although much of the play was in slow motion, which helped take up some time. The 2012 season was just slightly worse from an SRS perspective (-8.9) compared to this year’s team (-8.8). Their -10.3 point margin of victory was 2nd-worst, with an offense that was slightly more functional than this year’s group, but a worse defense. This was Andy Reid’s final season and, coming off an 8-8 record the year before, got off to a 3-1 start thanks to several last-second victories. The team then completely fell apart, losing 10 of their last 11 in what was clearly the end of an era. Mike Vick, who led the team on a miraculous run in 2010, couldn’t duplicate that feat and made just 10 starts for the 2012 Birds. Nick Foles, the back-up, made the other six. Outside of the QB, however, there were building blocks on that offense, including LeSean McCoy, DeSean Jackson, Jeremy Maclin, Jason Avant and Brent Celek. The defense started the season with Juan Castillo, the team’s long-time offensive coordinator, leading the defense for a second season, but he was replaced by Todd Bowles midway through the year. The defense gave up 30+ points in 7 of their last 10 games, and at least 25 in 27 or more in 9 of their last 10. This was one of the few cases where the defense was the weaker link. The team’s season highlight video was titled “A Season of Change.” That’s putting a positive spin on things. With half a season in the books, the 2026 Eagles’ SRS would put them 3rd on this list of awful teams, but nipping at the ‘12 Eagles’ heels. Just below them is the pandemic Birds of 2020. The entire country was desperate for live sports during the height of COVID, but fans in Philadelphia quickly reconsidered that desire watching this team play. But with fake, cardboard cutout fans in the stands “watching,” the Eagles in Doug Pederson’s final season in Philadelphia played like fake, cardboard cutouts themselves. At least the players didn’t have to deal with fans booing inside the stadium. And for 2020 , the team didn’t even bother with a full highlights package. Instead, they put together a compilation of the best plays only from their victories. Pretty smart, if you ask me. The Eagles were three seasons removed from their first Super Bowl title but even fresher off a wild card loss to the Seahawks at home in which Carson Wentz, playing in his first playoff game, was concussed in the first half. He never recovered from his litany of injuries and led an absolutely dreadful offensive effort in which he threw an NFL-leading 15 interceptions with a QB rating of 72.8. He was also sacked a league-high 50 times, with rookie Jalen Hurts eventually taking over for the final four games of the season. Those Eagles had a point differential of -84. By comparison, this year’s Birds have a point differential of -73. So this year’s team is on pace to blow past that number. That team averaged 20.9 points per game, this year’s Eagles are averaging 16.4. And at least that squad had an interesting young quarterback to get excited about. Last, the 1999 Eagles . This season launched the Andy Reid era, one of the most successful and exciting runs in franchise history. But it was a slow build under then-QB Doug Pederson, who tried to guide a brand new offensive system while rookie first round pick Donovan McNabb got his feet wet. Once McNabb got comfortable, the team played pretty well over the final three weeks, and it was clear this was an improving roster with competent coaching. And yet, the ‘99 Eagles finished 30th in the NFL in terms of yardage differential. This year’s Eagles are 31st, 2nd-worst in the league. But I’d say, right now, the ‘26 Eagles are worse than Reid’s first year in Philadelphia. Honorable mention must be given to the 1994 Eagles, who started 7-2 in Rich Kotite’s final year with the team, only to…

title: Joe Milton doesn’t expect many Eagles players will leave town during the bye week
summary: The Eagles lost to the Giants on Sunday, but it was quarterback Joe Milton’s first NFL start, and he talked about the experience and his performance in his post-game press conference. The QB was asked is he would be staying in Philly during his extended break, and he noted he might go home for like […]
full_text: Photo by Todd Olszewski/Getty Images | Getty Images The Eagles lost to the Giants on Sunday, but it was quarterback Joe Milton’s first NFL start, and he talked about the experience and his performance in his post-game press conference. The QB was asked is he would be staying in Philly during his extended break, and he noted he might go home for like two days, but he plans to be working during the bye week — and he expects his teammates to do the same. “Probably like two days, but if that, I just want to be better. We want to be better as a team, and I don’t think too [many] people going home, too many people going home. Sorry. I think everybody should be here and will be here, just trying to get better and closer.” Here’s what else Milton had to say: On his performance “For my first game here, I feel like I did all right. There are a lot of things that I can clean up as far as protection, just helping those guys out with protection. That’s something that we’re going to get better [at] this week coming up for sure.” Milton also agreed that they need to do a better job setting protections as a whole, and collectively need to make sure they are on the same page with their communication. Despite only being with the team for three weeks, the quarterback says that work starts with him. “It all depends [on] how the protection is taught. I feel like I was taught great here for the three weeks I’ve been here, so therefore I’ve just got to fix that right there, and that’s all on me for sure.” The QB also wouldn’t put any blame on the challenges of learning new terminology. He also talked about learning more every day and enjoying the process one step at a time. Milton was asked about what there was to learn from the last play, and while he hadn’t seen the film, he had some ideas. “I haven’t seen it. But playing out that play, I’d probably just stay behind the line of scrimmage and just let them chase me because I know I’m going to be able to get the ball down the field. But just putting the team in a better situation and understanding that situation and shoot, I don’t know if I’d be able to sleep tonight for that situation, so I’d probably practice it in my living room.” On carrying the ball if needed “If it’s there, I’m trying to get it. If not, I’m trying to throw the ball. Whatever the team needs at that moment, that’s what I’m trying to do. We’ve just got to clean up a lot of stuff tonight and just move on, keep going. With my three weeks being here, it’s been amazing seeing these guys never give up. Seeing them tonight, they still had excitement on their faces, and I knew it wasn’t over. It’s great to see.” On the Giants second-half adjustments “Man, the Giants played great today. They had a great defensive cause and great players over there. What they did today was just pressure and play over top. Shout-out to them for stopping us and making plays.” On the Eagles skill players Milton talked about how he felt a closer bond with the whole offense after being with them in the huddle and hearing his teammates cheer him on. “My first time playing with those guys in a real game and that type of setting at a home game. It’s not as loud for us, but at the same time, you’ve got the Giants fans out there chirping and whatever. Those guys were great in the huddle. Makai [Lemon] and Dallas [Goedert] were also great in the huddle, but everybody overall was great in the huddle and just the push and the want to that we wanted in the huddle. It was great.” He also showed his support for Makai Lemon, who had a rough drop on Sunday, and expressed confidence in the rookie moving forward. “You’re going to have drops, you’re going to have missed throws, you’re going to fumble, you’re going to do whatever. But at the end of the day, it’s what you’re going to do the next time it shows up. When your opportunity is called, when your name is called, just show up and show out. I trust in Makai that he’ll make that catch next time for sure.” On his first NFL start “I felt blessed, more blessed. That’s about it. I felt more blessed than anything. I was able to see my family in the stands, so it was great, but it was also just great to be out there with the guys that I’ve been here training with for the past three weeks and learning and just that communication and connection that the team has and just being a part of it. I love it. It’s great. I wouldn’t ask for no better situation than this.”

title: Steelers 2026 mid-season awards: Offensive Player of the Year
summary: Jaylen Warren was our consensus team MVP of the Pittsburgh Steelers halfway through the 2026 season. Considering the position he plays, it wouldn’t be a shock to see him win Offensive Player of the Year, as well. Will he get the clean sweep, or will another top offensive star for Pittsburgh get the crown? Our […]
full_text: (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Jaylen Warren was our consensus team MVP of the Pittsburgh Steelers halfway through the 2026 season. Considering the position he plays, it wouldn’t be a shock to see him win Offensive Player of the Year, as well. Will he get the clean sweep, or will another top offensive star for Pittsburgh get the crown? Our staff weighs in with our Steelers mid-season Offensive Player of the Year votes. Pittsburgh Steelers 2026 mid-season Offensive Player of the Year Joey Bray – C Zach Frazier: Jaylen Warren’s breakout starts with the way the Steelers offensive line has been playing since Week 3. Frazier has established himself as arguably the best center in the entire NFL this season. The former West Virginia Mountaineer is the top-graded center this season according to Pro Football Focus. The Steelers offensive line is becoming one of the strongest units on the team, and Frazier is the class of them all. Austin Bechtold – QB Aaron Rodgers: I didn’t want to give Warren both awards, so we flipped the NFL model of the quarterback winning MVP and any other offensive piece winning OPOY. Rodgers has been steady and playing very well under Mike McCarthy. He’s thrown for 1,871 yards and 13 touchdowns in eight games at 42 years old. Of his six interceptions, five have either been on tipped balls, passes off receivers’ hands, or while he was being hit on his arm by an offensive lineman. The stats aren’t eye-popping and indicative of how well Rodgers is playing. Zach Frazier and Max Iheanachor are also playing spectacular on the line and Frazier should be voted an All-Pro. Ryan Parish – RB Jaylen Warren: If you’ve been watching this season, it should come as no surprise that Warren is the best skill player Pittsburgh has. Unless some my colleagues decide to put Frazier in this spot and Warren in MVP, I wouldn’t be shocked if Warren is the unanimous selection here. Ryland Bickley – RB Jaylen Warren: Third in the NFL in yards from scrimmage, Warren finally earned a chance as a clear RB1 this year and never looked back. As I’ve written a few times, the Steelers haven’t had a star offensive weapon like this in years. Warren has been essential in both the run and pass game: Yes, he’s on track for nearly 1,500 yards on the ground, but he’s also second on the team in receiving yards and is somehow averaging more yards per grab than DK Metcalf. Mike Nicastro – RB Jaylen Warren: There’s some overlap here, but Warren gets my vote for Offensive Player of the Year as well. Aaron Rodgers deserves consideration. The veteran quarterback has been mostly good throughout the first half of the season and has provided valuable leadership and stability to Pittsburgh’s offense. However, Warren has simply outpaced him in terms of overall offensive impact. Jason Aponte – RB Jaylen Warren: Yes, Warren is the MVP and OPOY. The reasons given for him as the MVP choice apply here, but in critical moments, Warren delivers. Even when Rico Dowdle is involved and Warren’s opportunities shrink a bit, he remains efficient and reliable. Truly a breakout season for the running back. Jarrett Bailey – C Zach Frazier: May be a bit backwards in terms of how league wide awards go, but in the spirit of spreading out some of these awards, Frazier should get the nod for one of them. He’s become the game’s best center, and the Steelers’ run game would not be what it is without him. He should absolutely be the winner of the Protector of the Year when January rolls around. title: Mike McCarthy: Steelers improved since last Bengals matchup
summary: The Steelers and Bengals will meet for the second time this season on Sunday — a game between two 6-2 teams that will end with one moving into sole possession of first place in the AFC North. The last time Pittsburgh played the Bengals, the Steelers won 30-27 at home on Sept. 27. And talking […]
full_text: Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images | Getty Images The Steelers and Bengals will meet for the second time this season on Sunday — a game between two 6-2 teams that will end with one moving into sole possession of first place in the AFC North. The last time Pittsburgh played the Bengals, the Steelers won 30-27 at home on Sept. 27. And talking to the media on Monday, Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy said he’d “like the outcome to be the same” when the two teams clash again in Week 10. However, McCarthy acknowledged things will be different this week. This time, the game will be in Cincinnati, and on Sunday Night Football instead of the 1 p.m. EST time slot. Pittsburgh will be without Roman Wilson and could still be missing Michael Pittman Jr. at the wide receiver poison. But Pittsburgh has also improved in the weeks between the Bengals matchups, the Steelers head coach said. “I think we’re playing differently than we were the first time around,” McCarthy said. “I think we’re better … I think we’re definitely performing better in the trenches. I think, offensively, our ball distribution is better.” The Week 3 Bengals game was Pittsburgh’s first with Brock Hoffman and Max Iheanachor on the starting offensive line. It was also Jaylen Warren’s first 100-yard game of the season. McCarthy also credited with the defense with taking “a big step.” “I think the pressure, particularly in the last game, is something that will serve us very well moving forward against anybody,” he said. The Steelers managed eight sacks against the Browns in their last game in Week 8. “I think teams change,” McCarthy said. “It’s not who you’re playing — it’s when you play them. It’s November football. I think our football team is starting to reflect that. I think that’s what’s most important.” McCarthy said he watched the Bengals’ Week 9 game, a 34-17 drubbing of the Falcons in Madrid, live over the Steelers’ bye week. He said Cincinnati “looked great” on offense, but pushed back on talking about how the Bengals have changed since Week 3. “I wouldn’t say ‘change,’” McCarthy said. “I think Joe (Burrow) is on top of his game. That was an impressive oﬀensive performance yesterday. They’re rolling. … I think that’s the whole thing, is just make sure we’re dialed in on how we want to play and in touch with the matchups, ball distribution. I think (Burrow’s) time clock — the way he distributes the football and the connection he has with his receivers — is top notch.” Burrow currently ranks second in the NFL in passing yards with 2,386. His 23 passing touchdowns are the most in the league. Cincinnati also has two receivers in the top 15 for receiving yardage in Tee Higgins (758, six touchdowns) and Ja’Marr Chase (647, seven touchdowns). McCarthy said it was “fair” to say that the Steelers have a better handle on their secondary since the last Bengals game, when Joey Porter Jr. was still on the roster although not playing. “We’ve played eight games now,” he said. “We’ve had a chance to go through game plans. We’ve had a chance to build game plans as a staﬀ and with our players. We’ve had game day sideline adjustments. So, I think you could really say that for the whole team, as far as where we are today compared to where we were when we played them the first time.” McCarthy stressed the importance of combating Burrow’s ability to stay on time in the pocket and negate a pass rush; the Steelers only logged one sack in Week 3. “I think we’re in a rotation now. We’re in a good rhythm,” McCarthy said of the Steelers’ pass rush, now tied for third in the NFL with 26 sacks. “I think that’s all part of it. … I love the way our veteran guys communicate with our coaches and the younger guys. I think Cam (Heyward) and T.J. (Watt), and just the level of communication, the things they see and the adjustments they’re making for pass rush and creating those opportunities. So, that’s where things become a half second quicker.” Even if the pressure doesn’t result in a sack, McCarthy said “the little things matter.” “The pressure, that’s the diﬀerence between hitting the arm of the quarterback or bull rushing the A-gap where the quarterback can’t step into the throw,” he said. “I just think we’re better today than we were back four or five weeks ago.”

title: Steelers 2026 mid-season awards: Who is Pittsburgh’s MVP?
summary: We have reached the mid-season point of the 2026 NFL regular season (it always goes by too fast). The Pittsburgh Steelers have been one of the top teams in the league through nine weeks, sitting at the top of the AFC North with a 6-2 record while holding the No. 4 seed in the AFC […]
full_text: (Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) | Getty Images We have reached the mid-season point of the 2026 NFL regular season (it always goes by too fast). The Pittsburgh Steelers have been one of the top teams in the league through nine weeks, sitting at the top of the AFC North with a 6-2 record while holding the No. 4 seed in the AFC playoff picture. Over the course of this week, our staff here at Behind the Steel Curtain will roll out our mid-season awards, which begins today with the Steelers’ 2026 mid-season MVP. Pittsburgh Steelers 2026 mid-season MVP Joey Bray – RB Jaylen Warren : This award simply cannot go to anyone else. Warren was third in the NFL in scrimmage yards through eight weeks of play, and remains in fifth after the bye week. Plus, he is doing so with incredible efficiency. On an offense that lacks weapons on the outside, Warren is the engine that has the Steelers’ offense on an upward trend heading into the second half of their season. Austin Bechtold – RB Jaylen Warren: Warren entered the bye week with more rushing yards than Derrick Henry and Jonathan Taylor. His 6.93 yards per touch this season is the highest in football and 1.31 yards higher than the next closest running back (Bijan Robinson). Warren is the best weapon in the Steelers arsenal and has been revolutionary for an offense that has been relatively stagnant for half a decade. I’d be happy with Warren receiving additional carries, as long as his body can hold up. Warren seems like the obvious answer, but I think T.J Watt and Jalen Ramsey also have case. Ryan Parish – C Zach Frazier: It was tempting to put Jaylen Warren here, but Frazier is so crucial to what Warren and the rest of the offense do, he has to get the nod. He’s also the Steeler with the best case at being the best at his position in the entire NFL. Ryland Bickley – C Zach Frazier: I’m torn between Frazier and Jaylen Warren here, but will go with the star center as he’s been arguably the best at his position in the entire league this year. And hey, when it’s a toss-up like this, why not give the offensive line some much-needed credit? Frazier has anchored the group that’s been the story of the team’s season thus far. Jason Aponte – RB Jaylen Warren: This offense has had moments when it needed an answer, and Warren has consistently been the answer. Pittsburgh is down a running back? No problem. Receivers go down with injury? No problem. Steelers fans aren’t surprised by Warren, but the NFL is quickly learning about this dynamic running back. What a season so far for Warren. Mike Nicastro – RB Jaylen Warren: This one could certainly be up for debate, but my vote goes to Jaylen Warren. Warren has been the igniter of Pittsburgh’s offense and arguably the biggest reason the Steelers are sitting at 6-2. Whether it’s creating explosive plays, keeping the offense ahead of the chains or providing a spark when the passing game struggles, Warren has consistently delivered. Through eight games, Warren has rushed for 704 yards on 119 carries, averaging an impressive 5.9 yards per attempt. He’s also added 294 receiving yards on 25 receptions, giving him 998 yards from scrimmage and three total touchdowns. Warren has become the engine of this offense. While there are other deserving candidates, it’s difficult to overlook the impact he’s had on a team that has won four consecutive games. Jarrett Bailey – RB Jaylen Warren: It looks like I’m the tie-breaker here, but I’m going with Warren. Even after the bye week, he’s fifth in the NFL in scrimmage yards and has emerged as one of the game’s three-five best running backs. Without his productivity, there is zero chance the Steelers are 6-2. summary: We’ve reached NFL and therefore Seattle Seahawks trade deadline week, which often promises to have some interesting deals and rarely actually materializes. full_text: We’ve reached NFL and therefore Seattle Seahawks trade deadline week, which often promises to have some interesting deals and rarely actually materializes. Minor or mid-level deals have happened more recently on deadline day itself, so it’s not like we live in a “nothing happens” world. There have admittedly been prominent in-season trades already this year, including the Quenton Nelson and Jeffery Simmons trades just a couple of weeks ago, as well as Joey Porter Jr going to the Dallas Cowboys, and Marvin Harrison Jr heading for the Houston Texans. For the second year in a row, the trade deadline is during Week 10. The Seattle Seahawks are usually active during the deadline, and this year they’ve pulled off one major trade. Will John Schneider cook up another midseason masterclass like he did for Leonard Williams, Quandre Diggs, Carlos Dunlap, and other names from previous deadline deals? Follow Field Gulls’ trade tracker coverage throughout Monday and Tuesday, and we’ll see what the Seahawks will do as they look to get back on track after a sputtering 5-4 start. Have the Seattle Seahawks made any trades during the regular season? Yes. They acquired longtime Indianapolis Colts guard Quenton Nelson for a 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 fifth-rounder. Who could the Seahawks potentially put on the trade block? No one immediately springs to mind. The likes of Dante Fowler Jr have rarely played this year but likely wouldn’t fetch much on the trade market. Emanuel Wilson being an unofficial healthy scratch is worth monitoring, although similarly he’s not much of a valuable trade piece, and Seattle may not want to risk moving any capable RB given the injury concerns on the depth chart. Which positions would the Seahawks potentially be most interested in? Edge rusher and wide receiver might be two positions of need for Seattle. Rashid Shaheed’s injury and generally underwhelming receiving stats could impact what Seattle does at receiver. The edge rushing room is essentially three deep, and with only Derick Hall and Connor O’Toole under contract beyond 2027, there might be some forward thinking required. The New York Jets’ Will McDonald IV has reportedly requested a trade and could be one to watch. When does the NFL trade deadline window close? At 4 pm ET/1 pm PT on Tuesday, Nov. 10. Latest Seattle Seahawks trade news Notable NFL trade news (Nov. 10) The Eagles are trading pass rusher Arnold Ebiketie to the Cincinnati Bengals for a 2027 sixth-round pick. Notable NFL trade news (Nov. 9) WHOA! The Jaguars just traded for Philadelphia Eagles defensive tackle Jordan Davis , giving up a 2027 first-rounder and a 2029 second. The Atlanta Falcons have traded safety Jessie Bates to the Jacksonville Jaguars for a 2027 second-rounder and a 2028 fifth-rounder. The New York Jets have dealt safety Andre Cisco to the Detroit Lions for a 2028 sixth-rounder. The New Orleans Saints have agreed to trade defensive tackle Davon Godchaux to the Jacksonville Jaguars for a 2028 sixth-rounder, which could become a 2027 sixth-rounder.

title: Seahawks fan chat: Bills battle Vikings on ‘Monday Night Football’
summary: We’ve got ourselves a great game on Monday Night Football between a team with an elite offense and a team with an elite defense. Josh Allen is having another amazing season for the Buffalo Bills, while James Cook is on his way to another prolific year on the ground. The 6-1 Bills will be in […]
full_text: We’ve got ourselves a great game on Monday Night Football between a team with an elite offense and a team with an elite defense. Josh Allen is having another amazing season for the Buffalo Bills, while James Cook is on his way to another prolific year on the ground. The 6-1 Bills will be in tough against the Minnesota Vikings, whose penchant for blitzing under defensive coordinator Brian Flores borders on cartoon-like. Minnesota blitzes over 70% of all dropbacks, which is outrageous but it works. It’s also not completely impenetrable, as the Detroit Lions countered Minnesota’s aggressiveness by keeping in extra blockers and rushing for 230 yards. One worry for Buffalo is no Dion Dawkins. In fact, both their starting left tackle and left guard are out, so it’s backup OL against the Vikings defense. WELP. Minnesota quarterback Kyler Murray is out due to a “sore hamstring,” which can be exacerbated by not scoring any points. Carson Wentz gets the nod for the night as the Vikes look to stay atop the NFC North by improving to 7-1. I think it’s in Seahawks fans’ best interest to root for a Vikings loss. Someone in the NFC North needs to fall off to give Seattle a pathway to the postseason through the Wild Card, and it might as well be Minnesota. The Vikes have a vaunted defense and a gaunt offense. ESPN and ABC have you covered from Minneapolis at 5:15 pm PT! Enjoy! Join the conversation! title: Puka Nacua headed for injured reserve, could miss Seahawks game
summary: Although Sunday’s 20-13 victory over the Washington Commanders extended the Los Angeles Rams’ win streak to three games and put them over .500 for the first time this season, it came with a detrimental injury. Superstar wide receiver Puka Nacua is expected to be placed on injured reserve after he suffered MCL and PCL sprains […]
full_text: Although Sunday’s 20-13 victory over the Washington Commanders extended the Los Angeles Rams’ win streak to three games and put them over .500 for the first time this season, it came with a detrimental injury. Superstar wide receiver Puka Nacua is expected to be placed on injured reserve after he suffered MCL and PCL sprains as well as turf toe late in the fourth quarter during Sunday’s win, head coach Sean McVay told reporters. He did not provide a return timeline. The #Rams are expected to place WR Puka Nacua on Injured Reserve with MCL and PCL sprains, plus turf toe, coach Sean McVay told reporters. pic.twitter.com/LLWLyGwVMy — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) November 9, 2026 Nacua suffered the injury during the Rams’ final offensive snap of the game, where he took a handoff and cut upfield before being hit by safety Jeremy Reaves and linebacker Sonny Styles, which caused his leg to twist. He briefly remained on the field before walking off on his own power. It’s a brutal blow for Los Angeles, who arealready without WR Davante Adams (ruptured hamstring) for the foreseeable future, leaving Tutu Atwell, Jordan Whittington, Konata Mumpfield, Tyler Higbee and Colby Parkinson in line for more targets as the Rams look to keep their playoff hopes alive. Adams was injured in Week 5 and originally given a 6-10 week recovery timeline , although McVay said he expected the veteran wideout to return on the shorter side. The Rams and Seattle Seahawks don’t meet until Week 15, meaning he’ll likely be back on the field by then. However, Nacua may not be. Los Angeles is in line to play the Arizona Cardinals and Green Bay Packers before their bye in Week 1, seemingly putting them in a position to be without both their top receivers for at least two weeks. Like Seattle, they sit just outside the playoff picture: 1. San Francisco 49ers (7-1) 2. Minnesota Vikings (6-1) 3. New York Giants (5-2-1) 4. Carolina Panthers (3-5) 5. Chicago Bears (7-2) 6. Detroit Lions (6-2) 7. Green Bay Packers (6-3) Then, both the Seahawks and Rams stand at 5-4. Given the strength of the NFC, missing Nacua—even if he heals quick, could be detrimental for Los Angeles.
