title: Sam Darnold ruled out, Seahawks expect Drew Lock to start vs. Raiders despite oblique injury
summary: The potential of Jalen Milroe making his first career start in Week 10 appears to have faded as quickly as it arose. On Seattle Sports 710’s Brock and Salk on Monday, Seattle Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald was asked about quarterback Drew Lock’s status, after he suffered an oblique injury in Sunday’s win over the […]
full_text: The potential of Jalen Milroe making his first career start in Week 10 appears to have faded as quickly as it arose. On Seattle Sports 710’s Brock and Salk on Monday, Seattle Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald was asked about quarterback Drew Lock’s status, after he suffered an oblique injury in Sunday’s win over the Arizona Cardinals. Macdonald provided an optimistic update, saying, “Good exam for Drew. He’s dealing with an oblique. And, I think it’s something we can manage in him playing the game,” while adding starter Sam Darnold would need another week in his return from his quad injury. Lock, who entered Week 9 with what was reported as severe tendinitis , was seen grabbing his right hip in the third quarter of Seattle’s win over the Cardinals. Though he went into the blue tent, he remained in the game and didn’t miss a snap. Macdonald told reporters post game that Lock’s status for Week 10 against the Las Vegas Raiders was up in the air , but after encouraging news on Monday, it appears the Seahawks’ backup will be good to start a third game in 2026. Across two starts and the bulk of Seattle’s Week 1 win over the New England Patriots, Lock has completed 71.1% of his passes, throwing for 597 yards and five touchdowns against zero interceptions.

title: Seahawks Droppings: Beset by injuries, Seattle grinds it out and holds serve vs. Cardinals
summary: Sometimes you need to take a step back to move forward. The Seattle Seahawks seem to have done that this week, relying on the run game and defense in a 17-3 victory over the Arizona Cardinals at Lumen Field. Now, all the injuries that Seattle was his with for this week might have had a […]
full_text: Sometimes you need to take a step back to move forward. The Seattle Seahawks seem to have done that this week, relying on the run game and defense in a 17-3 victory over the Arizona Cardinals at Lumen Field. Now, all the injuries that Seattle was his with for this week might have had a big hand in the simplification of the game. No Sam Darnold, Leo Williams, Quenton Nelson, Uchenna Nwosu, Charles Cross, or Rashid Shaheed? No problem. It certainly wasn’t the prettiest game offensively as Seattle finished with 295 yards. Drew Lock managed the offense well and didn’t put the ball in harm’s way much at all. Don’t take that to mean he was conservative, however. Lock slung a few in some very tight windows. Brian Fleury stuck with the run game, and it helped to shorten the game. Would Seattle have beaten a better squad today the way they played? No idea. They won today and that’s all that matters right now. Seahawks Droppings Drew Lock made it work, but was still clearly injured. I’m not sure he threw a tight spiral at all today which I’m hoping was just a side effect of his elbow injury. There were also a number of throws behind the receivers. Oh yeah, and Lock hurt his oblique during the game and may not be able to go next week. Will it be Jalen Milroe time in Las Vegas? Zach Charbonnet brings toughness to the offense. Look no further than the last drive of the game where Charbonnet broke multiple tackles to keep moving the chains and end the game. He’s not the fleetest of foot, but runs tough. Charbonnet is like a middle ground between Jadarian Price and Emanuel Wilson. Less explosive than Price, but more than Wilson with just as much toughness. The one-two punch of Charbonnet and Price could be pretty lethal. The offensive line played much better. No sacks given up today, and there weren’t many dropbacks I can remember where Lock was even under pressure. Maybe that’s an indictment on the Cardinals’ pass rushers or a testament to Fleury getting the ball out early. The only downside of this would be the fact that when Nelson comes back, Zabel will have to move over to RG again. Best case scenario would’ve been Zabel and Nelson getting reps against the Cardinals and Las Vegas Raiders to be ready for the San Francisco 49ers after the bye week. That’s not a reality, sadly, so be ready for some rough weeks ahead. AJ Barner gets involved. I don’t know why they don’t use Barner more. The only thing he’s not great at is run after the catch since he always seems to get dropped within one or two yards of where he catches the ball. I’ll take that if it means more red zone TDs. Red zone issues improved. Both sides of the ball had better results in the red zone. The offense was 2-2 with Barner scoring both TDs. The defense held Arizona to 0-2 including that late-game fourth down stop from the two yard line. Short-handed defensive line stepped up. DeMarcus Lawrence looked like 2025 D-Law. He took accountability this week for some of the issues against the Chicago Bears. Whether or not it was really his fault, he took that personally this week and made his presence known with 1 sack, 2 TFL, and a forced fumble that was recovered by Arizona. Lawrence’s former Dallas Cowboy teammate, Dante Fowler Jr, also showed up for really the first time as a Seahawk with a sack and a forced fumble on Gardner Minshew to end the first half. With Big Cat and Nwosu out, Seattle needed others to step up and they did. The refs were pretty awful. It’s a good thing Seattle won this game or I would’ve been nearly apoplectic at the refs. Yes, the Seahawks had some very dumb self-inflicted penalties that they absolutely cannot afford to have playing against better competition. I’m looking at you, Jalen Sundell. And sure, the Cardinals made their own share of penalty mistakes to extend Seahawks drives. Yet, that defensive PI call on Josh Jobe was garbage. He barely touched Trey McBride and then turned to make the interception. Before the second Seahawks TD drive, the refs also called McBride’s forward progress stopped just prior to him fumbling which was recovered by the Seahawks. At least they didn’t overturn Barner’s TD which I was anticipating. Other pass catchers not named Jaxon Smith-Njigba made plays. I had to specify “pass catchers” instead of WRs because the leading receiver was actually RB Jadarian Price with 54 yards on 4 catches. I thought he couldn’t catch the football?? That over-the-shoulder catch early in the game was a thing of beauty! Cooper Kupp only had three catches for 32 yards, but I’m pretty sure all of those were for first downs. Tory Horton also had a key first down catch. The passing numbers overall won’t wow anyone with only 175 total yards receiving, but getting other players besides JSN involved is key. For the most part, this was Seahawks Football. If Mike Macdonald and crew can right the ship, it was a good step in the right direction. Theoretically, the running game should continue to gel and improve as Charbonnet and Price get more action. Play great defense, hold on to the ball, and make key passes when necessary to supplement…that’s how they will need to play. At least for one week, we can enjoy a victory with a whole host of backups no less.

summary: The trade deadline is a few hours away. Jordan Schultz predicted there would be over eight trades on Tuesday. We’ll see if that comes true. It’s been a relatively quiet morning so far. Nothing on the San Francisco 49ers front yet. Jake Moody found work again. The Falcons signed him to their 53-man roster from […]
full_text: (Photo by Rich von Biberstein/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The trade deadline is a few hours away. Jordan Schultz predicted there would be over eight trades on Tuesday. We’ll see if that comes true. It’s been a relatively quiet morning so far. Nothing on the San Francisco 49ers front yet. Jake Moody found work again. The Falcons signed him to their 53-man roster from the Ravens’ practice squad. We’ll keep track of every rumor, like the Niners having their eyes on wide receivers . Speaking of which, Schultz also said that Brandon Aiyuk could land with an unnamed NFC team, likely on their practice squad, once the 49ers release him. ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler said Broncos tight end Evan Engram has garnered interest, but is unlikely to be traded because the Broncos don’t have a replacement. Fowler also said the Jaguars plan to keep Brian Thomas Jr. through the deadline. The Commanders are listening to offers but, per Ben Standig, are unlikely to trade players before the deadline. The Vikings, off a dreadful Monday night performance from Carson Wentz, are making calls around the league for a quarterback. If you’re the 49ers, making a contender better makes little sense, unless Minnesota overpays for Mac Jones. That situation has Kirk Cousins all over it. The Eagles traded away edge rusher Arnold Ebiketie for a sixth-round pick in the 2027 draft. Ebiketie played under Raheem Morris in Atlanta. Albert Breer reported that the Jaguars made a significant offer for Will McDonald before Monday’s trades. Perhaps that’s a sign that the Jets’ asking price for McDonald is too high.

title: NFL trade rumors: The 49ers are ‘still lingering on the periphery’ for a wide receiver
summary: Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer had a trade column on Tuesday morning. In the section where he discussed the Indianapolis Colts wanting to make more moves, he mentioned Josh Downs. Breer listed the San Francisco 49ers among three teams still interested in adding a wide receiver: The Chiefs and Steelers have been the prime suitors for […]
full_text: (Photo by Lachlan Cunningham/Getty Images) | Getty Images Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer had a trade column on Tuesday morning. In the section where he discussed the Indianapolis Colts wanting to make more moves, he mentioned Josh Downs. Breer listed the San Francisco 49ers among three teams still interested in adding a wide receiver: The Chiefs and Steelers have been the prime suitors for receivers, with the Niners still lingering on the periphery. There was a belief from some teams over the weekend that Downs would be moved to Kansas City for a fourth-round pick. And again, the hope, for the Colts, would be that letting this all play out might sweeten whatever deal they get for the tough, resourceful middle-of-the-field target, who’s at the end of his rookie deal. Perhaps there are two Josh Downs, but that is not a player who has been overly impressive in my eyes this season. If you narrow his performance down to the last three weeks, it’s been underwhelming. He’s only catching 63% of his targets despite 90% of those being on target. He’s primarily a slot receiver, but doesn’t have the make-you-miss ability to create after the catch. When I watch, the separation comes from the scheme. In true man-to-man situations, Downs has failed to hold on to the ball in key moments for the Colts. He does not feel like the type of wideout who would raise the bar for the 49ers. We’ll find out by the end of the day if the Niners share those same sentiments. Here’s Breer on another popular wide receiver on the trade market, Jaguars’ Brian Thomas Jr.: One more Jaguars’ note: I don’t think the moves Monday affect their approach with wide receiver Brian Thomas Jr., and I figured they might at first, given Thomas would be a piece they could move to recoup some of the capital lost in the three trades. The reasoning for that is the same I’ve explained the past couple weeks. Thomas isn’t having a great year. He has 10 catches for 117 yards and two touchdowns. He’s playing 43.0% of the team’s offensive snaps, while Meyers is playing 75.41% and Washington is playing 74.59%. But that doesn’t mean he isn’t bringing value. While the third-year pro isn’t a great fit for Coen’s offense, which values the grit, toughness and after-catch production of Washington and Meyers, he does serve a unique purpose—his ability to threaten the defense downfield is unlike what the other two receivers bring, and opens things up underneath for those guys and in the run game. He’s also a good soldier, and so keeping him as a decoy hasn’t proven to be disruptive to the team. The other thing? He’s under contract next year. So in a year in which the Jaguars feel like they can compete at the highest level, the purpose Thomas serves now is more valuable than what might get back selling low on him, particularly when they can trade him after the season, when rookie Josh Cameron might be ready to replace him. Thomas Jr. has four targets in the past three games. He’s not involved in the Jaguars’ plans. Thomas Jr. needs a fresh start. The good news is, with the 49ers, he wouldn’t need to be “the guy.” Watching him run routes and seeing his targets, the speed is palpable. For whatever reason, Thomas Jr. and Trevor Lawrence aren’t on the same page. The timing is off by a split second, and that’s been the difference between him having a couple of catches and 10 during the past month or so. He’s worth buying low on and would be a great fit for Kyle Shanahan’s offense, the way Thomas Jr. can run away from coverage and stretch the field horizontally. Through the first month of the season, Dontayvion Wicks led Philly with 154 yards on downfield targets. He did that on just six receptions. Wicks hasn’t played since Week 6. He’s under contract through 2027. Drops have been an issue during his career, but the talent and skill set make him a fit for the 49ers. If you’re calling the Eagles about receivers, you’d be foolish not to ask about DeVonta Smith. While unrealistic, he’s a WR1 in every sense. Smith has only played four games this season, but he’s one of the most dangerous receivers in the NFL.

title: Kyle Shanahan on the 49ers’ safety rotation: ‘I don’t think we know what the end goal is’
summary: The San Francisco 49ers got back second-year safety Marques Sigle from an ankle injury in Week 9. We wondered how the safety rotation would work. The 49ers shuffled safeties on the first three drives. Malik Mustapha and Ji’Ayir Brown started. On the second series, it was Mustapha and Sigle. On the third series, it was […]
full_text: (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers got back second-year safety Marques Sigle from an ankle injury in Week 9. We wondered how the safety rotation would work. The 49ers shuffled safeties on the first three drives. Malik Mustapha and Ji’Ayir Brown started. On the second series, it was Mustapha and Sigle. On the third series, it was Brown and Sigle. By the end of the game, Mustapha led the way with 38 snaps. Brown played 30, while Sigle played 27. 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan was asked what the end goal was with the safety rotation. Shanahan said, “I don’t know what the end goal is. We’ve got three good guys that are playing at a very high level, so you just play that until it plays itself out.” Brown had one of the fastest GPS times for any 49ers player in Week 9 when he made a touchdown-saving tackle on a kickoff return. His goal-line tackle of Brock Bowers also saved a touchdown. Mustapha had a pass breakup and an interception. Sigle had three tackles. Each player allowed a reception of at least 18 yards, but that was the only catch they surrendered. Shanahan continued. “Just like Malik hurt his playing time just because of injuries in training camp, and then kind of the same thing happened to Sigle, who was playing at a real high level before he was hurt. Tig’s been the one who’s stayed consistent and healthy. So, all three of those guys have going, I think if two separate themselves way over another then obviously we would keep those guys out there longer. But, we’ll just keep doing it week-to-week, and we’ll see what it ends up, but it’s a pretty good problem to have.” It’s tough to fault the Niners for relying on Brown, given his clean bill of health this season. Week 9 was one of the first, if not only, times this season where a safety didn’t miss a tackle. That’s a good sign. They won’t run into another Brock Bowers, but the safety group will keep getting tested as the offenses they face get tougher in the second half. Will it be the player who makes the most plays, or the combination that makes the fewest mistakes? Which duo do you think gives the 49ers the best chance to win? Let us know in the comments below.

title: Week 10 NFL Power Rankings: Did the 49ers move up after big win over Raiders?
summary: The San Francisco 49ers blew past the Las Vegas Raiders 38-17 on Sunday, taking advantage of the opposing defense while forcing five turnovers in a dominant win. It was a good all-around performance for the 49ers, who remain tied for the NFL’s best record at 7-1 with the Buffalo Bills. After their big win on […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - NOVEMBER 08: Jaden Dugger #53 of the San Francisco 49ers celebrates with teammates after intercepting a pass and scoring a touchdown during the during the second quarter against the Las Vegas Raiders at Levi's Stadium on November 08, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers blew past the Las Vegas Raiders 38-17 on Sunday, taking advantage of the opposing defense while forcing five turnovers in a dominant win. It was a good all-around performance for the 49ers, who remain tied for the NFL’s best record at 7-1 with the Buffalo Bills. After their big win on Sunday, where do the 49ers rank in the Week 10 NFL Power Rankings? ESPN: No. 2 The 49ers stayed at No. 2 behind the Buffalo Bills in ESPN’s weekly power rankings, which makes sense given that Buffalo beat the Minnesota Vikings on Monday Night Football in a battle of one-loss teams. The top three included the Jacksonville Jaguars last week. That remained the same this week, while the Chicago Bears climbed up one spot to No. 4 and the Denver Broncos fell one spot to No. 5 despite both teams winning. The rest of the Top 10 remained the same, just in a different order. The Kansas City Chiefs stayed put at No. 6. The Cincinnati Bengals bumped up from No. 10 to No. 7 after a 34-17 win over the Atlanta Falcons. The Vikings fell one spot following their loss to the Bills, landing at No. 8. The Seattle Seahawks actually fell one spot to No. 9 after beating the Arizona Cardinals 17-3. And the Detroit Lions also fell one spot to No. 10 after beating the Miami Dolphins. Looking ahead at the rest of the schedule, ESPN believes Week 12 against the Seattle Seahawks is the most important game left on the docket. The Athletic: No. 2 Just like the previous ranking, the 49ers stay at No. 2 here again behind the Buffalo Bills, earning a midseason grade of an ‘A’. “The Niners have the second-best point differential in the NFL (plus-79), and they hardly broke a sweat Sunday in another multi-touchdown game from Christian McCaffrey,” The Athletic’s Chad Graff and Josh Kendall wrote. “His 37 career touchdown receptions are the most by a running back in the Super Bowl era, surpassing Marshall Faulk.” The Broncos remained at No. 3 here, while the Chiefs moved up one spot to No. 4 and the Jaguars moved up one spot to No. 5. Wrapping up the top 10 were the Bears (No. 6), Bengals (No. 7), Lions (No. 8), Packers (No. 9), and Vikings (No. 10). CBS Sports: No. 2 CBS Sports’s Pete Prisco’s rankings did not see a change inside the top five, meaning the 49ers stayed at No. 2 behind the Bills. “They just keep playing as well as anybody in the NFC, despite their many injuries,” Prisco wrote. “Brock Purdy is in the MVP talk.” The Bills, 49ers, Jaguars, Bears, and Broncos remained the top five here, while the Chiefs, Bengals, Lions, Steelers, and Packers rounded out the top 10. Each of those teams moved up one spot, while the Vikings dropped five to No. 11. FOX Sports: No. 3 The 49ers stayed the same as last week here, only that was at No. 3 behind the Bills and the Broncos. “The 49ers clearly fixed whatever it was that happened to them before the bye week when they lost to the Falcons — a game that now looks like a weird blip on their otherwise stellar season,” FOX Sports’s Ralph Vacchiano wrote. “They came out strong and fast, putting the Las Vegas Raiders in their place quickly. “And the fact that they did it without WR Mike Evans made it even more impressive. Of course, that’s what they do best: Overcome injuries. They’re that good and they’re that deep. They still look like they deserve to be the NFC favorites. And they’re clearly the NFC’s best team.” Behind the 49ers were the Chiefs and Bears, who were in the top five last week. Then came the Jaguars, Vikings, Bengals, Packers, and Lions, with Green Bay making a big jump from No. 15 to No. 9.
author: Rohan Chakravarthi

Big contributions from the team’s youth “Kittle said he loved the Niners drafting the older prospects because they “understand the sense of urgency that comes with football.” Indeed, the idea that the rookie class entered a locker room full of players who have been just short of the franchise’s sixth Lombardi Trophy was immediately evident. “Ever since we got here, everybody was trying to talk about how we’re like an old team or whatever, but we knew we have to contribute,” Dugger said. “When I got drafted, they told me you’re not just coming here to sit. Just coming in with that mentality, I feel like we knew we had to contribute early. I feel like we are just trying to do our job with the opportunities we have.” …. “In other locker rooms, the rookies can be the burdens,” Halton said. “For us, man, we got great vets in here, great guys that’s been through any type of adversity. We really just try to glue to them and that happens within the rookies … Getting the ring, that’s the goal every year. But we really want it bad just to do it for those guys, the vets.” Jordan Watkins is earning Brock Purdy’s trust. The 49ers’ WR has every reason to deliver (paywall) “My little sister,” Watkins said of his motivation. “She’s very similar to me. She’s very outgoing. She’s tall. She’s one of a kind for sure, I’ll tell you that much. And she looks up to me. She looks up to me a lot.” Her name is Abrielle. She’s 12 now, a promising softball player who wears the No. 11 because it was her big brother’s number in college. She’s playing up in age on her travel ball team, so now they’re both fighting to prove themselves….He was 8 years old when he watched police take away his mother, Paula Baker. She battled addiction and spent 18 months incarcerated. He didn’t see her for nearly two years. His father had never been a steady presence. The reunion with mom wasn’t easy after she regained custody. He struggled with resentment. Abrielle kept him tethered to the joy life tried to bury. Watson eventually embraced therapy. His mother eventually built a life in recovery. They repaired their relationship, and he developed into a college prospect. He’d already learned how a difficult beginning didn’t have to dictate the ending. A lesson he needed when a high ankle sprain impacted his first NFL preseason. Then a calf strain derailed his rookie campaign….Watkins keeps up with Abrielle’s softball exploits. She’s playing 13-and-under now. He bragged about her recently striking out three batters while pitching against older girls. He smiled in the 49ers locker room as he remembered competing with her. They’d pitch from the mound she’s got in the yard, see who could throw the most strikes. He’d laugh at her precocious moments, listen to her stories and play games. He sees himself in Abrielle. Her ambition. Her competitiveness. The hunger behind the wide smile. Even her occasional preteen stubbornness. “I try to call her and inspire her as much as possible,” he said. ‘Give her as much advice as I can. But, you know, being a kid, sometimes they don’t want to listen.”….His newest motivation is 2 years old. “Once I had my daughter, it kind of transformed into her,” Watkins said. “Just making sure I’m doing what I can do to be able to provide for her. (Make sure she doesn’t live) the lifestyle that I had growing up.” 49ers minutia minute: Deebo Samuel, CJ West expected back; Mike Evans still on hold (paywall) “ Williams didn’t give up a sack in his first six games but has now allowed one in two straight. Sunday’s came courtesy of defensive end Maxx Crosby. Williams blocked him well at first, but Purdy’s initial read wasn’t open and he had to hold the ball longer than designed, allowing Crosby to slip inside for the sack.” Kyle Shanahan provides 49ers injury updates, discusses Brandon Aiyuk “It has same as how I talked last time on him. I was just told that by [executive vice president of communications] Corry [Rush] when I walked in, so it means absolutely nothing to our team. I think we’ve got a two-week roster exemption. That’s all administrative stuff to me.” 49ers vs. Raiders PFF grades: Best and worst from the game, plus snap counts “Left guard Connor Colby earned an 82.7 overall offensive grade, the highest among all offensive linemen in the game. He also posted a game-best 82.4 run-blocking grade across 39 run-blocking snaps. Meanwhile, right guard Dominick Puni led all players with an 87.5 pass-blocking grade. He didn’t allow a single pressure against the Raiders across 34 pass-blocking snaps.” Brandon Aiyuk reinstated by NFL; 49ers have 2-game roster exemption for receiver “San Francisco has three options. It could release Aiyuk, the scenario that has remained the most plausible throughout the offseason. It could trade Aiyuk, which has long been its preferred option, but it hasn’t found a trade partner and the deadline for a deal is Tuesday at 4 p.m. ET.”

title: Vikings-Bills live discussion: A chaotic matchup between a pair of overrated teams
summary: The 6-1 Buffalo Bills take on the 6-1 Minnesota Vikings. These are two of the best teams in the NFL record-wise, but they are from the most complete teams. The Vikings’ offense has been asleep at the wheel all season. Justin Jefferson is on pace for a career worst year. He won’t have Kyler Murray […]
full_text: (Photo by Stephen Maturen/Getty Images) | Getty Images The 6-1 Buffalo Bills take on the 6-1 Minnesota Vikings. These are two of the best teams in the NFL record-wise, but they are from the most complete teams. The Vikings’ offense has been asleep at the wheel all season. Justin Jefferson is on pace for a career worst year. He won’t have Kyler Murray throwing him the ball tonight, but that might be a blessing in disguise, as Murray tends to be erratic and miss open receivers downfield. What Minnesota lacks offensively, they more than make up for it on the defensive side of the ball. They are comfortably the best stop unit in the league, thanks in large part to their ability to prevent success against the pass. Brian Flores blitzes over 3/4 of the time, and invites chaotic play. If there’s a quarterback who thrives in chaos, it’s Josh Allen. Allen makes play after play, usually off-script. He’s down left tackle Dion Dawkins, which might invite Allen to run more. I can see Allen and James Cook having big days on the ground, and Khalil Shakir pitching in on key third downs. The Bills are lousy defensively. They’ve allowed 33, 31, 29, 34, and 30 points this season. So, if there was a get-right spot for Carson Wentz, Jefferson, and the Vikings, it’s the Bills’ defense that gave up 30 points to the Raiders team we just watched. My gut says the NFC’s strength tops the AFC’s in this game, and the Vikings eke out a win. But going against Allen is asking for it. Deep down, I think these are two overrated teams that’ll be exposed come playoff time.
author: Kyle Posey

title: NFL trade deadline: The Jaguars are all-in; should the 49ers follow suit?
summary: The San Francisco 49ers have the best record in the NFL right now, with the Minnesota Vikings playing tonight on Monday Night Football. Trade rumors are swirling, and the team suffered a blow with the loss of defensive tackle Gracen Halton. The trade deadline is tomorrow, and there is plenty of time left to add […]
full_text: (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) The San Francisco 49ers have the best record in the NFL right now, with the Minnesota Vikings playing tonight on Monday Night Football. Trade rumors are swirling, and the team suffered a blow with the loss of defensive tackle Gracen Halton. The trade deadline is tomorrow, and there is plenty of time left to add to the roster. The Jacksonville Jaguars have sent a message to the AFC and the NFL with the acquisitions of safety Jessie Bates and defensive tackle Jordan Davis. It feels like just about any year you can say the NFL is “wide open,” but this season seems to be more open than seasons past. Kyle Shanahan and John Lynch haven’t indicated they are all-in or completely out in public statements. In my opinion, I’d bet the 49ers are working the phones right now. Evaluating the in-house talent and the incoming reinforcements is part of the equation for the 49ers. We do know the 49ers targeted Jauan Jennings in a trade with Minnesota, but that move felt like a depth improvement, given his familiarity with the offense. Should the 49ers take a page from the Jaguars’ playbook? Now, look, teams shouldn’t be reactionary to other teams’ moves or thought processes. It is possible for the 49ers to be fine with what they have. There is the possibility that the 49ers, who have run the ball very well in 2026, will shift their identity in January to a running team that controls the clock and wants their defense to eliminate offenses. You don’t suspect you will be in shootouts in the playoffs, and of course anything is possible. On the flip side, adding firepower is never a bad idea, provided the value of the return and the investment is reasonable. Do the 49ers have confidence in the returns of Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel, and De’Zhaun Stribling, potentially with Demarcus Robinson rounding into shape? The pass rush hasn’t flashed as much as you would like, but do the 49ers add a familiar face off the street, Leonard Floyd, anyone? The 49ers have taken swings in the past. Will the 49ers stand pat or bet on the return of CJ West to bolster the defensive tackle depth? Should the 49ers swing on a wide receiver or hope that Jordan Watkins’ development will continue? Calling the Jets about Will McDonald IV isn’t the worst idea. Sound off in the comments: should the 49ers follow Jacksonville’s trade process?

full_text: (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The NFL has reinstated San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk from the Reserve/Left Squad list, per the NFL’s transaction wire, after Aiyuk reported for his physical. The 49ers were also granted a roster exemption, per the transaction wire. Commissioner Roger Goodell has granted a two-game roster exemption for Aiyuk that will expire on Monday, November 23. According to The Athletic’s Jonathan Jones, it’s a two-week unpaid exemption for Aiyuk, since he’s reporting as a late player. Matt Barrows believes Aiyuk’s future has already been written. “It’s the same deal where he’s part of the team but really not part of the team. And then they, you know, they cut him ultimately. I don’t know if he would be ready to play in 2026. You’re picking him up because you think you can get him onto your practice field for a little bit, maybe in a game, but you’re picking him up for 2027.” Barrows said there was “pretty much 0% chance” that Aiyuk would play for the 49ers again.

title: Jordan Watkins’ first career touchdown was a testament to persistence
summary: Earlier this season, Jordan Watkins went to meet with Kyle Shanahan, the second-year wide receiver desperate for advice as to how to earn more snaps on a team bursting with more experienced offensive playmakers. After an injury-disrupted rookie season in which he played a minimal role, Watkins having any kind of significant impact this season […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - NOVEMBER 08: Jordan Watkins #17 and Demarcus Robinson #11 of the San Francisco 49ers celebrate after Watkins caught a touchdown pass against the Las Vegas Raiders in the third quarter at Levi's Stadium on November 08, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) | Getty Images Earlier this season, Jordan Watkins went to meet with Kyle Shanahan, the second-year wide receiver desperate for advice as to how to earn more snaps on a team bursting with more experienced offensive playmakers. After an injury-disrupted rookie season in which he played a minimal role, Watkins having any kind of significant impact this season looked unlikely heading into the 2026 season following the 49ers’ offseason additions at wideout. But on Sunday, as the 49ers faced their former Bay Area rivals the Las Vegas Raiders, Watkins was able to celebrate his first career touchdown after bringing down a 37-yard strike from Brock Purdy. That was the final touchdown of a 38-17 win for San Francisco that improved their record to 7-1, the best in the NFL heading into Monday Night Football, and ensured Watkins finished the game as the Niners’ leading receiver with 86 yards. The career day enjoyed by Watkins, which followed an extremely encouraging showing against the Atlanta Falcons before the bye in which he had a would-be touchdown overturned on review, was in large part a product of circumstance. The 49ers’ slew of injures at wide receiver, with Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel still out and Christian Kirk heading back to IR with a knee injury this week, have catapulted Watkins up the depth chart. As such, a greater role for Watkins was inevitable. However, his success versus Las Vegas was also a victory for the persistence that has underpinned what is now looking set to be a season of significant progress for the former fourth-round pick, and Watkins’ chemistry with his quarterback. Watkins was ruled to have failed to survive the ground while leaping to make a fourth-quarter touchdown grab against the Falcons, and that disappointment fueled his desire to make sure there was no repeat as he got a step on his defender while breaking back to the middle of the field on his deep route to end the game with the Raiders as a meaningful contest. “Obviously, two weeks ago at the ATL game, he [Purdy] gave me another op and I felt like that close to coming down with the play. So for him to go out there and trust me again, to come down with the play, it’s awesome,” Watkins told reporters. “It could have been PI, but whatever. You know, my job is to come down with the football. If the quarterback puts it up there, come down with the ball. That’s what I did. Brock Purdy launches it deep to Jordan Watkins to extend the 49ers lead 🚀 LVvsSF on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/DgGxhzVHmb — NFL (@NFL) November 8, 2026 “I was making sure that the ball wasn’t going to move on that one. I promise you that.” This season, Watkins has been targeted 13 times, making 10 catches for 224 yards and a touchdown. His passer rating when targeted is 111.9, with two of the incompletions to his name close calls in Atlanta on which he was ruled not to have maintained the process of the catch. For Watkins, those numbers and the targets that have come his way over the last two games represent a hugely positive consequence of his earlier discussion with Shanahan, and are reflective of the increasing faith both head coach and quarterback have in his abilities. “Going back to that week to where I did talk to Kyle, you know, for me, that was kind of, I wouldn’t say rock bottom, but almost for me,” he explained. “To be a drafted guy, to be able to not be out there to help my brothers win, just took a step back a little bit and to be able to talk to Kyle. “I feel like over these last couple of weeks, you can see it, being more involved in the offense and him being the play-caller and calling my number and then Brock being able to trust me to go in there and make the throw and for me to come down with the catch. These past couple of weeks, seeing the trust from Kyle is starting to grow. I’m super grateful. “Me and Brock have been working all offseason leading up to this moment. So, you know, like I said, I was that close two weeks ago. And then, you know, he put it up there again. I was able to come down with it. I’m just super grateful, super blessed to be able to be put in that position. We got a lot of couple guys coming back in a couple weeks. So we’ll see if I still have the same opportunity, but my job is to go out there and perform.” Jordan Watkins shows some nuance in his route at the bottom of the screen here. He gives the CB a little hesi move while working to his blind spot. Watkins puts the CB in a spin cycle before creating all kinda separation. Watkins changing speeds during his route is a great sign. pic.twitter.com/4DhWMZtexz — Kyle Posey (@KP_Show) November 9, 2026 There can be no argument that Watkins has performed over the last two weeks, with the persistence he showed in pressing Shanahan for answers, and in fine-tuning his rapport with Purdy paying huge dividends as he played a pivotal role in the 49ers getting back to winning ways. It is likely that Watkins will fall down the depth chart when Evans and Samuel return to the field but, through his desire to learn from his minor errors against the Falcons and his play when he does not have the ball, the former Ole Miss wideout has earned the opportunities that Purdy indicated will continue to come his way down the stretch. “I’m really excited for him,” Purdy said when asked about Watkins’ ascension. “Obviously more opportunities, more targets with some guys that have sort of been hurt. But regardless, I think he’s always sort of been getting ready since he’s been here. “I think something that’s cool too is the way he run blocks. He goes in there and he just shows that he’s down for the team. He’s down for the offense, whatever he needs to do when his number’s called. And then that sort of bleeds into him being reliable in the pass game and giving him opportunities with that. Like I’ve said, I think he does a great job with creating separation, getting in and out of cuts, coming down with contested catches. “So yeah, my trust has definitely grown in him more and more. And I’m excited to see what the rest of the season looks like playing with him.”
author: Nicholas McGee

title: 2026 NFL trade deadline: Will the Titans make any more moves?
summary: The Tennessee Titans already made the biggest move of the 2026 NFL trade deadline when they sent Jeffery Simmons to the Chicago Bears for two first round picks. That deal was made a week and a half before the deadline. It felt like that was just the beginning of moves Mike Borgonzi would be making. […]
full_text: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - OCTOBER 11: Calvin Ridley #0 of the Tennessee Titans runs with the ball against the Houston Texans at Nissan Stadium on October 11, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Tennessee Titans already made the biggest move of the 2026 NFL trade deadline when they sent Jeffery Simmons to the Chicago Bears for two first round picks. That deal was made a week and a half before the deadline. It felt like that was just the beginning of moves Mike Borgonzi would be making. Now, we sit just hours from the deadline, and the Titans have not made another move. There have been plenty of rumors surrounding guys like Amani Hooker, Tony Pollard, and Calvin Ridley, but to this point, those guys are all still in Nashville. That begs the question: Is Borgonzi done? Let’s take a look at the rumored players and see what makes sense as we approach today’s deadline: Amani Hooker Hooker is the most valuable of the three players who have been subject to rumors. He is coming off a 3-interception game against the Cincinnati Bengals. Yesterday, I asked on Twitter if you would trade Hooker for a second round pick. As of this writing, almost 77% said they would. Hooker is just 28 years old and playing at a high level. Borgonzi would probably need two picks, with one of them being on day 2, to move him. Tony Pollard Speaking of guys playing at a high level, Pollard is currently playing his best football as a Titan. He has 5 touchdowns in the Titans’ last two games. The reports out there suggest that Borgonzi doesn’t want to move him because he is important to Cam Ward’s development. That makes sense, but if he can get a fourth round pick or better for an aging running back, he needs to make that move. The thing that complicates this deal a little further is that there are a few running backs rumored to be available. Jonathan Taylor is at the top of the list. The rumors are the Indianapolis Colts are going to move him. Teams could be waiting to see that deal go down before making their best and final offer to the Titans. Calvin Ridley This one is easy to me. If a team calls and offers a pick, any pick, for Ridley, the Titans should take it. He isn’t going to be here after this year, and he hardly gets on the field as it is. When he does get on the field, he beats up every pass that is thrown his direction.

title: Titans, Cam Ward’s Week 10 challenge gets more complicated
summary: The Tennessee Titans were on the Week 9 bye. Everyone is excited to watch Cam Ward play football again after his Week 8 breakout versus the Cincinnati Bengals. The Week 10 matchup with the Jacksonville Jaguars will be difficult and is now more complicated following their trade for Pro Bowl safety Jessie Bates III. Ward […]
full_text: CINCINNATI, OHIO - NOVEMBER 01: Cam Ward #1of the Tennessee Titans against the Cincinnati Bengals at Paycor Stadium on November 01, 2026 in Cincinnati, Ohio. (Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Tennessee Titans were on the Week 9 bye. Everyone is excited to watch Cam Ward play football again after his Week 8 breakout versus the Cincinnati Bengals. The Week 10 matchup with the Jacksonville Jaguars will be difficult and is now more complicated following their trade for Pro Bowl safety Jessie Bates III . Ward was excellent against the Bengals . The sophomore No. 1 overall selection was accurate, decisive, and aggressive with ideal ball placement. Ward threw for 300+ yards for the first time in his career, and also had two touchdown passes (to Chimere Dike and Wan’Dale Robinson) for the first time this season. Trade: Falcons are sending former Pro Bowl safety Jessie Bates to the Jacksonville Jaguars in exchange for a 2027 2nd-round pick and a 2028 5th-round pick, sources tell ESPN. pic.twitter.com/zsvYXRXj0P — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) November 9, 2026 Ward completed 26/40 attempts for 304 yards, the aforementioned two TDs, and zero interceptions (and a lost fumble). Here’s another fact we hadn’t seen mentioned. In addition to Ward enjoying his first-ever 300-yard throwing performance, his 26 completions tied his second-most in a single game (he was 28/42 versus the Seattle Seahawks last season). The 65% completion percentage versus the Bengals tied his previous season-high (vs. the Eagles) from earlier this year. Ward is now tasked with building on that performance versus the Jaguars. This Anthony Campanile-coached unit is playing elite football. The Jaguars rank second in points per game allowed (15.1) and fifth in rushing (89.3). If there’s an area they’ve struggled, it’s against the pass, where they rank 22nd in yards allowed (229/game). Hence the trade for Bates. The three-time Pro Bowl safety is among the most consistent ballhawks in the league. Bates has one interception this year, bringing his career total to 28 INTs. He ranks third among active NFL defenders in interceptions, behind just Harrison Smith and Titans legend Kevin Byard. Bates has two career interceptions versus the Titans, including one in the painful 2021 postseason defeat. He’ll now play against the Titans twice in the coming weeks following his trade to Jacksonville from the Atlanta Falcons. Ward will have to navigate this challenge while attempting to continue improving.

title: Should Washington Commanders move Stefon Diggs at NFL trade deadline?
summary: On Monday, Sean McVay indicated that Puka Nucua is likely to be placed on injured reserve following multiple sprains to the ligaments in his knee, and with Davante Adams still on IR, the 5-4 L.A. Rams may now be motivated buyers for a wide receiver before Tuesday’s NFL trade deadline. One of their possible trade […]
full_text: On Monday, Sean McVay indicated that Puka Nucua is likely to be placed on injured reserve following multiple sprains to the ligaments in his knee, and with Davante Adams still on IR, the 5-4 L.A. Rams may now be motivated buyers for a wide receiver before Tuesday’s NFL trade deadline. One of their possible trade targets could be Washington Commanders wide receiver Stefon Diggs. The Rams are looking to win now, but one of their biggest stumbling blocks could be a lack of cap space to acquire a player at the deadline. There are, however, plenty of playoff contenders who need a receiver. Would the Commanders be willing to part with a DMV native they signed during training camp? And at what cost? Diggs is a proven, valuable commodity to the right team. According to Spotrac , since much of Diggs’ contract is tied to incentives, the team acquiring the Commanders wide receiver would only take on a $2.9 million cap hit. Diggs’ skill set and experience also make him a viable replacement for what Sean McVay will be missing while Nucua recovers from injury. Meanwhile, Diggs wasn’t used much early in Sunday’s game and ended up with three receptions on the day. His final catch, with under a minute left, got the Commanders within striking distance of beating the Rams and demonstrated his play-making ability but also caused some frustration for head coach Dan Quinn. In an interview with WUSA9, Quinn expressed how he would have liked Diggs to finish the play differently. Sometimes five extra yards can cost you more than they’re worth. Dan Quinn explained why he wanted Stefon Diggs to get out of bounds on the Commanders’ final drive instead of fighting for extra yards. Quinn breaks down Washington’s final seconds against the Rams. pic.twitter.com/jgunnTWXFz — Marshall Kramsky (@marshallkramsky) November 9, 2026 Diggs has been Washington’s most productive wide receiver this year, with 30 receptions for 303 receiving yards and 5 TDs, but also five drops, which have cost the team at various times during the season. The mercurial wide receiver also incurred a costly unsportsmanlike conduct penalty in Week 1 versus the Philadelphia Eagles. While the Commanders have significant losses of their own at the wide receiver position, at 2-5-1, their playoff hopes hang on the slim possibility they can overtake the Giants and Cowboys to win their division. A recent article floated Diggs’ trade value as a 2027 fourth-round selection, but that seems a bit steep for a soon to be 33-year-old wide receiver with only half the regular season left. The most likely compensation for any offer would be a 5th or 6th round selection. While Stefon Diggs still provides a proven receiving threat and veteran presence, Adam Peters may have to weigh the team’s current season outlook against the possibility adding more draft capital if the LA Rams or another team comes calling before today’s deadline. summary: The Daily Slop – 10 November 2026 Editor’s note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. Barroso/Europa Press via Getty Images) | Europa Press via Getty Images The Daily Slop – 10 November 2026 Editor’s note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. Enjoy! Commanders links Articles Bullock’s Film Room (subscription) Commanders Protection Plan Fails vs Rams Prior to the start of the season, not many people would have expected the Commanders to beat a Rams team consisting of Matthew Stafford, Puka Nacua, Aaron Donald and Myles Garrett. But the Rams were 4-4 entering the game and it was a game very much there for the taking. The Commanders defense held up relatively well, but the offense struggled to get much going after a strong start. One of the biggest issues the Commanders had on offense was the protection plan. The Rams had star pass rusher Myles Garrett back healthy after he missed most of the season injured. It was the first time the Rams had Garrett and star defensive tackle Aaron Donald on the field together. It’s a formidable pair. Donald may well go down in NFL history as the best interior defensive lineman ever and Garrett might well become the best edge rusher in NFL history. Both are freak athletes and are incredibly hard for even the best offensive lineman to block one-on-one. With such a strong pair of defensive lineman, it would make sense to build an entire game plan around preventing those two players from blowing up the entire offense. The last time the Commanders faced Garrett was in 2024, Jayden Daniels’ rookie season. Kliff Kingsbury was the offensive coordinator then and he put together a strong game plan to try and negate Garrett’s effectiveness . They used run plays, read-option plays, run-pass option plays (RPOs), multiple forms of misdirection, screens. Kingsbury also made sure to play with lots of tempo to tire out Garrett and used no-huddle to attack when Garrett wasn’t on the field and stop him from subbing back in. Most importantly, Kingsbury made sure to get a second pair of hands on him on almost every play. They would slide the line his way when they could, but they would always chip him. Everyone had a go at chipping him, receivers, tight ends and running backs. He never knew exactly who was going to chip him on any given play because of how often they switched it up. It was a terrific plan and Garrett failed to register a single stat in the game, which is a large part of why the Commanders were able to win that game back in 2024. Now, this game in 2026 is a different animal because the Rams also have Aaron Donald to worry about. But offensive coordinator David Blough was on Kingsbury’s staff back in 2024 and I had hoped he might have learned some lessons from Kingsbury’s plan to help deal with Garrett. Unfortunately, the protection plan was poor and nothing like that 2024 plan. The two most basic weapons you have in pass protection are chips and line slides. Chips are where you have a tight end, running back or occasionally a wide receiver align tight to the formation and bump the edge rusher before releasing into their routes. Line slides are when either all of the line, or at least part of it, slides to one side, providing extra help to that side. Far too often in this game, the Commanders didn’t use either of these weapons. The Commanders protection plan against Myles Garrett & Aaron Donald simply wasn't good enough. Commanders OLineman were left 1-on-1 against Garrett & Donald without any help from chips or line slides far too often. I broke down the faulty protection plan: https://t.co/uEhFT1rRBt pic.twitter.com/OLnZNNppNX — Mark Bullock (@MarkBullockNFL) November 9, 2026 Sports Illustrated Hughes’ View: The Commanders’ Center Gamble Left Jayden Daniels Exposed Lucas Patrick’s concussion sent rookie Matt Gulbin in against Myles Garrett while Nick Allegretti stayed on the sideline [Washington’s] latest issue on the offensive line stems from the center position: this past weekend, when their starter Lucas Patrick went down with a concussion, they turned to rookie Matt Gulbin. It’s ironic because Adam Peters and Dan Quinn spent the offseason trying to convince everyone that Nick Allegretti was that guy and would be the center for 2026. Allegretti has played two snaps since his last start, which came at right guard against the Seattle Seahawks in Week 3. In other words, he’s still the same journeyman offensive lineman who came here years ago looking for a chance to start, but better suited as a backup. They tried to sell the fanbase a pumpkin, hoping Cinderella logic would kick in and he’d turn into something more than a dried-up gourd that rots on a warm fall night. When asked about the situation Sunday after the game , Quinn said the staff has been working Allegretti more at guard now: “In that moment, I would have felt comfortable with Nick as well, but I thought, let’s give the guy who’s got the most reps.” Quinn also confirmed Allegretti was healthy. It makes sense that the coach would turn to the player who has practiced the most in the role; the problem is he said this in the preseason: “Nick is one of our smartest players, so that’s a position that you rely on.” Relied on so much that when the team looks for a replacement weeks later in crunch time with the season on the line, they turn to the sixth-round prospect with very little experience. Gulbin gave up a 12-yard sack to Myles Garrett on third-and-5 at the Rams’ 38, leaving Washington facing fourth-and-17, but who could be mad at a rookie who should have been given more help on that play? The Commanders’ protection plan failed when it mattered most Sunday. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Download the SB Nation app Commanders fans, take command of game day! Follow the action and share every cheer, question and instant reaction with fellow fans on the SB Nation app. Chat live during every game Browse with fewer ads Seamlessly move between communities Enjoy faster commenting and posting Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . The Athletic (paywall) The Commanders had a sixth-round rookie blocking Myles Garrett. How did we get here? Look, the Commanders didn’t lose to the Rams 20-13 solely because Patrick got dinged up and Gulbin had to replace him, tasked with trying to help block Myles Garrett and Aaron Donald when he hadn’t played in more than a month and had essentially just one game of experience in his NFL career. “It’s an excuse,” Gulbin said afterward. “I got to go out and do the expectations for the center position. I got to go out there and block them. And I don’t think I did a great job.” Credit for self-awareness. The situation is not of Gulbin’s making, and he can only perform the job in adverse circumstances to the best of his ability. But we’re focusing on Gulbin’s participation and Patrick’s injury and Allegretti’s absence because — well, in some way, the center position drove the talk around Washington’s entire offseason. And here it is, November now, with the Commanders’ season on the brink at 2-5-1, and it’s still dogging them as they head into a short week with a season’s-over-if-you-lose game at the New York Giants on Thursday night. This all sounds familiar, and some of it is definitely a rehash of old material. But it matters. It matters because, with the Commanders trailing by a touchdown and facing third-and-5 late in the fourth quarter, Garrett — playing for the first time in nearly two months — came from his position on the edge to rush up the middle. The issue isn’t that a rookie taken in the sixth round came in as an…

title: Washington Commanders Whiteboard: Notes and observations from Week 9
summary: Before the advent of media devices, football coaches at all levels used simple whiteboards to outline plays, map out player positions and explain schemes in real time. Nowadays digital playbooks and tablets have taken over, but coaches still use whiteboards on occasion to impart information quickly and effectively. The following are some quick notes and […]
full_text: LANDOVER, MD - NOVEMBER 08: Rams linebacker Myles Garrett (95) knocks the ball out forcing a fumble on Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels (5) during the second quarter during the Los Angeles Rams versus Washington Commanders National Football League game at Northwest Stadium on November 8, 2026 in Landover, MD. (Photo by Randy Litzinger/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Before the advent of media devices, football coaches at all levels used simple whiteboards to outline plays, map out player positions and explain schemes in real time. Nowadays digital playbooks and tablets have taken over, but coaches still use whiteboards on occasion to impart information quickly and effectively. The following are some quick notes and observations from the Washington Commanders ‘ 13-20 loss to the LA Rams at home. Daronte Jones had no answers for Puka Nucua Make no mistake, Puka Nucua is one of the best wide receivers in the league, and he is going to get his yards. This was a known fact heading into the matchup, but Daronte Jones and Washington’s defense knew the key was to simply limit him. Jones spoke openly about it in his Thursday presser , but when it came time to contain the All-Pro wide receiver, the defense appeared to have no idea how to accomplish it. Puka torched Washington’s secondary, hauling in 14 receptions for 150 receiving yards and one touchdown, and the Rams wide receiver didn’t have to work particularly hard to do it. The Commanders played zone coverage throughout the game and rarely tested Nacua with man or double coverage, and while Washington was successful limiting his yards after the catch, he picked them apart underneath. JP Finlay says the Commanders knew they had to stop Puka Nacua, but couldn't make enough plays. Also, they've got problems with protection. pic.twitter.com/AFGRD7usAS — 106.7 The Fan (@1067theFan) November 8, 2026 How did the rest of the Rams receivers fare? They combined for 78 total receiving yards and no touchdowns. There was simply no need to target them, as Washington’s defense never found a way to force the issue. The Rams ran the ball effectively in the second half with Kyren Williams, Blake Corum, and Nucua combining for 123 yards on the ground. It was enlightening to watch Sean McVay run a clinic on how to properly execute an offense with a heavy personnel emphasis. While some analysts were quick to point out that the defense wasn’t the reason the Commanders lost the game on Sunday, their performance is indicative of how coordinator Daronte Jones is unable to adjust his game plan from week to week. The pressure didn’t get home, the secondary couldn’t stop their playmakers, and the defense was reliant on turnovers to compete. Conversely, Minnesota DC Brain Flores changes his game plans weekly, and at times will shift away from his preferred zone schemes in favor of more man coverage when the matchup calls for it. David Blough’s offense does not have an identity yet When David Blough was promoted to offensive coordinator during the offseason, there was a lot of discussion about the number of quality offensive coordinators he had played or worked under and which he would draw from to build his own offensive scheme, including Jeff Brohm, Kevin O’Connell, Ben Johnson and even Kliff Kingsbury. Nine weeks into the season, fans are still wondering what Blough is trying to accomplish on the offensive side of the ball. At times, the Commanders’ offense leans into heavy personnel and under center looks before reverting to shotgun-based schemes with 11 personnel when things don’t go according to plan. Some plays are well-called and timely; others make little sense for the situation or the defensive looks. Blough spoke openly of wanting to utilize the screen game more, but never went back to it after having success early, and only one team has a lower percentage of screens than Washington this season. An excellent call by OC David Blough. Countered the blitz with a screen. White handled the rest. https://t.co/m5yS5ni9JF — Tashan Reed (@tashanreed) November 8, 2026 The Commanders are also supposedly implementing a wide-zone rushing attack, but with little to no evidence of it on the field or that offensive line coach Darnell Stapleton knows how to implement it. They actually found some success early in this matchup, then inexplicably went away from their running game later in the game. The pass protection also struggled and while a good portion of the problem is certainly on the offensive personnel, part of being an effective coordinator is scheming plays to maximize your strengths while providing a cohesive plan for the offense every week. The game plan versus the Rams should have called for chip blocks to help Brandon Coleman on the edge and designed roll-outs to move Daniels out of the pocket. Instead, fans saw very little of either one. I think this play perfectly explains the play-calling. Good design, lack of details kill it Good design to get Diggs an advantage in the slot, he's open but Jayden has to take off because Garrett is being blocked 1-on-1 by Sinnott Meanwhile two receivers are running to the flat pic.twitter.com/njjTGbTQYl — Nick Akridge (@nick_akridge) November 9, 2026 So far, David Blough seems to be simply calling plays instead of coordinating an NFL offense. The Week 5 edition of Whiteboard called for Anthony Lynn or another consultant to assist the rookie coordinator. Headed into Week 10, it may now be too late. The problems from Week 1 are still issues in Week 9 Similarly, the Week 1 Whiteboard article called out the fact that, while many of the faces had changed at the coordinator level, the same problems from last season persisted. Those include pre-snap penalties, and while Week 9 wasn’t quite as bad as the opener, the Commanders still had their fair share of false starts on their own home field. Meanwhile, other issues were also persistent and equally damaging. Both Stefon Diggs and Antonio Williams dropped catchable balls on critical downs, while looking ineffective at run blocking. Diggs also questionably tried to run for more yards instead of stepping out of bounds in the final moments of the game. Fans shouldn’t be surprised if Diggs is not invited back for another season, which would potentially have the wide receiver looking for his fourth new team in as many years. Antonio’s drop was brutal. Brutal. — Damien Bartonek (@tvBartonek) November 8, 2026 Jayden Daniels & Stefon Diggs connect to move the Commanders close to midfield with 30 seconds to go LARvsWAS on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/SYNnMl9V9Z — NFL (@NFL) November 8, 2026 It wasn’t all on Diggs. Dan Quinn also burned what would have been a valuable timeout earlier in the game by challenging a play that was clearly not going to be overturned. Once again, the Commanders were short on timeouts during the critical final moments of the game. The issues at the center spot had faded after the addition of Lucas Patrick in Week 2, but came back front and center after Patrick delivered a number of high snaps before leaving the game with a possible concussion. Instead of Nick Allegretti, who had received the unwavering support the coaching staff and front office all offseason, Patrick was replaced with sixth-round rookie Matt Gulbin. Whiteboard Week 2 concluded with this same question, following a game in which Jayden Daniels dislocated his elbow for a second time. At that point, it was theorized the team could make a comeback if Marcus Mariota could find a way to win a game or two and Daniels received positive news on a possible return. title: Commanders vs. Giants Monday injury report: Lucas Patrick in concussion protocol
summary: Commanders veteran Lucas Patrick has provided stability at the center spot, which was a point of chaos and poor performance before he was signed on Sept. 16. full_text: Commanders veteran Lucas Patrick has provided stability at the center spot, which was a point of chaos and poor performance before he was signed on Sept. 16. Nick Allegretti and rookie Matt Gulbin struggled before he got to Washington and when called to action, including Sunday’s loss to the L.A. Rams . That happened because Patrick suffered a concussion during the game and is now in the protocol. That puts his availability for Thursday’s game at the New York Giants in serious jeopardy. He was a DNP on the Monday injury report leading into that game, though it’s important to note that it was only an estimation because the Commanders didn’t conduct a formal workout. Head coach Dan Quinn was non-committal about whether Allegretti or Gulbin would fill in if Patrick can’t go during his Monday media session. Amik Robertson suffered an ankle injury on Sunday, but further evaluation shows that the veteran cornerback avoided a serious situation. Quinn told reporters on Monday that the Commanders are “optimistic” about Robertson’s availability for Thursday night’s game against the New York Giants . That was reflected in Monday’s practice report where he’s categorized as a full participant. Quinn also alluded to optimism surrounding WR Treylon Burks, who missed the Rams game with a foot injury, but it must be a bit guarded. Tuesday’s practice will be a big test for the receiver who is now part of the starting lineup. He was considered a non-participant on the estimated report. Center Lucas Patrick is in the concussion protocol and was also a DNP. Tight end Colson Yankoff (knee) was estimated to have been a non-participant. full_text: The Washington Commanders lost another game on Sunday, this one a 20-13 result against the Los Angeles Rams. Their record sits at 2-5-1 , putting their season on the brink if it isn’t over already. The 24-hour rule doesn’t even apply here despite extreme frustration with Washington’s inability to get out of it’s own way. Why? A defining matchup with the New York Giants is on the immediate horizon, scheduled for primetime on Thursday Night Football . While Quinn preached the fact that the Commanders must move on quickly, the Commanders head coach also addressed some missteps against the Rams in his Monday virtual press conference. Quinn backed offensive coordinator David Blough , whose play calling has taken sharp criticism from the fan base. He discussed the need for more consistent execution but also said there’s a need for better decision-making at the end of games. Quinn also outlined his communication routines with owner Josh Harris, the need for improvement in the run game and why Puka Nacua and Myles Garrett got loose and wrecked Sunday’s game. Here’s the Quinn press conference in its entirety, plus some highlights from the virtual session: Dan Quinn Changes coming? (Photo by Patrick Smith/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Daily Slop Editor’s note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. Enjoy! Commanders links Articles The Athletic Commanders’ mystifying final drive symbolic of an offense that keeps misfiring The Washington Commanders still had one more shot with eight seconds left, and if there was ever a team that desperately needed to show it could finally get things right with the game on the line in the final seconds, it was this one. Down by a touchdown with the ball at the Los Angeles Rams’ 31-yard line, Washington had time for at least one play, maybe two if necessary, to get the ball in the end zone. And somehow — somehow — the ball was not thrown there. Not once. Not on the Commanders’ first attempt, when Jayden Daniels’ deep pass over the middle sailed far over the head of receiver Stefon Diggs, and not on the second, when Daniels dumped the ball off on a crosser to tight end Chig Okonkwo, who broke a couple of tackles before the play sputtered. Okonkwo ran up against the sideline to about the Rams’ 11 and tried to pitch the ball backward to keep the play alive but instead tossed it onto the ground, at which point the play fizzled, along with one of Washington’s last hopes of keeping its season intact. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE The Athletic The Commanders had a sixth-round rookie blocking Myles Garrett. How did we get here? Nick Allegretti remained on the sideline. He did not play a snap. In the past five games, the player the Commanders said for six months they were counting on to be their starting center has played a total of two snaps. “We went with how we’ve been practicing,” coach Dan Quinn said. And that’s with Matt Gulbin, that sixth-round rookie, backing up Lucas Patrick — the center the Commanders signed off the street in September — at center, and Allegretti backing up Chris Paul at left guard. Look, the Commanders didn’t lose to the Rams 20-13 solely because Patrick got dinged up and Gulbin had to replace him, tasked with trying to help block Myles Garrett and Aaron Donald when he hadn’t played in more than a month and had essentially just one game of experience in his NFL career. “It’s an excuse,” Gulbin said afterward. “I got to go out and do the expectations for the center position. I got to go out there and block them. And I don’t think I did a great job.” To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Commanders fans, take command of game day!
